abstract: The issue of the transport network was touched upon in the RAN#91-bis meeting and was also discussed by email [3], where certain progress has been made [4]. In the present paper we discuss the issue in more detail and propose to build on the progress reached in the email discussion.
title: Fronthaul transport network aspects

abstract: In this contribution we propose to discuss the issue of different RAN functional splits and their transport network performance requirements, in accordance with the amendment to “requirements for architecture and migration of next generation radio access technologies” of TR 38.913 [2], specifically “the RAN internal function split”.
title: RAN functional split analysis

abstract: The issue of RAN-CN interfaces is currently being discussed in RAN3, RAN2 and SA2. Unfortunately, there are certain discrepancies between these groups. In this contribution we try to outline these and provide some additional RAN-CN interface scenarios to be captured in the TR.
title: RAN-CN interface aspects

abstract: New RAT supporting Ultra-Reliable and Low Latency Communications may support end-to-end latency of 1ms as specified in TR 22.862 [1]. The local breakout is one possible solution enabling the ultra-low latency. In this contribution the description of the existing local breakout solutions both specified in 3GPP and discussed in the mobile edge computing (MEC) is presented. Some aspects regarding the local breakout enabling in the NR RAN are discussed.
title: Local Breakout for Ultra-Low Latency Communications

abstract: In this contribution we discuss certain aspects pertaining to the issue of the control/user plane separate in RAN in accordance with the amendment to “requirements for architecture and migration of next generation radio access technologies” of TR 38.913 [2], specifically “the RAN architecture should allow for C-plane/U-plane separation”.
title: C-plane and U-plane separation of the next generation radio access network

abstract:
After offline discussion, we provide the following observations and proposals.
Observation 1: In current TS38.423, for NGEN-DC and NR-DC deployment (i.e. S-NG-RAN is gNB), the PCell ID IE shall be included for avoiding PCell confusion.
Observation 2: In current TS38.423, for NE-DC deployment (i.e., S-NG-RAN is eLTE), it is not clear whether PCell ID IE is included for avoiding PCell confusion
Proposal 1: Removal of restriction on when SN is gNB, i.e., for NE-DC deployment (i.e., the S-NG-RAN is eLTE), the PCell ID shall also be included to avoid PCI confusion.
title: PCI confusion: Summary of offline discussion

abstract:
It is proposed to note as agreed:
- RAN3 agrees to select either of the two solutions from the summary at the next meeting (RAN3 #106).
- In case of a HO with EN-DC configured, the source MeNB shall include all E-RABs of the UE in the HO REQ, irrespectively of the hosting point.
In order to enable possible data forwarding towards the target MeNB, all SN-terminated E-RABs shall be listed. If the “UE context keep” indicator is included, the SgNB shall maintain the EN-DC config acknowledged to the target MeNB for this UE.
- Possible indication of the EN-DC configuration in case of a HO with SN change will be discussed at RAN3 #106.

It is proposed to endorse R3-195322.

abstract:
Based on the offline summary, the following are proposed for agreement: 
Proposal 1: (Downlink) No need to send another SN STATUS TRANSFER to inform that HFN has been increased (for target’s encryption).
Proposal 2: WA: (Downlink) The last SN STATUS TRANSFER is the same as legacy, for which normal data forwarding follows.
Proposal 3: (Downlink) It is FFS in RAN3 whether/how the source informs discarding of already forwarded PDCP SDUs.
Proposal 4: (Uplink) UL delivery to the CN from the source continues until the source sends the last SN Status Transfer to the target (same as legacy). The target won’t forward uplink packets in-sequence to the CN until it receives this last SN STATUS TRANSFER (as in the legacy).
Proposal 5: (Uplink) The last SN STATUS TRANSFER sent for DL is also used for UL (for which the normal data forwarding follows as in the legacy)
Proposal 6: (Uplink) It is FFS in RAN3 whether we allow the source to send an intermediate SN STATUS TRANSFER (between the first and the last) to convey uplink out-of-sequence receiving status so that the target can send PDCP status report to the UE immediately when accessed.
Proposal 7: No need to inform CT4 about GTP-U extension header.

consequencesIfNotApproved: VoWiFi triggered EPS fallback or inter-RAT fallback for IMS voice is not supported.
reasonForChange:
T-Mobile has identified a critical NR SA deployment issue with VoWiFI that prevents VoWiFi calls from falling back to LTE after initialling being connected to gNB.  SA-2 approved the necessary specification changes in December 2019.  What remains to fix this issue is for RAN3 to align the text in TS 38.413 with the latest version of SA TS 23.502, this was submitted in R3-203334, however RAN3 was unable to treat this contribution because of limited resources. Due to the urgent nature of this problem the consigning companies submitted company CR to plenary for approval. 
As analyzed in discussion paper RP-200607, in the VoWiFi to NR mobility, the IMS PDU session with both QoS flow for SIP and QoS flow for voice media are established together. So, the PDU Session Resource Setup procedure and Initial Context Setup may further trigger EPS fallback or RAT fallback for IMS voice, refer to step 3-5 in Figure 4.13.6.3-1, TS 23.502.
Current NGAP standard only supports PDU Session Resource Modification triggered voice fallback. It is proposed to add procedural text for suport of PDU Session Resource Setup triggered voice fallback. The support is then impliclty extended to the Initial Context Setup procedure (as per general statement in section 8.3.1.2 concerning handling of PDU Session Resource Setup Request List IE).
summaryOfChange: Allow PDU Session Resource Setup procedural text to indicate that the cause value "IMS voice EPS fallback or RAT fallback triggered" in PDU Session Resource Setup Response Transfer IE and PDU Session Resource Setup Unsuccessful Transfer IE is applicable.

abstract: In RAN3#91-bis, splitting of the RAN architecture into a “central unit” and a “distributed unit” was discussed. However, the discussion focused more on the options of the functional split between the central and distributed units, and less was discussed about having a standard interface between them. In this contribution, we describe some motivation to study such a standard interface, and propose to create a section in the RAN3 TR to capture such study.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
New procedure needs to be triggered in certain scenarios just for the purpose of providing the NR UE Security Capabilities IE to the eNB.

Established MME behaviour for handling RAN impacting parameters during a TAU needs to be modified.
reasonForChange: The NR UE Security Capabilities IE was defined and included in several messages at RAN3#98. However one scenario was not considered in detail: after connected mode mobility from a non-supporting MME, the new MME receives the information on NR capabilities as part of the NAS TAU procedure, but needs to trigger a UE Context Modification procedure just for the purpose of providing the information to the eNB. This extra procedure will happen for every single supporting UE after such a handover. However it seems much simpler to enable the MME to provide the same information with the TAU response (i.e. in the DL NAS TRANSPORT) and this aligns with estabished MME behaviour for the change of any RAN impacting parameter (e.g. HRL) during the connected mode TAU procedure.
summaryOfChange: Add the NR UE Security Capabilities IE to the DL NAS TRANSPORT message .
title: Add NR UE Security Capabilities to DL NAS Transport message

consequencesIfNotApproved: MN is not aware of the situation and will not react appropriately when the SN releases the bearer due to reaching max Count value.

reasonForChange: In LTE DC, the SCG and MCG configurations were compiled into a single message for the UE. Therefore, the SN had to receive the most recent MCG configuration, to add SCG config to it before the combined config was sent to the UE. In EN-DC, MCG and SCG configurations are compiled separately. Therefore, it cannot happen that the SN adds outdated MCG config.

consequencesIfNotApproved: EN-DC would lack a means for the en-gNB to report inactivity to the MeNB.
reasonForChange: There is currently no function available on X2 to allow an en-gNB to report inactivity on the resources under its control. The only way how an en-gNB can report inactivity to the MeNB is to release resources. The MeNB could have good reasons to further keep the DC configuration if the en-gNB is able to keep resources under its control and is not forced to release them due to resource shortage.

"Maximum MCG admittable E-RAB Level QoS Parameters" is used to delivery MeNB admittable QoS parameters of GBR DRB to SgNB. However, this IE is encoded differently in two places: 
in “E-RABs To Be Added List” as “GBR QoS Information”; and 
in “E-RABs To Be Modified List” as “E-RAB Level QoS Parameters”.
Because this IE is for GBR DRB only, the one in “E-RABs To Be Modified List” is incorrect.
summaryOfChange:
Corrected "Maximum MCG admittable E-RAB Level QoS Parameters" in “E-RABs To Be Modified List” to “GBR QoS Information”.

summaryOfChange:
The main change is as follow:
1)Since MAC is responsible for the activation/deactivation of PDCP duplication, MAC entity needs to know the initial status of PDCP duplication i.e. active or inactive.
2)PDCP entity needs to know the LCID of the primary path. So, the information should be available on X2 interface.

reasonForChange:
In 9.3.1.75 Resource Coordination E-UTRA Cell Information, the E-UTRA PRACH Configuration IE is optional. There is no procedure text describing the optionality. But in ASN.1 this is added as a mandatory IE

In previous discussion, it was agreed that this IE is optional. This since the information is per cell and is not needed to be updated for each UE.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce a new IE to indicate when this mandatory IE shall be ignored. 

Impact Analysis: 
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because the possibility to ignore the IE is introduced with criticality reject, which means both nodes will understand whether this is allowed.
This CR has an impact under functional and protocol point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects the UE context management procedures.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Network sharing can not be supported completely in R15.
reasonForChange:
At the previous RAN3 meeting, it was argued that in the case of network sharing, according to TS 38.401 the Initial UL RRC message is used to transfer both the msg3 and the msg5 towards the gNB-CU. Based on that the following was agreed:

RAN3 agree to add RRC-Container-MSG5 IE to INITIAL UL RRC MESSAGE TRANSFER

We believe that the new gNB-CU should know how the UE was configured both, to handle it correctly now and to be able to generate a valid delta configuration in a subsequent reconfiguration. In order for the new CU to have the ability to apply delta RRC Configuration, the content of the RRCSetup sent by the old gNB-CU needs tobe known because a delta configuration is based on the RRCSetup content the old CU sent. This highlights the need for the new CU to know the msg4 content.
We also believe that the names MSG4 and MSG5 are prone to cause confusion. In fact, “Msg4” and “Msg5” are not official names to describe RRC messages.
summaryOfChange:
We add an RRC container for RRCSetup in INITIAL UL RRC MESSAGE TRANSFER.
Change the names of MSG4 and MSG5 to RRC-Container-RRCSetup and RRC-Container-RRCSetupComplete.

consequencesIfNotApproved: IPSec tunnel cannot be set up beforehand, which incurs additional end user delays.
reasonForChange: Current specification does not support an explicit mechanism to exchange IPSec addresses for U-Plane during setup and configuration update procedures. However, for IPsec, given that both gNB-CU-CP and gNB-CU-UP may be virtualized, IPsec addresses terminated directly at the node (e.g., when SEG is not used) may need to be updated as they may change over time due to up/down-scaling of resources. Further, for U-Plane case, exchanging IPsec addresses at interface setup and configuration update procedures allows “apriori” IPsec tunnel establishment. This is useful in order to avoid the incurred delayed when establishing the IPsec tunnel.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce means to convey IPsec addresses during interface setup and configuration update procedures.

reasonForChange:
It was discussed in R3-19xxxx that for auto discovery of Xn in case of disaggregated architecture for gNB, i.e. CU/DU split or CP/UP separation at gNB side, the GTP Transport Layer Address and corresponding IP-Sec Transport Layer Address should be provided by gNB-DU or gNB-CU-UP, but in current spec, these addresses are not available, i.e. not provided to gNB-CU-CP from gNB-DU over F1.
In addition, for F1-U itself, IPSec tunel for GTP traffic could also be established during F1 setup phase, and related endpoint addresses could be updated through gNB-CU/gNB-DU update procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The EN-DC Configuration Update procedure would lack the possibility to provide protocol level feedback by means of the Criticality Diagnostics IE.
ASN.1 definition and tabular representation of the EN-DC SETUP REQUEST, the EN-DC SETUP RESPONSE, the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE and the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE messages would stay misalined.
reasonForChange:
Tabular and ASN.1 of the EN-DC X2 SETUP REQUEST, the EN-DC X2 SETUP RESPONSE, the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE and the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE messages are not aligned:
In all messages, the CHOICE type IE does not show any assigned criticality as specified in ASN.1.
In the tabular representation of the EN-DC X2 SETUP REQUEST message, the NR Neighbour Information IEs erroneously shows an assigned criticality.
In the tabular representation of the EN-DC X2 SETUP RESPONSE message, the NR Neighbour Information IEs erroneously show an assigned criticality
In the tabular representation of the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE message, in the Served NR Cells To Modify IE, the order of the Served NR Cell Information IE and the NR Deactivation Indication IE is wrong and both IEs do not have any assigned criticality.
The ASN.1 definition of the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE message is lacking the Criticality Diagonstics IE. For backwards compatibilit reasons, the Criticality Diagnostics IE was inserted as last IE, both, in tabular and ASN.1.
In the tabular representation of the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE message, the List of Served NR Cells IE contains for the NR Neighbour Information IE an assigned criticality, which is not aligned with ASN.1.
summaryOfChange:
For 1), in tabular, criticality was included as specified in ASN.1
For 2) and 3), in tabular, respective assigned criticalities for the NR Neighbour Information IEw were removed.
For 4), in tabular, the order of the IEs has been corrected and the assigned criticality removed. 
For 5), in ASN.1, the Criticality Diagnostics IE is included 
For 6), in tabular, the assigned criticality for the NR Neighbour Information IE was removed.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
For the case of no RRC connection between UE and SN, not including UAI in the RRC transfer message would lead to power saving fail.
No clear cause value for MN for SN initiated SN release procedure
reasonForChange:
UE may release the SN for power saving in dual connection. RAN 2 has a conclusion that UE transmits SCG specific UE assistance information (UAI) in a transparent container to the MN and the MN then forwards the received container to the SN. For this case, the current release not includes UAI in RRC container. It would cause UAI cannot be sent from MN to SN by RRC transfer.
Since the power saving prodedure is triggered by UE, introducing UAI to RRC container as UE report IE achieving SN release procedure would be much reasonable. Furthermore, reusing the existing IE would have little impact on specifications.
In addition,  it is better to introduce “UE power saving” as a new cause value for SN initiated SN release procedure. Base on the conclusion in the last meeting for power saving procedure, it was agreed to introduce a new cause value.
summaryOfChange:
Adding UAI to RRC container as UE report IE.
Introducing“UE power saving”  as a new cause value for SN initiated SN release procedure
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR is a clarification and has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on power saving.
This CR is backward compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Confusion regarding the extensibility of the NGAP Elementary Procedure List.
reasonForChange: The definition of the NGAP-ELEMENTARY-PROCEDURES-CLASS-1 and NGAP-ELEMENTARY-PROCEDURES-CLASS-2 information object sets do not have extension marks, which is not aligned with other specifications (e.g. XnAP, F1AP, E1AP) and creates confusion when introducing new NGAP procedures.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce an extension mark in the following asn.1 definitions:
NGAP-ELEMENTARY-PROCEDURES-CLASS-1
NGAP-ELEMENTARY-PROCEDURES-CLASS-2

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
A receiving node not implementing this CR is not impacted since NGAP-ELEMENTARY-PROCEDURES-CLASS-1 and NGAP-ELEMENTARY-PROCEDURES-CLASS-2 are not directly used in any definitions. Instead, the higher level NGAP-ELEMENTARY-PROCEDURES is used which merges content of the above two Information Object Sets and includes an extension mark. This change is backwards compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: It will force the MeNB to understand the ASN.1 structure of 38.331, which will put implementation burden on eNB.
reasonForChange:
In the 36.423 RRC TRANSFER message, the IAB Information IE is defined, its content of the RRC Container IE is defined that it “includes the UL-DCCH-Message as defined in subclause 6.2.1 of TS 38.331 [31] containing the IABOtherInformation message.”.

This will force the eNB to understand and to dig into the detail of the  NR 38.331 ASN.1 in order to find the IABOtherInformation message from the 38.331 UL-DCCH-Message, then put into the 36.423 IAB Information IE in RRC Container IE.

From the Rel-15 we already specified that for all the 38.331 signalling messages that are transferred from UE via eNB to the SgNB, the eNB when received 36.331 ULInformationTransferMRDC message, just transparently transfer the content to the SgNB.
For this IABOtherInformation message, it is included in the UL-DCCH-Message as defined in 38.331, and 38.331 UL-DCCH-Message is contained in the 36.331 ULInformationTransferMRDC message the ul-DCCH-MessageNR-r15 IE. (refer to 36.331).
So when the eNB receive the 36.331 ULInformationTransferMRDC message, it can just transparently transfer the content of ul-DCCH-MessageNR-r15 via 36.423 RRC TRANSFER message to the SgNB, including this IABOttherInformtion message.
summaryOfChange:
Remove the IAB Information IE from the RRC TRANSFER message, instead, add in the semantic description in the RRC Container IE of the NR UE Report IE.

The procedure text is also removed to follow the existing way i.e. no special description of the receiving node behaviour when receive any content in the RRC container IE of the NR UE Report IE.


Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) under functional point of view. The impact can be considered isolated, because the changes concern to only the RRC Transfer message its RRC container. 
The change is ASN.1 NON-BACKWARD COMPATIBLE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the network is not implemented according to the CR; the UE does not receive user plane traffic prioritized per priority services (e.g. MPS) requirements.
reasonForChange:
In all cases except when a gNB operates as in IAB-donor, the DSCP marking of downlink user plane packets over the F1-U interface is conducted at the gNB-CU-UP per TS 38.474 (Rel-16). However, in support of IAB at the IAB-donor gNB, the DSCP marking responsibility is transferred to the gNB-CU-CP and the DSCP marking is signalled over the E1 interface to the gNB-CU-UP per TS 38.463 (Rel-16). 
In order to support priority services (e.g. MPS), DSCP marking at the gNB-CU-CP should be based on 5G QoS Identifier (5QI) , the Priority Level (if explicitly signalled), and other NG-RAN traffic parameters (e.g. ARP). The CR adds the necessary statements in TS 38.474 to be used for the DSCP derivation at the gNB-CU-CP.
summaryOfChange:
Specify that the DSCP derivation at the gNB-CU-CP is based on 5G QoS Identifier (5QI) , the Priority Level (if explicitly signalled), and other NG-RAN traffic parameters (e.g. ARP) for priority services (e.g. MPS) user plane traffic, when the gNB supports IAB and operates as an IAB-donor, as specified in the non-IAB case.  
Impact Analysis:
Impacted 5G architecture option:
NR-SA
Impacted functionality:
IAB operation at the IAB-donor node.
Inter-operability:
No impact to the UE.
If the network is not implemented according to the CR; the UE does not receive user plane traffic prioritized per MPS requirements.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The maxNARFCN value in ASN.1 is error.
reasonForChange:
For the maxNARFCN value, there is a mismatch in the tabular and in ASN.1.
In 9.2.1.151, the maxNARFCN is 3279165, the same as the maximum value of NR carrier frequency defined in TS 38.331.
In ASN.1, it is shown as “maxNARFCN	INTEGER ::= 32”.

So the maxNARFCN value in ASN.1 shall be corrected to align with TS38.331 as 3279165.
summaryOfChange:
The maxNARFCN value in ASN.1 is corrected to 3279165.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact because the change only affects the maxNARFCN value in ASN.1.
This is an NBC change for Rel-16.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The spec is not correct as originally intended and may unnecessarily create error handling which should not be.
reasonForChange: The SCG Activation Status IE has been introduced into SGNB ADDITION/MODIFICATION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE messages as criticality "ignore". However, in the final BLCR (R3-222903), in the SGNB ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message, it was mistakenly put it as "reject" (while in ASN.1 was with "ignore") and when the BLCR was incorporated into TS 36.423 v17.0.0, the ASN.1 criticality was fixed to "reject" to be aligned with the tabular. However, "ignore" is indeed correct as originally intended.
summaryOfChange:
1) In the SGNB ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message, the criticality of the SCG Activation Status IE is changed to "ignore" as originally intended.
2) ASN.1 is also fixed accordingly.
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on SCG activation status feedback function during SgNB Addition procedure.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the multicast MBS session modification function.
This CR is non backward compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The semantics of the Burst Arrival Time IE remain unclear.
reasonForChange:
The Burst Arrival Time IE reuses the same encoding as the RRC ReferenceTime IE, which is a sequence of four INTEGER values having decreasing time granularity as shown below:
ReferenceTime-r16 ::=           SEQUENCE {
    refDays-r16                         INTEGER (0..72999),
    refSeconds-r16                      INTEGER (0..86399),
    refMilliSeconds-r16                 INTEGER (0..999),
    refTenNanoSeconds-r16               INTEGER (0..99999)
}

It is unclear what “truncated to 1 us granularity” means in the context of the above encoding structure (since e.g. the value of the IE cannot be shortened, nor can the 10ns granularity of the IE be changed).
secretaryRemarks:
Endorsed CRs from RAN3#119bis-e

Source modified on 5/10/2023. Original source : Ericsson, Huawei, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell
summaryOfChange:
The semantics description of the Burst Arrival Time IE is reworded to: “provided with 1us accuracy”. 

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR does not have impact from protocol point of view.
This CR may have an impact under functional point of view because, along the current semantics, there are various interpretations (and implementations) of the current IE possible. The impact depends on which interpretation a potential implementation has chosen.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the Burst Arrival Time IE.
title: Correction of Burst Arrival Time semantics description

consequencesIfNotApproved: The gNB-CU-CP cannot provide the Unicast NG-U UL Transport Layer Information IE in MBS NG-U Information at 5GC IE to gNB-CU-UP.
reasonForChange:
For NG-U tunnel establishment procedure of both broadcast session and multicast session, the current version of NGAP does not specify the UL GTP-U tunnel info for NG-U unicast transport. In the current version of TS 37.483, MBS NG-U Information at 5GC IE uselessly includes Unicast NG-U UL Transport Layer Information when unicast transport, which is never provided by 5GC. Thus, the choice that Unicast NG-U UL Transport Layer Information IE in MBS NG-U Information at 5GC IE should be removed. 
And also, the presence of MBS NG-U Information at 5GC IE in the BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at 5GC IE is mandatory for BC Bearer Context To Setup IE according in tabular and in the ASN.1. However, the gNB-CU-CP cannot provide this if the 5GC doesn’t provide the multicast transport address. Therefore, the presence of BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at 5GC IE in BC Bearer Context To Setup IE should be updated to optional
secretaryRemarks:
Endorsed CRs from RAN3#119bis-e

summaryOfChange:

Impact Analysis:
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification, and will cause non-backward compatible issue on the NG-U tunnel establishment function.
title: Correction on NG-U tunnel aspect for MBS session

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Value 0 for priority level IE included in the Non Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE and Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE may be erroneously used in the specification.   
Not aligned between the Tabular and the ASN.1 for the priority level IE included in the Non Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE and Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE, and included in the NG-RAN Allocation and Retention Priority IE.
reasonForChange:
The priority level IE included in the Non Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE and Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE is used to indicate the priority level for a QoS flow, with its IE type as Integer (1..127).  However, in the ASN.1, its value range starts from 0, as shown as follows. 
QoSPriorityLevel ::= INTEGER (0..127, ...)
And in the NGAP and XnAP, it is correctly specified that its value starts from 1.  

In addition, the priority level IE included in NG-RAN Allocation and Retention Priority IE is used to indicate the ARP priority, with the IE type as INTEGER (1..15). But in the ASN.1, its value range starts from 0 as shown as follows. 

PriorityLevel	::= INTEGER { spare (0), highest (1), lowest (14), no-priority (15) } (0..15)
secretaryRemarks:
Endorsed CRs from RAN3#119bis-e

Source modified on 5/10/2023. Original source : Huawei, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, BT, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell
summaryOfChange:
To have backward compatible change, 
for 9.3.1.51 priority level IE included in the Non Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE and Dynamic 5QI Descriptor IE, add texts in the semantics description that the value 0 is not used in this version of the specification.  
for the 9.3.1.29 NG-RAN Allocation and Retention Priority IE, update the priority level starting from 0. 

 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has an impact under protocol point of view. 
The impact cannot be considered isolated because the change affects priority level included in the ARP and the QoS parameters.
title: Correction of Priority Level

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear which TNL associations should be removed/updated. It is unclear which port number is used for the endpoint of an added X2 TNL association.
reasonForChange:
For supporting multiple SCTP associations between one eNB and en-gNB pair, 
In the current specifications it is not clear how to interpret the TNLA To Update List IE and the TNLA To Remove List IE. Namely, it is not clear how to identify the TNL Associations to be updated or removed depending on the information contained in these IEs. 
It is unclear what port number is used when an X2 TNL association is added and if the endpoint that is added contains only an IP Address.
The text to describe the EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE and EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE messages implies that both nodes are able to initiate the update of TNL association, which is not aligned with the description in Successful Operation wherein the eNB is only given as the receving node for the update of TNL association operation.
secretaryRemarks: Endorsed CRs from RAN3#119bis-e
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that the total number of endpoints corresponding to the associations to be removed/updated may be multiple.
Clarify that when an TNLA To Add List IE is added and if the endpoint that is added contains only an IP Address, the port no. is assumed to be 36422.
Delete the text to describe the messages related to the update of TNL association in 9.1.2.34 and 9.1.2.35.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only implies a clarification of the EN-DC Configuration Update procedure description

title: Corrections on TNL association addition, update and removal (E1)

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear which TNL associations should be removed/updated. It is unclear which port number is used for the gNB-CU-CP endpoint of the TNL associations to be added with only an IP address.
reasonForChange:
In the current specifications it is not clear how to interpret the gNB-CU-UP TNLA To Remove List IE, the gNB-CU-CP TNLA To Remove List IE, and the gNB-CU-CP TNLA To Update List IE. Namely, it is not clear how to identify the TNL Associations to be removed or modified depending on the information contained in these IEs.
Moreover, it is unclear what port number is used when a new TNL association is added and if the newly added gNB-CU-CP endpoint contains only an IP Address.
secretaryRemarks: Endorsed CRs from RAN3#119bis-e
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that the total number of endpoints corresponding to the associations to be removed/updated may be multiple.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Discrepancy between the tabular and the ASN.1 definitions remains.
reasonForChange:
The gNB-CU-UP UE ID is mandatory in the RESOURCE STATUS UPDATE message, but optional in the ASN.1. The correct is the tabular definition – for an UE-associated signalling both IDs shall always be included. Also, the criticality is different in ASN.1 and in the tabular, but here the ASN.1 version may be assumed correct.
On the other hand, the HW Capacity information is optional in tabular definition of the message, while mandatory in ASN.1 – again, the tabular definition is correct definition considering intented functionality (the HW Capacity can be explicitly requested, so possibly may not be needed to be signalled).

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment between NGAP/XnAP for Value range of Extended Packet Delay Budget IE.
reasonForChange:
In order to support service that can be used over satellite access type, SA2 already agreed to extend PDB value for 5QI 10 to 1100ms in Rel-17 [S2-2106653]. 
Therefore, the maximum PDB value in RAN side should be extended to 1100ms for Rel-17. Also, it is good to support this extension while keeping the 0.01 ms granularity to be future-proof.

In order to align the PDB value in all RAN interfaces, it is proposed to extend the PDB value in E1AP.

consequencesIfNotApproved: When the IAB-node uses EN-DC where only the SN supports IAB-donor functionality, the IAB-DU may continue serving UE(s) even if it has been deauthorized.
reasonForChange:
In TS36.413, Section 8.3.4.2 (UE Context Modification Request) state for the IAB Authorized IE:
 If the IAB Authorized IE is set to "not authorized" for an IAB-MT, the eNB shall, if supported, initiate actions to ensure that the IAB node will not serve any UE(s).
In Rel-16, IAB supports the EN-DC scenario, where the IAB-node’s SN is the F1-terminating IAB-donor while the IAB-node’s MN (eNB) has no donor functionality. Since the MN maintains the CP connection towards the EPC, it receives the IAB Authorized IE, but it itself cannot initiate any actions to ensure that the IAB-node will not service any UE(s). It is therefore necessary to allow this MN to inform the SN about the IAB authorization status so that the SN can apply the actions defined above. This issue can be addressed by allowing the MN to insert the IAB Authorized IE into the SGNB ADDITION REQUEST message and the SGNB MODIFICATION REQUEST message toward the SN. In this manner, the SN can apply the above actions

consequencesIfNotApproved: Wrong Payload Protocol Identifier (PPID) for DTLS over SCTP in E1AP.
reasonForChange:
The Payload Protocol Identifier (PPID) to be used by SCTP for the application layer protocol E1AP should be assigned by IANA. As assigned by IANA, the PPID for DTLS over SCTP should be 69. However, in current specification, PPID for DTLS over SCTP in E1AP is wrongly set to 67.

Therefore, the misalignment PPID value for E1AP DTLS over SCTP
 between E1AP and IANA should be corrected.
summaryOfChange:
To introduce the new reference of IANA (Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) Parameters).
To replace the wrong PPID number with IANA reference.

reasonForChange:
There are some editorial errors in Section 5.3 (copied as below)

INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST	message:
-	the following IEs shall be ignored, when received:
-	Core Network Assistance Information for RRC INACTIVE IE
…
-	5G ProSe UE PC5 Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE
-	5G ProSe PC5 QoS Parameters IE-	RG Level Wireline Access Characteristics IE: the information given within this IE between the W-AGF and the AMF shall be stored in the UE context by the W-AGF as specified in TS 23.316 [6].
-	Notification Control IE included in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE
-	Alternative QoS Parameters Set List IE included in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE

The “5G ProSe PC5 QoS Parameters IE” is part of the IEs to be ignored, and it is incorrectlyed placed in the same bullet as RG Level Wireline Access Characteristics IE.
The Notification Control IE and Alternative QoS Parameters Set List IE are in the wrong place. They belong to “the following IEs shall be ignored, when received:”
summaryOfChange:

consequencesIfNotApproved: The procedure texts are not consistent for the user location information for N3IWF.
reasonForChange:
As agreed in NGAP CR1196 (see R3-247082), the N3IWF user location information IE was renamed as N3IWF user location information with port number IE to include the port number, and a new N3IWF user location information without port number IE was agreed to not include the port number. This is due to the fact that the port number is optional for the N3IWF user location information, as described in TS 23.501. 

However, the above agreements were not reflected over the procedure texts yet, where the N3IWF user location information IE was described.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The behaviour of eNB/en-gNB remains unclear.
reasonForChange:
In last meeting, it was agreed to clarify that eNB/NG-RAN node shall always include all neighbour cells in case there is any change on serving cell information or neighbour cell information in eNB/NG-RAN Node Configuration Update procedure. And the corresponding CRs are agreed in R3-247880 and R3-247881 respectively.

Similarly, the above working principle should be also applied to EN-DC case. However, there is no corresponding description in the current EN-DC Configuration Update procedure.


Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on EN-DC Configuration Update procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The value range for the Periodicity IE is not consistent between the Tabular and the ASN.1.
There may have incorrect interpretations of the TSC Traffic Characteristics IE when delivering different values for UL and DL.
reasonForChange:
The Periodicity IE included in the TSC Traffic Characteristics IE starts from zero in the Tabular while in the ASN.1 it starts from one. Note that the periodicity starts from zero in other specifications (e.g., NGAP) though value zero does not make much sense.  

In addition, the TSC Traffic Characteristics IE includes the TSC Assistance Information Downlink and TSC Assistance Information Uplink, but in the ASN.1, it includes both in the different order. This may lead to incorrect interpretations when delivering the different values for UL and DL.
summaryOfChange:
Update the periodicity IE starting from zero in the ASN.1.
Switch the TSC Assistance Information Downlink and TSC Assistance Information Uplink in the TSC Traffic Characteristics IE in the Tabular.  

This CR is NBC. 

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it impacts the TSC Traffic Characteristics.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Erroneous specification text for IE descriptions.
reasonForChange:
In accordance with clause 8.15 of the 38.401 specification, for NR MBS broadcast or multicast, during the E1AP bearer context setup process, if the provided shared NG-U transport has been assigned by the 5GC, it is of IP multicast type; if the provided shared NG-U transport has been assigned by the NG-RAN, it is of unicast type. 
This principle is not entirely and correctly reflected in the description of the respective IEs in TS 37.483 and needs to be corrected.
The respective IE descriptions also contain further inconsistencies.
summaryOfChange:
In 9.3.1.117, generalise the specifc term “single NG-U tunnel” to “shared NG-U resource”.
In 9.3.1.116 and 9.3.1.121 remove any reference to a specific shared NG-U resource and remove “also” from the sentence describing location dependent information, as this may be interpreted as if the IE may carry location independent and location dependent informaiton
In 9.3.1.127, remove any reference to a specific shared NG-U resource and correct the text refering to location dependent information, as that IE is able to carry only a single MBS Area Session ID not able to carry any.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Not correct descriptions and handllings of the gNB-CU-UP ID IE in the GNB-CU-UP CONFIGURATION UPDATE message and misalignment between ASN.1 and Tabular.
reasonForChange:
With respect to the gNB-CU-UP ID IE handling in the GNB-CU-UP CONFIGURATION UPDATE message, the following procedure text is specified.  
If the gNB-CU-UP ID IE is included in the GNB-CU-UP CONFIGURATION UPDATE message, the gNB-CU-CP shall associate the TNLA to the E1 interface instance using the gNB-CU-UP ID. 
However, the procedural text is unnecessary as presence of gNB-CU-UP ID IE is mandatory. Further, it is incorrectly described as optional in Tabular. To align with the ASN.1, both the above procedural text “if … included”, and presence in Tabular are not correct. 
There are two alternatives for the procedural text:
Remove the procedural text (since we typically don’t have procedural text for mandatory IEs).
Change the “If xxx is included in the yyy message” to “Upon receiving xxx in the yyy message”.

In this CR, it is proposed to use alternative a) to fix this issue.
summaryOfChange:
Remove the procedure texts regarding handling of gNB-CU-UP ID IE when included in the GNB-CU-UP CONFIGURATION UPDATE message.  
Update the presence of the gNB-CU-UP ID in the Tabular to algin with ASN.1. 

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it impacts the gNB-CU-UP ID IE included in the GNB-CU-UP CONFIGURATION UPDATE message by removing the incorrect procedure texts.

consequencesIfNotApproved: eNB behaviours are missing when the UE radio capability or the UE radio capability ID is not received in the Initial Context Setup Request, UE Radio Capability Match Request and the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION messages.
reasonForChange:
About the UE radio capability, it is specified that the eNB would request the UE radio capability from the UE, under the section 5.11.2 UE Radio Capability Handling in TS 23.401 as follows: 
If the UE is performing an Attach procedure or a Tracking Area Update procedure for the "first TAU following GERAN/UTRAN Attach" or for "UE radio capability update", the MME shall delete (or mark as deleted) any UE Radio Capability information that it has stored, and, if the MME sends an S1 interface INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST or UE RADIO CAPABILITY MATCH REQUEST message during that procedure, the MME shall not send any UE Radio Capability information to the E-UTRAN in that message. This triggers the E-UTRAN to request the UE Radio Capability from the UE and to upload it to the MME in the S1 interface UE CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION message.
For the CIoT EPS Optimisations, during the Attach procedure or the Tracking Area Update procedure e.g. for the "first TAU following GERAN/UTRAN Attach", or mobility between a cell that does not broadcast SystemInformationBlockType31(-NB) and an E-UTRA cell that broadcasts SystemInformationBlockType31(-NB)), if the MME does not send an S1 interface INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST to the E-UTRAN, the MME should obtain the UE Radio Capability information by sending either the DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT message indicating UE Radio Capability request or the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message without UE Radio Capability information included to the E-UTRAN. This triggers the E-UTRAN to request the UE Radio Capability from the UE and upload it to the MME in the S1 interface UE CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION message, as specified in TS 36.300 [5].
However, in the above three S1AP messages mentioned above (Initial Context Setup Request, UE Radio Capability Match Request and Connection Establishment Indication), the descriptions when the eNB does not receive any UE Radio Capability are missing.
summaryOfChange: Add descriptions related to the UE Capability Info Indication procedure for the S1AP messages (Initial Context Setup Request, UE Radio Capability Match Request and Connection Establishment Indication) when neither the UE Radio Capability nor the UE radio capability ID is indicated from the MME to the eNB.
title: Correction on UE Radio Capability Retrieval

consequencesIfNotApproved: The new vendor specific Trace Depth introduced by SA5 will not be supported in NG-RAN.
reasonForChange:
In S5-250077, SA5 agreed to add 3 new codepoints for the Trace Depth parameter for Trace Session level, better support vendor-defined content in a consistent manner. In XnAP, the existing Trace Depth IE contained in the Trace Activation IE needs to be updated  to introduce these new codepoints, namely:
MinimumOnlyVendorSpecificTraceRecord
MediumOnlyVendorSpecificTraceRecord
MaximumOnlyVendorSpecificTraceRecord
summaryOfChange:
Add 3 new codepoints to the Trace Depth IE:
MinimumOnlyVendorSpecificTraceRecord
MediumOnlyVendorSpecificTraceRecord
MaximumOnlyVendorSpecificTraceRecord
title: Trace Depth for Vendor Specific Trace Record

consequencesIfNotApproved: If not approved, retrieving the TNL address of the candidate eNB (using Multi-Operator Core Network (MOCN) might result in the inability to setup a signalling TNL connection between the (source) eNB and the candidate eNB
reasonForChange: There is a possibility that retrieving the X2 TNL address of the candidate eNB (e.g., if the candidate eNB uses a Multi-Operator Core Network (MOCN) may fail in certain deployment scenarios. There is currently no explicit requirement relative to which X2 TNL address the candidate eNB shall provide in the MOCN scenario.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce a new Requested TNL Information IE within SON Configuration Transfer indicating the PLMN ID which has to be taken into account by the candidate eNB when providing X2 TNL Configuration Info.

reasonForChange:
Some corrections on the UL link configuration are list as below:
1. In the descprition of SgNB modification request acknowledge message, both E-RABs Admitted To Be Added List IE and E-RABs Admitted To Be Modified List IE include UL configuration IE. The former is mandatory (i.e., C-ifMCGandSCGpresent) and the latter is optional. So that the description of UL configuration IE is not needed for E-RABs Admitted To Be Added List IE, but it is needed for E-RABs Admitted To Be Modified List IE.
2.In the descprition of SgNB modification request message, it shall be indicated that UL configuration IE is used for MN terminated split bearer.
3. In the tabular of SgNB modification request acknowledge message, SgNB uses UL configuration to MeNB for SN terminated bearer.
summaryOfChange:
1. Remove the description of UL configuration IE in E-RABs Admitted To Be Added List IE 
2. Add the description of UL configuration IE in E-RABs Admitted To Be Modified List IE
  3. It shall be clarified that UL configuration IE is used for MN terminated split bearer in case that MN is hosting node.
  4. In case that SN is hosting node (i.e. PDCP present in SN), SgNB uses UL configuration to MeNB.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The situation when multiple UE contexts have to be released must be handled with many separate Release procedures.

Rev.4: Partial Reset will not be possible to be initiated whenever necessary.
reasonForChange:
Coexistence of multiple UE contexts over longer period of time over X2 may lead to situations when some of them must be released. The situation is similar to S1AP and therefore a single message to release multiple UE contexts is needed.

Rev.4: The solution agreed for the X2 Partial Reset assumes that the Ue is identified by the two IDs, MN’s X2 UE Id and the SN’s X2 Ue ID. However, Partial Reset may be issued any time, also when addition for a given UE is still in progress. In that case, the ID may not be allocated yet. Currently, the MN must wait until all the additions of affected UEs is completed just to obtain the SN’s ID (or, it is necessary for the SN to allocate the ID just to start the Reset).
summaryOfChange:
A new procedure is defined, which enables releasing multiple UE contexts.

Rev.4: The SN’s X2 UE ID is made optional and it usage is defined.

consequencesIfNotApproved: PDCP Duplication with CA would not supported for EN-DC in Rel-15.
reasonForChange:
While activation and deactivation of PDCP duplication with CA is done with inband signalling, the setup of duplicated X2-U bearers is not yet part of the current X2AP although it should be.
The following scenarios have to be looked at and need to be supported:
1.	PDCP Duplication is only supported for NR access. Visibility for PDCP Duplication is therefore given on X2 for EN-DC for NR SCG bearers
2.	PDCP Duplication with CA is based on decisions in the en-gNB. But we can consider scenarios where the MeNB node has certain information about CA possibilities in the en-gNB and already allocates a second Xn-U bearer at resources set/modification, otherwise, setup of the second Xn-U bearer would require a second step for setting up the second Xn-U bearer by means of SGNB Modification.

Section 5.2.3.1.1 in TS38.322v15.2.0 
“When receiving a positive acknowledgement for an RLC SDU with SN = x, the transmitting side of an AM RLC entity shall:
-	send an indication to the upper layers of successful delivery of the RLC SDU;”
Section 5.1.3.1.1 in TS36.322v15.1.0 
“
-	if positive acknowledgements have been received for all AMD PDUs associated with a transmitted RLC SDU:
-	send an indication to the upper layers of successful delivery of the RLC SDU.
”

reasonForChange:
For NG-EN-DC, the RRC Container IE in the 38.423 RRC TRANSFER in message, its semantic description is currently referring to the NR UE Measurement report of TS38.331. This will require M-NG-RAN node (M-ng-eNB) to dig into the 38.331 ASN.1 structure detail in order to extract the NR measurementReport message.

Similarly, for NE-DC case, the RRC Container IE is referring to the LTE UE measurement report of TS36.331.
This will require the M-NG-RAN node (MgNB)  to dig into the the 36.331 ASN.1 structure detain in order to extra the LTE measurentReport message.
summaryOfChange:
Change the wording in the semantic description in the RRC Container IE so that for NGEN-DC and NE-DC case, the eNB/gNB do not need to dig into the detail of NR messages / LTE messages respectively.

In order to ease implementation also in MgNB for NR-DC case, similar handling is applied, i.e. the M-NG-RAN node only transparently transfers to the S-NG-RAN node without digging into the detail.

-	and while the MeNB issues the E-RAB Modification Indication procedure
-	the MME starts e.g.  E-RAB Setup (for a Voice Call) or Modification procedure (UE AMBR value change).

consequencesIfNotApproved: IPSec tunnel cannot be set up beforehand, which incurs additional end user delays.
reasonForChange: Current specification does not support an explicit mechanism to exchange IPSec addresses for U-Plane during setup and configuration update procedures. However, for IPsec, given that both gNB-CU-CP and gNB-CU-UP may be virtualized, IPsec addresses terminated directly at the node (e.g., when SEG is not used) may need to be updated as they may change over time due to up/down-scaling of resources. Further, for U-Plane case, exchanging IPsec addresses at interface setup and configuration update procedures allows “apriori” IPsec tunnel establishment. This is useful in order to avoid the incurred delayed when establishing the IPsec tunnel.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce means to convey IPsec addresses during interface setup and configuration update procedures.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Wasteful signaling due to unecessary restriction on usage of RRC Container. Further, it can incur IOT issues in multi-vendor operation due to differences in implementation.
reasonForChange:
Semantics in the UE Context Modification Request and the UE Context Modification Confirm messages both restrict the RRC Container to only be applicable to the “RRCConnectionReconfiguration” message. Such message is not defined in RRC specifications, hence we aassume it actually refers to “RRCReconfiguration” message. Nevertheless, applying such restriction incurs unecessary signaling in multiple scenarios if the gNB-CU must send the RRC Container in separate DL RRC Message Transfer instead, despite being able to carry it as part of the UE Context Modification procedure. Further, it can incur IOT issues in multi-vendor operation due to differences in implementation and understanding of the specification.
To avoid this issue, the semantics rather than referring to an individual RRC message, they should be generalized to indicate to which logical channel RRC IEs the container is applicable.
summaryOfChange:
Update in semantics of RRC Container in UE Context Modification Request, and UE Context Modification Confirm messages.

The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affect the UE Context Modification procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The PDCP version change, PDCP SN length change, RLC mode change, and full configuration cases are not specified for EN-DC, and the UE and receiving node of SN Status Transfer may expect different SN for the upcoming packets.

To prevent the UE and the receiving node from expecting different sequence number for the upcoming packets, the receiving node of SN Status Transfer message shall ignore the information received in this message.
The 8.2.2.1 General Section specifies how for EN-DC section 8.2.2.2, which is written mainly from an HO point of view should “translate” the terms “source eNB” and “target eNB” for EN-DC purposes into “MeNB” and “en-gNB”, however, the sentences are not entirely correct, as the case where SN STATUS TRANSFER is received by the MeNB is missing..
summaryOfChange:
Section 8.2.2.1 was corrected to also cover the case where the MeNB receives the SN STATUS TRANSFER
Specification text is added in Section 8.2.2.2 to require the “target eNB” (which is either the MeNB or the en-gNB in case of EN-DC) to ignore the information received for the E-RAB in the SN STATUS TRANSFER message.

consequencesIfNotApproved: There are ambiguities on how to interpret the SCell To Be Setup List IE and the SCell Failed To Setup List IE
reasonForChange:
The specification states that “If the SCell To Be Setup List IE is included in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message, the gNB-DU shall act as specified in TS 38.401 [4].”, where [4] refers to TS 38.401. However, TS 38.401 does not include any description of how the SCell To Be Setup List should be handled by the gNB-DU. 
Likewise, the description of node behaviour at reception of the SCell Failed To Setup List IE seems unclear as it says: “If the SCell Failed To Setup List IE is contained in the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message, the gNB-CU shall regard the corresponding SCell(s) failed to be established with an appropriate cause value”. The latter seems to indicate that the gNB-DU attempted to establish the SCell for UE usage but this procedure failed, while the UE configuration at the time of issuing the SCell Failed To Setup List IE has not yet been generated and signalled to the UE. 

Impact Analysis: This CR has no impact
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that the SCell To Be Setup List IE shall be interpreted by gNB-DU as a list of candidates SCells to be set up.
Clarify that the SCell Failed To Setup List IE indicates that the cells could not be configured for usage by gNB-DU.

consequencesIfNotApproved: X2 setup will fail if the receiving node is an eNB with X2 message size capability limitation.
reasonForChange:
In an X2 Setup procedure an en-gNB may signal up to 16384 served NR cells and for each of such served cell may signal up to 1024 neighbour cells information. This leads to very large X2 messages that may not be decodable due to ASN.1 decoding capability issues.
It is therefore necessary to allow for reduced size messages and for failure notifications pointing at excessive message size as the main root of failure.

consequencesIfNotApproved: SgNB addition may be triggered for UE without 5G NR subscription.
reasonForChange: In case of X2 handover from a Rel-14 eNB to a Rel-15 eNB, the target eNB might initiate SgNB addition for an EN-DC capable UE even if the UE does not have a 5G NR subscription. This is because the Handover Restriction List transferred from source eNB to target eNB via X2 in the HANDOVER REQUEST message is the Rel-14 version which does not contain NR restrictions.
summaryOfChange:
The Handover Restriction List IE is added to the PATH SWITCH REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message, which enables the target eNB to receive the NR restrictions at completion of the handover.

It is up to the MME to decide when to include the Handover Restriction List IE, e.g. to certain target eNBs based on configuration, or whenever NR restrictions are present in the HRL, or all the time, etc.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The RF parameters in NR cell information IEs remain inaccurate.
reasonForChange:
For E-UTRA Cells, we include one “EARFCN” (indicating the central frequency of the transmission band) and one “transmission bandwidth” per UL/DL/TDD within the “Cell Information” IEs. These two IEs are enough to deduce the exact location of the entire transmission band, i.e. the frequency of the lowest carrier and the highest carrier.
For NR Cells we include one “NR ARFCN” (indicating the “Point A” rather than the central frequency), one SCS and one “transmission bandwidth” per UL/DL/TDD within the “Cell Information” IEs.
However, the mechanism to determine the frequency raster has changed a lot for NR cells compared with E-UTRA ones, making these parameters far not enough to deduce the location of the entire transmission band, e.g. lack of the “offset to carrier” to indicate the frequency of the lowest carrier.
For the UL,it has been corrected in Rel-16 SON/MDT WI.However,for DL,it is suggested to correct via a separate CR.
summaryOfChange:
Adding one optional DL Carrier List for each DL, which further contains one NR SCS, one Offset to Carrier and one Carrier Bandwidth, and clafitying that if this IE is present the original “transmission bandwidth” IE should be ignored.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR is a clarification and has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the Cell information.
This CR is backward compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: An NG-RAN node would not know that a cell served by its peer NG-RAN node is configured to operate as PSCell/Scell only.
reasonForChange:
NR cells connected to 5GC do not broadcast the TrackingAreaCode if the NR cell only supports PSCell/SCell functionality. Nevertheless, such a cell is configured with a TAC in order to apply roaming and access restrictions also to PSCell/SCells.
If a gNB serves an NR cell as PSCell/SCell, the peer NG-RAN node would not know which Xn function may be applied to such cell. 
Signalling means are necessary to indicate this to the peer NG-RAN node.
summaryOfChange:
The Served Cell Information NR IE is updated to include an indication whether the TAC is broadcast.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it corrects the XnAP to support NR cells not broadcasting a TAC.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the Xn interface management functions.

consequencesIfNotApproved: CA-based PDCP duplication for Industrial IoT may not work properly.
reasonForChange:
(1) During the MN-initiated SN modification procedure, currently SN is not able to configure/de-configure CA-based PDCP duplication for an already established SN terminated MCG bearer, due to missing PDCP Duplication Configuration IE, Duplication Activation IE, and secondary SN UL PDCP UP TNL Information IE in the DRBs To Be Modified List of 9.2.1.10 PDU Session Resource Modification Response Info – SN terminated. (Note that the counterpart from MN is possible via DRBs To Be Modified List of 9.2.1.11 PDU Session Resource Modification Info – MN terminated). 

(2) If SN triggers CA-based duplication in MN side for a SN terminated bearer via SN MOD REQD, the MN needs to provide the primary LCID to the SN via the nested MN-initiated SN modification procedure, so that the SN can configure the primary LCID to the UE accordingly. However, providing LCID from MN was wrongly implemented onto DRBs Admitted to be Setup or Modified List of  9.2.1.21 PDU Session Resource Modification Confirm Info – SN terminated, which happens after reconfiguration to the UE was completed.
summaryOfChange:
(1) PDCP Duplication Configuration IE, Duplication Activation IE, and secondary SN UL PDCP UP TNL Information IE are added into DRBs To Be Modified List of 9.2.1.10 PDU Session Resource Modification Response Info – SN terminated + corresponding ASN.1.

(2) The semantic of the LCID IE under DRBs Admitted to be Setup or Modified List of 9.2.1.21 PDU Session Resource Modification Confirm Info – SN terminated is changed to “Shall be ignored by the S-NG-RAN node if received”. Moreover, for 8.3.4 SN-intiated SN modification procedure, the interaction with the MN-initiated SN modification procedure is updated not to fall onto abnormal condition for LCID provided from the MN for CA-based PDCP duplication.
title: Correction for Industrial IoT PDCP duplication for Carrier Aggregation

consequencesIfNotApproved:
It is ambiguous about the NG-RAN user location reporting operation. 
IOT issue between the NG-RAN and AMF.
reasonForChange:
Currently the Location Reporting Request Type IE can be signalled in multiple NGAP messages, e.g. LOCATION REPORTING CONTROL, INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST and HANDOVER REQUEST. 
Even, the current specification allows the AMF to send multiple LOCATION REPORTING CONTROL messages including different Location Reporting Request Type contents. 

But it is not clear whether the “change of serving cell” event and “UE presence in the area of interest” event can be supported simultaneously by the NG-RAN node, i.e. whether the NG-RAN performs the replace operation or the addition operation? 

Also it is not clear about the interpretation of the location Reporting Reference IDs in multiple Location Reporting Request Types.

And the NG-RAN report the UE presence for Area of Interest for inter-NG-RAN handover and intra-NG-RAN handover should be clearer.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that For inter-NG-RAN handover, the NG-RAN reports the full set of UE presence per Location Reporting Reference ID.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it clarifies the NG-RAN behaviour regarding the location report.
The impact can be considered isolated.

Currently only a single event type is included in the Location Reporting Information IE in the HANDOVER REQUEST and RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT RESPONSE message. If the source NG-RAN or the old serving NG-RAN node keep these two events and perform location report correspondingly, it can not send these two event types to the target NG-RAN node or the new NG-RAN node. 
Also this may result at that the AMF and NG-RAN are not aligned in terms of the location report event type
summaryOfChange:
Introduce a new codepoint “change of serving cell and UE presence in the area of interest” in the event type.

CR0360 aimed at enabling an NG-RAN node to include Cell Assistance Information E-UTRA IE in the NG-RAN NODE CONFIGURATION UPDATE message, as was already possible within the XN SETUP REQUEST message.
However, an ng-eNB is not able to respond to that request, as the NG-RAN NODE CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE message does not contain any Served E-UTRA Cell IE, as specified in the procedural text.
Further, E-UTRA Cell related IE names within the existing procedure text for the NG-RAN node Configuration Update procedure are incorrectly referenced.
summaryOfChange:
Correct the NG-RAN node Configuration Update procedure procedural description and add Served E-UTRA Cell IE in the NG-RAN NODE CONFIGUATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE message.
Further, semantics of the Served E-UTRA/NR cells IEs have been updated to make clear, that this IE is provide in response to NG-RAN node1.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it introduces corrects the NG-RAN node Configuration Update function for exchange of E-UTRA cell information upon request from the initiating NG-RAN node.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the NG-RAN node Configuration Update function for E-UTRA cells.

The CR as ASN.1 impact and is realised in a backwards compatible way.
title: Correction of CR0360 – Enabling an ng-eNB to reply to Cell Assistance Information E-UTRA.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The IAB functionality does not work well. e.g :
The IE used for IAB specific RACH configure invoked in F1AP specification misalign with the real IE defined in TS38.331.
May cause some logical error for the receiving node that some IEs are included in the message but the actual content is absent.
The FDD cell related resource configuration is not supported.
The ASN.1 part not align with the tabular, e.g. the Child-Node Cells List in tabular of clause 9.2.9.3 is optional while the child-Node-Cells-List IE in ASN.1 is mandatory.
reasonForChange:
The RACH Config Common IAB IE contained in the GNB-DU RESOURCE CONFIGURATION message, refers to the IAB specific RACH configuration, which should correspond to the rach-ConfigCommonIAB-r16 IE as defined in TS38.331. In current specification, the rach-ConfigCommon IE in the tabular shown in clause 9.2.9.3 is wrongly used as the corresponding IE.
The Uplink Non-UP Traffic Mapping List IE is the only content for its parant IE, i.e. Uplink BH Non-UP Traffic Mapping IE as defined in clause 9.3.1.103, it is impossible that the Uplink BH Non-UP Traffic Mapping IE is carried in a message but the real content is blank, thus the presence of Uplink Non-UP Traffic Mapping List IE in clause 9.3.1.103 should be set as mandatory. 
The IAB-MT Cell List IE is the only content for its parant IE, i.e. the Multiplexing Info IE as defined in clause 9.3.1.108, it is impossible that the Multiplexing Info IE present in a message but its content is blank, then the presence of IAB-MT Cell List IE in clause 9.3.1.108 should be set as mandatory.
The IAB STC-Info List IE is the only content for for its parant IE, i.e. the IAB STC Info IE as defined in clause 9.3.1.109, it is impossible that the IAB STC Info IE present in a message but its real content is blank, then the presence of IAB STC-Info List IE in clause 9.3.1.109 should be set as mandatory.
The DUF Slot Configuration IE in clause 9.3.1.107 uses CHOICE format, the presence of the two sub-IEs, i.e. Explicit Format IE, and Implicit Format IE are not necessary, can keep void. Currently, the presence of the two sub-IEs are set as mandatory.
The SSB Transmission Bitmap IE in clause 9.3.1.109 uses CHOICE format, the presence of the three sub-IEs, i.e. Short Bitmap IE, Medium Bitmap IE and Long Bitmap IE are set as optional in current specification, they should be set as mandatory to avoid a void Choice IE.
The gNB-DU Cell Resource Configuration IE defined in clause 9.3.1.107 can be used to configure the resource parameters for either TDD cell or FDD cell, as invoked by the TDD Info IE and FDD info IE in clause 9.2.9.3. The description about the gNB-DU Cell Resource Configuration IE 9.3.1.107 only mentions TDD, the FDD is still missing. 
The DUF Transmission Periodicity IE contained in the gNB-DU Cell Resource Configuration IE is used to configure the period of slot format (DUF pattern), apparently this DUF configuration is not need for FDD cell resource configuration, since the FDD cell configuration for UL and DL using separate IEs. But the gNB-DU Cell Resource Configuration IE will be used by both the FDD info IE and the TDD Info IE, so the presence of DUF Transmission Periodicity IE should be set as optional.
For ASN.1 part, the presence of several IEs are inconsistent with the tabular in 9.2 and 9.3, which are listed as following: 
For the configuration in the Child-Node-Cells-List-Item, e.g. cSI-RS-Configuration and sR-Configuration etc., they are not aligned with tabular, and according to the agreement from last meeting, they shall be set to optional while it is current mandatory in ASN.1.
For dUFTransmissionPeriodicity and dUF-Slot-Config-List, since the DUF configuration is not need for FDD cell resource configuration, it shall not be set to mandatory.
For child-Node-Cells-List, multiplexingInfo and iAB-STC-Info in IAB-Info-IAB-DU, noofDownlinkSymbols and noofUplinkSymbols in DUF Slot Configuration Item, and dsInformationList, they are not aligned with tabular in ASN.1 part.
In clause 9.3.1.107, the HSNA Slot Configuration List IE is set as optional in the tabular, the ASN.1 part is not align with the tabular.
summaryOfChange:
For the RACH Config Common IAB IE in clause 9.2.9.3, change the rach-ConfigCommon IE in the tabular to the rach-ConfigCommonIAB-r16 IE as defined in TS38.331.
Change the Uplink Non-UP Traffic Mapping List IE in clause 9.3.1.103 to mandatory.

Change the IAB-MT Cell List IE in clause 9.3.1.108 to mandatory.
Change the IAB STC-Info List IE in clause 9.3.1.109 to mandatory.
Delete the presense field of Explicit Format IE, and Implicit Format IE in clause 9.3.1.107.
Change the presense field of Short Bitmap IE, Medium Bitmap IE and Long Bitmap IE from optional to mandatory in clause 9.3.1.109.
Add the description for FDD cell resource configuration in clause 9.3.1.107.
Change the DUF Transmission Periodicity IE in clause 9.3.1.107 to be optioanl.
Add OPTIONAL in the ASN.1 part for the IE listed in the 9 of the Reason for change section.

Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because the changes only impact the IAB functionality .
This CR has an impact under protocol point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects the IAB specific gNB-DU resource configuration and BAP mapping configuration function.
This CR is non backward compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The AMF would unnecessarily send PAGING messages to gNBs.
reasonForChange:
NR cells connected to 5GC do not broadcast the TrackingAreaCode if the NR cell only supports PSCell/SCell functionality. Nevertheless, such a cell is configured with a TAC in order to apply roaming and access restrictions also to PSCell/SCells.
If a gNB serves, for a given Tracking Area, only cells as PSCell/SCells, the 5GC may optimise NG-C signalling towards that gNB, e.g. not page a UE in those cells, if the configured Tracking Area is part of the UE’s registration area.
Signalling means are necessary to indicate this to the 5GC.
summaryOfChange:
The NG SETUP REQUEST and the RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE message are updated to include a per Tracking Area indication whether the TAC is not broadcast. The behaviour of the AMF is not mandated.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it corrects the NGAP to support gNBs serving NR cells for a given Tracking Area in PSCell/SCell mode only.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the NG interface management functions.
title: Support of PSCell/SCell-only operation mode

consequencesIfNotApproved: Storing at the gNB-DU of information concerning the Measurement Configuratino that are not need to be kept at the gNB-DU. Possible issues of interoperability between gNB-CU and gNB-DU
reasonForChange: In the case that the the gNB-DU has some specific measurement gaps configured and at some point the gNB-CU realizes that some of those measurement gaps are no longer needed and wants them to be deactivated, TS 38.473 is not providing clear guidelines on the way that gNB-CU informs the gNB-DU about its decision.
summaryOfChange:
We provide an explanation that the gNB-CU via measObjectToAddModList IE informs the gNB-DU about all the measurement gaps that need to be configured, while at the same time measurement gaps previously configured may be removed by means of the measObjectToRemoveList IE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the network is not implemented according to the CR; the UE does not receive user plane traffic prioritized per priority services (e.g. MPS) requirements.
reasonForChange:
In all cases except when a gNB operates as in IAB-donor, the DSCP marking of downlink user plane packets over the F1-U interface is conducted at the gNB-CU-UP per TS 38.474 (Rel-16). However, in support of IAB at the IAB-donor gNB, the DSCP marking responsibility is transferred to the gNB-CU-CP and the DSCP marking is signalled over the E1 interface to the gNB-CU-UP per TS 38.463 (Rel-16). 
In order to support priority services (e.g. MPS), DSCP marking at the gNB-CU-CP should be based on 5G QoS Identifier (5QI) , the Priority Level (if explicitly signalled), and other NG-RAN traffic parameters (e.g. ARP). The CR adds the necessary statements to be used for the DSCP derivation at the gNB-CU-CP.
summaryOfChange:
Specify that the DSCP derivation at the gNB-CU-CP based on 5G QoS Identifier (5QI) , the Priority Level (if explicitly signalled), and other NG-RAN traffic parameters (e.g. ARP) for priority services (e.g. MPS) user plane traffic, when the gNB supports IAB and operates as an IAB-donor, as specified in TS 38.474.  
Impact Analysis:

NR-SA
Impacted functionality:
IAB operation at the IAB-donor node.
Inter-operability:
No impact to the UE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: It would remain unclear whether the NRPPa “Reporting of General Error Situations” function uses UE-associated or non-UE associated signaling over NGAP. Also, it would remain unclear whether the NRPPa Transport procedures use UE-associated or non-UE associated signaling.
reasonForChange:
Clause 8.10.1 describes how each NRPPa function maps to an NRPPa Transport procedure over NGAP. However, one NRPPa function is missing from the description (Reporting of General Error Situations).

Also, the text in clause 8.10.1 is written as if “NRPPa Transport Procedure” is itself a single NGAP procedure that can use both UE-associated and non-UE associated signalling. However, it is actually a set of four different NGAP procedures, each using either UE-associated or non-UE associated signalling (but not both).
summaryOfChange:
The NRPPa “Reporting of General Error Situations” function is added, and maps to either UE-associated or non-UE associated signaling depending on the NRPPa message that triggers the error.
The Downlink UE Associated NRPPa Transport procedure and the Uplink UE Associated NRPPa Transport procedure use UE associated signaling.
The Downlink Non UE Associated NRPPa Transport procedure and the Uplink Non UE Associated NRPPa Transport procedure use non-UE associated signaling.

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an impact under protocol point of view. The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the NRPPa Transport Procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the MN does not inform the SN of its SL resource configuration, resource collision can happen for the SN’s Uu UEs through SRB3
reasonForChange:
In MR-DC, resources being interfered by other concurrent transmission in neighboring cells is a general issue that is addressed today by the means of the MeNB Resource Coordination Information IE present in Dual Connectivity procedures. 

When V2X comes into scope, the sidelink (SL) transmission is controlled at the MeNB which is in charge of scheduling, but the SN on the other hand cannot know what are the resources configured by the MN for SL transmission. This may cause resource collision at the SN for its allocated Uu UEs through SRB3 which can be on the same bandwidth as the MN’s SL resources.

In order to address this issue and complement the Rel-15 MR-DC resource coordination for Uu, MN must communicate to the SN its SL resource configuration, so that MR-DC communication will not be impacted during SL transmission.
summaryOfChange:
This CR proposes to allow the existing IE MeNB Resource Coordination Information IE to be used for the purpose of sidelink resource coordination form the MN to the SN.  


Impact analysis: 
This CR has isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release) because it is addition of new IEs.
The impact can be considered isolated because it does not put any new requirements on the network or the UE.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Cannot support en-gNB initiated EN-DC Resource Status Reporting Initiation.
Cannot inform MeNB about the action failed because E-UTRAN node Measurement-ID is unknown.
reasonForChange:
In en-gNB initiated EN-DC Resource Status Reporting Initiation, the en-gNB is not able to provide the eNB measurement ID, and the en-gNB Measurement ID shall always be included instead of C-ifRegistrationRequestStoporAdd.

In order to enable both eNB initiated and en-gNB initiated EN-DC Resource Status Reporting Initiation, it is needed to update the eNB Measurement ID IE and en-gNB Measurement ID IE to E-UTRAN node1 Measurement ID IE and E-UTRAN node2 Measurement ID IE in X2AP: EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS REQUEST, EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS RESPONSE and EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS FAILURE messages.

In order to align the EN-DC Resource Status Reporting Initiation procedure and the EN-DC Resource Status Reporting procedure, it is also needed to do the same change in X2AP: EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS UPDATE message.

Similar to existing cause value “Unknown eNB Measurement ID”, it is also needed to introduce a new cause “Unknown E-UTRAN node Measurement ID” to indicate that the action failed because some E-UTRAN node Measurement-ID is unknown.
summaryOfChange:
Update the eNB Measurement ID IE and en-gNB Measurement ID IE to E-UTRAN node1 Measurement ID IE and E-UTRAN node2 Measurement ID IE in the following X2AP messages:
EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS REQUEST
EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS RESPONSE
EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS FAILURE
EN-DC RESOURCE STATUS UPDATE
Introduce a new cause “Unknown E-UTRAN node Measurement ID” to indicate that the action failed because some E-UTRAN node Measurement-ID is unknown.
Add the definition of E-UTRAN node.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
