consequencesIfNotApproved: The Target NG-RAN Node to Source NG-RAN Node Failure Transparent Container IE cannot be used for other purposes than for providing information of the supported CAGs in the target cell to which HO has failed.
reasonForChange:
Rel-16 introduced the possibility for the target NG-RAN node to notify the source NG-RAN node about the supported CAG IDs for the target cell.
Unfortunately, the respective transparent container includes this information as a mandatory IE in ASN.1, which makes this transparent container not re-usable for other features.
This CR corrects the presence of the IE in ASN.1.
summaryOfChange:
The Cell CAG Information IE in the Target NG-RAN Node to Source NG-RAN Node Failure Transparent Container IE was corrected to be only optionally present in ASN.1

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it introduces corrects the NPN related function for informing the source NG-RAN node about the CAGs supported by the target cell, to which the NG-based handover has failed.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the NPN function in case an NG-based handover to a CAG cell .

This CR introduces a non-backwards compatible change to TS 38.413.

consequencesIfNotApproved: There can be problem in multi-vendor deployments with different AMF implementations, if the limitation of the Routing ID maximum length is not known at RAN level, or supposed to be inferior to what can be used.
reasonForChange:
Contrary to the E-SMLC Routing ID in LTE coded as INTEGER (0..255), the LMF Routing ID in NR has an unspecified octet string. According to TS 23.273 sections 6.11.2:

“The AMF forwards the Network Positioning message to the serving NG-RAN node in an N2 Transport message. The AMF includes a Routing identifier, in the N2 Transport message, identifying the LMF (e.g. a global address of the LMF).”

The general identification of the LMF ID is defined in TS 29.518 as the string NfInstanceId, which is defined in TS 29.571 (UUID, i.e. 16 octets)

TS 29.518:

And then TS 29.571:

Different AMF implementations cannot unfortunately guarantee that the Routing ID is coded in a unique way. A size limitation is required for a safe inter-vendor operable networking. This is important so that RAN can be aware of the maximum Octet String length to compare two Routing IDs when, for e.g., it receives NRPPa messages from different LMFs. It is proposed hence to clarify the octet string maximum size of the LMF Routing ID in NG-AP to be that of the NfInstanceId, set to UUID format, i.e. 16 octets.
summaryOfChange: Clarify the Routing ID IE Type OCTET STRING’s maximum size to be that of the NfInstanceId string per TS 29.571, used to identify the LMF.
title: Clarification on the specified maximum length of the Routing ID Octet String

reasonForChange:
The Positioning Measurement Request message contains the “System Frame Number” IE and “Slot Number” IE. These two IEs have specific meaning of the activation time of SRS transmission. However, the current spec does not have any descriptions regarding these two IEs in Positioning Measurement Request message. The gNB-DUs cannot know how to use this information when receiving these two IEs.

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the Positioning Measurement Request.

consequencesIfNotApproved: NEA1 (second bit according to current asn.1) could be understood as the first bit instead of the second bit leading to critical error.
reasonForChange:
In the Security Capabilities IE, the “semantics” column says that the “first bit” corresponds to NEA1. 
According to X.680 the “first bit” of a bit string called leading bit should have number 0. However, in the IE “Type and Reference” column and in the asn.1 the NEA1 has currently allocated number 1 which corresponds to second bit. 
So there is a conflict between the “semantics” and the asn.1. It is decided to align the semantics with the asn1 to avoid a non-backwards compatible asn.1 CR at this late stage.
summaryOfChange:
The semantic description of the UE Security Capabilities IE is updated to align with the asn.1.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the security function.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Control information regarding location reporting information at change of PSCell would be lost at X2 mobility.
reasonForChange:
Rel-15 has introduced location reporting of PSCell in case of EN-DC. While an eNB can be configured to apply this function for a UE, it is not possible to transfer that information to the target/new eNB in case of X2 mobility.
Note, that stage-2 specification (TS 23.401) assumes transfer of such information via X2.
summaryOfChange:
The an Additional Location Reporting Information is included in the Location Reporting Information to allow transferring respective control information received from the EPC.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it introduces the possibility to transfer control information regarding report of PSCell via X2 within the UE context.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the location reporting function.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Unclear specification on NAS-PDU delivery
reasonForChange:
When NG-RAN node receives a NAS-PDU from AMF,it would just transparently send the NAS-PDU to UE.However,in current specification,there is following description：

“For each PDU session successfully established the NG-RAN node shall pass to the UE the PDU Session NAS-PDU IE, if included, and the value contained in the PDU Session ID IE received for the PDU session.
However, the sending of the PDU Session ID IE to the UE is not directly tied to the sending of the NAS PDU which contains its own PDU Session ID. Usually, NGAP does not describe the sending of information elements over RRC unless transparently relayed such as the NAS PDU.
summaryOfChange:
Remove the second half of the sentence i.e. and the value contained in the PDU Session ID IE received for the PDU session

reasonForChange:
The reply LS from RAN2 in R2-2111492 indicates that it is up to gNB implementation to deliver DL packets to UE via any configured DRB of the PDU session before the new QFI to DRB mapping is configured for the QoS flow. 

However, in case of CU-CP/CU-UP split architecture, the gNB-CU-UP behaviour is unclear as to how the DL QoS flow packets are delivered before the QFI to DRB mapping configuration is provided by the gNB-CU-CP, as discussed at R3-220988.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify whether or how the gNB-CU-UP delivers the DL packet(s) including a QFI value not configured by the gNB-CU-CP.

For direct routing for IAB network in EN-DC, “QoS Mapping Information” IE may be transmitted to MeNB by the SN-initiated modification procedure for the E-RAB configured as MN-terminated SCG/split bearer.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The mandatory inclusion of UL related frequency information may lead to confusion for ENDC SDL cell.
reasonForChange:
Last RAN3#114bis-e meeting agreed the CR R3-221214 on the frequency information for DL only cell over Xn interface, where the semantic description is updated so that for SDL cell, the UL related frequency information is ignored. 

Then for EN-DC over X2 interface, the same logic should be applied for the Served NR Cell Information/ NR Neighbour Information. 

Otherwise, as indicated in section 5 in TS 38.104, the SDL is operating in the DL operating band only. If the cell is SDL cell, the UL FreqInfo/UL transmission bandwidth are indicated as well in the Served NR Cell Information/ NR Neighbour Information IE, which may potentially lead to confusion and errors.  

Note that for LTE UL EARFCN in the Served Cell Information, it is already clearly indicated that:
Corresponds to NUL in TS 36.104 [16] for E-UTRA operating bands for which it is defined; ignored for E-UTRA operating bands for which NUL is not defined.
summaryOfChange:
Update the semantic descriptions for Served NR Cell Information/ NR Neighbour Information that for SDL cell, the UL related frequency information is ignored. 

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the Served NR Cell Information/ NR Neighbour Information.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The above NR MBS related errors remain in E1AP specification.
reasonForChange:
This CR fixed some errors in latest versino of E1AP specifications
The criticality of the gNB-CU-UP MBS E1AP ID IE in BC BEARER CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message should be ignore, since the gNB-CU-UP can ignore this IE if not comprehend.
RAN2 agreed to extend MRB ID space beyond current 32 limit and up to 512, in case there are limited MBS services within a cell or a DU, the same MRB ID can be used for all the UEs for the same MBS service, note that during HO, the UE may need to be re-configured to change the MRB ID used in the new cell.
Thus, the value of MRB ID should be INTEGER (1.. 512, ...) in E1AP  specification.
The MBS NG-U Information at NG-RAN IE is used to provide the shared DL NG-U tunnel information, in which the UP Transport Layer Information is generated by gNB for shared NG-U unicast transport. Thus, the "UL" may be a typo, and the description about shared NG-U multicast unicast transport in BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE should be removed.
In the current version specification, the presence of the BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE and the MC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE are "C-ifunicast", which conditions are expressed as that this IE shall be present if the MBS NG-U Information at NG-RAN IE within the MC/BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE contains unicast TNL information. However, in the MC/BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE, there is no alternative other than unicast TNL information. So, determine the the presence of the MC/BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE denpend on whether including unicast TNL information is unfeasibly. It can be simply changed to optional. In ASN.1 part, the notes should be removed.
summaryOfChange:
Change the criticality of the gNB-CU-UP MBS E1AP ID IE to ignore, in BC BEARER CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message.
Update the value of MRB ID from INTEGER (1.. 32, ...) to INTEGER (1.. 512, ...).
Update "Shared NG-U UL Transport Layer Information" to "Shared NG-U DL Transport Layer Information" in MBS NG-U Information at NG-RAN IE, and remove the description about shared NG-U multicast unicast transport in BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE and MC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE.
Update the presence of the BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE in BC Bearer Context To Setup Response IE and the MC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN IE in MC Bearer Context To Setup Response IE from “C-ifunicast” to “O”, and remove the conditions, explanations and notes in ASN.1 part for “ifunicast”.
title: Correction on NR MBS in E1AP

consequencesIfNotApproved: The eNB cannot know the Masked IMEISV for UEs using CP only CIoT EPS solution
reasonForChange:
The IMEISV value with a mask is used to identify a terminal model without identifying an individual Mobile Equipment. Currently, the eNB can get this information from MME via the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST or HANDOVER REQUEST messages.
However, for UEs using Control Plane CIoT EPS optimisation, the eNB cannot get the “Masked IMEISV” from MME since AS security is not activated.
One possible way to fix this issue is to add the Masked IMEISV IE into the UE INFORMATION TRANSFER, so that eNB can retrieve this IE from MME after msg3.

Additionally, the masked IMEISV IE should also be added in the procedures related to CP CIoT EPS optimisation DL NAS TRANSPORT and the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION messages to cover all signalling aspects.
summaryOfChange:
Addition of the Masked IMEISV IE in the UE INFORMATION TRANSFER,  DL NAS TRANSPORT and the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION messages from MME to eNB. 

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the changes only affect the CP CIoT EPS optimisation procedures.

reasonForChange:
Handling of duplication elimination for MRBs during non-MBS-supporting to MBS-supporting handover requires gNB-CU UP to know the mapping between MBS QoS Flows and associated Unicast QoS Flows.
Note: it is applicable as long as the gNB-CU-UP which delivers the multicast packets supports this feature, including support handling unicast packets. The target gNB-CU-CP may have selected a different gNB-CU-UP during the handover preparation phase, but after the path switch procedure the gNB-CU-CP can perform a conventional gNB-CU-UP change procedure to switch (at least) the associated PDU session toward the gNB-CU-UP which delivers the multicast packets, and then the duplication elimination procedure can be performed as usual.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The E1AP spec is misaligned with RRC spec.
reasonForChange:
In RAN2#119e meeting, there are agreement about PDCP configuration:
multicastHFN-AndRefSN is renamed to initialRX-DELIV and update the corresponding description to ‘Indicates an initial value of RX_DELIV for multicast MRB PDCP window initialization as specified in TS 38.323 [5].
In the current E1AP specification, the CU-UP may indicate the Initial HFN and Reference PDCP SN IE to CU-CP during MC Bearer Context Setup, MC Bearer Context Modification, and MC Bearer Context Modification Required procedures. In which, the Initial HFN and Reference PDCP SN IE is descripted as “Refer to the multicastHFN-AndRefSN IE as specified in the TS 38.331 [10].”
E1AP specification should be updated to align with latest RAN2 agreement. 
In addition, the format of the IE in the E1AP is currently not clarified, e.g., which bits are used to identify the PDCP SN. Therefore, the format needs to be clarified to avoid misunderstanding.
Thus, RAN3 shall rename the “MBS Initial HFN and Reference PDCP SN” IE in E1AP into “MBS PDCP COUNT”, and adjust its description into “Encoded in the same format as the initialRX-DELIV IE and to be taken into account to configure the UE, as specified in the TS 38.331 [10]”
summaryOfChange:
Rename the “MBS Initial HFN and Reference PDCP SN” IE in E1AP into “MBS PDCP COUNT”, and adjust its description into “Encoded in the same format as the initialRX-DELIV IE and to be taken into account to configure the UE, as specified in the TS 38.331 [10]”.

consequencesIfNotApproved: At mobility, the UE Context handling process within gNB-CU-CP would not be able to reference the correct MRB resource at the gNB-CU-UP for retrieving accurate MRB Progress Information.
reasonForChange: F1-U resources for provision of multicast session data is controlled by the gNB-DU. At mobility, if the gNB-CU would like to retrieve progress information, there is currently no MBS Multicast F1-U Context reference available within the UE Context at the gNB-CU, assuming deployments that follow current F1AP protocol structure which allows separation of UE Context and MBS Session Context handling.
summaryOfChange:
The gNB-DU is enabled to provide MBS Multicast F1-U Context  reference information to the gNB-CU at F1AP UE Context Modification (CU and DU triggered) to allow retrieving as accurate MRB Progress Information as possible as follows: 
-	a new Multicast F1-U Context Reference CU IE is introduced in the DISTRIBUTION SETUP RESPONSE and provided from the CU to the DU. This new IE refers to the Multicast F1-U Context ReferenceE1 IE, if E1 is deployed.
-	the new Multicast F1-U Context Reference CU IE is then provided by the DU to UE Context within the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE message and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUIRED message.

Note, that this issue becomes more apparent if considering E1 deployment, however, one can assume distributed implementation also without explicit E1 support and 5G specifications should support such deployments even without explicit E1 support. The CR aims at general protocol definition without necessarily assuming E1 deployment.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it introduces corrects the MRB Progress information function for multicast MBS sessions.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the MRB Progress information function for multicast MRB sessions.
title: Provision of MBS Multicast F1-U references to UE Context in gNB-CU enabling retrieval of data forwarding progress information

This will cause the parent optional IE is included in a message but the content of the parent IE is totally blank.
reasonForChange:
In section 9.2.9.7, the “UL UP TNL Information to Update List Item IEs” IE is mandatory, but in ASN.1 part, the corresponding IE “id-UL-UP-TNL-Information-to-Update-List-Item” is optional. Considering that the “UL UP TNL Information to Update List Item IEs” IE is the only sub-IE contained in the optional IE “UL UP TNL Information to Update List”, it is reasonable to set the presence of “UL UP TNL Information to Update List Item IEs” to be mandatory in ASN.1 part. Otherwise, it is possible that the parent IE “UL UP TNL Information to Update List” is included in a message but the content of this parent IE is blank. 
Same issue for the “UL UP TNL Address to Update List Item IEs” in 9.2.9.7, the corresponding IE in ASN.1 is “id-UL-UP-TNL-Address-to-Update-List-Item”.
Same issue for the “DL UP TNL Address to Update List Item IEs” in 9.2.9.8, the corresponding IE in ASN.1 is “id-DL-UP-TNL-Address-to-Update-List-Item”.
summaryOfChange:
In  section 9.4.4, change the presence of the following IEs to be mandatory:  id-UL-UP-TNL-Information-to-Update-List-Item, id-UL-UP-TNL-Address-to-Update-List-Item, id-DL-UP-TNL-Address-to-Update-List-Item.


Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).

consequencesIfNotApproved: The ASN.1 and the tabular definitions of the S-NODE RELEASE REQUEST message remain different.
reasonForChange:
The tabular and ASN.1 definitions of the S-NODE RELEASE REQUEST message are different: the list of PDU Sessions in the request is optional in the tabular definition, while mandatory in the ASN.1 definition. 
The list of PDU sessions concern sessions that are hosted in the S-Node (so that the data can be forwared to the MN and the PDCP transferred). Therefore, in case when there is no PDU Session hosted in the S-Node, the MN shall not provide any reference. The list of PDU session used there is defined so, it is not allowed to have an empty list – thus, the optional presence of the list in the message is correct.
summaryOfChange:
The correction can be made either by making the IE mandatory in the tabular definition, or by correcting the ASN.1 definition. Since in some scenarios there is no use for the list, making it mandatory requires also adding textual description which explains when the list is actually valid and when it should be ignored. This, though backward-compatible, is easily confusing method.
Therefore, it is proposed to correct the ASN.1 definition by making the relevant IE optional there.
The correction starts from Rel-17 onwards although such inconsistency between tabular and ASN.1 has existed from Rel-15, considering there is no functional issue by applying the change.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
The change is a non-backward compatible correction of the ASN.1 code.

consequencesIfNotApproved: When the IAB authorized information is changed to “not authorized”, the IAB incorrectly continue its operation.
reasonForChange:
IAB’s authorization can be changed to “not authorized” during its normal operation. MME may choose to detach the IAB-MT (including MME initiate the UE Context Release procedure to MeNB), or MME may keep the IAB-MT attached as a normal UE (e.g. has an optional PDN connection for OAM). In the later case, MME initiates the UE Context Modification procedure to inform the MeNB that the IAB authorized is changed to “not authorized”. MeNB need to ensure the IAB’s operation is stopped, e.g. initiate Secondary Node Release procedure, etc. 

However, current specification only defines “the eNB shall store the received IAB Authorized IE, if supported, in the UE context”, but does not define the MeNB to take actions to stop the IAB operation.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify the eNB need to take actions to ensure the IAB node will not serve the UE(s).

consequencesIfNotApproved: When the IAB authorized information is changed to “not authorized”, the IAB incorrectly continue its operation.
reasonForChange:
IAB’s authorization can be changed to “not authorized” during its normal operation. MME may choose to detach the IAB-MT (including MME initiate the UE Context Release procedure to MeNB), or MME may keep the IAB-MT attached as a normal UE (e.g. has an optional PDN connection for OAM). In the later case, MME initiates the UE Context Modification procedure to inform the MeNB that the IAB authorized is changed to “not authorized”. MeNB need to ensure the IAB’s operation is stopped, e.g. initiate Secondary Node Release procedure, etc. 

However, current specification only defines “the eNB shall store the received IAB Authorized IE, if supported, in the UE context”, but does not define the MeNB to take actions to stop the IAB operation.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify the eNB need to take actions to ensure the IAB node will not serve the UE(s).

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Misinterpretion of the procedure texts applicable for the NR access. 
Misalignment between the RAN3 and SA2 specifications.
reasonForChange:
In order to support User Plane CIoT 5GS optimization, it is specified as follows that the resume cause is sent in the Path Switch Request message when received over the radio interface. Then the AMF can inform the SMF of the UE’s use of MO Exception Data accordingly (see the agreed R3-203267, and see the section 4.8.2.3 in TS 23.502). 
When the NG-RAN node has received from the radio interface the RRC Resume Cause IE, it shall include it in the PATH SWITCH REQUEST message.

But according to the current procedure text, in case of NR access, e.g, in case when inactive UE moves to a different cell from its anchor cell, the gNB should send the resume cause as well. 
First this is not specified in SA2 specifications to deliver the resume cause during the RRC inactive context relocation. Also, there is no need for the AMF to be aware of the resume cause for RRC-inactive state since the CN considers the UE at CM-connected state.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The RAT type - E-UTRA may be erroneously used for the EN-DC data usage report in this version of the specification. 
Misalignment between the ASN.1 and the Tabular for the RAT Type IE.
reasonForChange:
In the 9.3.1.44 Data Usage Report List IE used to report the secondary RAT data usage for EN-DC, the RAT Type IE is used to indicate the RAT type, with the IE type as ENUMERATED (NR, …). This IE is used when the en-gNB is CP/UP split, the gNB-CU-UP will include the NR codepoint to the gNB-CU-CP to report the data usage for the UE. 

However, in ASN.1, it is erroneously referring to the RAT-Type as follows. 
RAT-Type	::=	ENUMERATED	{
	e-UTRA,
	nR,
	...
}
This IE was initially intended to be used also for NE-DC, but eventually another message (MR-DC DATA USAGE REPORT) was defined for that deployment. Therefore, the IE must always be set to ‘NR’. 
This e-UTRA codepoint in the ASN.1 not only leads to the mis-alignment between the tabular and the ASN.1, but also leads to the mis-implementation that the e-UTRA RAT type can be used for EN-DC data usage report in this release.
secretaryRemarks:
Endorsed CRs from RAN3#119bis-e

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the secondary RAT data usage report for EN-DC.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The meaning of “the lowest index of RB of the IAB-DU cell” in Number of RB Sets IE is not clear and would lead to misunderstanding.
reasonForChange:
In current specification, the description of the start RB index of the first RB set in RB Set Configuration is “The start RB index of the first RB set is the lowest index of RB of the IAB-DU cell.”. However, the meaning of “the lowest index of RB of the IAB-DU cell” is not clear and would lead to misunderstanding. In RAN3#119bis-e meeting, the reply LS from RAN1 was received in R3-231105 with the following answer:  
Based on the reply LS from RAN1, the description for the start RB index of the first RB set in the RB Set Configuration IE needs to be corrected to reflect the latest RAN1 agreement.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Burst Arrival Time remains unclear.
reasonForChange:
The Burst Arrival Time IE reuses the same encoding as the RRC ReferenceTime IE, which is a sequence of four INTEGER values having decreasing time granularity as shown below:
ReferenceTime-r16 ::=           SEQUENCE {
    refDays-r16                         INTEGER (0..72999),
    refSeconds-r16                      INTEGER (0..86399),
    refMilliSeconds-r16                 INTEGER (0..999),
    refTenNanoSeconds-r16               INTEGER (0..99999)
}

It is unclear what “truncated to 1 us granularity” means in the context of the above encoding structure (since e.g. the value of the IE cannot be shortened, nor can the 10ns granularity of the IE be changed).

consequencesIfNotApproved: Inconsistency between the call flow of MBS multicast context establiment and the NGAP specification.
reasonForChange:
In the RAN3#119 meeting, the GTP-UL TEID info in the broadcast session establishment procedure had been deleted to align with stage 3 specification. However, for NG-U tunnel establishment procedure of multicast session, the current version of NGAP also does not specify the GTP UL TEID for NG-U unicast transport in Distribution Setup procedure. Therefore, the GTP UL TEID for NG-U unicast transport in steps 4/5 of Multicast session establishment procedure should be removed .
To provide the 5GC NG-U TNL address for multicast transport from gNB-CU-CP to gNB-CU-UP, the MC BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message should be used. In the current TS 38.401, the steps 5a/5b added in the RAN3#119 meeting shall include the NG-U TNL, which should be corrected to address for multicast transport instead of GTP UL TEID. And also steps 11/12 in the callflow is updated to only include the F1-U TNL DU info and remove the NG-U TNL info, while the description of steps 11/12 still include the NG-U TNL redundantly. Thus, the description of steps 11/12 should be aligned.

Redundancy between step 10 and step 11/12.

consequencesIfNotApproved: In case of split PDU session and the updated security indication received by the MN in the Path Switch Request Acknowledge message is “preferred” and if the MN sends the “preferred” security policy to the SN, the SN can not know and follow MN’s decision on whether to apply the updated security policy.
reasonForChange:
At RAN3 114bis meeting, it was agreed to add the Security Indication IE in the PDU Session Resource Modification Info - SN terminated IE in the SN modification request message, and add the Security Result IE in the PDU Session Resource Modification Response Info - SN terminated IE in the SN modification request acknowledge message so that the MN can send the updated security indication to the SN and receive the corresponding result from SN.
In case of split PDU session, the MN shall determine the UP security policy as specified in the clause 6.10.4 of TS 33.501. However, if the updated security policy received by the MN is “preferred” and if the MN forwards the “preferred” security policy to the SN, the MN is not able to notify the SN whether this updated security policy is applied or not and therefore the SN cannot follow the MN decision.
Therefore, it is necessary to clarify how to treat this situation.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Reusing the SDAP Configuration IE which was cerated for DRB and has no use case for MBS can only lead to mistakes e.g. in the settings of the configuration, while this IE is not needed.
reasonForChange:
Both BC MRB Setup Configuration IE and MC MRB Setup Configuration IE contain SDAP Configuration IE as mandatory. This SDAP Configuration IE contains itself three mandatory fields which are obviously intended for DRBs: Default DRB, UL SDAP Header, DL SDAP Header whereas these three fields don’t apply to MBS.
Even though these fields could be set respectively to “false, absent, absent” there is no case that can be true or present.
So to avoid any issue and be cleaner it is better to remove this SDAP Configuration IE. Even if in the feature some SDAP is added for MBS, a new specific IE could be then be created.
summaryOfChange:
Remove the SDAP Configuration IE from the BC MRB Setup Configuration IE and the MC MRB Setup Configuration IE.  

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the MBS function.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
It is unclear whether only one or multiple TNL associations have been supported between one eNB and en-gNB pair.
If a TNLA for UE associated signalling is failed or removed while UEs are still served by the TNLA, the the eNB or the en-gNB is not able to signal any X2AP messages for these UEs because it is not able to reselect a TNLA for the affected UEs.
reasonForChange:
Multiple SCTP associations between one eNB and en-gNB pair have been supported since Rel-16. However, the current spec in TS 36.422 still states that there shall be only one SCTP association established between one eNB and en-gNB pair. And such statement should be removed.
In addition, besides TNL binding update case, the SCTP association can also be changed during the communication of the UE-associated signalling due to other reasons including the failure or the removal of the current SCTP association.
summaryOfChange:
Remove the statement on ‘there shall be only one SCTP association established between one eNB and en-gNB pair’.
Add the failure or the removal of the current SCTP association as additional reasons which causes the SCTP association change during the communication of the UE-associated signalling.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only implies a clarification on SCTP association related description

consequencesIfNotApproved: Cannot support MC MBS session level forwarding resource to support handover to a gNB not supporting NR MBS.
reasonForChange:
In R3-225246, the MBS Session Associated Information IE was introduced to establish a MC MBS session level forwarding resource to support handover to a gNB not supporting NR MBS.
As forwarding data packets are transmitted over GTP-U tunnels, the MBS Session Associated Information IE includes an MBS Session Forwarding Address IE which refers to the UP Transport Layer Information IE. But in asn.1, the mbsSessionForwardingAddress is wrongly defined as TransportLayerAddress, which means the GTP-TEID is missing.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 8/11/2023. Original source : Huawei, CBN, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, Qualcomm Incorporated, CATT, Ericsson, Orange, ZTE, BT
summaryOfChange:
In the MBSSessionAssociatedInformation, change the mbsSessionForwardingAddress from TransportLayerAddress to UP-TNL-Information.
Impact Analysis:
This CR is an NBC CR, which has an impact under functional/protocol point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the data forwarding from MBS supporting to non-supporting node.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
1/ Unused references to 5GC UL tunnel endpoints for unicast transport creates confusion.
2/ Risk of erroneous inclusion of a CU TNL address instead of a DU TNL address which breaks the protocol.
reasonForChange:
1/ It was concluded at RAN3#119bis that 5GC doesn’t provide an UL tunnel endpoint of NG-U tunnel for unicast transport and corresponding references have been removed from NGAP. However, some corresponding references have not been removed from E1AP.
2/ The MC Bearer Context F1-U TNL Info at DU in contained in the MC Bearer Context To Modify IE which is sent from gNB-CU CP to gNB-CU UP therefore it should rather contain a transport layer address of a DU, not a transport layer address of a CU.
summaryOfChange:
1/ Remove the erroneous references related to 5GC TNL addresses and NG-U unicast transport in section 9.3.1.112 and 9.3.1.122.
2/ Replace the CU F1-U TNL Information by DU F1-U TNL Information in section 9.3.1.124. 

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the MBS function.

title: Correction on Temp no data and DL data arrival for Activate Multicast Session

consequencesIfNotApproved: The gNB is not able to move the UE to RRC_INACTIVE state in case there is temporarily no data for an active multicast session.
reasonForChange:
TS 38.300 allows the gNB to move the UE to RRC_INACTIVE state in case there is temporarily no data for an active multicast session:
When there is temporarily no data to be sent to the UEs for a multicast session that is active, the gNB may move the UE to RRC_INACTIVE state.
But currently in E1AP, the gNB-CU-UP is not able to inform the gNB-CU-CP about “inactivity” and “DL data arrival”, therefore it is needed to introduce a new E1AP class 2 procedure to notify the gNB-CU-CP about these.
And similar to PDU session handling, to help the gNB-CU-UP to trigger the above new procedure, there is also needed for the gNB-CU-CP to provide Multicast Session Inactivity Timer and MC Bearer Context Status Change in the MC BEARER CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION REQUEST messages.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 11/3/2023. Original source : Lenovo, Huawei, ZTE, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell
summaryOfChange:
Enable DL data arrival detection function and suspension/resumption of bearer context for MBS.
Introduce new class 2 procedure to notify the gNB-CU-CP about “inactivity of MC Bearer context” and “DL data arrival”.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only enable the gNB-CU-UP to inform the “temp no data” and “DL data arrival” to the gNB-CU-CP.

summaryOfChange:

This CR may have an impact from functional point of view because the Geographical Coordinates IE may be received by the LMF instead of the NG-RAN Access Point Position IE. The impact can be considered isolated because it impacts only OnDemand measurements for NR E-CID .

(BLCR to 38.300) On introduction of R18 eNPN

consequencesIfNotApproved: The gNB is not able to move the UE to RRC_INACTIVE state in case there is temporarily no data for an active multicast session.
reasonForChange:
TS 38.300 allows the gNB to move the UE to RRC_INACTIVE state in case there is temporarily no data for an active multicast session:
When there is temporarily no data to be sent to the UEs for a multicast session that is active, the gNB may move the UE to RRC_INACTIVE state.
But currently in E1AP, the gNB-CU-UP is not able to inform the gNB-CU-CP about “inactivity” and “DL data arrival”, therefore it is needed to introduce a new E1AP class 2 procedure to notify the gNB-CU-CP about these.

And similar to PDU session handling, to help the gNB-CU-UP to trigger the above new procedure, there is also needed for the gNB-CU-CP to provide Multicast Session Inactivity Timer and MC Bearer Context Status Change in the MC BEARER CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION REQUEST messages.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 20/11/2023. Original source : Huawei, CBN, Samsung, CMCC, Ericsson, Lenovo, ZTE, Qualcomm Incorporated, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell
summaryOfChange:
Introduce new class2 E1AP: MC Bearer Notification procedure, with MC BEARER NOTIFICATION message to notify the gNB-CU-CP about “inactivity of MC Bearer context” and “DL data arrival”.
Introduce a MC Bearer Context Inactivity Timer IE (refer to Inactivity Timer 9.3.1.54) in the MC BEARER CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION REQUEST messages
Introduce a MC Bearer Context Status Change IE (ENUMERATED (Suspend, Resume, …)) in the MC BEARER CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION REQUEST messages.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only enables the gNB-CU-UP to inform the “temp no data” and “DL data arrival” to the gNB-CU-CP.
title: Correction on Temp no data and DL data arrival for Activate Multicast Session

title: Avoiding unnecessary setup of DRB(s) in indirect data forwarding [Indirect Data forwarding]

secretaryRemarks: Technically endorsed
title: Correction to 37.320 on the user consent for trace reporting

consequencesIfNotApproved: The unnecessary DRB(s) or PDU session(s) set up for those already terminating in T-SN may result in the unnecessary overload to T-MN-CU-UP, and further more result in unsuccessful indirect data forwarding.
reasonForChange:
According to current spec TS 37.483, to support indirect data forwarding, the address of T-SN could only be provided to T-MN-CU-UP after T-SN-terminated bearer setup at T-MN-CU-UP, while such bearer setup at the T-MN-CU-UP is unnecessary. Moreover, the unnecessary DRB(s) or PDU session(s) set up for those already terminating in T-SN may result in the overload to T-MN-CU-UP, which might result in unsuccessful indirect data forwarding. The indirect data forwarding is supported since Rel-15, and the load on T-MN-CU-UP will be more serious in CHO with candidate SCG(s).

Therefore, the solution is proposed to avoid the unnecessary setup of DRB or PDU session for indirect data forwarding, i.e., indicate the purpose for the setup of DRB or PDU session is for indirect data forwarding with the indirect data forwarding information.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Management of a BC Bearer context, which is performed by means of E1AP BC Beaer Modification, would be limited to one F1-U tunnel context for one DU,  and multiple F1-U tunnels for one broadcast MRB (towards multiple gNB-DUs) will not be supported .
reasonForChange:
For split gNB scenario, it is possible that MBS session contexts for the same MBS session are established in multiple gNB-DUs which means there maybe multiple F1-U tunnels for one MRB.However, management of mutiple F1-U tunnels for one MRB is not supported for broadcast service.
Current E1AP functionality for BC Bearer Context modification is limited to setup one F1-U tunnel context.  In order to enable setup of multiple F1-U bearer contexts, one per DU, every new instance of the gNB-CU-CP initiated BC Bearer Context modification procedure containing a per MRB BC Bearer Context F1-U TNL Info at DU IE procedure is interpreted as an addition of one (set of) new F1-U tunnel(s) (towards one gNB-DU).
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 2/19/2024. Original source : CATT,Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, Huawei, Samsung, ZTE, Qualcomm, CMCC, CBN, Lenovo, Ericsson,China Broadnet
summaryOfChange:

2.	Adding new IEs “F1-U TNL Info to Add List” into the “BC MRB To Add Item” structure for managing multiple F1-U TNL contexts, as well as adding a new IE “F1-U TNL Info Added List” into the response structure.
3. 	Introducing a “Broadcast F1-U Context Reference” IE type in order to enable correlating F1-U resources to the respective resources at the gNB-CU-UP.

reasonForChange:
In Rel-16 IAB, the MME/AMF authorizes the IAB-node during network integration. TS 38.401 presently does not describe the RAN’s behavior in case the IAB-node is not authorized.

TS 38.401 presently does not describe the RAN’s behavior when receiving an authorization change from the MME/AMF.

RAN3 agreed that during IAB-MT migration for an IAB-node operating in SA, the authorization status is also included in the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST message and in the NGAP PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLEDGE message to the target IAB-donor-CU. summaryOfChange:
A section on IAB-node authorization is added to TS 38.401. This section describes the RAN's behavior when receiving the IAB-node authorization indicator for the IAB-node.

The general behavior of the IAB-donor-CU receiving the IAB-node’s authorization status is the following:
In case the authorization status is “not authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU does not configure BAP address, BAP configuration or IP address, or, in case these parameters are already configured, it removes the configuration of these parameters.
In case the authorization status is “authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU follows phase 2 and phase 3 of the respective network integration procedure.

In case the IAB-node is dual-connected to an eNB and an IAB-donor operating in ENDC. In this case, the authorization status is passed via the SeNB Addition/Modification Request message.

TS 38.401 presently does not describe the RAN’s behavior when receiving an authorization change from the MME/AMF.

summaryOfChange:
A section on IAB-node authorization is added to TS 38.401. This section describes the RAN's behavior when receiving the IAB-node authorization indicator for the IAB-node.

The general behavior of the IAB-donor-CU receiving the IAB-node’s authorization status is the following:
In case the authorization status is “not authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU does not configure BAP address, BAP configuration or IP address, or, in case these parameters are already configured, it removes the configuration of these parameters.
In case the authorization status is “authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU follows phase 2 and phase 3 of the respective network integration procedure.

In many IAB scenarios, the RAN node receiving the IAB-node’s authorization status from the AMF/MME is not the IAB-donor. In these cases, the authorization status is passed via Xn/X2 to the IAB-donor. This applies to the following scenario:
(1): The IAB-node is dual-connected to an eNB and an IAB-donor operating in ENDC. In this case, the authorization status is passed via the SeNB Addition/Modification Request message.
(2): The IAB-node is dual-connected to a non-IAB-capable gNB and an IAB-donor, and the non-IAB-capable gNB is the MN. In this case, the authorization status is passed via the SN Addition/Modification Request message.
(3) The IAB-MT is connected with a non-F1-terminating IAB-donor and the IAB-DU has F1 connection with an F1-terminating IAB-donor. In this case, the authorization status is sent from the non-F1-terminating IAB-donor to the F1-terminating IAB-donor via the Transport Management Modification Request message.

consequencesIfNotApproved: NG-RAN nodes do not know how to handle the IAB authorization status which is transferred by the core network.
reasonForChange:
To support IAB operation, the CN that the IAB-node connects provides authorization status of the IAB-node to RAN.
If the IAB-node connects to EPC, the MME provides the IAB authorization status to the eNB which the IAB-node connects. It’s specified in TS36.413 that if the authorization status is received from MME for an IAB-MT, the RAN should use it accordingly, e.g., to ensure that the IAB-node will not serve any UE if the authorization status is “not authorized”.

However, it has not been specified how the RAN node uses the authorization status of IAB-node that is received from the core network.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The MME may not know whether it is proper time to initiate de-registration for  an unauthorized IAB-node in EN-DC.
reasonForChange:
At the RAN3#122 meeting, as a part of mIAB-node authorization handling, RAN3 agreed that the mIAB-MT’s donor can indicate to the AMF that the unauthorized mIAB-MT can be de-registered. At the RAN3#123 meeting, RAN3 specified authorization handling for IAB-nodes, and made the following agreements related to de-registration handling:
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the RAN node serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After RAN node serving the IAB-MT is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the AMF that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting. 
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the eNB serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After the eNB serving the IAB-MT in EN-DC is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the MME that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting. 
Based on the above, RAN3 should specify S1AP signalling to support the 4th agreement above.

After the MeNB of the IAB-node receives the updated “IAB-node not authorized” status indication from the MME, it will send the updated status to the en-gNB acting as the SN of the IAB-node. After the SN has completed the handling of the unauthorized IAB-node, it can inform the MN that the handling has been completed. Then, the MN can inform the MME accordingly.
summaryOfChange:
A new NAS-related cause value “IAB not authorized” is specified.

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).

consequencesIfNotApproved: The gNB-CU-CP cannot inform the SMF that the PDU session release is requested due to receiving a GTP-U Error Indication over NG-U.
reasonForChange:
Per C4-235602, it was agreed that when the 5G-AN receives a GTP-U Error Indication over a NG-U tunnel that is not an indirect forwarding tunnel, the 5G-AN shall initiate a PDU Session Resource Notify procedure, and indicate the release is due to receiving a GTP-U Error Indication (also see the agreed CR in R3-241117). 

In the CU-CP/CU-UP split architecture, it is the gNB-CU-UP that receives a GTP-U Error Indication over a NG-U tunnel. Then the gNB-CU-UP should report to the gNB-CU-CP so that the gNB-CU CP can inform the SMF.

consequencesIfNotApproved:

Tabular and asn.1 not aligned.
reasonForChange:
In R3-237968, the SpecialTriggeringPurpose IE was introduced to inform the gNB-CU-UP about that the setup of the DRB or the PDU session for which the IE is included is for the purpose of indirect data forwarding.

It is noticed that in BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, in the PDU Session Resource To Modify List IE, for each PDU session, the DRB To Setup List IE is optionally included to setup DRB, and in such case it is also possible for the gNB-CU-CP to trigger the setup a new DRB for the purpose of indirect data forwarding, but currently in 9.3.3.11, the SpecialTriggeringPurpose IE is not included in the DRB To Setup List IE in the PDU Session Resource To Modify List IE.

On the other hand, in asn.1 part, SpecialTriggeringPurpose IE is included in the DRB-To-Setup-List-NG-RAN IE, and it is included in PDU-Session-Resource-To-Modify-Item IE, because same DRB-To-Setup-List-NG-RAN IE is also used in PDU-Session-Resource-To-Setup-Item IE.

Therefore, the inclusion of SpecialTriggeringPurpose IE is missing in the tabluar of the DRB To Setup List IE within the PDU Session Resource To Modify List IE, and missing in the procedural text part, but no need to chagne asn.1.

It is also noticed that SpecialTriggeringPurpose IE is named as “SpecialTriggeringPurpose” in all places, it is better to update it to “Special Triggering Purpose” in the procedural text and tabular.
summaryOfChange:
In 9.3.3.11, include SpecialTriggeringPurpose IE in the DRB-To-Setup-List-NG-RAN IE within the PDU Session Resource To Modify Item IE.

In 8.3.2.2, add the corresponding procedural text.

Update the SpecialTriggeringPurpose IE to Special Triggering Purpose IE in the procedural text and tabular.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
For split PDU session, the gNB-CU CP cannot inform the gNB-CU-UP to allocate new NG-U tunnel address upon receiving the UP-failure indication from the core network.
Not aligned with CT4 specification.
reasonForChange:
Per C4-241525, when the UPF receives a GTP-U Error Indication from a 5G-AN for a split PDU session or when detects a user plane path failure, CT4 agreed the CR specifying that, the SMF may indicate those errors to the NG-RAN using a PDU session resource modification procedure, so that the NG-RAN may allocate a new N3 DL tunnel or move the QoS flows conveyed by the failed GTP-U tunnel to the other healthy GTP-U tunnel. 

Then over the E1 interface, in case of single connection, the CU-CP may indicate the UP failure indication to the CU-UP to allocate new DL tunnel address. 
In case of dual connection, when the MN-CU-CP receives the failure indication by the PDU session resource modification procedure, it can perform the following actions. 
if the UP error happens at the MN side, the MN-CU-CP may send the failure indication to the MN-CU-UP, so that the MN-CU-UP can allocate a new NG DL tunnel address.
If the UP error happens at the SN side, the MN-CU-CP may send the failure Indication to the SN-CU-CP via S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUEST message and then SN-CU-CP may send the failure indication to the SN-CU-UP, so that the SN-CU-UP can allocate a new NG DL tunnel address.
summaryOfChange:
Add UP failure indication in the PDU Session Resource To Modify List IE in the BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, so that the CU-UP can allocate new NG DL tunnel address and signal back to the CU-CP.

summaryOfChange:

consequencesIfNotApproved: Sending PDCP SN Gap Report is not supported in gNB-CU-UP.
reasonForChange:
Enhancements to Rel-18 discard (i.e., PDU Set discard and PSI-based discard) for XR services may increase the frequency and duration of gaps in the PDCP SN. This could lead to unnecessary delays, as the receiving PDCP entity depends on the PDCP reordering timer. To address this issue, RAN2 has agreed to introduce SN Gap Reporting from the PDCP transmitter to the PDCP receiver. 
RAN2 agreed following:
Agreements
1.	To define a mechanism for PDCP Transmitter to report to PDCP Receiver about the gap on the PDCP SN (i.e., transmitting PDCP entity can inform the receiving PDCP entity about the discarded SDUs).  
2	To agree that the usage of a PDCP SN gap report is under network control (i.e. network configures UE whether/when PDCP SN gap report can be used).  The UE should report only if there gaps (i.e. if the UE does re-association and there are not gaps, the UE is not required to transmit).   
3	Define a new UE capability to indicate the support of PDCP SN Gap reporting.

According to these agreements, for UL, the UE is configured to send the PDCP SN gap report by gNB via RRC signalling. For DL, in case of split architecture, the gNB-CU-UP should be configured to send the PDCP SN Gap Report by gNB-CU-CP.

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Incorrect handling could occur at the gNB-CU-UP, i.e. providing wrong MBS data towards some areas. 
Incorrect explanation of IE exists.
reasonForChange:
Issue #1: wrong IE name
As the MBS Service area only needs to be provided to the gNB-CU-UP in case of location dependent, therefore the MBS Area Session ID IE is included in the MBS Service Area Information Item IE as mandatory IE, and different with other RAN3 specs, the MBS Service Area IE is not defined as CHOICE type to include two branches one for location dependent, one for non-location dependent. 
It is found that in the Explanation of maxnoofMBSServiceAreaInformation, the MBS Service Area Information Location Dependent List IE is mentioned but it does not exist.

Issue #2: wrong IE presence
As mentioned above, the MBS Service Area IE in E1AP was introduced for location dependent scenario only, and the MBS Service Area Information List IE is defined as mandatory IE. 
It is found that in asn.1 part, the mBS-ServiceAreaInformationList IE in the MBS-ServiceArea IE was wrongly defined as optional. Therefore, when it should be inlcuded but absent, wrong handling could occur at the gNB-CU-UP side, i.e. providing wrong data towards some areas.
summaryOfChange:
Issue #1: correct the incorrect explanation of maxnoofMBSServiceAreaInformation.

Issue #2: align the Tabular to ASN.1, change the presence of the MBS Service Area Information List as Optional, and update the procedure text.


Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only updates the IE related to the MBS service area.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN cannot be supported.
reasonForChange:
In TS 23.316, the AUN3 device is define as follows. 
Authenticable Non-3GPP (AUN3) device: A device that does not support NAS signalling, is connected to 5GC via a RG and can be authenticated by 5GC over the RG.
In section 7.2.8.1, the AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN procedure is specified as follows.

7.2.8.1	AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN
An authenticable non-3GPP devices (AUN3) may get connected behind 5G-RG as defined in clause 4.10c.
This clause specifies how an AUN3 device can be registered via 5G-RG.
<Irrelevant Text Omitted >
4.	The W-AGF selects an AMF based on the received AN parameter provided by the 5G-RG and based on local policy, as specified in clause 6.3.5 of TS 23.501 [2]. The W-AGF shall determine that a W-CP connection is for an AUN3 device and apply corresponding policies.
	The W-AGF sends an NGAP INITIAL UE message to the selected AMF. For an AUN3 device, the W-AGF indicates to AMF if the N2 connection relates to an AUN3 device and if there is an existing N2 connection for a 5G-RG connected to the same GLI/GCI (where the initial NAS message related with NGAP INITIAL UE message has been received).
	If the W-AGF indicated for an AUN3 device that there is no existing 5G-RG N2 connection for a 5G-RG connected to the same GLI/GCI, then the AMF rejects the registration request and further steps of this procedure are skipped. Otherwise, the procedure continues.
It can be observed that during the AUN3 device Registration procedure, in the Initial UE message, the W-AGF needs to indicate:  
if the N2 connection relates to an AUN3 device, and
if there is an existing N2 connection for a 5G-RG connected to the same GLI/GCI. 
 But it is missing in the NGAP specification.
summaryOfChange:
Add procedural texts that the AUN3 Device Access Information is included in the NGAP initial UE message for the AUN3 device Registration.  


Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it enhances the Initial UE message to support the AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN.

consequencesIfNotApproved: In case the network enables Broadcast resource efficiency for RAN sharing, in case of shared NG-U path change, packet discard may occur at the UE.
reasonForChange:
In Broadcast RAN sharing discussion, it was discussed that for an ongoing broadcast service, if the PDCP COUNT of the packets received by the UE is outside of the UE’s receiving window, the UEs will drop these packets, whic is not preferred.

In case of MOCN, if the gNB-CU-CP decides (e.g., in case the 5GC1 triggers Broadcast Session Release) to establish shared NG-U resources with the 5GC2 with which the shared NG-U was not established, considering that the shared F1-U tunnel is kept, after shared NG-U path change, the gNB-CU-UP should keep the PDCP COUNT continuity after the shared NG-U change to avoid above mentioned unexpected packet discard by the UE.
summaryOfChange:
Add related NOTE on gNB-CU-UP handling in case of MOCN to avoid unexpected packet discard by the UE.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it describes the handling and gNB-CU-UP to avoid packet discard by the UE after shared NG-U path change in case of MOCN.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The actual Carrier Bandwidth to support Less than 5MHz configuration is not clear.
reasonForChange:
In the RAN2 #129 meeting, the feature on Less than 5MHz and carrier configuration has been discussed and make the following agreement.
RAN2 confirms the following understanding for the case where only 12/20 PRB transmission bandwidth can be used:
The network shall configure carrierBandwidth to 15 PRB (for the 12 PRB case) and 25 PRB (for the 20 PRB case) respectively in SIB1 and in RRC dedicated signaling. 
The UE shall use 12/20 PRB as the transmission bandwidth, even though carrierBandwidth is configured to 15 PRB (for the 12 PRB case) and 25 PRB (for the 20 PRB case) respectively in SIB1 and in RRC dedicated signaling.  
The corresponding CR R2-2501513 is agreed, as below.

Based on the RAN2’s clarification, for the same reason, RAN3’s specifications also need to clarify Carrier Bandwidth to support Less than 5MHz configuration.
summaryOfChange:
To introduce the clarification on Carrier Bandwidth to support Less than 5MHz configuration.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release). This CR only has an impact on the less than 5MHz function.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The S-NG-RAN node may use wrong S-NG-RAN node Security Key for S-CPAC case.
reasonForChange:
In SN addition request message, the S-NG-RAN node Security Key IE shall be ignored if the S-CPAC Request Information IE is present in the Conditional PSCell Addition Information Request IE. The reason is that, the S-CPAC Request Information IE also includes S-NG-RAN node Security Key IE which is used for S-CPAC function.
Therefore, in SN modification request message, the S-NG-RAN node Security Key IE shall also be ignored if received and if the S-CPAC Request Information IE is present in the Conditional PSCell Addition Information Modification Request IE. However, it is missing, then SN will use wrong Secuirty Key for S-CPAC.
summaryOfChange:
In SN modification request message, it is added that the S-NG-RAN node Security Key IE shall be ignored if the S-CPAC Request Information IE is present in the Conditional PSCell Addition Information Modification Request IE.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release). This CR only has an impact on SN modification request message.
title: Correction on S-CPAC for the presence of SN security Key IE

consequencesIfNotApproved: The new serving gNB-CU-UP is not aware of the security activation status used in last serving cell, and RRC setup may occur between the UE and the new serving gNB-CU-CP.
reasonForChange:
Per TS 33.501, during the context relocation procedure for the RRC inactive UE, the UP security activation status with the corresponding PDU session ID(s) shall be sent to the target gNB/eg-eNB via Xn-AP Retrieve UE Context Response message. And the target RAN node would use the UP security activation status when resuming the RRC connection as specified below. 
If the UP security activation status can be supported in the target gNB/ng-eNB, the target gNB/ng-eNB shall use the UP security activations that the UE used at the last source cell. Otherwise, the target gNB/ng-eNB shall respond with an RRC Setup message to establish a new RRC connection with the UE.
For the CU-CP/CU-UP split architecture, when the UP security policy is set to "preferred," the CU-UP can determine whether to activate UP security based on its local strategy. In order to align with the UP security activation status that the UE used at the last serving cell, the CU-CP may change the security indication and send it to the CU-UP if the UP security policy retrieved from the old NG-RAN node is "preferred".
summaryOfChange:
To add a NOTE in clause 8.6.2 to clarify that the security indication may be changed and sent to the CU-UP if the UP security policy retrieved from the old NG-RAN node is "preferred".

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
title: Clarification on security indication during State Transition from RRC_INACTIVE to RRC_CONNECTED

reasonForChange: The UE Trajectory Collection Configuration IE shall be included in the DATA COLLECTION REQUEST message when measured UE trajectory is requested. However, there is no explicit procedural text to describe this behaviour.
summaryOfChange:
Add procedural text that mandates the presence of the UE Trajectory Collection Configuration IE in the DATA COLLECTION REQUEST message when measured UE trajectory collection is requested.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an impact from protocol and functional point of view.
The impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the NR AI/ML RAN function, namely measured UE trajectory information over Xn interface.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The condition for the presence of the Requested Prediction Time IE and UE Performance Collection Configuration IE is not specified.
reasonForChange:
The Requested Prediction Time IE shall be included in the DATA COLLECTION REQUEST message when predicted information is requested. 
Likewise, the UE Performance Collection Configuration IE shall be included in the DATA COLLECTION REQUEST message when UE Performance is requested. 
However, there is no explicit procedural text to describe this behaviour.
summaryOfChange:
Add procedural text that mandates the presence of the Requested Prediction Time IE in the DATA COLLECTION REQUEST message when predicted information is requested and that mandates the presence of the UE Performance Collection Configuration IE in the DATA COLLECTION REQUEST message when UE Performance is requested.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has no impact from protocol and functional point of view.
The impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the NR AI/ML RAN function.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The integrity protection indication for the concerned E-RABs in the en-gNB CU-UP separation is not correctly indicated. 
The confidentiality Protection Indication for the concerned E-RABs in the en-gNB CU-UP separation is applied in error.
reasonForChange:
The Security Indication could be included in the DRB To Setup List E-UTRAN IE to provide the security polices, when the en-gNB is in split architecture for EN-DC.  And as observed from TS 36.413, only the Integrity Protection Indication can be included in the security indication. 

However, in 9.3.1.23	Security Indication, there are several issues. 
The general descriptions of security indication are limited to the PDU session resources, not covering the E-RABs in the en-gNB CP-UP separation. 
The integrity Protection Indication does not cover the E-RABs in the en-gNB CP/UP separation. 
For the Confidentiality Protection Indication and the Maximum Integrity Protected Data Rate, it is not clear whether to apply to the E-RABs in the en-gNB CP/UP separation. 
The similar issues exist for 9.3.1.52	Security Result.
summaryOfChange:
Update the security indication and security results to specify the security policies and results for the concerned E-RABs for the en-gNB CU-UP separation.  

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it impacts the security indication and security result for the concerned E-RABs in the en-gNB CU-UP separation.
title: Correction of security Indication and security Result

consequencesIfNotApproved: Will cause some unpredictable error at NG-RAN node, who expects that the MDBV will always be included in the alternative QoS parameter for delay critial QoS flow, if the CN does not provide MDBV in alternative QoS.
reasonForChange:
SA2 agreed that the MDBV can be included in the Alternative QoS Profile for Delay-critical traffic, the following sentence is excerpted from TS 23.501 “For a GBR QoS Flow using the Delay-critical resource type, an Alternative QoS Profile may also include the QoS parameter MDBV.” 
To align with SA2, RAN3 also included the MDBV in the Alternative QoS Parameters, the semantics description part includes “This IE is included if the Delay Critical IE is set to "delay critical" and is ignored otherwise.” Such statement indicates that the MDBV will always be included in the alternative QoS parameter if the traffic is delay critial. But this is not align with SA2’s specification because the MDBV is optionally included in the alternative QoS parameter for the delay critical traffic.
summaryOfChange:
Update the semantics description for the Maximum Data Burst Volume to be “This IE may be included if the Delay Critical IE is set to "delay critical" and is ignored otherwise”.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has no impact with the previous version of the specification (same release). 
This CR has impact on the functional point of view. The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the alternative QoS parameter configuration for delay critical traffic.
title: Correction for MDBV in alternative QoS

consequencesIfNotApproved: Not consistent with the message level criticality.
reasonForChange:
A set of class 2 E1AP messages have the message level criticality not consistent with the ASN.1. It seems the simple way is to align the Tabular with ASN.1. But it may be worthwhile to have a thorough analysis. 

For example, for MR-DC Data Usage Report message and the Data Usage Report message used for report data volumes, RAN3 can discuss whether the criticality can be set to “reject”, in order for the sending node to be aware of the function supported by the receiving node. Note that it can be observed that the XnAP SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message has the criticality as “reject”, while “ignore” for the NGAP SECONDARY RAT DATA USAGE REPORT message.  

Another example is whether the gNB-CU-CP Measurement Result Information message should be corrected to have the criticality “reject”. 

After online discussion, it was agreed to simply align the Tabular with the ASN.1.
summaryOfChange: Correct the message-level criticality for a set of E1AP procedures, to align with ASN.1.
title: Correction of message level criticality of E1AP procedures

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is not possible for the gNB-CU-CP to deactivate user inactivity monitoring in the gNB-CU-UP.
reasonForChange:
Current Stage 2 (TS 38.401) specification in section 6.1.1 mandates inactivity monitoring at the CU-UP.

“The node hosting user plane part of NR PDCP (e.g. gNB-CU, gNB-CU-UP, and for EN-DC, MeNB or SgNB depending on the bearer split) shall perform user inactivity monitoring and further informs its inactivity or (re)activation to the node having C-plane connection towards the core network (e.g. over E1, X2).”

Hence, the Inactivity Timer IE shall always be configured to the CU-UP over E1AP, regardless of monitoring being carried out per UE, PDCP session or per DRB. The range of this timer is 1-7200 seconds. Hence, at maximum 7200 seconds of inactivity the CU-UP will report inactivity to the CU-CP.

In case of Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) deployments, the mobile operator’s may want to ignore or disable UE inactivity reporting. 

Therefore, it is beneficial to allow configuring the CU-UP to stop inactivity monitoring and reporting to the CU-CP when the “inactivity timer” expires. A backwards compatible approach is to introduce a new IE to signal to the CU-UP to stop inactivity monitoring for the bearer context.
summaryOfChange: Introduce Inactivity Monitoring IE in BEARER CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message.
title: Inactivity Timer for Fixed Wireless Access [Inactivity_Timer_FWA]

consequencesIfNotApproved: Wrong cause will be provided from the eNB to the MME in case of EDT
reasonForChange:
In Rel-13, in the RRCConnectionRequest-NB message and the RRCConnectionResumeRequest-NB message, the EstablishmentCause-NB-r13 IE is provided from the UE:
RRCConnectionRequest-NB-r13-IEs ::=		SEQUENCE {
	ue-Identity-r13							InitialUE-Identity,
	establishmentCause-r13					EstablishmentCause-NB-r13,
	multiToneSupport-r13					ENUMERATED {true}				OPTIONAL,
	multiCarrierSupport-r13					ENUMERATED {true}				OPTIONAL,
	earlyContentionResolution-r14			BOOLEAN,
	cqi-NPDCCH-r14							CQI-NPDCCH-NB-r14,
	spare									BIT STRING (SIZE (17))
}

RRCConnectionResumeRequest-NB-r13-IEs ::=	SEQUENCE {
	resumeID-r13								ResumeIdentity-r13,
	shortResumeMAC-I-r13						ShortMAC-I,
	resumeCause-r13								EstablishmentCause-NB-r13,
	earlyContentionResolution-r14				BOOLEAN,
	cqi-NPDCCH-r14								CQI-NPDCCH-NB-r14,
	anr-InfoAvailable-r16						BOOLEAN,
	spare										BIT STRING (SIZE (3))
}

In Rel-15, EDT was introduced during the discussion of CIoT:
new RRCEarlyDataRequest message was introduced, with a new establishmentCause-r15 field contained in the RRCEarlyDataRequest-r15-IEs IE. And in Rel-16, MT-EDT was further introduced, and a new establishmentCause-v1610 field contained in the RRCEarlyDataRequest-5GC-r16-IEs IE was introduced.
RRCEarlyDataRequest-r15-IEs ::=	SEQUENCE {
	s-TMSI-r15						S-TMSI,
	establishmentCause-r15			ENUMERATED {mo-Data, delayTolerantAccess},
	dedicatedInfoNAS-r15				DedicatedInfoNAS,
	nonCriticalExtension				RRCEarlyDataRequest-v1590-IEs			OPTIONAL
}
RRCEarlyDataRequest-v1610-IEs ::=	SEQUENCE {
	establishmentCause-v1610			ENUMERATED {mt-Access, spare3, spare2, spare1},
	nonCriticalExtension				SEQUENCE {}					OPTIONAL
}

New RRCEarlyDataRequest-NB message was introduced, with a new establishmentCause-r15 field contained in RRCEarlyDataRequest-NB-r15-IEs IE 
RRCEarlyDataRequest-NB-r15-IEs ::=	SEQUENCE {
	s-TMSI-r15							S-TMSI,
	establishmentCause-r15				ENUMERATED {mo-Data, mo-ExceptionData, delayTolerantAccess, mt-Access-v1610},
	cqi-NPDCCH-r15						CQI-NPDCCH-NB-r14						OPTIONAL,
	dedicatedInfoNAS-r15				DedicatedInfoNAS,
	nonCriticalExtension				RRCEarlyDataRequest-NB-v1590-IEs		OPTIONAL
}

But currently the cause value related to the fields/IEs introduced above are missing/incorrect in the S1AP: RRC Establishment Cause IE.
summaryOfChange:
Update the S1AP: RRC Establishment Cause to refer to the correct fields in TS 36.331 in case of EDT.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it impacts the RRC Establishment Cause in case of EDT. 
This CR is functional NBC.
title: Correction on RRC establishment Cause for CIoT

reasonForChange: In SA2 CR S2-2409198, it was agreed for operators to control Time Reference distribution information to UEs based on subscription. title: Time Reference Distribution Information in S1AP

consequencesIfNotApproved: N3mb recovery not aligned with TS 23.527.
reasonForChange:
RAN3 received the LS from CT4 in C4-244467 informing that CT4 has agreed the attached 23.527 CR 0082 defining a new stage 2 restoration procedure in Rel-19 for recovery of N3mb path failure for unicast transport of multicast session. CT4 asks RAN3 group to consider alignment to support the new Rel-19 restoration procedure.
In case of CP UP separation, upon receiving the Shared NG-U Path Failure IE from 5GC, the gNB-CU-CP should trigger the gNB-CU-UP to allocate new unicast transport resources in replacement of existing ones accordingly.
The MC Bearer Context To Modify Request IE in the MC BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message currently contains an MC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN Request IE but this is used for requesting unicast transport resources when not existing. This IE cannot be reused to be backwards compatible reason because in this new restoration use case the gNB-CU UP has already allocated unicast transport resources and needs to consider the request instead as a “replace” action whereby the current unicast transport resources are to be considered released.
summaryOfChange: Update the MC Bearer Context To Modify Request IE in the MC BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message to include a MC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at NG-RAN Replace Request IE to request the gNB-CU-UP to consider the current unicast transport resource as released and re-allocate unicast transport resources in replacement of existing resources, and in per MBS Area Session granularity in case of location dependent service.
title: Recovery of N3mb path failure for unicast transport of multicast session

consequencesIfNotApproved: The Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure will fail even if one of the requested information cannot be admitted by the gNB-CU-UP.
reasonForChange:
In the context of the Rel-19 “Enhancements for Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) for NG-RAN” RAN3 introduced in TS 37.483 the Data Collection Reporting Initiation and Data Collection Reporting procedures to enable the gNB-CU-CP to request the reporting of information by the gNB-CU-UP, in alignment with the procedures specified in Rel-18 for the Xn interface.
The Data Collection Reporting (Initiation) procedures in XnAP support the partial reporting of information, allowing the reporting node to report a subset of the information requested by the sending node, hence avoiding to fail the reporting procedure if not all the requested information is admitted. The reporting node indicates in the DATA COLLECTION RESPONSE message the list of information that cannot be admitted. Such information includes both predicted information as well as measurements.
This CR aims at introducing the partial support feature also for the Data Collection Reporting (Initiation) procedures over the E1 interface, in alignment with Xn.
summaryOfChange: The partial reporting is introduced in the Data Colletion Reporting (Initiation) procedures in E1AP.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The function of default DRB would not work well.
reasonForChange:
As described in TS 38.300, the default DRB may be configured per PDU session, i.e. if an incoming UL packet matches neither an RRC configured nor a reflective "QoS Flow ID to DRB mapping", the UE then maps that packet to the default DRB of the PDU session.
But the gNB-CU-CP is not aware of the event that a QoS flow mapped to default DRB arrives at gNB-CU-UP, thus there would no chance for the gNB-CU-CP to reconfigre the mapping for this new coming QoS flow. So, there is a need to introduce the notification of the arrival of a QoS flow data over the default DRB from gNB-CU-UP to gNB-CU-CP.

Although it has been clarified in RAN3#99bis, AH1807, 101 and captured in section 8.4.1.1 of TS 38.401 that 
“the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message may contain source cell group configuration to allow gNB-DU to perform delta configuration”, 
“In case the gNB-DU receives the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message without the source cell group configuration …, it shall perform full configuration and indicate that it has applied full configuration in the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message.”, 
and “On Inter-gNB-CU Mobility, same method is performed to achieve full configuration and delta configuration”, 
it may be beneficial to capture also in stage 3 how the gNB-CU allows or does not allow gNB-DU to perform delta configuration by including or not including source cell group configuration in UE Context Setup procedure.
summaryOfChange:
Add the corresponding description that if the received CU to DU RRC Information does not include the source cell group configuration, the gNB-DU shall generate the cell group configuration using full configuration. Otherwise, delta configuration is allowed.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Not aligned with SA2 and CT4 specifications; inconsistency between specifications in TS 23.501 and TS 38.414.
The transport level packet marking in NR is not specified precisely at the gNB and may be different than the marking in the rest of the core network.
reasonForChange:
The current normative text for the DSCP derivation does not include the Priority Level or the ARP. Should reach alignment with SA2 specification TS 23.501 per LS from SA2 S2-1902800 and the Reply LS R3-191988 from RAN3. 

The current normative text in TS 38.414 §5.4 specifies that the "mapping between traffic categories and Diffserv code points shall be configurable by O&M based on 5QI characteristics and other NG-RAN traffic parameters."
Based on SA2 agreements (S2-1902731) as reflected in TS 23.501 §5.8.2.7 (and consistent with CT4 material in TS 29.244 §5.4.3), the SMF uses Priority Level in addition to 5QI and ARP to determine the DSCP value to be provided to the UPF for packet marking in the DL. 

Similarly, TS 23.501 (§5.7.1.7) states that "(R)AN performs transport level packet marking in the UL on a per QoS Flow basis with a transport level packet marking value that is determined based on the 5QI, the Priority Level (if explicitly signalled) and the ARP priority level of the associated QoS Flow."
summaryOfChange:
Update the derivation of the DSCP at the gNB to explicitly reference the Priority Level and the ARP. Add a note to address the IRAT handover case between LTE and NR, that the E-UTRAN QCI/ARP to DSCP mapping should have matching 5QI/PL/ARP to DSCP implementation in NR. 

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):

The change affects NR data transport behavior only. No other impact to gNB to core network mechanisms.
title: Use of Priority Level and ARP for the DSCP Derivation at the gNB
