consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment between RRC, Stage 2 and Stage 3 specifications, as well as unexpected behaviour in multivendor scenarios.
reasonForChange:
In regard to INITIAL UL RRC MESSAGE TRANSFER, current F1AP specification mandates that gNB-DU includes CellGroupConfig IE when the gNB-DU is able to serve the UE, and that gNB-CU configures the UE and transparently includes the received CellGroupConfig IE as follows.

“If the DU to CU RRC Container IE is not included in the INITIAL UL RRC MESSAGE TRANSFER, the gNB-CU should reject the UE under the assumption that the gNB-DU is not able to serve such UE. If the gNB-DU is able to serve the UE, the gNB-DU shall include the DU to CU RRC Container IE and the gNB-CU shall configure the UE as specified in TS 38.331 [8] and transparently include the received CellGroupConfig IE. The gNB-DU shall not include the ReconfigurationWithSync field in the CellGroupConfig IE as defined in TS 38.331 [8] of the DU to CU RRC Container IE.”

The above statement is conflicting with the RRC Connection Reestablishment scenario and message contents that gNB transmits defined in TS 38.331. Specifically, the contents of CellGroupConfig received in the INITIAL UL RRC MESSAGE TRANSFER message cannot be transparently used as received in the subsequent RRC Connection Recofiguration message sent from CU to DU. 

Therefore, a change is needed to clarify that the CellGroupConfig cannot be transparently included from CU to DU as received.
summaryOfChange:
Clarification on usage of CellGroupConfig IE in Initial UL RRC Message Transfer procedure.
 
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has an impact under functional point of view 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change is limited to scenarios for RRC connection re-establishment. 
This CR is ASN.1 backwards compatible

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is the risk of cross cell interference between systems adopting different time references
reasonForChange:
ITU-T WG 15 has sent an LS to RAN3 in R3-193344, where it is recommended that a common recognised time standard source is taken as reference when tracing continuous time in an operator network. Given the 3GPP requirement for a “continuous time without leap seconds”, the actual implementation in this case could make use of the content of the UTC information that is being distributed and that is not impacted by leap seconds.   
The LS from ITU-T also implies that radio frames timing is calculated on the basis of a standardized reference point in time and that such timing is created on the output synchronously with the input synchronization reference.
summaryOfChange:
Add UTC as the time reference to which continuous time without leap seconds is traceble. Clarify that the radio frame on the output should be synchronous with the input time reference.
The common SFN initialisation time for all gNBs shall be determined with respect to the GPS EPOCH 1980-01-06 T00:00:19 International Atomic Time (TAI)

SA2 sent LS S2-1907955 asking RAN1, RAN2 and RAN3 whether increasing the MDBV (Maximum Data Burst Value) by the suggested value of 500 times would cause any issues in RAN, and asking CT3 and CT4 to provide feedback on whether it is acceptable to increase the maximum allowed value of MDBV for signalled 5QI characteristics to 2000 kbytes (or another maximum value suggested by RAN1/RAN2).

RAN2 sent a reply LS R2-1911859 indicating that “RAN2 did not identify a blocking issue with increasing the values of MDBV”. RAN3 also replied that this is feasible in R3-194553. Other WGs also provided similar feedback.

In response, SA2 has now asked (in S2-1910663) RAN3, CT3 and CT4 to support the increased maximum allowed value of MDBV for signalled 5QI characteristics, to 2000 kbytes.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The PWS Cancel functionality may not work as expected.
reasonForChange: In the PWS CANCEL REQUEST message, the Cancel-all Warning Messages Indicator IE and the Notification Information IE are both optional. However, if both IEs are included, it is not clear which one has precedence (i.e. whether the gNB-DU shall stop broadcasting all warning messages or just one). Also, if neither IE is included, it is not clear whether the gNB-DU replies with a PWS CANCEL RESPONSE message (omitting the Cell Broadcast Cancelled List IE since no warning messages are cancelled) or if it is considered a logical error.
summaryOfChange:
If both IEs are included, the gNB-DU acts on the Cancel-all Warning Messages Indicator IE and ignores the Notification Information IE. This behavior is consistent with NGAP.
If neither IE is included, the gNB-DU considers this a logical error. This is because at least one of the IEs is always provided over NGAP, and the alternative (replying with a PWS CANCEL RESPONSE) could result in a status mismatch between the RAN and CBC, i.e. CBC thinks that no broadcast needed to be cancelled but gNB-DU continues broadcasting of warning message(s).

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an impact under protocol point of view. The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects one system function, namely PWS Cancel.
title: Addition of abnormal conditions in PWS Cancel procedure

(Note that the counterpart from MN is possible via DRBs To Be Modified List of 9.2.1.11 PDU Session Resource Modification Info – MN terminated). 

(2) If SN triggers CA-based duplication in MN side for a SN terminated bearer via SN MOD REQD, the MN needs to provide the primary LCID to the SN via the nested MN-initiated SN modification procedure, so that the SN can configure the primary LCID to the UE accordingly. However, providing LCID from MN was wrongly implemented onto DRBs Admitted to be Setup or Modified List of  9.2.1.21 PDU Session Resource Modification Confirm Info – SN terminated, which happens after reconfiguration to the UE was completed.
summaryOfChange:
(1) PDCP Duplication Configuration IE, Duplication Activation IE, and secondary SN UL PDCP UP TNL Information IE are added into DRBs To Be Modified List of 9.2.1.10 PDU Session Resource Modification Response Info – SN terminated + corresponding ASN.1.

(2) The semantic of the LCID IE under DRBs Admitted to be Setup or Modified List of 9.2.1.21 PDU Session Resource Modification Confirm Info – SN terminated is changed to “Shall be ignored by the S-NG-RAN node if received”. Moreover, for 8.3.4 SN-intiated SN modification procedure, the interaction with the MN-initiated SN modification procedure is updated not to fall onto abnormal condition for LCID provided from the MN for CA-based PDCP duplication.

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is ambiguous for the NG-RAN operation when the NG-RAN can not perform the location report signalled in the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message and HANDOVER REQUEST message.
reasonForChange:
The Location Reporting Request Type IE is included in the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message and HANDOVER REQUEST message. If the location report request type contains multiple areas of interest set with the same Location Reporting Reference ID, or some other reasons, the NG-RAN can not perform the location report, and need to inform the AMF. 
However it is not clear which option the NG-RAN shall perform: 
Option1: fail the initial UE context setup or handover procedure with failure response
Option 2: succeed the initial UE context setup or handover procedure. Then the NG-RAN sends a LOCATION REPORTING FAILURE INDICATION message to the AMF with a cause value.  
Option 3: introduce a new indicator in the successful response message to inform AMF (new IE is needed), but not fail the procedures. 

Option 2 is preferable. But currently the Location Reporting Failure Indication is used on in case of the Location Reporting Control Procedure as follows. 
The purpose of the Location Reporting Failure Indication procedure is to allow the NG-RAN node to inform the AMF that the Location Reporting Control procedure has failed. The procedure uses UE-associated signalling.
Hence it is proposed to update the purpose of the Location Reporting Failure Indication procedure.
summaryOfChange:
Update the purpose of the Location Reporting Failure Indication procedure to allow the NG-RAN to report in case that the requested location reporting action has failed, so as to cover all location reporting failure cases 
 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it corrects the NG-RAN behaviour when it is not able to perform the location report signalled in the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message and HANDOVER REQUEST message.
The impact can be considered isolated.
title: Failure case of user location report

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear how the IAB-donor-CU cannot decides which gNB-DU is an IAB-donor-DU.
reasonForChange:
As described in section 8.2.3.2 of TS38.473, if the F1 SETUP REQUEST message is received from an IAB-donor-DU, the gNB-CU shall, if supported, include the BAP Address IE in the F1 SETUP RESPONSE message. However, it is not clear how IAB-donor-CU identifies that the F1 SETUP REQUEST message is from IAB-donor-DU. Then, how can the IAB-donor-CU recognize the IAB-donor-DU is worth to be clarified.
This problem has been discussed in previous meeting, and companies has common understanding that no explicit information will be introduced to indicate the gNB-DU is an IAB-donor-DU. In fact, the IAB-donor-CU can recognize the IAB-donor-DU from normal gNB-DUs according the iab-support IE included in the SIB1 which will be included in the F1 SETUP REQUEST message from an IAB-donor-DU, and the IAB-donor-CU also can distinguish the IAB-donor-DU and an IAB-DU from whether the BAP address is carried in the F1 SETUP REQUEST message,  because the IAB-DU will include a BAP address in the F1 SETUP REQUEST message, but the IAB-donor-DU will not. There may also exist some other solutions for CU to identify the IAB-donor-DU, e.g. OAM configuration. In a word, this can be achieved by proper implementation, but a clarification is still needed, to address this issue.
summaryOfChange:
In the procedure description in 8.2.3.2, add an NOTE to clarify that how the IAB-donor-CU recognize an IAB-donor-DU is up to implementation.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The BAP address IE in the F1AP spec cannot be used to indicate a parent node’s BAP address, and an IAB-donor-DU’s BAP address. The F1AP spec is not align with RRC spec in TS38.331.
reasonForChange:
In 9.3.1.111, the BAP address IE is defined, and this IE will be used for multiple cases, including indicate the parent node’s BAP address, or the child node’s BAP address, or the allocated BAP address to an IAB-node or the IAB-donor-DU. However, the semantics description of the BAP address IE only refers the bap-Address-r16 in 6.3.2 of TS38.331, which only refer to the allocated BAP address for an IAB node. 
So this BAP address IE in the F1AP spec cannot be used to indicate a parent node’s BAP address, which should refer to the bap-Address-r16 defined in 6.3.2 of TS38.331, and an IAB-donor-DU’s BAP address, which should refer to the iab-donor-DU-BAP-address-r16 defined in subclause 6.2.2 of TS 38.331. Apparently, such constraint does not reflect the real intention of introducing such IE in F1AP specification.
summaryOfChange:
Modify the Semantics description of the BAP address IE as “Corresponds to the bap-Address-r16, defined in subclause 6.2.2 or subclause 6.3.2 of TS 38.331 [8], or the iab-donor-DU-BAP-address-r16 defined in subclause 6.2.2 of TS 38.331[8].” to include all the correlations.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The RACS feature is not supported for some UEs using Connection Establishment Indication procedure.
reasonForChange:

Similarly, the gNB-DU System Information IE contains several IEs, named as SIBx message with semantics of “SIBx messages, as …”. consequencesIfNotApproved: A parent gNB-DU (either an IAB-DU or an IAB-donor-DU) may not be able to find a BH RLC channel to transmit the downstream BAP control PDU if none of the BH RLC channel is configured for BAP control PDU after the UE Context Modification procedure.
reasonForChange:
In the UE Context Modification procedure, some BH RLC CH may be configured for transmit the BAP control PDU among a parent gNB-DU and its child IAB node, this can be achieved by including the BAP Control PDU Channel IE in the BH RLC Channel to be Modified List IE. 
And according to the BAP specification (TS38.340), if none of the BH RLC CH is configured for transmitting the BAP control PDU in a BH link, an IAB node/IAB-donor-DU can select any egress BH RLC channel in the egress link.  
However, the current specification in  the UE Context Modification procedure stated that “If the BAP Control PDU Channel IE is included in the BH RLC Channel to be Modified List IE, the gNB-DU shall, if supported, consider that the configured BH RLC channel can be used to transmit BAP Control PDUs, and use this BH RLC channel as specified in TS 38.340 [30]. Otherwise, the gNB-DU shall consider that the configured BH RLC channel cannot be used to transmit BAP Control PDU.” It reads like that the BH RLC channel cannot be used to transmit BAP control PDU if it is modified and not configured for BAP control PDU during the UE context modification procedure. However, this is contradict with the R16 agreements and the BAP specification because it should be possible for such BH RLC channel to be used for carrying the BAP Control PDU if none of the BH RLC channel in the same BH link is configured for transmitting the BAP control PDU.  For example, the BH RLC CH selection for the flow control polling (one kind of BAP control PDU) is described as following in TS38.340:
-	if the egress BH RLC channel for the BAP Control PDU is configured as specified in TS 38.473 [5]:
-	submit this BAP Control PDU to the configured egress BH RLC channel of the egress link, indicated by BH RLC CH ID IE which is associated with BAP Control PDU Channel IE that is set to true in TS 38.473[5];
-	else:
-	submit this BAP Control PDU to any egress BH RLC channel of the egress link.
So the highlighted sentence is incorrect, it should be removed to avoid misunderstanding.
summaryOfChange:
In section 8.3.4.2:
Change the description of “Otherwise, the gNB-DU shall consider that the configured BH RLC channel cannot be used to transmit BAP Control PDU” to “Otherwise, if the BAP Control PDU Channel IE is not present, any available BH RLC channel can be used to transmit BAP Control PDUs as specified in TS 38.340 [30].” from the paragraph related to the receiving operation about the BAP Control PDU Channel IE in the BH RLC Channel to be Modified List IE . 

Impact analysis

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because the changes only impact IAB functionality.
This CR has an impact under functional point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the IAB related configuration about the transmitting of BAP control PDU.
The changes are backward compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Wrong RATRestriction information will be provided from lower release NG-RAN node to higher release NG-RAN node.
reasonForChange:
In the semantics description of the XnAP: RAT Restriction Information IE, it is said that the sending node shall set bits 2-7 to "0", the sender shall ignore bits 2-7. With that, a lower release MN will propagate wrong information towards a higher release SN, e.g. CN send RAT restriction (00100000) to a Rel-15 MN, the Rel-15 MN will forward (00000000) towards the Rel-16 SN.

The issue also exist in non-DC case, i.e. lower release NG-RAN node1 will provide wrong information towards a new release NG-RAN node2 in Mobility Restriction List IE. In non-DC case the issue could be solved by using existing 5GC Mobility Restriction List Container IE provided from source/old NG-RAN node to the target/new NG-RAN node. But as 5GC Mobility Restriction List Container IE is an optional IE, the issue will still exist if 5GC Mobility Restriction List Container IE is not provided.
summaryOfChange:
Change the last part of semantics description of the XnAP: RAT Restriction Information IE to “Bits 2-7 are reserved for future use.”

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The MICO mode indication can not be deactivated towards the NG-RAN. 
Not aligned with stage 2 CN specification.
reasonForChange:
The MICO Mode Indication IE included in the Core Network Assistance Information for RRC INACTIVE IE could be signaled in many interface messages. 

When checking into section 5.4.1.3 in TS 23.501, the AMF may deactivate the MICO mode and signal to the UE as follows. 
When the UE is in CM-CONNECTED, the AMF may deactivate MICO mode by triggering Mobility Registration Update procedure through UE Configuration Update procedure as described in clause 4.2.4 of TS 23.502 [3].

This means that the MICO Mode Indication included in the Core Network Assistance Information for RRC INACTIVE IE may be updated. However, as specified in the UE context modification request message, the NG-RAN just stores the received new information. 

If the Core Network Assistance Information for RRC INACTIVE IE is included in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, the NG-RAN node shall, if supported, store this information in the UE context and use it for the RRC_INACTIVE state decision and RNA configuration for the UE and RAN paging if any for a UE in RRC_INACTIVE state, as specified in TS 38.300 [8]

Then if the MICO Mode Indication is received initially by the NG-RAN node, but later it is not included in the UE Context modification request message, the NG-RAN may misunderstand that this MICO Mode Indication is not changed. 

There are two potential options as follows. 
Option 1: add a new codepoint for MICO Mode Indication
Option 2: specify the “overwrite” operation for the Core Network Assistance Information for RRC INACTIVE in the UE context modification request procedure. 

Both options could work. Option 2 is proposed in the CR.
summaryOfChange:
Specify the “overwrite” operation for the Core Network Assistance Information for RRC INACTIVE in the UE context modification request procedure. 
 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the MICO mode function.

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is a risk that the total number of established EHC contexts exceeds UE’s capability maxNumberEHC-Contexts
reasonForChange:
With current EHC parameters transferred via E1, CU-UP has no knowledge of UE’s capability. There is a risk that CU-UP establishes too many DL EHC contexts such that the total number of established EHC contexts exceeds maxNumberEHC-Contexts.
The number of EHC contexts for DL should be less than or equal to maxNumberEHC-Contexts - maxCID_EHC_UL across all DRBs.
summaryOfChange:
To add a maxCID-EHC-DL IE which is configured per-DRB. The maxCID-EHC-DL IE is included within the EHC Downlink IE and indicates the maximum number of EHC contexts that can be established in DL for the corresponding DRB. Since CU-CP has the knowledge of both maxCID_EHC_UL and maxNumberEHC-Contexts, it can distribute the overall available contexts space between different DRBs that require it, as long as the distributed maxCID-EHC-DL satisfies: 
 Summation of maxCID-EHC-DL and maxCID-EHC-UL across all DRBs is less than or equal to maxNumberEHC-Contexts.

This CR has an impact under protocol and functional point of view.

consequencesIfNotApproved: DAPS HO handling during Bearer Context Modification procedure is incorrect.
reasonForChange:
During Rel-16 mobility enhancement work, R3-204512 (BL CR for 38.463) introduced DAPS Request Information IE onto DRB To Setup List of 9.3.3.2 PDU Session Resource To Setup List to support DAPS HO when establishing bearer context in the target CU-UP (via Bearer Context Setup procedure). In ASN.1, the IE was added to DRB-To-Setup-List-NG-RAN but since DRB-To-Setup-List-NG-RAN is also used for DRB To Setup List of 9.3.3.11 PDU Session Resource To Modify List, so the CR R3-216162 in RAN3#114-e meeting fixed the misalignment and added the IE onto the tabular of DRB To Setup List in 9.3.3.11 PDU Session Resource To Modify List. 
While fixing this misalignment between tabular and ASN.1 is correct, in fact there is no usage to establish new DRB for DAPS HO during Bearer Context Modification procedure. The only usage during Bearer Context Modification procedure is to support intra-gNB-CU-UP DAPS HO, where the DAPS Request Information IE is carried by DRB To Modify List within 9.3.3.11 PDU Session Resource To Modify List, not by DRB To Setup List. As a result, it is proposed to deprecate this IE in DRB To Setup List of 9.3.3.11 PDU Session Resource To Modify List.
summaryOfChange:
Fixed the semantic of DAPS Request Information IE in DRB To Setup List of 9.3.3.11 PDU Session Resource To Modify List by "This IE is not used in this version of the specification".
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change is limited to DAPS function during Bearer Context Modification procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The positioning information cannot be configured to the UE and the positoning will fail.
reasonForChange:
In TS 38.473 sub-clause 5, the following description can be found:
“Unless explicitly indicated in the procedure specification, at any instance in time one protocol endpoint shall have a maximum of one ongoing F1AP procedure related to a certain UE.”

Thus, after the gNB-CU sends the Positioning Information Request message for a UE, it will wait for the Positioning Information Response/Failure message, before processing any other procedures.

On the other hand, after the gNB-DU recieves the Positioning Information Request message, it will determine the SRS configuration for the UE and send the UE Context Modification Required message to the CU TS 38.305 figure 8.10.4-1. The gNB-DU will not send the Positioning Information Response/Failure message to the gNB-CU, before it receives the UE Context Modification Conform/Refuse message.

It can be easily found that the SRS configuration cannot be configured to the UE, because the CU would not be able to process the UE Context Modification Required message after it sends the Positoning Information Request message. Then the positioning will fail. 

The interaction between procedure is explictly indicated.
summaryOfChange:
Added an interaction between procedure in the UE Context Modification Required message, including an indicator and added the corresponding procedure text.

Rev1: remove additional IE, capture a single sentence for the interaction


Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).The CR has functional impact.

consequencesIfNotApproved: IAB deployments with IPsec tunnel mode cannot support fine granular QoS or traffic differentiation using IPv6 Flow Label.
reasonForChange:
When IPsec tunnel mode is used to protect DL F1 or X2 traffic to IAB nodes, the IPv6 Flow Label information needs to be available on the outer IP header, so that it can be used for the DL mapping at the IAB-donor-DU. This implies that for deployments with IPsec tunnel mode, the IPv6 Flow Label information is set on the inner IP header by the IAB-donor-CU for F1 traffic and by the MeNB for Xn traffic, and it must then be copied from the inner IP header to the outer IP header by the security gateway.
The need of IPv6 Flow Label copying by the security gateway to support these IAB deployment scenarios is presently missing in the spec.
summaryOfChange:
Add description to section “8.9.9.1 Traffic Mapping from IP-layer to Layer-2” on the copying of IPv6 Flow Label copying at the security gateway for IAB when using IPsec tunnel mode for F1 or X2 protection.

consequencesIfNotApproved: No support for determination of serving AMF based on UE location.
reasonForChange:
SA2 has agreed an optional requirement on the RAN in S2-2009486, according to which the RAN may, if configured, select an AMF based on the UE’s location (i.e. country where the UE is located). In principle this covers two scenarios (i.e., coverage spillover across border, and non-spillover) which are of interest for NTN since (1) RAN nodes may host cells in different countries, and also (2) cells may span large cross-border areas.

For the spillover case, the UE location needs to be available to the RAN node. 

For the non-spillover case, the country where the UE is located is implicitly known by the identity of the access cell and the selected PLMN (which must be one of the broadcast PLMNs). However, according to TS 38.300, it is not precluded that a cell served by a gNB does not broadcast the PLMN ID included in the Global gNB ID. With that statement, it seems possible that different cells in the same gNB broadcast different PLMNs, and the same logical gNB will have connectivity to different CNs. This scenario may happen for NTN where a single gNB provides coverage in multiple countries.

Under this arrangement, it is important to ensure that a UE accessing the network via a cell of country A does not use the CN of country B, in any scenario (including when the UE provides a 5G-S-TMSI, or a GUAMI as per S2-2009486).
summaryOfChange: Specify that RAN may optionally take into account UE location information when determining the AMF.
title: Clarification of NAS Node Selection Function for NTN nodes providing access over multiple countries

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment between F1AP and RRC specifications.
reasonForChange:
The current encoding of the PDC Measurement Periodicity IE within the PDC Measurement Reporting messages is not aligned with RAN2 agreements for RRC specification. 
For RTT-based PDC method, when the gNB configures the UE to perform RxTx measurement reports, it can configure the report to be periodical with the following values according to the RRC specification:
RxTxPeriodical-r17 ::= SEQUENCE {
    rxTxReportInterval-r17        RxTxReportInterval-r17,
    reportAmount-r17              ENUMERATED {r1, infinity, spare6, spare5, spare4, spare3, spare2, spare1},
    ...
}

RxTxReportInterval-r17 ::= ENUMERATED {ms80,ms120,ms160,ms240,ms320,ms480,ms640,ms1024,ms1280,ms2048,ms2560,ms5120,spare4,spare3,spare2,spare1}

However, in RAN3 F1AP specification, when the gNB-CU requests periodical PDC measurements from the gNB-DU different periodicity values are supported:
PDC Measurement Periodicity	C-ifReportTypePeriodic		ENUMERATED (120ms, 240ms, 480ms, 640ms, 1024ms, 2048ms, 5120ms, 10240ms, 20480ms, 40960ms, 1min, 6min, 12min, 30min, …)
It is proposed to align reporting periodicity values in 38.473 with RRC agreed values.
summaryOfChange: Align F1AP PDC Measurement Periodicity values with RRC RxTxReportInterval-r17 values.
title: Correction of PDC Measurement Periodicity values

consequencesIfNotApproved: The ASN.1 and the tabular definitions are not aligned.
reasonForChange:
The solution for inter-RAT load reporting assumes using a set of levels distributed evenly between the low and the high CAC threshold. Therefore, to cover the full scale of the CAC, the thresholds can have values between 0% and 100%. However, in ASN.1 the type is defined as starting from 1%.
Also, the number of levels is defined in ASN.1 differently than in the tabular. Considering that having only 1 level is likely wrong, the ASN.1 is assumed to be wrong.
Finally, the Inter-system Resource Status Request and Reply use the same IE type for the Reporting System. However, in the tabular, this IE is defined explicitly in each message, which may in future lead to problems when one message is to be enhanced. Therefore, either ASN.1 is corrected to use different IE types (even if defined identically for the time being), or the tabular is corrected to refer to the same IE. Of these two options, in this case, the latter seems better, because indeed the Request and Reply are logically to carry the same information.
summaryOfChange:
The ASN.1 definition of the threshold and of the number of the levels is aligned with the tabular.
The tabular is corrected so that the Request and Reply refer to a separate IE used in both messages.
title: Alignment of ASN.1 and tabular for inter-RAT MLB solution

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is a misalignment between 38.331 and E1AP IE structure for drb-ContinueEHC-DL/drb-ContinueEHC-UL IE.
reasonForChange: The presence of ehc-uplink/ehc-downlink indicates whether Ethernet header compression is configured for uplink only or for downlink only or for both uplink and downlink. In the meanwhile, the drb-continueEHC-UL/ drb-continueEHC-DL IE is also an optional IE which is used to indicate whether the PDCP entity continues or resets the uplink/downlink EHC header compression protocol during PDCP re-establishment. This means there is no coupling relationship between the two IEs, both IEs should be optional and have their own meanings for presence and absence. However, in the current E1AP, the existence of drb-continueEHC-UL/ drb-continueEHC-DL IE is coupled with the existence of EHC uplink/EHC downlink IE, and the IE value can only be set to ‘true’. This violates the RAN2 meaning in 38.331 and should be fixed.
summaryOfChange:
For addressing the issue in a backward compatiable way, the proposed solution is to extend drb-continueEHC-UL/ drb-continueEHC-DL with a new value set to ‘false’. By this way, we can realize the scenario where we choose to apply EHC configurations for DL and/or UL while we can also reset downlink/uplink EHC header compression protocol during PDCP re-establishment.
Add related procedure text

consequencesIfNotApproved:
MN would always provide the prepared PSCell list in the SN CHANGE CONFIRM message which is incorrect. 

There will be problem to associate prepared PSCells with target SN in SN initiated CPC.

There will be problem to associate the suggested PSCells with target SN in SN initiated CPC

In SN initiated CPC, the target SN does not know up to how many candidate PSCells can it prepare.
reasonForChange:
In case of SN initiated inter SN CPC, if the step 2 is skipped, i.e., MN informs S-SN about the list of PSCells prepared by T-SN using SN MODIFICAITION REQUEST message, MN will include the list of prepared PSCells to S-SN in the SN CHANGE CONFIRM message.

For SN initiated CPC, in step 2, MN may inform the source SN about the prepared PSCells before configuring UE with CPC using the SN MODIFICATION REQUEST message. Since there could be PScells from multiple target SNs, target SN ID is added following the same principle as for SN CHANGE CONFIRM message. 

For SN initiated CPC, in the SN CHANGE REQUIRED message, source SN may indicate the suggested PSCells for multiple target SNs using RRC container carrying CG-Config. In the current RRC spec, the CG-Config not designed for multiple RAN node operation and MN may not understand the association between the target SN and suggested PSCells. 

The “Maximum Number of PSCells To Prepare” IE in the SN CHANGE REQUIRED message should be present as Mandatory, otherwise the target SN does not know up to how many candidate PSCells can it prepare. 

Editorial for better consistency with rest of the spec. 

Based on the SoD R3-223789, RAN3 has the following agreement in the Chair’s note. 
For SN initiated Inter-SN CPC, RRC Container for CG-Config message can be sent in per target SN manner for better association between the suggested PSCells in CG-Config and target SN.
In case of SN initiated inter SN CPC, if the step 2 is skipped, i.e., MN does not inform S-SN about the list of PSCells prepared by T-SN using SN MODIFICAITION REQUEST message, MN will include the list of prepared PSCells to S-SN in the SN CHANGE CONFIRM message
The “Maximum Number of PSCells To Prepare” IE in the SN CHANGE REQUIRED message should be present as Mandatory.
Add Target SN-ID of accepted PSCells in SN MODIFICATION REQUEST message for SN initiated CPAC.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The IAB-donor-CU-CP can not provide correct security info to the IAB-donor-CU-UP to protect F1-U.
reasonForChange:
In previous RAN3 meeting, the IAB PSK Notification procedure has been introduced in E1 interface to allow the IAB-donor-CU-CP to send the security key info to the IAB-donor-CU-UP. Each IAB-donor-CU-UP PSK info item includes an IAB-Donor-CU-UP PSK, an IP address of IAB-DU, and an IP address of CU-UP. 
Then the problem is how can the IAB-donor-CU-CP know the IP address of CU-UP and IAB-DU in advance. There are two possible way for the IAB-donor-CU-CP to know the IP address:
Option 1: IAB-donor-CU-CP know the IP address of IAB-DU and IAB-donor-CU-UP from UE associated signaling in E1 and F1 interface, i.e. from the UL/DL UP parameters contained in the bearer context management procedure (including the Bearer context setup procedure and the Bearer context modification procedure) via E1 interface, and the UE Context management procedure (including the UE context setup procedure and UE context modification procedure) via F1 interface.
Option 2: IAB-donor-CU-CP know the IP address of IAB-DU and IAB-donor-CU-UP from non-UE associated signaling in E1 and F1 interface, if the IP address(es) has been updated during the topology update procedure. The mentioned NUA signaling is the message in IAB UP TNL address Update procedure in E1 inerface, and the IAB-UP configuration update procedure in F1 interface.
Therefore, the current procedure in E1 and F1 interface can provide the IP address information which is necessary for the IAB PSK Notification procedure, and these procedures should be performed before the IAB PSK Notification procedure.  But the relationship between these procedures is missing in the current specification, then it is unclear how will the IAB-donor-CU-CP know the IP address of CU-UP and IAB-DU to provide the  security key info towards the IAB-donor-CU-UP.
summaryOfChange:
Add NOTE in the clause 8.5.2.1 to clearly state that the IAB PSK Notification procedure will be performed after the IAB-donor-CU-CP obtaining the IP address of IAB-DU and IAB-donor-CU-UP.

reasonForChange:
In TS 38.331, the ul-GapFR2-Config-r17 IE is introduced in RRCReconfiguration message (as first agreed in R2-2204230), which is used to indicate the FR2 UL gap configuration to UE. 
UL-GapFR2-Config-r17 ::=      SEQUENCE {
    gapOffset-r17                 INTEGER (0..159),
    ugl-r17                       ENUMERATED {ms0dot125, ms0dot25, ms0dot5, ms1},
    ugrp-r17                      ENUMERATED {ms5, ms20, ms40, ms160},
    refFR2-ServCellAsyncCA-r17    ServCellIndex                                                      OPTIONAL -- Cond AsyncCA
}

In addition, in MR-DC case, as specified in TS 38.331 below, 
In EN-DC and NGEN-DC, the SN decides and configures the FR2 UL gap pattern. In NE-DC, the MN decides and configures the FR2 UL gap pattern. In NR-DC without FR2-FR2 band combination, the network entity which is configured with FR2 serving cell(s) decides and configures the FR2 UL gap pattern.

This is to support one objective in RAN4 lead WI NR_RF_FR2_req_enh2-Core in RP-213666 which was completed in June 22: UL gaps for self-calibration and monitoring. The main use case of the UL gap is to let UE detect whether human body is close to the Tx antennas during UL gaps, thus avoiding any unnecessary P-MPR.   

In CU/DU split scenario, it should be the DU that decides the UL-GapFR2-Config as octet string, and signal to the CU.

consequencesIfNotApproved: SDT RLC bearer configuration cannot be derived by last serving gNB.
reasonForChange:
Issue: RLC bearer configuration query for RA-SDT
To support the RA-SDT, the RLC-BearerConfig for each SDT bearer should be forwarded from last serving gNB-CU(-CP) to receiving gNB. The last serving gNB-CU(-CP) cannot derive RLC-BearerConfig since such configurations are included in CellGroupConfig, which is provided to gNB-CU(-CP) as a container. To solve this issue, two options can be considered:
Option 1: allow gNB-CU(-CP) decode the content of CellGroupConfig so as to derive RLC-BearerConfig for each SDT bearer. This option is functional NBC since from Rel-15, the gNB-CU is not required to decode the CellGroupConfiguration from the gNB-DU. 
Option 2: gNB-CU requests the RLC-BearerConfig from gNB-DU for SDT bearers via explicit indication, and then gNB-DU provides the corresponding configuration
To avoid the NBC change, we prefer to Option 2
Proposal: the gNB-CU(-CP) can request the RLC-BearerConfig from gNB-DU for RA-SDT

consequencesIfNotApproved: When UE uses RA-SDT or CG-SDT resource to send RRCResumeRequest message, the gNB-CU-CP’s behaviour is not specified.
reasonForChange:
When a UE’s mode is changed from RRC_inactive to others (e.g., RRC connected or RRC_idle), the UE shall send RRCResumeRequest message via either RACH resource or CG resource to network, then, the network shall, retrieve UE context via I-RNTI if needed, and verify it via MAC-I, by means of RRCResumeRequest message. If successfully, the network will send RRCResume message to UE, and it will, for split gNB, set up F1 connection and modify E1 bearer. Otherwise, i.e., either not retrieve or not verify the UE context data, the network will reject the RRC Resume procedure.
For RACH based RRC Resume procedure, it has been captured in TS38.300 (section 9.2.2.4.1	UE triggered transition from RRC_INACTIVE to RRC_CONNECTED) and TS38.401 (section 8.6.2	RRC inactive to other states).
However, for RA-SDT and CG-SDT, it is not specified whether the gNB-CU-CP shall verify UE context after receiving RRCResume message.
summaryOfChange:
When UE uses RA-SDT or CG-SDT resource to send RRCResumeRequest message, the gNB-CU-CP’s behavior shall be specified, i.e., it shall retrieve UE context via I-RNTI and verify it via MAC-I by means of RRCResumeRequest message. If successfully, the gNB-CU-CP is allowed to resume SDT bearer.

reasonForChange: In Rel-17, NR supports to configure eDRX for RedCap UE in RRC INACTIVE/IDLE.  If IDLE eDRX cycle is longer than 10.24s, the PH, PTW_start and PTW_end shall be calculated for paging as specified in TS 38.304, and the UE_ID_H (13 most significant bits of the Hashed ID) is needed for these calculation. However, the UE hashed ID information is missing in Xn paging message.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The gNB-DU may not take the MBSInterestIndication message into account when configuring resources for the UE.
reasonForChange:
The following is from section 5.9.4.2 in 38.331 v17.4.0.

NOTE: The UE may send MBS Interest Indication even when it is able to receive the MBS services it is interested in i.e. to avoid that the network allocates a configuration inhibiting MBS broadcast reception.

Based on the above, the gNB-DU should be informed of the MBSInterestIndication of a UE so that the gNB-DU does not allocate a configuration inhibiting MBS broadcast reception in the UE. 

MBSInterestIndication is optionally included in the CU to DU RRC Information as UEAssistanceInformation. However, a procedure text for the gNB-DU to consider the MBSInterestIndication message when configuring resources for the UE is missing.

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear which TNL associations should be removed/updated. It is unclear which port number is used for the AMF endpoint of the TNL associations to be added with only an IP address.
reasonForChange:
In the current specifications it is not clear how to interpret the NG-RAN TNL Association to Remove List IE, the AMF TNL Association to Remove List IE and the AMF TNL Association to Update List IE. Namely, it is not clear how to identify the TNL Associations to be removed or modified depending on the information contained in these IEs.
Moreover, it is unclear what port number is used when a new TNL association is added and if the newly added AMF TNL endpoint contains only an IP Address.
secretaryRemarks: Endorsed CRs from RAN3#119bis-e
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that the total number of endpoints corresponding to the associations to be removed/updated may be multiple.
Clarify that if an AMF TNL association is added and if the endpoint that is added by the AMF contains only an IP address, the port number is assumed to be 38412.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only implies a clarification of the RAN Configuration Update and AMF configuration Update procedure description

reasonForChange:
The TNL association could be identified by means of a single TNL association endpoint with IP address and port no. or, by means of TNL endpoints identified only by their IP address, which implies that there might be many TNL associations could be involved in the TNL removal of update procedure, while in the current specifications it is not clear how to interpret the TNLA To Add List IE, the TNLA To Update List IE and the TNLA To Remove List IE. consequencesIfNotApproved: CHOICE types would not be extendable using XnAP abstract syntax protocol means, i.e. lacking the possibility for further extensions to identify unknown extensions and specifiying the action at the receiver if the extension is not comprehended.
reasonForChange:
Some CHOICE type defintions introduced in Rel-16 are missing extension containers.
The advantage of introducing extension containers as early as possible, ideally at introduction of a new ASN.1 type (SEQUENCE or CHOICE) allows to improve the interaction between nodes of different implementation status, i.e. to identify the extension in case of non-comprehension and specifying the related action (ignore or reject).
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 5/11/2023. Original source : Ericsson, InterDigital, Orange, CATT, Deutsche Telekom, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, AT&T, ZTE
summaryOfChange:
The followng ASN.1 CHOICE types have been introduced with an extension:
AreaScopeOfMDT-NR, AreaScopeOfMDT-EUTRA, MeasurementThresholdL1LoggedMDT, ReportType.
The CHOICE type definitions of the above ASN.1 types did contain an ellipsis, which allowed the extension to be included in a backwards compatible way.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only corrects ASN.1 type definitions of CHOICE types missing an extension container.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change concerns ASN.1 type definitions of CHOICE types related to MDT functions only.
The CR has impact under protocol point of view and is backwards compatible towards the previous version (same Release) of the specification.

reasonForChange:
In the tabular, the QoS Mapping Information IE is included as a child IE of the GTP tunnel IE (refer to 9.2.3.30), which corresponds to the GTPtunnelTransportLayerInformation in ASN.1 part.
In ASN.1 part, the QoS-Mapping-Information is included as sub IE of UPTransportParametersItem, which corresponds to the UP Transport Item IE in the tabular (defined in 9.2.3.76). 
However, from the tabular, we can see that the UP Transport Item IE is the parent IE of UP Transport Layer Information  which contains the GTP tunnel IE as one option in choice structure.  
Therefore, the QoS-Mapping-Information IE in ASN.1 was added in wrong place.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Not aligned between the Tabular and the ASN.1 for the Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE.      
The Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE may be erroneously used by the gNB-CU-UP upon received.
reasonForChange:
The Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE is included in the 9.3.1.26 QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE (see the agreed CR in R3-193005), and in the DL DATA NOTIFICATION message respectively. Its IE type is given as INTEGER (0.. 7, …). 

However, in ASN.1, the paging-Policy-Indicator is defined as INTEGER (1..8) in the QoSFlowLevelQoSParameters. While it is correctly defined for the DLDataNotification message. 

For this Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE included in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE, it was initially removed from the Tabular in the agreed CR in R3-185358 since it was agreed to add the PPI field into the DL PDU SESSION INFORMATION frame of TS 38.415, but kept intact in the ASN.1  (see the agreed CR in R3-185127). Afterwards this IE was added back to the Tabular in the R3-193005 to align with the ASN.1. Given the above analysis, it should clarify that this IE is not used in this version of the specification.
summaryOfChange:
For the Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE included in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE
Update IE name to Paging Priority Index, and update the IE type to be the same as the definition in ASN.1;
Update the semantics description and ASN.1 so that this IE is not used in this version of the specification. 


Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the Paging Priority Indicator in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE.
title: Correction of Paging Priority Indicator in QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters

consequencesIfNotApproved: Ambiguous descriptions of positioning SI signalling and acquisition over F1
reasonForChange:
First, there is ambiguous description about the signalling of the Positioning SIBs over F1. In fact, once the gNB-CU receives the Positioning Assistance Information from the LMF containing the available positioning SIBs encoded by the LMF, the gNB-CU transmits the information transparently as an OCTET STRING in the Positioning Assistance Information IE within the POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION CONTROL message to the gNB-DU, so that gNB-DU broadcasts them in SI message. 

Second, once the UE is aware of the available positioning SIBs, the mechanism to support Positioning SI acquisition is similar to Other SI, as agreed to be clarified last meeting in R3-233411. 

Therefore, a clarification is needed on the gNB-CU and gNB-DU’s interaction that happens after receiving the RRC request from the UE.
summaryOfChange:
To clarify that the gNB-CU transmits transparently the positioning SIBs over F1 using the POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION CONTROL message to the gNB-DU.
To clarify that the gNB-CU commands the gNB-DU to broadcast the requested Positioning SI message list in a similar way as Other SI.  

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the procedures related to the positioning SI broadcast.

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the gNB-CU UP cannot associate the NG-U TNL address it provides with any Area Session ID, then it cannot bind the NG-U tunnel with the F1-U tunnel when it receives later on the F1-U tunnel information which breaks the function.
reasonForChange:
For MBS location dependent service and first UE joining the multicast session, the gNB-CU CP receives the Area Session ID in the NGAP PDU session Resource modify Request message. The gNB-CU CP then sends the E1AP MC Bearer Context Setup Request to the gNB-CU UP to fetch the NG-U TNL CU addresses for this area session. However the Area Session ID is missing in the E1AP MC Bearer Context Setup Request message which creates three issues:
This prevents the CU UP to associate the NG-U TNL address it provides with any Area Session ID. 
The Area Session ID must be included in the reply from CU UP in E1AP Bearer Context Setup Response which is not possible if the CU UP does not receive it in the E1AP Bearer Setup Request message.
In case a shared NG-U termination exists, the gNB-CU UP cannot correlate the proper (already configured) resources to the MC Bearer Context.
summaryOfChange:
Add the Area Session ID in the MC Bearer Context to Setup IE.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the MBS function.
This CR has impact from functionl and protocol point of view. The protocol impact is backwards compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Cannot support data forwarding for split PDU session at handover when source node is disaggregated.
reasonForChange:
During Xn Handover, in case the PDU session split has been allowed by the 5GC (i.e. two UL TEID addresses of UPF are provided from the source gNB), when the target node decides to split PDU session for one PDU session, the source NG-RAN node is able to get two data forwarding addresses for different set of QoS flows, one for the data forwarding towards the target MN, one for forwarding towards the target SN. This has been specified in the handover preparation procedure as follows
For each PDU session resource successfully setup at the target NG-RAN, the target NG-RAN node may allocate resources for additional Xn-U PDU session resource GTP-U tunnels, indicated in the Secondary Data Forwarding Info from target NG-RAN node List IE.

In case the source NG-RAN node is a disaggregated node with CU-CP and CU-UP separation, for a PDU session, the source CU-CP should also be able to provide two data forwarding addresses for different set of QoS flows, especially in case of PDU session split during Handover, or split PDU session QoS flow reallocation during Handover.
summaryOfChange:
Provide additional data forwarding addresses for a set of QoS flows:
add Secondary PDU Session Data Forwarding Information IE (referring to the Data Forwarding Information 9.3.2.6) in the PDU Session Resource To Modify List IE.
 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification because it adds additional data forwarding addresses to support split PDU session data forwarding.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The Source gNB cannot signal the UE Inactive Time to a Target gNB in disaggregated gNB architecture with CP-UP separation.
reasonForChange:
In handover scenarios, a gNB is able to over Xn, forward the “inactive” time spent for the UE to the target gNB. This is part of RRC: HandoverPreparationInformation can include rrm-Config, which can include ue-InactiveTime IE.

However, for disaggregated architecture with CP-UP separation, the gNB-CU-CP is not aware of the “inactive” time as it is measured at gNB-CU-UP and not reported with E1AP. Hence, this has negative result that for mobility, the gNB-CU-CP cannot forward the “inactive” period to the target gNB even though it is supported to be signaled over Xn interface. Thus, UE inactivity at the Source gNB is not accounted for.

To support this functionality in disaggregated gNB architecture with CP-UP separation, at the source gNB, the gNB-CU-CP needs means to request the gNB-CU-UP to report the “inactive” time.
summaryOfChange:
Add Inactivity Information Request IE to BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message.
Add UE Inactivity Information IE in BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE message.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change is limited to inactivity reporting.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The NG-RAN node unnecessarily stores the useless information and may further transfer the useless information to other NG-RAN node during the handover procedure.
reasonForChange:
Current specification mandates the NG-RAN node to store the the Area Of Interest List IE while Location Reporting Request Type IE is NOT set to ‘UE presence in the area of interest’. In this case the information of ‘Area Of Interest List IE’ is useless.
In case of UE mobility, the useless information will be propagated to other RAN node.
At RAN3#117, there is a common understanding captured:
NG-RAN node performs location reporting of AOI when Event type is set as ‘UE presence in the area of interest’ and Area of Interest information is provided.
But it just regulates the NG-RAN performing the ULI report, but not the behaviour of NG-RAN storing information.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify it is an abonormal condition that the NG-RAN node receives the Area of Interest IE but the Location Reporting Request Type IE is NOT set to ‘UE presence in the area of interest’

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has no impact with the previous version of the specification.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The field description of the IAB-DU Cell Resource Configuration-Mode-Info IE is misleading.
reasonForChange:
In R16 IAB, the GNB-DU RESOURCE CONFIGURATION message is used by a gNB-CU to provide the resource configuration to an IAB-DU, including DU cell resource configuration of an IAB-DU and/or its child node. In R17 IAB, the GNB-DU RESOURCE CONFIGURATION message is enhanced to provide DU cell resource configuration of an IAB-DU’s neighbor gNB-DU’s cell or peer parent-node’s cell. And the IAB-DU Cell Resource Configuration-Mode-Info IE is introduced in R17 to provide the DU cell resource configuration for all the four cases, i.e. for an IAB-DU cell or its child node’s cell or neighbor gNB-DU’s cell or peer parent-node’s cell. 
However, the field description for the IAB-DU Cell Resource Configuration-Mode-Info IE only covers the two cases introduced in R17, i.e. indicates DU cell resource configuration for neighbor gNB-DU’s cell or peer parent-node’s cell. In other words, the case of the IAB-DU Cell Resource Configuration-Mode-Info IE indicates the DU cell resource configuration for an IAB-DU and/or its child node is missing.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that the IAB-DU Cell Resource Configuration-Mode-Info IE can indicate DU cell resource configuration of the gNB-DU cell.
Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has no impact on the functional point of view.
title: Clarification on gNB-DU Cell Resource Configuration for IAB

consequencesIfNotApproved: Errors remain in E1AP: RESOURCE STATUS REQUEST message.
reasonForChange:
In R3-204502, the resource status report related procedures were introduced, but the Assigned Criticality of the Registration Request IE and Reporting Periodicity IE were not aligned in tabular and asn.1.
Considering of the functionality, and aligned with XnAP and F1AP, it is better to use criticality reject for the Registration Request IE, and use criticality ignore for the Reporting Periodicity IE.

It is also noticed that the Report Characteristics IE was defined as Size 32 in the tabular but 36 in the asn.1. Although in XnAP and F1AP the similar IE is defined as size 32, considering of backward compatibility, it is better to change the tabular to align with asn.1.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Cannot support RRC_INACTIVE in case of ng-eNB-CU-CP and ng-eNB-CU-UP split architecture.
reasonForChange:
Since Rel-17, the E1 specification is updated to support the interconnecting an eNB-CP and an eNB-UP of an eNB within an E-UTRAN, or for interconnecting an ng-eNB-CU-CP and an ng-eNB-CU-UP of an ng-eNB within an NG-RAN.

As defined in TS 36.300:
E-UTRA connected to 5GC additionally supports RRC_INACTIVE state, which has the same characteristics as RRC_INACTIVE of NR connected to 5GC, as specified in TS 38.300 [79].
As defined in TS 38.401 Section 8.9.6.1, during the procedure for changing the UE state from RRC-connected to RRC-inactive, and the step5 says:
The gNB-CU-CP sends BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message with a Bearer Context Status Change to the gNB-CU-UP, which indicates that the UE is entering RRC-inactive state. The gNB-CU-CP keeps the F1 UL TEIDs.

With the above statements, it can be understood that the Bearer Context Status Change IE should also be applicable in case of interconnecting an ng-eNB-CU-CP and an ng-eNB-CU-UP of an ng-eNB. But in current E1AP specific, it was wrongly marked as not applicable.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment remains between TS 38.413 and TS 23.502.
reasonForChange:
There is a misalignment between TS 38.413 and TS 23.502 related to UE context Release.
In TS 38.413, Chapter 8.3.2.2, it states:
Interactions with UE Context Release procedure:
The UE Context Release procedure should be initiated upon reception of a UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message. 
In TS 23.502, from later release in Rel-16, it states in chapter 4.2.6:
If N2 Context Release Request cause indicates the release is requested due to user inactivity or AS RAI then the AMF continues with the AN Release procedure unless the AMF is aware of pending MT traffic or signalling.

There is a misalignment between the two specifications: after the NG-RAN node has initiated UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST due to e.g. Inactivity, the NG-RAN node according to TS 38.413 awaits for the UE Context Release, but AMF observes the DL data and signaling and may initiate e.g. PDU session setup procedure or SMS.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 27/11/2023. Original source : Ericsson, China Telecom, ZTE, Verizon Wireless, China Unicom, CATT, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, Lenovo
summaryOfChange:
Update the 8.3.2.2 to specify that the UE Context Release procedure is initiated:
when the release cause is not user inactive, 
when the release cause is user inactive, and there is no pending downlink signaling.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).

The CR is backwards compatible.
title: Solving Misalignment in UE Context Release procedure

consequencesIfNotApproved: Source NG-RAN node incorrectly considers target NG-RAN node support CHO with Time-based Trigger Condition, and cause problems to other CHO related procedures.
reasonForChange:
In current NGAP and XnAP, the Assigned Criticality for the new timing information IE is “ignore”. This is different to the Assigned Criticality of other conditional HO related IEs (e.g., Conditional Handover Information Request IE) that is set to “reject”. 

By current Assigned Criticality “ignore”, source NG-RAN node incorrectly considers a non-supporting target NG-RAN node support CHO with Time-based trigger condition. This cause problem later, when the source NG-RAN node initiates other CHO related procedure, e.g. cancel the CHO, or initiate early status transfer procedure, etc. 

The Assigned Criticality should be “reject” to allow a non-supporting target NG-RAN node reject the CHO with Time-based Trigger Condition.

Similar issue also applies to IoT NTN.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The mobile TRP location information may not be reported to the LMF, so that the UE location may not be correctly calculated.
reasonForChange:
For acquiring the mobile TRP’s location information to calculate the UE location, the Mobile TRP Location Information IE is reported from the NG-RAN node to the LMF in the TRP Information IE and some measurement result report IEs, i.e., E-CID Measurement Result IE and TRP Measurement Result IE. 
According to the current spec, the Mobile TRP Location Information IE contains three child IEs: Location Information, Velocity Information, and Location Time Stamp, which are all optional. In TS38.473, the Location information is mandatory in the Mobile TRP Location Information IE. So there is misalignment for the IE design in the two specifications. We tend to think the “Location information” should be set as mandatory, for the following two reasons:
The Mobile TRP Location Information IE is designed to transfer at least the location information, which should not be optional. 
Moreover, if all the child IEs of the Mobile TRP Location Information IE are optional, it looks possible that the content of the parent IE will be nothing, such abnormal case should be avoided.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 2/19/2024. Original source : Huawei
summaryOfChange:
Change the presence of the “Location Information” IE in the “Mobile TRP Location Information” IE to “Mandatory” in the tabular and ASN.1.

Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has impact on the functional point of view, which will impact the mobile TRP location information report.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The UL packets sends by IAB-node may be dropped by the IAB-donor-DU, in case the IAB-node obtains IP address from OAM.
reasonForChange:
In Rel-16, considering that the source IP address filtering may be deployed at the IAB-donor-DU as well as the transport network nodes, the IAB-node should determine which source IP address to be used based on the UL mapping. The suitable procedure is: the IAB-node first obtains the target donor-DU’s BAP routing ID according to the UL mapping, and then select the IP address anchored on that donor-DU. This procedure requires the IAB-node knows the mapping between the IP address and the BAP address of the corresponding donor-DU. 
The IAB-node may obtain IP address(es) either from the IAB-donor or from the OAM system. For the donor-based IP allocation, the donor-CU sends the IP address(es) to the IAB-node together with the BAP address of the corresponding donor-DU. 
However, for the OAM-based IP allocation, the OAM has no idea of the donor-DU’s BAP address, causing the IAB-node cannot obtain the mapping between the IP address and the BAP address of donor-DU. The source IP address cannot be selected properly for UL traffic. In the worst case, some UL packets without proper source IP address may be dropped by the donor-DU in case the source IP filtering is configured.
To solve this issue, it is important to describe that the IAB-donor-CU and the IAB-node should know the mapping between donor DU’s BAP address and the IP address allocated to the IAB-node, because the DL mapping which includes the IAB node’s IP address is configured to the corresponding donor DU by the IAB-donor-CU, and the IAB-node should select proper source IP address for UL traffic. How to achieve this can be left to implementation.
summaryOfChange:
Add a sentence in the section of IP address allocation for IAB-node, to indicate that in case the IAB-node obtaining IP address from OAM, the IAB-donor-CU and IAB-node should know the mapping between the BAP address of the donor-DU and the IP address, by implementation. 
Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has impact on the functional point of view, will impact the OAM based IAB IP address allocation procedure.
title: Correction on IP address allocation for IAB via OAM

In R18 TEI, RAN2 feedback in R2-2313759 that it was agreed that a resume indication can be provided in RRCRelease message to terminate SDT and trigger UE to initiate another RRC resume procedure to transit to RRC CONNECTED state, in case the non-SDT data arrival or large size SDT data arrival during the ongoing SDT without anchor relocation, as specified in TS 38.331： 

resumeIndication
Indicates that the UE shall trigger the RRC connection resume procedure after receiving this RRCRelease message, as specified in clause 5.3.8.3. The network only includes this field in the RRCRelease message used to terminate an ongoing SDT procedure.

However, the above is not reflected in the RAN3 defined SDT call flows in TS 38.401. With this, the gNB does not have to move the UE to RRC_Inactive in the related scenarios, but in current spec, the gNB has to move the UE to RRC_Inactive or RRC_Idle.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 4/28/2024. Original source : Huawei, Qualcomm Incorporated, Lenovo, ZTE, LG Electronics, Samsung
summaryOfChange: Capture RRCRelease message with resume indication in the stage 2 procedures for SDT without anchor relocation.
title: SDT RRC Release with resume indication [SDT_ReleaseEnh]

reasonForChange: In the mobile IAB-MT migration procedure introduced in 8.23.1, step 2 refers to the step 15 of IAB-MT migration, where the gNB-DU Configuration Update procedure is described in this step to transfer the new TNL information for the F1 transmission on the target path. In fact, the F1AP procedure in step 3 also use the gNB-DU Configuration Update procedure. So, step 2 and step 3 can be performed using same F1AP procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Overall UL SDT procedure is incomplete to support the MT Communication Handling for the UE in RRC_INACTIVE with eDRX cycle longer than 10.24 seconds.
reasonForChange:
For the UE in RRC_inactive with eDRX cycle longer than 10.24 seconds, CN based MT communication handling procedure is specified in SA2. As specified in TS 23.502, i.e., 4.8.2.2 UE Triggered Connection Resume in RRC_INACTIVE procedure.

4a.	[Conditional] N2 Path switch procedure.
	If the accessed NG-RAN is able to retrieve the UE Context, the accessed NG-RAN node initiates N2 Path Switch procedure, i.e. steps 1 to 8 of clause 4.9.1.2.2 and including Xn data forwarding.
	If the Connection Resume procedure is a response to RAN paging which is triggered by 5GC due to an N2 interface procedure, NG-RAN and 5GC handle the N2 interface procedure as a collision described in clause 4.9.1.2.
	If Connection Inactive procedure with CN based MT communication handling (see clause 4.8.1.1a) has been performed previously then when the path switch procedure is performed downlink data or signalling delivery is triggered, if there is any.

So, in case of anchor relocation, if MT communication handling is already activated, the receiving gNB shall deactivate it by sending Path switch request message to the AMF.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 5/10/2024. Original source : ZTE, Qualcomm, CATT, China Telecom, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, Ericsson, Huawei, Xiaomi
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that in case of anchor relocation, If MT communication handling is already activated, the receiving gNB shall deactivate it by sending Path switch request message to the AMF.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it clarified the UL SDT procedure combined with MT communication handling.

consequencesIfNotApproved: CU encodes the SIB23 which violate current sidelink design.
reasonForChange:
To support Sidelink positioning, a new SIB23 is introduced to provide cell level sidelink positioning configuration.
According to agreements in RAN3 106/107e, sidelink related configuration(SIB12,13,14) should be generated by DU. However, current specification requires CU to encode the SIB23, which is not aligned with current sidelink principle:


Moreover, if sidelink positioning resources is configured by CU, then DU needs to know the corresponding configuration for sidelink positioning resource scheduling. However, we do not have corresponding signaling exchange in F1 interface for both sidelink and sidelink positioning. Therefore, SIB23 should be encoded by DU.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The current textual description of early data forwarding and DL discarding for CHO is not clear.

“For each DRB in the DRBs Subject To Early Status Transfer List IE for which the DISCARD DL COUNT Value IE is received in the EARLY STATUS TRANSFER message, the target NG-RAN node does not transmit forwarded downlink SDUs to the UE whose COUNT is less than the provided and discards them if transmission has not been attempted.”
“For each DRB in the DRBs Subject To Early Status Transfer List IE, the source M-NG-RAN node shall forward to the target, the value of the received FIRST DL COUNT Value IE or DISCARD DL COUNT Value IE.”
According to the IE table in 9.1.1.14, the DISCARD DL COUNT Value IE is included in the DRBs Subject To DL Discarding List rather than the DRBs Subject To Early Status Transfer List.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Unnecessary protocol limitation.
reasonForChange:
Based on functions specified in TS 38.300 (16.10.5.2) and corresponding RRC protocol support in TS 38.331, a gNB is able to configure UEs with PTM configuration via the RRCRelease message, and UE is able to apply the configuration upon session activation (e.g., through enhanced group paging). Information necessary for this “pre-configuration” is partly provided by the gNB-DU and may be updated by gNB-DU through Multicast Context Notification.

However in current specification, there is a restriction on when this procedure can be applied, i.e., only “during an active multicast MBS session”, which is not necessary.

Given the above mentioned specificaton status in TSs 38.300 and 38.331, there is no need to for such limitation in F1AP, i.e., network should be able to configure UE with the latest configuration, e.g., whenever network finds the previous pre-configuration is not valid anymore, besides, it is probably more adviseable to not perform such configuration change during an active multicast session.
summaryOfChange:
Remove the restriction on when Multicast Context Notification applies (currently limited to active session only).

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
title: Correction on configuration update for an inactive Multicast session

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is gap between RAN2 and RAN3 specs on the understanding of the SRB0/1 relaying Uu Relay RLC channel configuration. SRB0/1 relaying Uu Relay RLC channel may be configured during F1 UE context setup procedure, which is not reasonable.
reasonForChange:
In RAN2 spec TS 38.300, it specifies that Uu Relay RLC channel for Remote UE’s SRB0 relaying is configured after Relay UE’s RRC connection establishment procedure and sending SUI to gNB. However, in RAN3 specs TS 38.401 and TS 38.473, it specifies that it is possible to configure Uu Relay RLC channel for Remote UE’s SRB0/1 relaying during Relay UE’s F1 UE context setup procedure and before sending SUI to gNB. There is gap between RAN2 and RAN3 specs on the understanding of the timing for Uu Relay RLC channel setup for SRB0/1 relaying.

Since there is no relay related indication during relay UE RRC connection setup, the gNB-CU does not know the UE is a relay UE or whether the UE is capable of L2 U2N relay UE operation, it is not reasonable to configure the Uu Relay RLC channel during F1 UE context setup procedure. In addition, it is not reasonable for gNB to configure Uu Relay RLC channel before getting knowledge of the capability of the UE (i.e. receiving relayUE-Operation-L2-r17 in UECapabilityInformation from UE). What’s more, the Uu Relay RLC channel will only be used after bearer mapping is configured, and bearer mapping can be configured after relay UE sending SUI including remote UE’s L2 ID to gNB. So there is no benefits to configure the Uu Relay RLC channel in advance. 

Based on the discussion above, it is suggested that Uu Relay RLC channel is not configured during F1 UE context setup procedure.

Since there is a “NOTE 1” in step 15 in Figure 8.19.1-1 to clarify the SRB1 relaying Uu Relay RLC channel (step 15) may be performed earlier via steps 5~8, the “SRB1” can be removed from steps 5/7/8.
summaryOfChange:
In 8.19.1, remove “gNB may configure the U2N Relay UE with Uu Relay RLC channel(s) for relaying of U2N Remote UE’s SRB0/1” in step 3.
Remove the “SRB1” from steps 5/7/8.


Impact analysis

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the L2 U2N relay operation.
title: Corrections on Uu Relay RLC channel configuration

reasonForChange:

reasonForChange:
The procedure code for PosSystemInformationDeliveryCommand is different in different releases of the specification:

gi0: ProcedureCode ::= 59

We usually align the procedure code between releases to allow for interworking between releases. The procedure code was added in CR1059r3 for version 16.12.0 of the specification (2022-12). Procedure code 59 is used by id-BroadcastContextSetup in Rel-17 and Rel-18.

The CR is Non-Backward Compatible (NBC).
title: Aligning procedure code between releases

consequencesIfNotApproved: different coding interpretation in gNB and AMF leads to failure e.g. AMF encodes modulo 12 bits and gNB decides UE based subgrouping using modulo 15 bits.
reasonForChange:
TS 38.304 section 7.1 has two possible encodings for UE_ID.
If eDRX is being used, UE_ID should be 5G-S-TMSI mod 4096 per section 7.1 in 38.304 for proper calculation of PF & PO
If PEIPS is being used, UE-ID should be 5G-S-TMSI mod 32768 (when eDRX is used) or 8192 (when eDRX is not used) per section 7.3.2 in 38.304.
This UE_ID is assumed to be sent in the Extended UE identity index value IE in the NGAP Core Network Assistance Information for RRC Inactive IE because it has more than 10 bits. In the first case it means 12 bits in the second case it means 15 bits or 13bits. This means three possible encoding ways are possible:

Coding 1: the AMF always encodes with a modulo of 16 bits and the gNB is in charge of taking a further modulo of 12 bits, 13 bits or 15 bits depending if it is eDRX or PEIPS case.
Coding 2: the AMF always encodes with a modulo of 15 bits (i.e. the leftmost bit is set at zero) and the gNB is in charge of taking a further modulo of 12 bits, 13 bits or take the 15 bits depending if it is eDRX or PEIPS case. In the current release this is enough as there is no use case using 16 bits and it allows to minimize the number of bits of S-TMSI disclosed over the interface.
Coding 3: the AMF encodes a modulo of 12 bits, 13bits or 15 bits depending if it is eDRX or PEIPS case (i.e. leftmost bits set at zero).
TS 38.304 doesn’t help to decide between these three interpretations because it does not specify the CN-RAN interface encoding part.
summaryOfChange:
The encoding of the Extended UE Identity index value when used for eDRX and when used for PEIPS is clarified according to coding 1.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has an impact on the core network assistance information function.
title: Correction of Extended UE Identity Index Value

consequencesIfNotApproved: The (e)RedCap and 2RX XR UEs cannot make emergency calls in a cell where access for these UE are enabled but these UEs with 1Rx or 2Rx branches are barred.
reasonForChange:
In the RAN2 #125bis meeting, RAN2 sent an LS R3-243012 to RAN3, to introduce a mechanism to allow RedCap UEs to have access to the cell to make an emergency call or receive emergency information broadcast.
However, in the RAN2 #126 meeting, RAN2 re-discussed this mechanism and decided to use a common solution for (e)RedCap and 2RX XR UEs.
Agreements
1	NES (i.e. ingoring MIB barring) will not be considered in our common solution discussion.  FFS if anything specific for NES will need to be done.  If anything needs to be done, it would not be part of the common solution.
2	For Rel-18, we introduce 1 bit that enables EM call for RedCap, eRedCap, and 2Rx XR. One RRC Rel-18 with magic sentence that it is early implementable in Rel-17.  A CR for 38.304 doesn’t need to have the magic sentence. 
3	This replaces the previous agreement and we will notify RAN3 verbally via delegates

Based on the above RAN2 agreement, the endorsed CRs included in the LS R3-243012 are withdrawn, and a set of new RAN2 CRs are agreed in R2-2405956, R2-2405957 and R2-2405958.
So that, RAN3 shall enhance TS38.423 and TS38.473 accordingly.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The stage 2 description of mobile IAB node authorization is incorrect and incomplete.
reasonForChange:
it is specified that “During the mobile IAB-MT migration procedure and the mobile IAB-node RLF recovery procedure, the target/new RRC-terminating IAB-donor-CU receives the authorization status of the mobile IAB-node from the source/initial RRC-terminating IAB-donor-CU as well as from the 5GC during Path Switch Request procedure. ”. As we know, the mobile IAB-MT migration procedure comprises mobile IAB-MT migration via NG handover and mobile IAB-MT migration via Xn handover as captured in clause 8.23.1 and clause 8.23.2 respectively. So the above sentence is incorrect since it only applies to the mobile IAB-MT migration via Xn handover case. 
For a mobile IAB-node, the IAB donor-CU receives the authorizations from 5GC or from another IAB donor CU, when the authorization status is received for the first time and “not authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU neither establishes the backhaul resources nor allocates any BAP address, TNL address or default BAP configuration for this mobile IAB-node. However, when the authorization status is not received for the first time, different action shall be taken, e.g. the IAB-donor-CU attempts to hand over the UEs served by the mobile IAB-node to other cell(s), releases the F1 interface towards the mobile IAB-DU, and releases all backhaul resources (including the BAP address, TNL address and default BAP configuration) for this mobile IAB-node. As we can see, different actions are taken by the IAB donor CU for the two cases. However, the two cases when the authorization status is received are not distinguished in the current description in 38.401.
summaryOfChange:
Add “ via Xn handover ” to clarify that during the mobile IAB-MT migration via Xn handover procedure, the target/new RRC-terminating IAB-donor-CU receives the authorization status of the mobile IAB-node from the source/initial RRC-terminating IAB-donor-CU as well as from the 5GC during Path Switch Request procedure. 
Clarify that if the authorization status is received for the first time and the status is “not authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU neither establishes the backhaul resources nor allocates any BAP address, TNL address or default BAP configuration for this mobile IAB-node.  

Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has impact on the functional point of view, the impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the mobile IAB-node authorization.
title: Correction on mobile IAB-node authorization
