In case of SDT without UE context relocation, upon receicing the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT REQUEST from the receiving gNB, the last serving gNB decides to keep the UE context, it will trigger a nested Partial UE Context Transfer procedure, to provide partial UE context including the SDT related RLC context, and once the last serving gNB decides to terminate the SDT, it responds to the receiving gNB with the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT FAILURE message.
That is to say, the unsuccessful operation of the Retrieve UE Context procedure also happens in case of SDT without UE context relocation case, in which the last serving gNB provides partial UE context to the last serving gNB.

Add in the unsuccessful operation of the Retrieve UE Context procedure an Interaction paragraph with the Partial UE Context Transfer procedure to describe the case of SDT without UE context relocation in which partial UE context is provided to the new NG-RAN node.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
- The SN behavior procedure text is missing for the Security Indication IE contained in the PDU Session Resource Modification Info - SN terminated IE of the SN modification request message.
- The SN behavior procedure text is inconsistent in different release and not future proof for subsequent updates (e.g. ng-eNB support of UP integrity protection).
reasonForChange:
There is procedure text to specify SN behavior when the SN or the MN is an ng-eNB and the Integrity Protection Indication IE contained in the Security Indication IE is set to “required” or “preferred” in the PDU Session Resource Setup Info - SN terminated IE in the SN addition request message and the SN modification request messages.
However, there is no such procedure text for the Security Indication IE contained in the PDU Session Resource Modification Info - SN terminated IE of the SN modification request message. This absence was present since RAN3 114-bis meeting when R3-221336 and R3-221276 were agreed to add the Security Indication IE in the PDU Session Resource Modification Info - SN terminated IE in the SN modification request message. 
Thus the SN behavior procedure text needs to be added for the Security Indication IE contained in the PDU Session Resource Modification Info - SN terminated IE of the SN modification request message.
In addition, the UP security related to ng-eNB is already specified in TS 33.501 and therefore it can be referenced in this specification. This is future proof considering any update in TS 33.501.
summaryOfChange:
- Add the SN behavior procedure text for the Security Indication IE contained in the PDU Session Resource Modification Info - SN terminated IE of the SN modification request message.
- Reword the procedure text related to ng-eNB UP security and only refer to TS 33.501.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment of tabular and asn.1, errors to use DC related parameter for SDT.
reasonForChange:
In case of SDT without UE context relocation, there will be data forwarding between the anchor node and the new serving node, therefore during Partial UE Context Transfer procedure, the two NG-RAN nodes exchange their data forwarding addresses in a per SDT DRB manner.

It is noticed that in tabular part, in the Partial UE Context Information for SDT IE in the PARTIAL UE CONTEXT TRANSFER message, the UL TNL Information IE refers to “UP Transport Parameters 9.2.3.76”, but in the PARTIAL UE CONTEXT TRANSFER ACKNOWLEDGE message, the DL TNL Information IE refers to the “UP Transport Layer Information 9.2.3.30”, and in the asn.1 part, both of them refers to the “UPTransportParameters”.

Considering that DC is not applicable for SDT, both of these two UL and DL data forwarding addresses should refer to the “UP Transport Layer Information 9.2.3.30” instead of “UP Transport Parameters 9.2.3.76”.
summaryOfChange:
Change the tabular of ULTNL Information IE in Partial UE Context Information for SDT IE to refer to the “UP Transport Layer Information 9.2.3.30”.
Change the asn.1 of both uL-TNLInfo and dL-TNLInfo from “UPTransportParameters” to “UPTransportLayerInformation”.

Impact Analysis:
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification, and the change is asn.1 NBC. 
This CR only has an impact on the Partial UE Context Transfer procedure which is only to be used in case of SDT without UE context relocation.

The CR is NBC.
title: Correction on SDT Data Forwarding

consequencesIfNotApproved: It remains unclear how the CellGroupConfig is handled if it is received at the gNB-CU during SDT procedures. This could misalign with stage 2 description
reasonForChange: If the DU to CU RRC Information is received at the gNB-CU, the CellGroupConfig is mandatorily included. The CellGroupConfig is used by the gNB-CU for the RRC reconfiguration or RRC connection resume when the UE is moved to RRC_CONNECTED. However, while the DU to CU RRC Information is either mandatory or required for the UE context procedures for SDT, the CellGroupConfig is not to be used by the UE as the UE stays in RRC_INACTIVE. (In the RACH based SDT the UE Context Setup procedure is for exchanging packet transmission required configuration/information while in the CG based SDT the UE Context Modification procedure is for CG-SDT resource configuration query.)
summaryOfChange:
Add descriptions in the UE context setup procedure that, for the RACH based SDT, the CellGroupConfig is ignored by the gNB-CU and the gNB-CU does not perform RRC reconfiguration or connection resume to send the UE to RRC_CONNECTED.
Add descriptions in the UE context modification procedure that, for the CG based SDT, the CellGroupConfig is ignored by the gNB-CU and the gNB-CU does not perform RRC reconfiguration.


Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the handling of the CellGroupConfig in the DU to CU RRC Information and the related procedure text.
title: Correction to CellGroupConfig handling for SDT

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the correct notification mechanism is not enabled, use of MN-initiated conditional mobility (CHO and CPC) is difficult in case of Dual Connectivity, because of possible interactions of SN-related reconfigurations.
reasonForChange:
When MN initiated conditional reconfiguration has been prepared at UE, (inclduing CHO and MN initiated inter-SN CPC), if any SCG (conditional) configuration is executed by UE which may impact the prepared MN initiated conditional reconfiguration, the MN’s conditional reconfiguration may need to be updated or deleted. Because of that, it has been agreed that the SN must notify the MN about the SCG reconfiguration.
Depending on the situation, the notification may concern deletion of the MN-initiated conditional reconfiguration and use of SRB1 for delivery of the SCG reconfiguration.
summaryOfChange:
The notification agreed at RAN3 #117-bis, which aimed at coordinating CHO and intra-SN CPC is not sufficient. To complete the solution, the additional flags must be added to the existing notification IE to address all scenarios created in RAN2. Also, appropriate description is needed to record these scenarios correctly.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
The change modifies existing functionallity within a single IE.
title: Completion of the work on CHO-CPC coordination

For seqence length L571, the scs480 should be included. 
For sequence length L1151, the scs480 is not needed. 
And according to the TS 38.331 below, the range of the root sequence index for L1151 should be corrected.  
    prach-RootSequenceIndex-r16             CHOICE {
        <Skip the irrelevant>
        l1151                                   INTEGER (0..1149)
    }   OPTIONAL   -- Need R

This CR is NBC.

consequencesIfNotApproved: When the IAB authorized information is changed to “not authorized”, the IAB incorrectly continue its operation.
reasonForChange:
IAB’s authorization can be changed to “not authorized” during its normal operation. AMF may choose to de-register the IAB-MT (including AMF initiate the UE Context Release procedure to IAB-donor), or AMF may keep the IAB-MT registered as a normal UE (e.g. has an optional PDU session for OAM). In the later case, AMF initiates the UE Context Modification procedure to inform the IAB-donor that the IAB authorized is changed to “not authorized”. IAB-donor need to ensure the IAB’s operation is stopped, e.g. release BH RLC CH, deactivate the IAB-DU cell(s), etc. 

However, current specification only defines “the NG-RAN node shall, if supported, store the received IAB Authorization information in the UE context”, but does not define the NG-RAN node to take actions to stop the IAB operation.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify the NG-RAN node need to take actions to ensure the IAB node will not serve the UE(s). 

Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has impact under functional point of view. The NG-RAN node need to take actions to ensure the IAB node will not serve the UE(s).

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear what is the maximum length of Routing ID used in NRPPa transport message for LMF identification.
reasonForChange:
Regarding the maximum size of LMF routing ID in NRPPa transport message, CR R3-213847 tried to clarify the maximum size of Routing ID should be limited to 16 octets for inter vendor operability in its cover page. However in CR’s main body, it only clarified that the maximum length of Routing ID shall correspond to NfInstanceId defined in TS 29.571. 
Since there is no texts clearly describe that maximum size of NfInstanceId shall be 16 octets in TS 29.571, it is controversial whether the maximum size of routing ID should be limited to 16 octets. 

In LS R3-233705, CT4 informed RAN3 that the Routing ID is suggested to be encoded as UUID version 4 defined in RFC 4122.
summaryOfChange:
In semantics description of Routing ID, it is clarified as following 

The maximum length is 16 octets, referring to the length of a Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) version 4 as specified in section 4.4 in IETF RFC 4122.

Imapct analysis:
This CR has isolated impact on NRPPa transport procedure.
title: Clarification on maximum length of Routing ID

consequencesIfNotApproved: gNB is not able to determine whether all QoS flows are accepted in at least one cell, thus not able to finish the NGAP procedure.
reasonForChange:
In current spec the condition of successful Broadcast session setup on NGAP is, NG-RAN node accepts all the MBS QoS flows in the MBS session at least in one of its cell as quoted below. However, based on current F1AP spec (38473-h50), CU-CP won't be able to know whether all the successful MRB (and the QoS flow mapped into this MRB) is accepted in one cell or separate cells.
For example, for one specific DU, there are MRB1, MRB2 and MRB3. If MRB1/2 are successfully accepted by cell_1, and MRB2/3 are accepted by cell_2, DU might still report all MRB (MRB1/2/3) as successfully established in this DU. Therefore the condition defined in 38.413 (as quoted below) will be impossible to be known and really carried out by CU-CP. 
// quoted from 38413-h50.
"The AMF initiates the procedure by sending a BROADCAST SESSION SETUP REQUEST message to the NG-RAN node. If the NG-RAN node accepts all the MBS QoS flows in the MBS session at least in one of its cells, the NG-RAN node responds with the BROADCAST SESSION SETUP RESPONSE message."
summaryOfChange:
Update the condition in section 8.14.1.3 of an unsuccessful operation of Broadcast Context Setup following the unsuccessful condition of NGAP:
"If the gNB-DU is not able to establish the requested MBS session context for all the MRBs in any of its cells it shall consider the procedure as failed and reply with the BROADCAST CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message." 
Impact Analysis:
This CR is an BC CR. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the understanding for existing procedural text and ASN.1.
title: Correction on condition of successful MBS Broadcast Context Setup

consequencesIfNotApproved: If a cell supports multiple PLMN/NPNs, it is unclear how the information provided in the F1AP IAB Barred IE corresponds to information provided in the SIB1 of gNB-DU’s cell.
reasonForChange:
The IAB Barred IE is lacking a clear correspondance to information provided in the SIB1 message. In case of RAN sharing scenarios, the corresponding iab-Support as defined in TS 38.331 may correspond to more than one PLMN/NPN as it may be associated to a CellIdentifier associated with multiple PLMNs/NPNs.
See the defintion of the iab-Support and how it is encoded in RRC below:
This field combines both the support of IAB and the cell status for IAB. If the field is present, the cell supports IAB and the cell is also considered as a candidate for cell (re)selection for IAB-nodes; if the field is absent, the cell does not support IAB and/or the cell is barred for IAB-node. 
And the iab-Support in SIB1 is provided per PLMN/NPN according to TS38.331:
PLMN-IdentityInfoList information element
-- ASN1START
-- TAG-PLMN-IDENTITYINFOLIST-START

PLMN-IdentityInfoList ::=               SEQUENCE (SIZE (1..maxPLMN)) OF PLMN-IdentityInfo

PLMN-IdentityInfo ::=                   SEQUENCE {
    plmn-IdentityList                       SEQUENCE (SIZE (1..maxPLMN)) OF PLMN-Identity,
    trackingAreaCode                        TrackingAreaCode                                            OPTIONAL,       -- Need R
    ranac                                   RAN-AreaCode                                                OPTIONAL,       -- Need R
    cellIdentity                            CellIdentity,
    cellReservedForOperatorUse              ENUMERATED {reserved, notReserved},
    ...,
    [[
    iab-Support-r16                     ENUMERATED {true}                                               OPTIONAL       -- Need S
    ]],
    [[
    trackingAreaList-r17                SEQUENCE (SIZE (1..maxTAC-r17)) OF TrackingAreaCode             OPTIONAL,      -- Need R
    gNB-ID-Length-r17                   INTEGER (22..32)                                                OPTIONAL       -- Need R
    ]]
}
-- TAG-PLMN-IDENTITYINFOLIST-STOP
-- ASN1STOP
summaryOfChange:
Include semantics description for the IAB Barred IE in the tabular of the GNB-CU CONFIGURATION UPDATE message.

This CR has impact on the functional specification of the IAB Barred IE provided from CU to DU. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the configuration of a cell with IAB Barred information.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Deadlock can happen between NG-RAN node and 5GC nodes in multi-vendor scenario.
reasonForChange:
Race condition can happen between SMF/AMF triggering the NGAP PDU Session Resource Setup/Modification procedure and NG-RAN node triggering the NGAP PDU session Resource Modify Indication procedure.
Not specifying this interaction can lead to a deadlock in multi-vendor case and similar interaction was therefore specified in LTE:
8.2.4           E-RAB Modification Indication
Interactions with E-RAB Setup procedure or E-RAB Modify procedure:
If the E-RAB MODIFICATION INDICATION message is received by the MME during an ongoing E-RAB Setup procedure or an ongoing E-RAB Modify procedure, the MME shall proceed with the E-RAB Modification Indication procedure.
However, this interaction is unspecified in 5G and also involve two different 5GC nodes AMF and SMF.
summaryOfChange:
The interaction between PDU Session Resource Setup/Modification procedure and PDU Session Modify Indication procedure is specified.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the PDU session Resource modification and PDU session modify indication functions.
title: Correction of Interaction with PDU Session Resource Indication

abstract: Related to incoming LS in R3-240022
consequencesIfNotApproved: Incorrect reference for TL Containers during PDU session release.
reasonForChange:
An LS from SA2 in R3-240022 indicates that “SA2 has not described the TL-Container in PDU Session Release as there is no Stage 2 parameter that is required during the release.”

This means that only CT4’s stage 3 specification (TS 29.585 clauses 5.2.2.2 & 7.3.3.1) describes Set Request in TL Containers during PDU session release. Note that the same CT4 specification also describes TL-Containers during PDU session establishment (clause 5.2.1.1) and PDU session modification (clause 5.2.2.1).
summaryOfChange:
§8.2.2: In the procedural text for PDU Session Resource Release, the references to TS 23.501 for the Downlink TL Container IE and Uplink TL Container IE are changed to TS 29.585 since the SA2 LS indicates there is no stage 2 level description in TS 23.501.
§8.2.1.2, 8.2.3.2: For consistency, the same changes are made in the procedural text for PDU Session Resource Setup and PDU Session Resource Modification.
title: Correction for procedural text of TL Containers

consequencesIfNotApproved: Incorrect behavior in a gNB-DU that does not support Multi-path.
reasonForChange:
The Assigned Criticality for the Path Addition Information IE is “ignore”. This can cause issue to a gNB-DU that does not support the SL Relay Multi-path. The gNB-DU may just ignore the Path Addition Information IE, and incorrectly treat the UE directly connected with the gNB-DU. 

The Assigned Criticality should be changed to “reject” to allow a non-supporting gNB-DU reject the UE Context Setup/Modification procedure.

summaryOfChange: Change the Assigned Criticality for Path Addition Information IE to “reject”
title: Correction on the Assigned Criticality for SL Relay related IE

consequencesIfNotApproved: The incorrect description where AMF cannot use the reporting status IE to deduce whether ECN marking at NG-RAN or reporting information for ECN marking at UPF or congestion information reporting is active or not active.
reasonForChange: In previous discussion, RAN3 agreed to introduce ECN Marking or Congestion Information Reporting Status IE to indicate whether ECN marking at NG-RAN or reporting information for ECN marking at UPF or congestion information reporting is active or not active. The reporting status IE is included in PDU Session Resource Setup Response Transfer IE or PDU Session Resource Modify Response Transfer IE which is transparent to AMF, thus SMF is the right node uses the IE to deduce the status of activation. Also, currently there is no reference in TS 23.501 to describe how to use the ECN Marking or Congestion Information Reporting Status IE, it is better to remove this description.
summaryOfChange:
1. When the ECN Marking or Congestion Information Reporting Status IE is received, replace the receiving entity from AMF by SMF.
2. Remove the description on “as described in TS 23.501”.
title: Correction on the behavior description of ECN Marking or Congestion Information Reporting over NGAP

consequencesIfNotApproved: The description of primary source events remains unclear/inaccurate.
reasonForChange:
RAN TSS reports are triggered when the gNB-DU detects a primary source event. However, the description of “event c)” is not entirely clear/accurate:
The wording “event a) occurred and b) has not yet been reached” is intended to mean that event b) has not yet been reached for every attribute for which event a) has occurred.
Periodic reporting is not an event, and it seems overly restrictive to require that reports are sent periodically even when no RAN TSS attribute values have changed (this should be left to implementation).
summaryOfChange:
To avoid possible misinterpration of “event a) occurred and b) has not yet been reached”, it is clarified that it is for a (particular) RAN TSS attribute.
Rather than requiring time-triggered reports to be sent at periodic intervals, it is softened to “implementation-dependent time interval” (e.g. gNB-DU implementation may skip a report if no RAN TSS attribute values have changed).
title: Clarification of primary source event

consequencesIfNotApproved: The direct data forwarding from the source MN to the target SN can’t be supported in NR-DC to NR-DC handover.
reasonForChange:
RAN3 has agreed to support direct data forwarding at the DC to DC handover and CHO with DC. The following text has been captured in TS37.340:
In case of NR-DC to NR-DC handover, direct data forwarding from source SN to target MN, from source SN to target SN and from source MN to target SN is supported.
The target SN determines whether there is a direct forwarding path between the target SN and the source MN based on the source MN node ID. However, in the S-NODE ADDITION REQUEST message, a Source M-NG-RAN node ID IE is provided in the CHO Information SN Addition IE, which is present only when the S-NG-RAN node Addition Preparation procedure is triggered as part of a conditional handover.
Therefore, a new IE “The source MN node ID” should be introduced in the S-NODE ADDITION REQUEST message for the target SN to determine whether there is a direct path between the target SN and the source MN in case of NR-DC to NR-DC handover.

consequencesIfNotApproved: RAN TSS reporting may not operate as expected when there are multiple requesting TSCTSFs.
reasonForChange:
SA2 has agreed that multiple TSCTSF can request RAN TSS information. Therefore, the TSS-related messages include a Routing ID IE which identifies the requesting TSCTSF.

This means that there can be parallel TSS reporting procedures, each concerning a different TSCTSF. However, the current procedural text is unclear whether e.g. a "stop" request stops all RAN TSS reporting or only reporting for a specific TSCTSF.
summaryOfChange:
It is clarified that TSS-related procedures over NG interface are performed per TSCTSF:
In the Timing Synchronisation Status procedure, a “start” or “stop” request is for the TSCTSF indicated by the Routing ID IE.
In the Timing Synchronisation Status Report procedure, a report is for the TSCTSF indicated by the Routing ID IE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The AMF may not know whether it is proper time to initiate de-registration for  an unauthorized IAB-node.
reasonForChange:
At the RAN3#122 meeting, as a part of mIAB-node authorization handling, RAN3 agreed that the mIAB-MT’s donor can indicate to the AMF that the unauthorized mIAB-MT can be de-registered. At the RAN3#123 meeting, RAN3 specified authorization handling for IAB-nodes, and made the following agreements related to de-registration handling:
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the RAN node serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After RAN node serving the IAB-MT is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the AMF that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting. 
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the eNB serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After the eNB serving the IAB-MT in EN-DC is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the MME that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
Based on the above, RAN3 should specify NGAP signalling to support the 2nd  agreement above.

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).

title: Correction on IAB-node de-registration handling

consequencesIfNotApproved: De-registration handling for an IAB-MT in NR-DC is not supported.
reasonForChange:
At the RAN3#122 meeting, as a part of mIAB-node authorization handling, RAN3 agreed that the mIAB-MT’s donor can indicate to the AMF that the unauthorized mIAB-MT can be de-registered. At the RAN3#123 meeting, RAN3 specified authorization handling for IAB-nodes, and made the following agreements related to de-registration handling:
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the RAN node serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After RAN node serving the IAB-MT is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the AMF that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting. 
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the eNB serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After the eNB serving the IAB-MT in EN-DC is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the MME that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
Based on the above, RAN3 should specify XnAP signalling to support the 1st  agreement above.
After the MN of the IAB-node receives the updated “IAB-node not authorized” status indication from the AMF, it will send the updated status to the IAB-donor-CU acting as the SN of the IAB-node. After the SN has completed the handling of the unauthorized IAB-node, it can send the S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUIRED message or the S-NODE RELEASE REQUIRED message towards the MN, to indicate that the handling has been completed. Then, the MN can inform the AMF accordingly.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Some sub-feature for QMC in NR-DC is not fully supported.
reasonForChange:
RAN2 has defined a session status information in the QoE report to indicate whether the application layer session has started or stopped. However, if the QoE report is received over the non QoE configuring node, the QoE configuring node cannot obtain the session status information according to the current spec. As a consequence, the QoE configuring node has no clue on whether to release the QoE/RVQoE configurations even if the application session has stopped.
Moreover, there was comment that if the QoE configuring node would like to understand the session status while the QoE report is received over non QoE configuring node, the QoE configuring node can instead request to receive the QoE report over QoE configuring node in order to obtain the session status. However, such mechanism brings more complexity on coordination, considering the fact that the QoE configuring node only needs to know the application layer session status.
Therefore, transferring the application layer session status is needed.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The IE is completely missing from the tabular which is inconsistent with the ASN.1 in the NG-RAN Node Configuration Update procedure.
reasonForChange:
In the NG-RAN node configuration update message, the Served Cell Specific Info Request IE can be used to request the additional MTC configuration.  
However, in ASN.1 the NG-RAN Configuration Update Acknowledge message may include served-NR-Cells, which includes also the ServedCellSpecificInfoReq-NR. This leads to the misalignment between the ASN.1 and the Tabular. And it should be understood that the IE should not be signalled in the acknowledge message, given that there are no corresponding procedure texts. 

Also, in the ASN.1 of the NG-RAN Configuration Update message, the ServedCellSpecificInfoReq-NR can be included in two places: 
under the top level of the gNB branch 
the Served Cells To Update NR IE. 
For the latter case, this is because the ServedCellsToUpdate-NR includes the served-Cells-ToAdd-NR referring to the ServedCells-NR, which includes the ServedCellSpecificInfoReq-NR. But this IE is missing under the Served Cells To Update NR IE in the Tabular.
summaryOfChange:
In the NG-RAN Node Configuration Update Message, add the Served Cell Specific Info Request IE under the 9.2.2.15 Served Cells To Update NR IE. 
In the NG-RAN Node Configuration Update Acknowledge message, add the Served Cell Specific Info Request IE under Served NR Cells IE. 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it impacts on the Served Cell Specific Info Request in NG-RAN Node Configuration Update procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved: gNB-CU behavior for handling Early Synch Information is unclear.
reasonForChange: RAN3 has agreed to introduce the Early Sync Information IE in both the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE messages. Once received from gNB-DU, gNB-CU shall consider it as the generated early sync information from the accepted candidate cell in the candidate gNB-DU. Currently the procedural text for the behaviour of gNB-CU when it receives the Early UL Sync Configuration IE or the Early UL Sync Configuration for SUL IE in UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE message is not specified.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The stage 2 description of IAB node authorization is incorrect and incomplete.
reasonForChange:
For an IAB-node, the IAB donor-CU receives the authorizations from 5GC or from another IAB donor CU, when the authorization status is received for the first time and “not authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU neither establishes the backhaul resources nor allocates any BAP address, TNL address or default BAP configuration for this IAB-node. However, when the authorization status is not received for the first time, different action shall be taken, e.g. the IAB-donor-CU attempts to hand over the UEs served by the IAB-node to other cell(s), releases the F1 interface towards the IAB-DU, and releases all backhaul resources (including the BAP address, TNL address and default BAP configuration) for this IAB-node. As we can see, different actions are taken by the IAB donor CU for the two cases. However, the two cases when the authorization status is received are not distinguished in the current description in 38.401.
The current description for the case when MT is dual-connected with two donors is incomplete and incorrect. Based on current specification, when the IAB-MT is NR dual-connected, two cases are described separately, i.e. case 1: the non-F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU is the MN, case 2: the F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU is the MN.  
For case 2 (i.e. the MN is the F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU), it’s specified “upon reception of the authorization status, the IAB-node’s authorization procedure follows the same steps as described in clause 8.9.17.2.1.”. However, clause 8.9.17.2 and even 8.9.17.1 which is referred by clause 8.9.17.2 only describes the case when IAB-node connects to a single IAB-donor wherein some step (e.g., F1-terminating donor informing the non-F1 terminating donor that the corresponding operation (e.g. handover of UEs) has completed) is missing. Actually, these operations applies to all scenarios when the IAB node is served by two IAB-donors, not only to part of scenarios as described currently in 38.401.  
It’s impossible for an IAB-node to connect with a gNB incapable of serving the IAB-MT. Thus, it’s not correct to use the term “non-IAB-capable gNB” in clause 8.9.17.2.2.
For the scenario of NR-DC with single IAB-donor, it is not appropriate to say the MN/SN is the IAB-donor-CU since the MN/SN comprises both CU and DU functionality.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that if the authorization status is received for the first time and the status is “not authorized”, the IAB-donor-CU neither establishes the backhaul resources nor allocates any BAP address, TNL address or default BAP configuration for this IAB-node. 
Update the description for the case when the IAB-MT is NR dual-connected with two IAB-donors.
Remove the term “non-IAB-capable” in clause 8.9.17.2.2.
Replace “IAB-donor-CU” with “IAB-donor” in IAB authorization chapters.
 
Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has impact on the functional point of view, the impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the IAB node authorization.
title: Correction of IAB-node authorization

consequencesIfNotApproved: UE contexts for RRC connected UE are erroneously deleted POSITIONING SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY procedure.
reasonForChange:
In the previous RAN3#118 meeting, it was agreed in R3-226395 to update the procedural text for the SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND as follows: 
“Upon reception of the SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND message, the gNB-DU shall broadcast the requested Other SI, and if the UE corresponding to the confirmed UE ID IE is not in RRC connected state, delete the UE context corresponding to the confirmed UE ID IE, if any.”
The intention is to clarify that the UE context corresponding to the Confirmed UE ID IE, can be deleted by the DU, only for idle or inactive UEs (i.e. the deletion of the UE context is not applicable for connected UE).
However, the same issue still exists in the POSITIONING SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY message. It is proposed to update the procedural text for the POSITIONING SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY message to indicate that when the UE is not in RRC connected state, the UE context can be deleted.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Ambiguity concerning usage of the IE.
reasonForChange:
In the XnAP (and in NGAP), the description of UE History Information refers to “active state”. This is a description copied from X2AP, where it was added already in Rel-8. At the time, the LTE RRC had two possible states: RRC_IDLE and RRC_CONNECTED. Thus, the “active state” was clear. However, in NR, the term may be ambiguous: RRC has two states where UE may be “active”, the RRC_CONNECTED and the RRC_INACTIVE. The name of the latter suggests the UE is not “active”, but if looked at from the CN perspective, the CM-CONNECTED does include RRC_INACTIVE. Also, the RRC_INACTIVE, in some scenarios (when UE is “active”) does enable tracing cells that the UE uses. Thus, it may be unclear when exatly the UE History Information is to be collected.
The original purpose of the UE History Information was to enable tracing ping-pong handovers. Thus, it can safely be assumed the term “active state” refers to the states where UE’s mobility is based on handovers. Also, the fact that it was introduced in LTE when the RRC_INACTIVE was not yet defined hints that the usage of the UE is limited to RRC_CONNECTED.
summaryOfChange:
In order to clarify that the UE History Information is to be collected in RAN only when UE is in RRC_CONNECTED, it is proposed to replace “active” with “RRC_CONNECTED”.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only clarifies usage of the IE.
title: Clarification of the usage of the UE History Information

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the NG-RAN node does not temporarily support the requested feature, the behaviour of the NG-RAN node is not compliant, it is not clear if the procedure should continuing for other measurements, which is not aligned with intention of the specification.
reasonForChange:
In Measurement Request, the following description is provided: 
If the Measurement Beam Information Request IE is included in the MEASUREMENT REQUEST message, the NG-RAN node shall include the Measurement Beam Information IE in the TRP Measurement Result IE of the MEASUREMENT RESPONSE message.

The NG-RAN node may not have temporarily the capability to provide measurement beam information to the LMF with in general supporting the feature. The wording “shall” is not appropriate. Indeed in this case, the feature and Elementary Procedure are supported, not mandated and should proceed with other measurement as compliant way.

The similar issue is observed in 8.2.6, the NR-RAN node may not be able to configure the area-specific SRS configuration temporarily, and therefore the feature should not be mandated. It is noticed that in F1AP, “shall, if supported” is used: 
If the Positioning Validity Area Cell List IE and Validity Area specific SRS Information IE within the Requested SRS Transmission Characteristics IE are included in the POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST message, the gNB-DU shall, if supported, take this information into account for configuring SRS transmissions for the UE in the indicated validity area, and shall include the SRS-PosRRC-InactiveValidityAreaConfig IE, the SFN Initialisation Time IE and the Positioning Validity Area Cell List IE in the POSITIONING INFORMATION RESPONSE message.

 It is suggested to add “if supported”, which is more normative 3GPP language.

Please note the definition of “Shall, if supported”
The procedure text indicates that the receiving node "shall, if supported," perform a certain function Y under a certain condition. If the receiving node supports procedure X, but does not support functionality Y, the receiving node shall proceed with the execution of the EP, possibly informing the requesting node about the not supported functionality.
And definition of “Shall” which lead to failure in measurement is not reported 
The procedure text indicates that the receiving node "shall" perform a certain function Y under a certain condition. If the receiving node supports procedure X but cannot perform functionality Y requested in the REQUEST message of a Class 1 EP, the receiving node shall respond with the message used to report unsuccessful outcome for this procedure, containing an appropriate cause value.
summaryOfChange:
Revise the sentence to “… shall, if supported, …”

reasonForChange: According to Clause 5.11.2 of TS 38.323, if the successful delivery of a PDCP Data PDU is confirmed by one of the associated AM RLC entities and the AM RLC entity is not associated with an SRAP entity, the transmitting PDCP entity shall indicate to the other AM RLC entities to discard the duplicated PDCP Data PDU. consequencesIfNotApproved: The LTM procedures for Inter-DU case and CU-UP change are incomplete.
reasonForChange:
In Section 8.2.1.5 Inter-DU LTM, 
Steps 7-8 that happens with the candidate DU(s) for subsequent LTM should be invoked per candidate cell, but it is currently written as if invoked per DU.

In Section 8.2.1.6 LTM with gNB-CU-UP change, 
The last agreed R3-243090 changed the Step 10-11 from mandatory to optional given that data forwarding is a optional feature. However, according to TS 38.401 Section 8.9.4 Steps 12c-d, during conditional mobility, the Bearer Context Modification procedure toward the source CU-UP after the UE successfully accessed is always executed to indicate the source CU-UP to stop packet delivery to the UE (and while doing so, may retrieve PDCP UL/DL status or exchange TNL address for data forwarding). Given that LTM shares the same principle with conditional mobility from CU-UP functional point of view, those steps needs to be reverted back to mandatory with the correct descriptions.
The target DU, once the UE successfully accessed, informs the UE’s access to the target CU-UP via sending initial DDDS frame. This was specified in Rel-15 to fastly inform CU-UP of the UE’s access during legacy mobility, and later extended for conditional mobility family (CHO, CPAC, subsequent CPAC) as a way to initiate DL data delivery from the target CU-UP. This part was also missing in the figure.
summaryOfChange:
In 8.2.1.5, fixed the Step 7-8 descriptions as invoked per candidate cell.
In 8.2.1.6, reverted the optional Step 10-11 back to mandatory with the correct description including indicating the source CU-UP to stop packet delivery.
In 8.2.1.6, added the step of the target DU sending DDDS (Downlink Data Delivery Status) frame to the target CU-UP.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Not aligned with RAN1 parameter list.
reasonForChange:
The following agreement can be found in RAN1 parameter list R1-2312708 on measurement time window(s):

The Measurement time window(s) introduced for Rel-18 CPP, according to RAN1, are also applicable to perform the legacy measurements, i.e., UL measurements for UL-TDOA and Multi-RTT within indicated time window(s) only. 

According to RAN1, the parameters for each time window includes the start of the time window. The parameter is currently missing in clause 9.2.91 due to the presence of SFN and Slot number in Measurement Request message, which are introduced by R3-204970 for sp-SRS to indicate the SRS transmission. Therefore, the existing IEs cannot be reused and an additional parameter is needed to indicate the start of the measurement time window. 

It is therefore proposed to associate a start time with each measurement window Item.
summaryOfChange:
Enhance the Time Window Information Measurement List IE to enable the LMF to request the gNB to perform measurements for UL-TDOA or Multi-RTT occurring within indicated time window(s) only or not. 

It is also introduced the Time Window Start IE within the Time Window Information Measurement List IE as RAN1 parameters description.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Misinterpretation of the clause 8.2.1.2 may lead to wrongful signalling of Data Collection Update messages immediately after a successful handover execution, without the triggering of any exit condition.
The text in Clause 8.4.13.2 prevents from periodic reporting of the UE Performance metrics, which was agreed by RAN3 during Rel18.
reasonForChange:
The Rel.18 work item on AI/ML for NG-RAN specified data collection enhancements and signalling support for AI/ML-based use cases. Among the specified enhancements were two new procedures- Data Collection Reporting Initiation (class 1) and Data Collection Reporting (class 2) procedures. 

The Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure is used by an NG-RAN node to request from another NG-RAN node the reporting of information to support, e.g., AI/ML in NG-RAN. After successful execution of the Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure, the requested metrics are reported to the requesting NG-RAN node over the Data Collection Reporting procedure. 

For the Measured UE Trajectory and UE performance after handover, the measurement ID of the Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure is included in the Handover Request message as an implicit indication for reporting of metrics as requested by the corresponding Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure to the requesting node. The measurement of the requested metrics commences after a successful handover and is reported to the requesting NG-RAN node after at least one of the specified exit conditions is satisfied. The collected measurements are signalled to the requesting node over the following transmission of Data Collection Update message, after at least one of the exit conditions have been satisfied, depending on the periodicity configured by the original Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure.

The text describing the above in TS 38.423 is as follows: “If the Data Collection ID IE is contained in the HANDOVER REQUEST message, the target NG-RAN node shall, if supported, report to the source NG-RAN node after successful handover, via the Data Collection Reporting procedure, the requested information configured via the previous Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure corresponding to the NG-RAN node1 Measurement ID IE, allocated by the source NG-RAN node, and the NG-RAN node2 Measurement ID IE, allocated by the target NG-RAN node.”. The statement “… the target NG-RAN node shall, if supported, report to the source NG-RAN node after successful handover, via the Data Collection Reporting procedure …” may be interpreted as the target NG-RAN node reporting the measurements to the source NG-RAN node immediately after a successful handover via the Data Collection Reporting procedure. While the intention is to specify that the reporting happens via the Data Collection Reporting procedure after a successful handover and after the exit conditions have been triggered and at the specified reporting periodicity of the Data Collection Reporting procedure. 

The above-described conditions for terminating the feedback collection and signalling the collected feedback, i.e., after the exit conditions are triggered and at the next transmission of the Data Collection Update message, are also described in Clause 8.4.13.2 in TS 38.423, however, this description does not respect the agreement taken in RAN3-119bis stating the following:

UE performance feedback can be reported through one-time reporting or periodic reporting.
Therefore, the text in Clause 8.4.13.2 in TS 38.423 prevents the option of periodic reporting of the UE Performance feedback.
summaryOfChange:
The clause describing the interaction between the Handover Request and the Data Collection Reporting and the Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedures in 8.2.1.2 in TS 38.423 is corrected to mention that UE performance reporting as part of Data Collection Reporting is triggered according to clause 8.4.13.2.
The clause describing the Data Collection Reporting Initiation procedure in 8.4.13.2 in TS 38.423 is corrected to clarify that the result of the UE performance collection may be reported periodically during the Collection Time Duration for UE Performance via DATA COLLECTION UPDATE messages and, after collection is terminated, it shall be reported at the next available DATA COLLECTION UPDATE message.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has no impact from protocol point of view. The CR has impacts from a functional point of view.
The impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the way UE Performance information is reported.
title: Correction for Data Collection Reporting procedure's interaction with Handover Request procedure

consequencesIfNotApproved: The functionality of Area-specific SRS configuration is not complete.
reasonForChange:
In Rel-18, Validity Area Specific SRS Information IE was introduced in the Requested SRS Transmission Characteristics IE. The NG-RAN may take this information into account for configuring SRS transmissions for the UE in the indicated validity area during Positioning Information Exchange procedure, and/or may reserve the indicated SRS information during SRS Information Reservation Notification procedure. 
However, the current information contained in the Validity Area Specific SRS Information IE corresponds to only one SRS resource, which leads to the following situations,
During Positioning Information Exchange procedure, the LMF can recommend only one SRS resource for NG-RAN to configure SRS configuration containing multiple SRS resource sets and multiple SRS resources in each SRS resource set. Resulting in more chances for different NG-RAN node to allocate the same area-specific SRS resources for different UEs, which should be avoided.
During SRS Information Reservation Notification procedure, the LMF can notify the NG-RAN to reserve only one SRS resource in each SRS INFORMATION RESERVATION NOTIFICATION message, which is inefficient if the LMF needs to notify NG-RAN to reserve multiple SRS resources.
summaryOfChange:
Add Validity Area Specific SRS Information Extended IE in 9.2.27.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has an impact from protocol and functional point of view. The impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the functionality to support NR positioning while in RRC Inactive state.

consequencesIfNotApproved: It remains unclear how Average UE Throughput DL and Average UE Throughput UL are derived.
reasonForChange:
In the context of the Rel-18 “AI/ML for NG-RAN” RAN3 introduced in TS 38.423 a set of metrics representing the UE performance that could be requested by the source gNB to be reported by the target gNB via the Data Collection Reporting (Initiation) procedures after an AI/ML-driven mobility decision. 
UE performance metrics, i.e., Average UE Throughput DL/UL, Average Packet Delay DL/UL and Average Packet Loss DL, are intended to be collected by the target gNB on a per-UE basis. 
However, there is no clear understanding on how a gNB could derive such per-UE metrics.
In RAN3#126 it was agreed to send a LS to SA5 (R3-247775) to check whether the Average UE Throughput DL/UL measurements in TS 28.558 are already defined with per-UE granularity, and SA5 confirmed in R3-253023 (S5-252056) that Average UE Throughput DL/UL in TS 28.558 are per-UE measurements, originating from corresponding per-DRB measurements being aggregated to reflect a per-UE throughput.
This CR clarifies in the semantics description of Average UE Throughput DL and Average UE Throughput UL IEs that the corresponding measurements refer to TS 28.558 clauses 6.3.1.4.1 and 6.3.1.4.2, respectively. 

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous release of the specification because the changes only affect the AI/ML for NG-RAN function.

consequencesIfNotApproved: RAN behavior is missing when the UE radio capability and the UE radio capability ID are not received in the above mentioned messages.
reasonForChange:
According to the following description in the current TS 23.501:
If the AMF sends an N2 REQUEST (i.e., INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST or UE RADIO CAPABILITY CHECK REQUEST) message to NG-RAN without UE Radio Capability information in that message and there is no UE Radio Capability information available in RAN, this triggers the RAN to request the UE Radio Capability from the UE and to upload it to the AMF in the N2 UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION message.

And the following descriptions for the CIoT EPS optimization in TS 23.401 applies to CIoT 5GS optimization. 
For the CIoT EPS Optimisations, during the Attach procedure or the Tracking Area Update procedure e.g. for the "first TAU following GERAN/UTRAN Attach", or mobility between a cell that does not broadcast SystemInformationBlockType31(-NB) and an E-UTRA cell that broadcasts SystemInformationBlockType31(-NB)), if the MME does not send an S1 interface INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST to the E-UTRAN, the MME should obtain the UE Radio Capability information by sending either the DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT message indicating UE Radio Capability request or the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message without UE Radio Capability information included to the E-UTRAN. This triggers the E-UTRAN to request the UE Radio Capability from the UE and upload it to the MME in the S1 interface UE CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION message, as specified in TS 36.300 [5].

However, the current description of the Initial Context Setup procedure, UE Radio Capability Check and Connection Establishment Indication procedure in TS 38.413 are defined only considering the case of UE Radio Capability information included and the behavior of the RAN when the request message does not include the UE Radio Capability information is missing.
summaryOfChange: Add some Interactions with UE Radio Capability Info Indication procedure to clarify the behavior of the RAN when the request message does not include the UE Radio Capability information.
title: Correction on UE Radio Capability Retrieval

consequencesIfNotApproved: LTM cell switch may fail due to missing TCI states information.
reasonForChange: In Rel-18 LTM, the TCI states configuration are only included when early synchronization is requested, but they are also required during a cell switch (since the LTM cell switch MAC CE includes a TCI state which the UE should use). If no TCI state list is configured for an LTM candidate, an LTM cell switch MAC CE indicating that TCI state cannot be executed by the UE since the UE would not have any TCI state to refer to and the result would be that the procedure will fail. To ensure TCI state information is always available for cell switch, it should be included beyond early synchronization. Therefore, we propose adding a new IE in the F1AP LTM Configuration Information IE to reference it, and clarify its usage in Stage 2.
summaryOfChange:
Add clarification that when TCI States Configurations List IE is received from Candidate gNB-DU during LTM preparation phase, the gNB-CU will include it in its signaling to Source gNB-DU respectively.

Therefore, the target DU should be able to map the CSI-RS resources with an SSB Index so that the source DU can understand which SSB beam it should select next time. consequencesIfNotApproved:
gNB-CU or gNB-DU can not only send the SRS resource configuration information request to its peer entity by using CLI Indication message.
The CLI Measurement Result IE name is incorrect, and semantics are incorrect and open to wrong interpretations.
reasonForChange:
In RAN3#129 meeting, RAN3 finally agreed to use CLI Indication message for either CLI measurements reporting or SRS resource configuration information request between gNBs and gNB-CU and gNB-DU. But based on the current tabular design of this F1AP message, the CLI Measurement Result IE is mandatory which is not fully reflect the RAN3 agreement.
In the tabular for the CLI Indication message the CLI Measurement Result IE shall be named CLI Measurement Result List IE.
The semantic description for the CLI Indication IE is “Indicates to request CLI mitigation”. This semantics is badly written and it should be corrected. Besides, the IE is part of a Class 2 message and as such it is incorrect to state that the IE represents a request. Requests are followed by responses and a class 2 message has no response messages. The semantic description should be corrected.
summaryOfChange:
To fulfill the RAN3 agreement, correct the CLI Measurement Result range in the tabular from 1 to 0..1 and correct the CLI Measurement Result IE from Mandatory to Optional in ASN.1.
Update CLI Measurement Result IE name and semantic description for the CLI Indication IE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Unnecessary limitations on the use of DL discard procedures are in place. It is unclear what PDCP PDUs to discard in case of DL discard usage
reasonForChange:
At the last RAN3 meeting it was proposd that DL discard indications can be applied to different bearer configurations, not only to bearers configured for PDCP duplication. This view is acknowledge and clarifications on what PDUs to be discarded are needed.
An ambiguity exists on whether a discard command includes the PDCP SN up to where PDUs need to be discarded.
summaryOfChange:
DL Flush and DL Discard Blocks could apply not only to bearers configured for PDCP duplication but also to discard PDCP PDUs in a node subject to radio link outage. The use of the DL discard indications is made generic. 
It is clarified that in case of DL discard the PDUs to be discarded are up to and including the PDU SN indicated.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The NR UP message may not be possible to be transferred in the GTP protocol.
reasonForChange:
When defining content for the NR RAN Container, RAN3 decided to enable flexible message length for the DL DATA DELIVERY STATUS and DL USER DATA messages. However, the values agreed then enabled the messages to exceed 1018 octexts, which is the maximum size of the payload for the GTP header extension. Such messages, if created, could not be transferred.
Also, currently, it is necessary to include in the DL USER DATA at least one block of numbers for discard, which may not be necessary.
summaryOfChange:
The limits for the blocks to include is corrected to make sure that the message does not exceed the 1018 bytes and that optional information may indeed be skipped. The limits are selected so that 34 octets are left for future extension of the PDUs.
In addition, the upper limit of the message size is explicitly added to the format description.
title: Avoiding exceeding the max size of the NR RAN Container

consequencesIfNotApproved: gNB-DU may not be able to get the PDCP SN info.
reasonForChange: In TS 38.323, either 12 or 18bits are supported for NR PDCP SN. For EN-DC case, PDCP-config is contained in mcg-RB-Config of CG-ConfigInfo. It is agreed that, gNB-CU will provide CG-ConfigInfo in CU to DU RRC information for EN-DC case. However, it depends on implementation whether gNB-CU will forward all the information of CG-ConfigInfo to gNB-DU. e.g., gNB-CU may only forward lower layer related information of CG-ConfigInfo to gNB-DU. For standalone case, there’s no way for gNB-CU to provide PDCP-Config to gNB-DU as it is assumed that gNB-DU can’t fetch RRC reconfiguration message for the UE. While in 38.425, gNB-DU needs to know PDCP SN in order to feedback the highest transmitted/delivered PDCP SN.

For instance, UE identification within a gNB-CU-UP and over E1 interface is currently based on the gNB-CU-CP UE E1AP ID and gNB-CU-UP UE E1AP IE pair. However, these identifiers are not visible/used by gNB-DU nor transferred over the air interface. Thus, it is not possible to identify and correlate UEs between air interface, F1 interface and E1 interface based on existing identifiers specified in E1 as they lack commonality. Without means for this correlation, troubleshooting and taking corrective actions in case of e.g., throughput degradation, packet drops, etc. is very difficult.

For the SN side, when the MN or SN-CU wishes to provide some information toward the SN-DU, e.g. the CellGroupConfig of the SCG at source side during SN change or intra-SgNB-CU SgNB-DU change, such information shall be delivered to the SN-DU via the RRC container CGConfigInfo.
For the MN side (i.e. how to provide some information toward the MgNB-DU), however, the case is not clear. consequencesIfNotApproved: Misallignment with TS 24.501.
reasonForChange:
In the HANDOVER REQUEST message, the NASC IE is included which is a NAS-PDU containing either the “Intra N1 mode NAS transparent container” or the “S1 mode to N1 mode NAS transparent container” specified in TS 24.501. 
However, according to the TS 24.501, only the value part of the “Intra N1 mode NAS transparent container” or the “S1 mode to N1 mode NAS transparent container” information element is included within the RRC message sent to the UE. Specifically, 
In clause 9.11.2.6 in TS 24. 501: 
The value part of the Intra N1 mode NAS transparent container information element is included in specific information elements within some RRC messages sent to the UE.

In clause 9.11.2.9 in TS 24.501
The value part of the S1 mode to N1 mode NAS transparent container information element is included in specific information elements within some RRC messages sent to the UE. 

Currently in TS 38.331, only the content reference to TS 24.501 is included within the NAS-Container. 

In order to keep align with the TS 24.501 and TS 38.331, it is proposed to clarify that NASC IE contains contents specified in TS 24.501.
summaryOfChange:
Update the semantics description of NASC IE in the HANDOVER REQUEST message.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
CU cannot determine gap sharing scheme, thus unable to send MeasGapSharingConfig to UE.

Area-specific other SI might not be operated properly.
reasonForChange:
In the MeasConfig configured to the UE, MeasGapSharingConfig is used to define the scheme for sharing gaps when UE is required to perform different types of gap-needed measurements, which was introduced by RAN2 for R15.
In CU-DU architecture, gaps are generated by DU and sent to CU. However, in the current DU to CU RRC Information, MeasGapConfig is included whereas MeasGapSharingConfig is missing.

On the other hand, in SIB1, SI-SchedulingInfo contains the systemInformationAreaID, which are used by UE to check whether it needs to re-acquire the area-specific SI or not. Besides, the areaScope is associated with each other SI to indicate whether the other SI is cell-specific or area-specific. In current specification, gNB-CU sends SIB type, SIB message and value tag of other SI to gNB-DU, and gNB-DU encodes SI-SchedulingInfo of other SI in SIB1.
summaryOfChange:
Add MeasGapSharingConfig into DU to CU RRC Information.
Introduce systemInformationAreaID and areaScope IE into gNB-CU System Information

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment between stage 2 and stage 3 specifications.
reasonForChange:
It is described in section of 4.9.1.2.2 in 23.502 that:
" 6.	SMF to AMF: Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext Response (N2 SM information)
……
If the Source NG-RAN does not support Alternative QoS Profiles (see TS 23.501 [2]) and the Target NG-RAN supports them, the SMF sends the Alternative QoS Profiles (see TS 23.501 [2]) to the Target NG-RAN on a per QoS Flow basis, if available.
7.	AMF to NG-RAN: N2 Path Switch Request Ack (N2 SM Information, Failed PDU Sessions, UE Radio Capability ID). "
The main intention is to allow the NG-RAN to receive the AQP parameters from the CN during the Xn based handover, and perform the notification control at the first place. Hence there is a need to align stage3 spec with the stage 2 spec. 

Note that at this time, the QoS flow already successfully passes the admission control at the target NG-RAN node based on the requested QoS parameters sent from the source NG-RAN. This means that there is no need for the target NG-RAN node to feedback any admission control result upon reception of the Alternative QoS Parameters Set List IE.
summaryOfChange:
Add the AQP parameters in the PATH SWITCH REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message.

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the CR is not approved, non-DRB configuration for IAB-MT is not supported during the handover or secondary node addition procedure, and the BH RLC channel mapping for UL cannot be configured via UA signalling.
reasonForChange:
In last RAN3 108e meeting, it agreed that “DRB setup is optional for NR SA since Rel-15; E-RAB setup is mandatory in LTE since Rel-8.”
However, in current specification, it is stated that “The gNB-CU shall only initiate the UE Context Setup procedure for handover or secondary node addition when at least one DRB is setup for the UE”, such constraint should be different for the IAB-MT, since the IAB-MT may not setup any DRB but only BH RLC channel, and in such case, the IAB-node should also be able to perform migration or SN addition.
Also in RAN3 108 meeting, it has been agreed that both UA F1AP signalling and NUA F1AP signaling can be used for BH RLC channel mapping configuration. If the UA signalling is used, the BH RLC CH ID IE (included in the BH RLC Channel to be Setup List IE of UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message or UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, or included in the BH RLC Channel to be Modified List IE of UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message ) is used to indicate the ingress BH RLC channel for the UL mapping configuration, or indicate the egress BH RLC channel for the DL mapping configuration. 
However, in section 8.3.1.2 of current specification, it has been stated that “the gNB-DU shall store the mapping information contained in the BAP layer BH RLC channel Mapping Info To Add IE, if present, for the egress BH RLC channel identified by the BH RLC CH ID IE”, only the downstream case for bearer mapping is included, the upstream case is missing.  
The term BAP-layer used in the UE Context Setup procedure (8.3.1.2) should be “BAP sublayer” to align with TS 38.300 
The Configured BAP Address IE in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message is to let the parent node know the BAP address of the child node. Since the child node is identified by the BAP address in the routing table. Thus this IE will be used when perform routing, and the routing related operation is specified in TS38.340. Thus, the reference for the procedure text about the Configured BAP Address IE should be TS38.340, not the TS38.401
summaryOfChange:
In section 8.3.1.2:
Add “or ingress” as an alternative case after the “egress” in the following sentence “the gNB-DU shall store the mapping information contained in the BAP layer BH RLC channel Mapping Info To Add IE, if present, for the egress BH RLC channel identified by the BH RLC CH ID IE ”, in the description about the BAP layer BH RLC channel Mapping Info IE 
Add “, or at least one BH RLC channel is set up for IAB-MT” after the description of “The gNB-CU shall only initiate the UE Context Setup procedure for handover or secondary node addition when at least one DRB is setup for the UE”, in order to capture the agreement on non-DRB configuration for IAB-MT.
Update “BAP-layer” to “BAP sublayer”.
Update the reference in “TS38.401” to “TS38.340”, after the description of “if the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message contains the Configured BAP Address IE, the gNB-DU shall, if supported, store this BAP address configured for the corresponding child IAB-node and use it as specified in”

In section 8.10.1.2:
Update “BAP-layer” to “BAP sublayer”.

In section 9.3.1.98:
Update “BAP layer” to “BAP sublayer”.

reasonForChange:
In clause 8.2.3.2, the original description did not cover the possibility that the same flow ID is included in both the QoS Flow Add or Modify Request List IE and the QoS Flow to Release List IE. 
When that happens, either option

consequencesIfNotApproved: Signalling-based means for the LMF to construct the assistance data to help UE quickly acquire the LTE reference cell is not supported.
reasonForChange: When the UE is served by a NR cell, and the LMF requests the UE to perform measurements for OTDOA positioning, the LMF may provide assistance data including optionally timing information to enable the UE to quickly acquire the LTE reference cell. However the LMF is not aware of timing relationships between the LTE and NR cells because it does not receive the SFN Initialization Time for NR cells, although it is of course able to do so for LTE cells.
summaryOfChange:
The OTDOA Cell Information IE is enhanced to include the relevant NR IEs:
CGI NR 
SFN Initialisation Time NR

Since the OTDOA Information Exchange procedure is not restricted to ng-eNBs, this enables the LMF to retrieve timing and access point location information for cells in a gNB, from which it becomes possible to construct the assistance data in LPP.

Note that NR CGI IE is not added in this mirror CR (compared to the root CR for rel15, CR#0013) because this IE already exists in rel16.

Also, criticality columns are added to the table in 9.2.15, and criticality for the existing TDD Configuration EUTRA IE is added.

Impact analysis: 
This CR has isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release). The impact can be considered isolated because it enables an existing procedure to be used by the LMF towards a gNB, and existing use of the procedure is not changed in any way.
title: Support OTDOA assistance data for case of NR serving cell

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment of behavior between XNAP and NGAP regarding QoS flows list not admitted.
reasonForChange:
The 5G QoS model is based on QoS Flows.The QoS Flow is the finest granularity of QoS differentiation in the PDU Session. During Handover, it is possible that not all QoS flows in admitted PDU Session are accepted by target gNB. Take XNAP as example, in HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message, the target gNB sends back both admitted and not admitted QoS flows list in PDU Session Resources Admitted List IE. Based on the information, source gNB is able to be aware of the failure reason for not allowed QoS flows and can do subsequent handover optimization.
However, for NG Based Handover, the failed QoS flows list is missing in HANDOVER COMMAND message.

Introduce QoS Flow Failed to Setup List IE in HANDOVER COMMAND message.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The LMF cannot know the angle information for the measurements related of each PRS resource.
reasonForChange:
In the current NR-PRS Beam Information IE, the PRS Resource Set ID is included, but there is no resource ID:


The NR-PRS Beam Informatrion provides the beam angle information for each PRS resource. The UE can measure the PRS and report the measurement results for each PRS resource to the LMF for the DL-AoD positioning. For example, the UE can report the following information in the LPP message Provide Location Information.
NR-DL-AoD-MeasElement-r16 ::= SEQUENCE {
	dl-PRS-ID-r16					INTEGER (0..255),
	nr-PhysCellID-r16				NR-PhysCellID-r16						OPTIONAL,
	nr-CellGlobalID-r16				NCGI-r15								OPTIONAL,
	nr-ARFCN-r16					ARFCN-ValueNR-r15						OPTIONAL,
	nr-DL-PRS-ResourceID-r16		NR-DL-PRS-ResourceID-r16	 			OPTIONAL,
	nr-DL-PRS-ResourceSetID-r16		NR-DL-PRS-ResourceSetID-r16 			OPTIONAL,
	nr-TimeStamp-r16				NR-TimeStamp-r16,
	nr-DL-PRS-RSRP-Result-r16		INTEGER (0..126),
	nr-DL-PRS-RxBeamIndex-r16		INTEGER (1..8)							OPTIONAL,
	nr-DL-AoD-AdditionalMeasurements-r16
									NR-DL-AoD-AdditionalMeasurements-r16	OPTIONAL,
	...
}

Then LMF can then match the measurements to the PRS angle information based on the NR-PRS Beam Information IE of the TRP. The LMF can then calculate the AoD information and further calculate the UE location.

In order the enable the LMF to match the measurements per PRS resource to the PRS angle, the “PRS Angle Item” should include the PRS resource ID information. Otherwise, an easier way can have the clarification in the semantics description, such as, “The PRS angle items are associated with the PRS resource in the ascending order in each resource set”. 

Thus, two options can be considered:
Option 1: Add the “Resource ID” IE in each “PRS Angle Item” IE.
Option 2: Add the semantics description for the “PRS Angle Item” IE: “The PRS angle items are associated with the PRS resource in the ascending order in each resource set”.
This CR provides the solution of Option 2.

Rev1: group as preference for option 1, Option 1 is implemented
summaryOfChange:
Add the “Resource ID” IE in each “PRS Angle Item” IE.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release), the impact is functional.
title: Correction on PRS Beam information

In case NG-RAN is not able to provide the service over radio, due to lack of radio resources, it is beneficial for NG-RAN to notify CN to introduce a RAN initiated Broadcast Session Release Required procedure. Thus, the introduction of a non-UE associated Class2 NGAP procedure is essential.

title: CR to TS38.413 for introduction of broadcast session release required procedure

consequencesIfNotApproved: MBS could not be supported well.
reasonForChange:
1. gNB-CU does not know which cell in the gNB-DU has established the broadcast service successfully. However, in MCCH, the neighbour cell list which also support the ongoing broadcast serivice in included which means this information is needed on Xn and F1 interface. The MBS service area included in NG interface is not reliable since 5GC does not know which cell has admit the service successfully.
2. The presence of PLMN-Identity IE is missing in the tabular.
3. Currently, for multicast, there is one Mandaroty IE MBS CU to DU RRC Information included in MULTICAST CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message. However, the context included in MBS CU to DU RRC Information IE is broadcast related information which is awared/decided by CU while transmit via MCCH by DU. For multicast, this information is not needed.
Besides, since RAN2 does not define a structure for MRB configuration, configruation for both DRB and MRB could only be included in RadioBearerConfig and CellGroupConfig IE which is UE specific. There is no way to transfer MRB specific configuration for multicast.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce Broadcast area scope IE in BROADCAST CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message to let gNB-CU know the cell list that has established the MBS context successfully.
Add the presence of IE PLMN-Identity
Remove MBS CU to DU RRC Information IE included in MULTICAST CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message and MULTICAST CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message
title: F1AP corrections on MBS feature

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is a misalignment between 38.331 and E1AP IE structure for drb-ContinueEHC-DL/drb-ContinueEHC-UL IE.
reasonForChange: The presence of ehc-uplink/ehc-downlink indicates whether Ethernet header compression is configured for uplink only or for downlink only or for both uplink and downlink. In the meanwhile, the drb-continueEHC-UL/ drb-continueEHC-DL IE is also an optional IE which is used to indicate whether the PDCP entity continues or resets the uplink/downlink EHC header compression protocol during PDCP re-establishment. This means there is no coupling relationship between the two IEs, both IEs should be optional and have their own meanings for presence and absence. However, in the current E1AP, the existence of drb-continueEHC-UL/ drb-continueEHC-DL IE is coupled with the existence of EHC uplink/EHC downlink IE, and the IE value can only be set to ‘true’. This violates the RAN2 meaning in 38.331 and should be fixed.
summaryOfChange:
For addressing the issue in a backward compatiable way, the proposed solution is to extend drb-continueEHC-UL/ drb-continueEHC-DL with a new value set to ‘false’. By this way, we can realize the scenario where we choose to apply EHC configurations for DL and/or UL while we can also reset downlink/uplink EHC header compression protocol during PDCP re-establishment.
Add related procedure text

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):

consequencesIfNotApproved: UE contexts for RRC connected UE are erroneously deleted during the System Information Delivery procedure.
reasonForChange:
As specified in TS 38.300, from Rel-16, the connected UE can on-demand request Other SI towards the network, then the network can broadcast the requested Other SI, in addition to the RRC dedicated signaling, as follows. 
Other SI encompasses all SIBs not broadcast in the Minimum SI. Those SIBs can either be periodically broadcast on DL-SCH, broadcast on-demand on DL-SCH (i.e. upon request from UEs in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, or RRC_CONNECTED),……

Currently the SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND message was introduced first for idle/inactive UEs. Specifically, the Confirmed UE ID was introduced as a mandatory IE, and with the following procedure texts.
Upon reception of the SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND message, the gNB-DU shall broadcast the requested Other SI, and delete the UE context corresponding to the Confirmed UE ID IE, if any.

However, when using this message to broadcast the requested other SI for connected UE, the UE context corresponding to the Confirmed UE ID is erroneously deleted, according to the above procedure texts.   

At previous RAN3#117 meeting, there were some comments about the updated procedure texts in R3-224727 whether the DU could identify the UE RRC state based on confirmed UE ID IE. Given that the DU can identify the UE is in RRC connected state anyway, to make the procedure texts clear, it is simply updated to indicate that when the UE is not in RRC connected state, the UE context can be deleted.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify that the UE context corresponding to the Confirmed UE ID IE, can be deleted by the DU, only for idle or inactive UEs (i.e. the deletion of the UE context is not applicable for connected UE). 
 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the System Information Delivery.
title: Correction of on-demand SI for connected UE

consequencesIfNotApproved: 5G to 4G handover is not possible to an open access HeNB.
reasonForChange:
Inter-system handover from 5GS to 4GS is supported since Rel-15. However, the Target ID IE in the HANDOVER REQUEST message is erroneously encoded as Global ng-eNB ID rather than Global eNB ID. The difference between the two is as follows:
eNB ID (in E-UTRAN) supports four different ID lengths: 20-bit macro, 18-bit short macro, 21-bit long macro, and 28-bit home eNB ID lengths.
ng-eNB ID (in NG-RAN) supports three different ID lengths: the same as eNB ID except the 28-bit home eNB ID (since there is no HeNB in the NG-RAN architecture).
The consequence of this error is that 5G to 4G handover to an open access HeNB is unintentionally precluded by stage 3 specifications, even though it is supported since Rel-15 by stage 2 specifications as confirmed by LS from SA2 in R3-225323.
summaryOfChange:
Target Home eNB ID is introduced as a new choice in the Target ID IE, in order to fill the gap caused by the erroneous encoding of the E-UTRAN choice in the Target ID IE.

Impact analysis:

reasonForChange:
As defined in TS 38.331, for each MBS Session, the gNB optionally broadcast over MCCH about mtch-neighbourCell which indicates neighbour cells which provide this service on MTCH. In order to provide such information over MCCH, the gNB-CU should optionally provide such information to the gNB-DU via the MBS CU to DU RRC Information IE. 
In current 9.3.1.225, the tabluar of MBS CU to DU RRC Information IE, the mtch-neighbourCell IE is defined as optional. But in the asn.1 part, the mtch-neighbourCell IE is wrongly defined as mandatory.

In section 9.2.13.6, in the Broadcast MRB to Be Setup Item IEs IE, the BC Bearer Context F1-U TNL Info at CU IE is Mandatory, but in the asn.1 bcBearerCtxtF1U-TNLInfoatCU IE is Optional in the BroadcastMRBs-ToBeSetupMod-Item IE, the asn.1 part should be updated.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The PO, PF, and the UE-ID based subgroup ID selected between UE and RAN may be different, and the RAN paging will fail
reasonForChange:
In Rel-17, NR supports to configure eDRX for RedCap UE in RRC INACTIVE/IDLE. According to TS 38.304 spec, if eDRX is used to page UE, 12 bits of UE identity index is used for the PF and PO calculation. 

Furthermore, As specified in TS 38.304, when the UE determines the UE-ID based subgrouping ID, it shall use 15bits if eDRX is applied, otherwise, 13bits of UE identity index.

However, only 10 bits UE Identity Index for NR is included in XnAP RAN paging message, it is not enough.

This change only impacts the RAN PF and PO calculation for RedCap UE, and the UE-ID based subgroup ID calculation.
This CR is BC.
