consequencesIfNotApproved: The ng-eNB may reject the establishment of the UE-associated logical NG-connection in case of AMF change with CIoT CP Optimization
reasonForChange:
In 5GC, upon change of serving AMF, the subscription of mobility event is transferred from the old AMF to the new AMF in the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST and DL NAS TRANSPORT messages.
However, in case of E-UTRA connected to 5GC, if the 5GS CIoT CP Optimization connection is established and there is an AMF change, the new AMF cannot indicate to the ng-eNB in the NGAP Connection Establishment Indication procedure that the AMF has been changed from an old AMF to this AMF that is sending the message.
According to the specification, this might result in a UE AP ID inconsistency, and ng-eNB, without knowing that the connection is moved to a new AMF, may reject the CP Connection Establishment Indication procedure due to the UE AP IDs consistency check.

Introduce an Old AMF IE in the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION message

This CR is BC.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Not aligned between the Tabular and the ASN.1 for the Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE.      
The Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE may be erroneously used by the gNB-CU-UP upon received.
reasonForChange:
The Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE is included in the 9.3.1.26 QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE (see the agreed CR in R3-193005), and in the DL DATA NOTIFICATION message respectively. Its IE type is given as INTEGER (0.. 7, …). 

However, in ASN.1, the paging-Policy-Indicator is defined as INTEGER (1..8) in the QoSFlowLevelQoSParameters. While it is correctly defined for the DLDataNotification message. 

For this Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE included in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE, it was initially removed from the Tabular in the agreed CR in R3-185358 since it was agreed to add the PPI field into the DL PDU SESSION INFORMATION frame of TS 38.415, but kept intact in the ASN.1  (see the agreed CR in R3-185127). Afterwards this IE was added back to the Tabular in the R3-193005 to align with the ASN.1. Given the above analysis, it should clarify that this IE is not used in this version of the specification.
summaryOfChange:
For the Paging Priority Indicator (PPI) IE included in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE
Update IE name to Paging Priority Index, and update the IE type to be the same as the definition in ASN.1;
Update the semantic descriptions and ASN.1 so that this IE is not used in this version of the specification. 


Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the Paging Priority Indicator in the QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE.

The reason why the QoE Area Scope IE shall be optional is that the target NG-RAN node does not need to receive the area scope from source NG-RAN node during the NG based handover if the target NG-RAN node has already received it, which is the case, for management based QoE.

reasonForChange:
For a UE DRB supports intra-gNB-DU CA-based PDCP duplication, the BH information is contained in the Additional PDCP Duplication TNL Items which is configured for each F1-U tunnel, in the following messages from gNB-CU to gNB-DU: UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST, and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION CONFIRM. Accordingly, in ASN.1 part, the extension part of the AdditionalPDCPDuplicationTNL-Item IE includes the BHInfo IE.
However, the AdditionalPDCPDuplicationTNL-Item IE also be contained in the following gNB-DU to gNB-CU messages: UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE, and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUIRED. So, in ASN.1, the BHInfo IE has been contained as optional IE for the F1-U tunnels identified by the additionalPDCPDuplicationUPTNLInformation in the DU to CU messages, while the BH Information IE is not included in the corresponding tabular in 9.2.2.2, 9.2.2.8, and 9.2.2.10.
Considering that the per F1-U tunnel BH information is only needed to be configured to the gNB-DU by the gNB-CU, the BH Information is not needed for the Additional PDCP Duplication TNL Items in the  gNB-DU to gNB-CU messages. To keep the tabular align with the ASN.1 part in backward compatible way, the BH information should be added with some clarification that it should be ignored by the receiver (gNB-CU).
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 8/11/2023. Original source : Huawei, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, CATT, Lenovo, Samsung
summaryOfChange:
Add the BH information IE as child IE of Additional PDCP Duplication TNL Items, and clarify this IE will not be used in this release, in the tabular of the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE, and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUIRED message.

Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has impact on the functional specification of the BH information configuration for supporting the intra-gNB-DU CA-based PDCP duplication. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the BH information configuration for additional F1-U tunnels if the IAB-node served UE DRB supports more than 2 RLC channels in CA based duplication.
title: Configuration of BH information for DRBs support CA based duplication

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is nonalignment with other SI required to be broadcast from gNB-CU to gNB-DU
reasonForChange:
In RAN3#120, it was agreed in R3-233521 to correct the SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND by clarifying that the SystemInformation message list is required by the gNB-CU to be sent to the gNB-DU for broadcast of one or several Other SI.  

Since according to TS 38.331, the SystemInformation message is used to convey one or more System Information Blocks or one or more Positioning System Information Blocks, a similar clarification is needed in the POSITIONING SYSTEM INFORMATION DELIVERY COMMAND message regarding the positioning SI message to be broadcast.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
1/ References pointing to unknown IEs (deleted from a previous version).
2/ no means to release multicast dedicated F1-U tunnels.
3/ erroneous receiver behavior.
reasonForChange:
1/ The procedural text of the distribution setup request still contains references to NR CGI and UE reference which have been replaced by indicating instead an MBS Multicast F1-U Context Descriptor IE. 
2/ The description of the Multicast Distribution Release procedure seems to restrict its usage to the removal of shared F1-U tunnel. It can however also be used to remove dedicated F1-U tunnels established for multicast.
3/ the gNB-DU is said receiving the multicast distribution release command message but this is wrong as the receiver of this message should be the gNB-CU.
summaryOfChange:

2/ the purpose of the ditribution release command procedure is made broader to encompass all cases.
3/ the receiver of the distribution release command message is replaced by gNB-CU.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the MBS function.

consequencesIfNotApproved: UE continues SDT without anchor relocation transaction in case large size of SDT data arrived which would result in in poor radio efficiency for the data transfer.
reasonForChange:
In the technically endorsed draft CR to TS38.300 R3-234736, the following note is captured for large size of UL SDT data arrival in case SDT without anchor relocation.
NOTE x:	The last serving gNB may terminate the SDT procedure and direct the UE to continue in RRC_INACTIVE state by sending the RRCRelease message based on the BSR received from the UE in case of uplink SDT data exceeding the data size threshold.
But in case of SDT without UE context relocation, the Last serving gNB is not able to receive the BSR from UE, therefore, it cannot determine large size UL SDT Data Arrival. 

To support such feature, in case the BSR received from the UE indicates oversize UL SDT data, the receiving gNB informs the last serving gNB about it.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 11/1/2023. Original source : Huawei, China Telecom, Ericsson, Qualcomm Incorporated, China Unicom, ZTE, LG Electronics, CATT, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, Samsung
summaryOfChange: Extend the SDT Termination Request IE in the XnAP: RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT CONFIRM message with a new codepoint “Large SDT volume from BSR”.
title: Support of oversize UL SDT Data Arrival [Large SDT Uplink Data]

consequencesIfNotApproved: Errors in SDT procedure text, missing abbreviation, “shall” in Notes.
reasonForChange:
Abbreviation for SDT is missing.
Error in Note 4 in 8.18.1, upon receiving UE INACTIVITY NOTIFICATION message from the gNB-DU, if the gNB-CU is not the serving gNB-CU, i.e. the receiving gNB in case of without anchor relocation, this gNB-CU will not be the node to make decision on SDT termination.
Note 4 in 8.18.1, Note 1 in 8.18.2, contains “shall” which should be avoided. Considering the paragraphs below Note 4, it is better to void these Notes and change the text as normative procedure text.
Considering that there are “terminate the SDT” and “terminate the ongoing SDT procedure”, it is better to use the latter one in all the related parts.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The target IAB donor is not able to obtain IAB authorized status during the Handover Preparation procedure, thus cannot determine whether to allocate and include IAB operation related configurations in the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message.
reasonForChange:
According to TS 23.501, the IAB node can access the network when it is not authorized for IAB operation, or when the authorization status changes from “authorized” to “not authorized”, which is cited in the below. 
In R17, inter-CU topology adaptation for IAB node has been supported. Therefore, inter-CU migration procedure may be initiated (e.g., due to deterioration of radio link quality) for an IAB node which is not authorized. Currently, the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST message doesn’t include the authorization status of the IAB node. Although the IAB Node Indication IE is already included in the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST message, it can only indicate that the handover is for an IAB node and cannot indicate the authorization status of the IAB node. 
As we can see, during inter-CU migration, the target donor cannot obtain the authorization status until reception of NGAP PATH SWITCH ACK message. That means the target donor cannot obtain the authorization status before sending the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message. According to TS 38.401, during inter-CU migration, the target donor allocates BAP address, new TNL address and default BAP configuration for the IAB node after receiving HO request. And then the target donor includes these configurations in the new RRC configuration as part of the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message. So it is not clear whether the target donor allocates and includes the IAB operation related configuration (i.e. BAP address, new TNL address and default BAP configuration) in the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message even though it doesn’t know the authorization status of the IAB node. 
This CR provides the 38.423 modification for the target donor including the IAB authorization status in the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST message.
summaryOfChange:
The IAB Authorization Status IE is added in the XnAP HANDOVER REQUEST message.

Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR has impact on the Handover Preparation procedure for an IAB-MT.
title: Handling of IAB authorization status during MT migration

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The S-NG-RAN node would not be able to indicate an appropriate cause value for not admitted PDU sessions at S-NG-RAN node modification.

Tabular protocol representation would not be aligned with ASN.1 protocol specification.
reasonForChange:
In 8.3.3, the M-NG-RAN node initiated S-NG-RAN node Modification Preparation procedure, it says that “The S-NG-RAN node shall include the PDU sessions that have not been admitted in the PDU Session Resources Not Admitted List IE with an appropriate cause value.”.

In S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message, there is an IE named as id-PDUSessionNotAdmitted-SNModResponse in asn.1, but in the tabular, it was wrongly named as PDU Session Resources Not Admitted to be Added List IE, which should be updated to PDU Session Resources Not Admitted List IE, as this IE includes both the PDU session not admitted to be added and modified, and to be aligned with above mentioned procedural text.

This IE should refer to 9.2.1.3 but it was wrongly referred to 9.2.1.27 which is the PDU Session List without cause and hard to be extended to include cause for each PDU session. RAN3 agreed to introduce a new optional sub-IE refer to PDU Session Resources Not Admitted List IE and mark the existing one as to be ignored if received.
summaryOfChange:
In 9.1.2.6, introduce a new optional sub-IE refer to PDU Session Resources Not Admitted List IE and mark the existing one as to be ignored if received. 

In 9.3.4, update asn.1 accordingly.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has an impact under protocol & functional point of view. The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the indication of not admitted PDU Sessions during S-NG-RAN node modification.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Improper criticality is used for some IE in mobile IAB.
reasonForChange: Currently, the Assigned Criticality of RRC Terminating IAB-Donor gNB-ID IE in F1 SETUP REQUEST message and RRC Terminating IAB-Donor Related Info IE in GNB-DU CONFIGURATION UPDATE message are ignore. That means F1-terminating donor will ignore the procedure if it doesn’t comprehend the two IEs. However, the two IEs are used to let the F1-terminating donor know the gNB ID of RRC-terminating donor (and the BAP address) so that the F1-terminating donor can initiate TMM procedure towards the RRC-terminating donor to migrate the traffic. If the F1-terminating donor simply ignore it, the UE F1-U traffic cannot be transferred via the RRC-terminating donor. So it’s preferred to set the criticality of the two IEs as reject.
summaryOfChange: Correct the Assigned Criticality of RRC Terminating IAB-Donor gNB-ID IE in F1 SETUP REQUEST message and RRC Terminating IAB-Donor Related Info IE in GNB-DU CONFIGURATION UPDATE message to be reject.
title: Corrections on F1AP for mobile IAB

consequencesIfNotApproved: NG-RAN nodes do not know how to handle the IAB authorization status which is transferred by the core network.
reasonForChange:
To support IAB operation, the CN that the IAB-node connects provides authorization status of the IAB-node to RAN. 
If the IAB-node connects to 5GC, the AMF initiates the NG procedure to provide the IAB authorization status to the IAB-donor which provides the C-plane connection to 5GC for the IAB-MT. It’s specified in TS38.413 that if the authorization status is received for an IAB-MT from the AMF, the NG-RAN should use it accordingly, e.g., to ensure that the IAB-node will not serve any UE if the status is set to “not authorized”.
However, it has not been specified how the RAN node uses the authorization status of IAB-node that is received from the core network.
summaryOfChange:
Clause 8.3.1, 8.3.4, 8.4.2 add the reference to TS 38.401 with respect to IAB-node authorization.

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Incorrect delivery of the Uncertainty and Time Information Type IEs to the UE when these two IEs are not needed. 
Misalignment between the ASN.1 and the Tabular.
reasonForChange:
In the Reference Time Information Report message, the Time Reference Information IE is included to indicate the time reference information, wherein it can be observed that the presence for the Uncertainty IE and the Time Information Type IE are optional in the Tabular, but are mandatory in the ASN.1. 
 As specified in TS 38.331 below, both the uncertainty and the timeInfoType IEs are optional. 
ReferenceTimeInfo-r16 ::= SEQUENCE {
    time-r16                            ReferenceTime-r16,
    uncertainty-r16                     INTEGER (0..32767)          OPTIONAL,   -- Need S
    timeInfoType-r16                    ENUMERATED {localClock}     OPTIONAL,   -- Need S
    referenceSFN-r16                    INTEGER (0..1023)           OPTIONAL    -- Cond RefTime
}


Note that the presence of the Reference SFN IE in the Time Reference Information IE is correct since the gNB-CU should always include the referenceSFN and send to UE in the RRC DLInformationTransfer message.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The mobility of mobile IAB node in case the IAB-MT has no PDU session will not be supported.
reasonForChange:
The CR S2-2403710 attached in the SA2 Reply LS S2-2403712 has clarified the details of the handover procedure for a mobile IAB-node with no PDU session.
For NG-based handover, the source NG-RAN node includes the dummy PDU session information in the Handover Required message to inform the AMF of the case that the mobile IAB-MT has no PDU session, so that the AMF will not further involve any SMF and will include the no PDU session indication in the Handover Request message to the target NG-RAN node. 
For Xn-based handover, the target NG-RAN node includes the dummy PDU session information in the Path Switch Request message. In this way, the AMF can know the mobile IAB-MT has no PDU session, so that it will not further involve any SMF and will include a dummy PDU session information in the Path Switch Acknowledge message as well.
Therefore, if we want to support the mobility of mobile IAB-node without any PDU sessions, RAN3 should update the related procedure description to align with SA2.

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).

consequencesIfNotApproved: The AMF may have no knowledge which PDU session(s) have active user plane resource connection and cannot correctly identify SMF(s) with activated user plane PDU session resources.
reasonForChange:
The current MT Communication Handling procedure is lacking information to meet SA2 requirements.
In fact, SA2 requirements are as follows:
In clause 4.8.1.1a of 23.502, it reads:
“For each of the PDU sessions with user plane resources have been activated, the AMF invokes Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext Request (PDU Session ID, Cause, Operation type, User Location Information, Age of Location Information, N2 SM Information (Secondary RAT usage data), CN based MT handling indication) towards SMF. The Operation Type is set to a value that indicates to stop user plane DL data transmissions towards the UE and enable data buffering. The SMF starts data buffering for MT data if the data buffering is handled in SMF.”
This is missing in the NGAP message, and the AMF has no precise knowledge if the user plane resources for a given PDU session is established or not. 
Similarly, during resume, 4.8.2.2 of 23.502

“4b.2       The AMF invokes Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext Request towards SMF indicating the Downlink data delivery for each PDU session with active user plane, if the AMF has requested data buffering as described in clause 4.8.1.1a.”
The AMF may not have knowledge of the list of PDU sessions that have active user plane connection, and requiring the AMF to remember there was DL data/signaling for a given PDU session from the SMF and generate the Update SM Context request towards that SMF correspondingly adds a new requirement to the AMF, and actually it is not needed.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 5/9/2024. Original source : Ericsson, Huawei, Nokia, Xiaomi, Qualcomm Inc., ZTE, CATT
summaryOfChange:
Since the NG-RAN should be able to tell AMF which PDU sessions have corresponding PDU session resources established in the NG-RAN, the NG-RAN can include the list of those PDU session IDs in the MT COMMUNICATION HANDLING REQUEST message to instruct the AMF that the user plane connections for these PDU sessions are to be “Suspended” / “activated” since the UE enters RRC Inactive with long eDRX, so that the AMF can trigger UpdateSmContext correspondingly.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it affects the MT Communication Handling procedure only.
The CR has impact from functional and protocol point of view.
The CR is backwards compatible from a protocol point of view.
title: Correction of MT Communication Handling procedure

consequencesIfNotApproved: Network can not configure the SL-DRX-Config to UE.
reasonForChange:
According to current specification, SL configuration generated by DU is included in SL-PHY-MAC-RLC-Config, and corresponding configuration is included in DU to CU RRC container.
In R17, SL-PHY-MAC-RLC-Config with v1700 suffix is used to capture DRX configuration in 38.331, as shown in below:
SL-PHY-MAC-RLC-Config-v1700 ::=      SEQUENCE {
    sl-DRX-Config-r17                    SL-DRX-Config-r17                                                      OPTIONAL,    -- Need M
    sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-r17      SEQUENCE (SIZE (1..maxSL-LCID-r16)) OF SL-RLC-ChannelID-r17            OPTIONAL, -- Cond L2U2N
    sl-RLC-ChannelToAddModList-r17       SEQUENCE (SIZE (1..maxSL-LCID-r16)) OF SL-RLC-ChannelConfig-r17        OPTIONAL, -- Cond L2U2N
    ...,
}

However, sl-DRX-Config-r17  is missing in DU to CU RRC information.

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is functional gap in the S-CPAC handling between the MN-target SN signalling and MN-source SN signalling. This gap may render SN-initiated S-CPAC not usable.
reasonForChange:
In Rel-18, SN-initiated S-CPAC procedure was enabled. The signalling for the initiation of the procedure reuses Rel.17 CPAC signalling, with added flag to indicate the request is meant to initiate S-CPAC. This request from the SN is converted into a set of S-CPAC Addition requests towards the target SNs. The problem is that the S-CPAC Addition procedure may be acknowledged successfully, but as a “classic” CPAC preparation. The MN is aware of this – but the source SN is not.
The information is important for the source SN, because in case of preparation of a “classic” CPAC, some later steps of the procedure are different between CPAC and S-CPAC (or, to be precise, different in case the source remains prepared for S-CPAC or is to be released).
summaryOfChange:
A new flag is added in the list of prepared target SNs in the S-NODE CHANGE CONFIRM. The flag indicates that the target SN accepted the request as S-CPAC and the source SN will remain prepared.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
The change concerns only one procedure. The change may be considered non-backward-compatible from functional poin of view.
title: Addition of a missing indication in SN-initiated S-CPAC

consequencesIfNotApproved: Mismatch between procedure text and actual behaviour, which may cause implementation to use it in a way that triggers abstract syntax error with criticality reject.
reasonForChange:
The Candidate Cells To Be Cancelled List in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST is included as a conditional IE, but where the conditional text is expressed with a “may”. Further, the procedure text describes that if this IE is included: “only the resources reserved for the cells identified by the included NR CGIs are about to be released”
Conditional IEs are however mandatory if the condition is met so using a may statement and describing behaviour if absent does not comply with the principles of the specification. The error handling is specified in TS 38.413 section 10.3.3 as follows “If an IE/IE group is not included in a received message and the presence of the IE/IE group is mandatory or the presence is conditional and the condition is true according to the version of the specification used by the receiver, an abstract syntax error occurs due to a missing IE/IE group.”
In existing specification, it is currently not possible to use the intended functionality – to delete all if the IE is absent.
summaryOfChange:
It is proposed to remove the possibility to remove all by not including this IE in the procedure text and change it to “shall” in the conditional statement.

abstract: Related stage-2 CR is proposed in R3-244122
consequencesIfNotApproved: The method to provide DL LBT information to the source node, as defined in stage-2, can’t be implemented correctly.
reasonForChange:
At RAN3 #123, additional signalling was defined on F1 to enable the DU to provide information, if needed, concerning the DL LBT failures. This signalling was based on the assumption that the DU of the target gNB will always know when such reporting is needed. This is, however, not true: in case of either “too early handover” or “handover to wrong cell” due to RLF shortly after successful handover, the target DU may not realise that the failure occurred. Once the target CU receives the Failure Indication from the re-establishment node, it can only release the context in the DU. Thus, the collected DL LBT information for the UE will never be provided to the target CU.
Furthermore, the existing description is formulated in a confusing way.
summaryOfChange:
The information about the need to report the recorded DL LBT information is provided to the target DU in the UE Context Release procedure. The description is clarified with a reference to stage-2.

consequencesIfNotApproved: There is gap between RAN2 and RAN3 specs on the understanding of the SRB0/1 relaying Uu Relay RLC channel configuration. SRB0/1 relaying Uu Relay RLC channel may be configured during F1 UE context setup procedure, which is not reasonable.
reasonForChange:
In RAN2 spec TS 38.300, it specifies that Uu Relay RLC channel for Remote UE’s SRB0 relaying is configured after Relay UE’s RRC connection establishment procedure and sending SUI to gNB. However, in RAN3 specs TS 38.401 and TS 38.473, it specifies that it is possible to configure Uu Relay RLC channel for Remote UE’s SRB0/1 relaying during Relay UE’s F1 UE context setup procedure and before sending SUI to gNB. There is gap between RAN2 and RAN3 specs on the understanding of the timing for Uu Relay RLC channel setup for SRB0/1 relaying.

Since there is no relay related indication during relay UE RRC connection setup, the gNB-CU does not know the UE is a relay UE or whether the UE is capable of L2 U2N relay UE operation, it is not reasonable to configure the Uu Relay RLC channel during F1 UE context setup procedure. In addition, it is not reasonable for gNB to configure Uu Relay RLC channel before getting knowledge of the capability of the UE (i.e. receiving relayUE-Operation-L2-r17 in UECapabilityInformation from UE). What’s more, the Uu Relay RLC channel will only be used after bearer mapping is configured, and bearer mapping can be configured after relay UE sending SUI including remote UE’s L2 ID to gNB. So there is no benefits to configure the Uu Relay RLC channel in advance. 

Based on the discussion above, it is suggested that Uu Relay RLC channel is not configured during F1 UE context setup procedure.
summaryOfChange:
In clause 8.3.1.2, remove Uu Relay RLC channel setup related procedural text.
In 9.2.2.1, clarify that the “Uu RLC Channel to Be Setup List” in UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message is not used in this version of the specification.
In 9.2.2.2, clarify that the “Uu RLC Channel Setup List” and “Uu RLC Channel Failed to be Setup List” are not used in this version of the specification.

consequencesIfNotApproved: LMF does not know the preconfigured SRS is the activated.
reasonForChange:
According to TS 38.331 and TS 38.305, the SRS for positioning configuration in RRC_INACTIVE state may be pre-configured in the target device. The target device may send an "RRC Resume Request" message with a new specific resume cause to the receiving gNB when a configured periodic or triggered location event has been detected to request activation of the pre-configured SRS for positioning. 

In this case, the LMF needs to know the activation of the preconfigured SRS so that it can send the measurement request to other gNBs. To support it, it’s proposed to indicate the activation in Positioning Information Update message. As for the preconfigured multiple SRS configurations, the UE is configured with only one SRS for positioning configuration for each validity area, if using Positioning Information Update message with one activation indication, LMF knows the validity area that the UE’s current serving cell belongs, then it can know which preconfigured SRS is activated.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The multi-path relay based PDCP duplication may be not implemented properly.
reasonForChange:
In clause 8.3.3.2, Execute Duplication IE could also be applied to multi-path SRB. That is, if the RRC-Container IE for multi-path SRB and the Execute Duplication IE are both included in the UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message, the gNB-DU shall perform multi-path relay based duplication for the multi-path SRB for the included RRC-Container IE.
In legacy, when CU requests to setup/modify a SRB configured with CA based PDCP duplication, DU shall indicates the LCID for the primary path in the response message, as shown below. 

For multi-path split SRB with duplication, the same procedure is needed. That is, when CU requests to setup/modify a multi-path SRB with PDCP duplication (more than 1 leg on direct path), DU needs to indicate the LCID for the primary path (LCID for primary RLC entity) in the response message. However, in the following procedural text in clause 8.3.4.2, the multi-path related description is missing.
-	A list of successfully established SRBs with logical channel identities for primary path shall be included in the SRB Setup List IE only if CA based PDCP duplication is initiated for the concerned SRBs.
-	A list of successfully modified SRBs with logical channel identities for primary path shall be included in the SRB Modified List IE only if CA based PDCP duplication is initiated for the concerned SRBs.
As shown below, Duplication Activation IE is reused for multi-path relay based PDCP duplication. However in the semantics description in the tabular in 9.2.2.7, the multi-path related description is missing.
summaryOfChange:
In clause 8.3.3.2, add “or multi-path relay based duplication” to clarify the procedure also applies for multi-path SRB.
In clause 8.3.4.2, add “or multi-path relay based duplication” for SRBs to clarify that DU should also indicate LCID for the primary path in the response message for multi-path SRBs (if there are more than 1 leg on direct path).
In clause 9.2.2.7, add “or multi-path relay based” in the semantics description of Duplication Activation IE to align with the procedural text.


Impact Analysis:

consequencesIfNotApproved: Wrong procedural text exists and wrong criticality is used by the Retrieve UE Context Confirm procedure.
reasonForChange:
Issue #1:
The Retrieve UE Context Confirm procedure is used in two scenarios:
new NG-RAN node to inform the old NG-RAN node whether the S-NG-RAN node associated with the old NG-RAN node for the UE that was indicated during UE context retrieval is kept or not by the new NG-RAN node during RRC resumption.
in case of RACH based SDT without UE context relocation, to request the termination of SDT session from the new NG-RAN node to the old NG-RAN node.

The following procedural text is found: 
Upon reception of the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT CONFIRM message, the old NG-RAN node shall release the resources related to the UE-associated signalling connection between the old NG-RAN node and the new NG-RAN node, as specified in TS 37.340 [8].
In case of (a), the old NG-RAN node will only release the resources related to the UE-associated signalling connection between the old NG-RAN node and the new NG-RAN node upon receiving the UE CONTEXT RELEASE message from the new NG-RAN node, therefore, the above procedural text is incorrect.
In case of (b), if the old NG-RAN node decides to terminate the ongoing SDT, it will send RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT FAILURE message to the new NG-RAN node, and if the old NG-RAN node decides to not terminate the ongoing SDT session, the SDT session will keep going, therefore, the above procedural text is incorrect as well.

Issue #2:

In 9.1.1.16, the message type is defined as reject, this aligns with the other procedures related to Retrieve UE Context or Partial UE Context Transfer, but in asn.1 criticality ignore is used.
 
Issue #3:
In 9.2.3.68, it is said that 
This IE indicates whether the UE Context is kept at the S-NG-RAN node in case of an M-NG-RAN node handover without S-NG-RAN node change or inter-M-NG-RAN node RRC resume without S-NG-RAN node change.
It is unclear what is “M-NG-RAN node handover without S-NG-RAN node change”, considering that this IE will not be used in case of intra-M-NG-RAN node handover, it is better to update it to “inter-M-NG-RAN node handover without S-NG-RAN node change”.
summaryOfChange:
For Issue #1: remove the mentioned incorrect procedural text.

For Issue #2: change the criticality of retrieveUEContextConfirm procedure from ignore to reject in asn.1. (NBC)

For Issue #3: update the “M-NG-RAN node handover without S-NG-RAN node change” to “inter-M-NG-RAN node handover without S-NG-RAN node change”.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only impacts the handling of Retrieve UE Context Confirm procedure and the related IEs.
This CR has functional and protocol impact, and it is NBC.
title: Correction on Retrieve UE Context Confirm

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The Port Number is always indicated in the N3IWF user location information when not possible (e.g., if NAT is not detected.). 
The TCP source port number is not consistent with SA2 specification.
reasonForChange:
In TS 23.501, it is described that the port number is optional for the N3IWF user location information as follows. 

The User Location Information may correspond to:
<Skip the irrelevance >
-	In the case of Untrusted non-3GPP access: TAI, the UE local IP address used to reach the N3IWF and optionally the UDP source port number if NAT is detected.
-	In the case of Trusted non-3GPP access: TAI, TNAP/TWAP Identifier, the UE/N5CW device local IP address used to reach the TNGF/TWIF and optionally the UDP source port number if NAT is detected.
However, in the UserLocationInformationN3IWF in the ASN.1, the port number is mandatory, while it is optional in the Tabular correctly.  

In addition, it can be observed above that only UDP source port number is indicated, but in the semantic descriptions the TCP source port number is described. 

Note that the TAI IE is included in the N3IWF user location information IE starting from Rel-17.  Hence the new N3IWF user location information also includes the TAI IE.
summaryOfChange:
Add a new N3IWF user location information without port number IE including the IP Address and the optional TAI.  
Update the presence of the Port Number in the legacy N3IWF user location information IE to be mandatory to align with the ASN.1. 
Remove the “TCP” from the semantic descriptions. 
Rename the N3IWF user location information IE to N3IWF user location information with port number IE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment with LPP and CT4 specs
reasonForChange:
RAN2 agreed in RAN2#126 a CR R2-2405861 to TS 37.355 correcting Local Cartesian Coordinates in LPP. 
One change that affects RAN3 is that RAN2 have specified a new element in the Relative Cartesian coordinates for local origin representation that indicates the horizontal axes orientation information for the reference point:

Extract from R2-2405861 starts here:
=======================================
NOTE 5:	The locations may be provided in either geodetic coordinates (RelativeLocation) or local Cartesian coordinates (RelativeCartesianLocation), but not both. 
======================================= End of extract.

Currently, in NRPPa, the Relative Cartesian coordinates are defined in section 9.2.46 as the TRP Position Relative Cartesian IE, that refers to Relative Cartesian Location IE on 9.2.50 and is associated to a Reference Point IE defined in 9.2.51.

To align with LPP and CT4 specifications, RAN3 can introduce the horizontal axes orientation information and Reference Point High Accuracy Access Position to the Reference Point IE, when the ReferencePoint in the  Reference Point IE CHOICE is set to Coordinate ID .  

However, due to NBC issue, it is not possible to add the IEs directly in 9.2.51 in the SEQUENCE (it is not extensible in ASN.1). Instead, a BC solution that does not impact legacy functionality is to introduce an additional LocalOrigin IE as new CHOICE in the Reference point IE (9.2.51) that includes the Coordinate ID, Reference Point High Accuracy Access Position and the horizontal axes orientation information. 

To avoid introducing another way to signal the Coordinate ID as a standalone choice, the horizontal axes orientation information is mandatorily present in the Local Origin IE.
summaryOfChange:
Addition of new LocalOrigin IE CHOICE in the Reference Point IE (9.2.51), that includes Coordinate IE (M), Reference Point High Accuracy Access Position (O) and Horizontal Axes Orientation (M), encoded as in LPP, i.e., INTEGER(0..3599)

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR does not have impact from protocol point of view. 
This CR may have an impact from functional point of view because 
it impacts only the Reference Point IE IE .
title: Correction of TRP Geographical coordinates [PosLocalCoords]

consequencesIfNotApproved: LMF cannot know the reference signal that was used for measuring UE Rx-Tx time difference.
reasonForChange:
RAN3 agreed to reuse PDC’s UE Rx-Tx Time Difference measurement in NRPPa also for positioning purpose. UE Rx-Tx Time Difference as specified in RRC can be configured to be reported using either CSI-RS for tracking or PRS. However, these information are not currently captured in NRPPa.
The IE MeasObjectRxTxDiff is used to configure the measurement object for UE Rx-Tx time difference measurement.
MeasObjectRxTxDiff information element
-- ASN1START
-- TAG-MEASOBJECTRXTXDIFF-START


MeasObjectRxTxDiff-r17 ::=      SEQUENCE {
    dl-Ref-r17      CHOICE {
        prs-Ref-r17             NULL,
        csi-RS-Ref-r17          NULL,
        ...
    }                               OPTIONAL,   -- Need R
    ...
}

-- TAG-MEASOBJECTRXTXDIFF-STOP
-- ASN1STOP

 
It can be helpful for LMF to know the reference signal used for the measurement, especially since LMF knows the source of the signal for all measurements currently reported in E-CID. For example, if the UE reports a UE Rx-Tx time difference using CSI-RS, LMF knows that this signal comes from a narrower beam than the PRS. It can hence correlate the CSI-RS RSRP/RSRQ measurement, if present, and UE Rx-Tx time difference measurement together to determine the accuracy of the measurements and derive the UE's location uncertainty when reporting the result to the LCS client.
summaryOfChange:
Include helpful information on the reference signal that was used for measuring the UE Rx-Tx Time Difference.

Impact Analysis

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it is only adding the reference signal type for UE Rx-Tx time difference measurement in the E-CID measurement result.
This CR has functional and protocol impact.
title: Correction of UE Rx-Tx Time difference measurement

consequencesIfNotApproved: Unclear behaviour of NG-RAN when receiving the Positioning Broadcast Cells IE.
reasonForChange:
The description of the Assistance Information IE in the ASSISTANCE INFORMATION CONTROL message is not clear. If the information is received, it is immediately broadcasted and not stored.

The Assistance Information has to be present when the Broadcast IE is set to ‘start’.

The Broadcast IE is mandatory. There is no gNB behavior defined for the case when the Broadcast IE is absent. therefore the procedure should fail in this case.

If the NG-RAN receives the Positioning Broadcast Cells IE in the ASSISTANCE INFORMATION CONTROL message, then the information in the procedure (i.e., Assistance Information and Broadcast IE) is valid only for the indicated list of cells.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify in 8.4.1.2 that the received Assistance Information IE replaces any previously received assistance information, rather than “stored”.
Clarify in 8.4.1.3 that the Assistance Information IE has to be included when the Broadcast IE is set to ‘start’.
Clarify in 8.4.1.3 that the Broadcast IE is mandatory.
Clarify that when the Positioning Broadcast Cells IE is received, the procedure is limited to those cells only. Delete IE semantics.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
The CR has isolated impact because the change affects only the Assistance Information Control procedure.
The CR is backwards compatible from a protocol point of view.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The CPAC MCG configuration cannot be cancelled for the split gNB once configured.
reasonForChange:
For CPAC, it was captured that the MN sends to the UE an RRC reconfiguration message including a list of RRC reconfiguration* messages including both MCG and SCG configuration (RRC reconfiguration**) which are to be applied together upon CPAC execution. In addition, in RAN3#115 chairman notes, the following agreements can be found for CPAC:
In CPA and MN/SN initiated inter-SN CPC, MN can: 
Update/modify previous CPAC configurations provided in CPAC addition using MN initiated SN modification procedure 
Cancel all prepared PSCells at target SN and release the target SN using MN initiated SN release procedure 
In CPA and MN/SN initiated inter-SN CPC, target SN can:
Update/modify previous CPAC configurations provided in CPAC addition using SN initiated SN modification procedure 
Add prepared PSCells within the limit given by the MN or source SN using SN initiated SN modification procedure
Cancel some of the prepared PSCells using SN initiated SN modification procedure. 
Cancel all prepared PSCells using SN initiated SN release procedure 
In SN initiated inter-SN CPC, source SN can:
Update/modify previous CPC configurations provided in CPC preparation using SN change required procedure
Cancel all prepared PSCells at target SN and release the target SN using SN change required procedure
New IEs are introduced in SN change required message indicating CPC configuration modification and target SN release. 
In MN/SN initiated inter-SN CPC, MN can inform source SN about the triggered target SN release or some prepared PSCells cancellation at a target SN using:
A new class2 XnAP procedure
A new class2 X2AP procedure 
However, in case that the MN is a split gNB, it is unclear how the MN cancels the prepared MCG configuration(s) at the gNB-DU corresponding to the cancelled conditional SCG configuration(s) for CPAC.
summaryOfChange:
Editorial reorgnization of the procedure text for the CPAC MCG Information IE 
Add a new codepoint CPAC-cancel to the CPAC Trigger in the CPAC MCG Information IE to handle the canclelation scenario
Add correspodning procedure text
Add corresponding ASN.1 changes

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the MCG configuration and the related procedure text for the CPAC operation.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The tabular is not aligned with ASN.1.
The IAB-DU migration triggered by the source CU will fail because one logical gNB-DU can only maintain F1 connection towards one CU.
reasonForChange:
To support the mobile IAB-DU migration, R18 mobile IAB introduced two new the MIAB F1 SETUP TRIGGERING message and the MIAB F1 SETUP OUTCOME NOTIFICATION message. The Criticality of these two messages are designed to be “reject”, same as other IAB related messages. However, in the ASN.1 part, the criticality of the two messages are assigned to be “ignore”. 
To support the additional ULI report for the UE served by the mobile IAB-node, the Mobile IAB-MT User Location Information IE can be reported by the mobile IAB-DU to the F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU. This IE contains the NR CGI and TAI of the mobile IAB-MT’s serving cell. The TAI is optionally included, because it is possible that the mIAB-DU’s cell share same TAI as the mIAB-MT’s serving cell. In ASN.1, the presence of the TAI is assigned as Mandatory in the Mobile IAB-MT User Location Information IE, not align with the tabular.  
In the procedure text for Mobile IAB F1 Setup Triggering procedure, the executor of the establishing TNL connection/security connection to target F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU is the gNB-DU who receiving the message. But actually, it should be the target logical gNB-DU to establish connection towards the target CU.

In ASN.1, change the criticality of the MIAB F1 SETUP TRIGGERING message and the MIAB F1 SETUP OUTCOME NOTIFICATION message to “reject”.
In tabular, change the presence of the TAI in the Mobile IAB-MT User Location Information IE as “M”.
Update the procedure text for Mobile IAB F1 Setup Triggering procedure to clarify it is the target logical gNB-DU to estabilish connection towards target F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Human readable AMF name is not available to the gNB when removing NG. This may cause errors if the AMF had previously signaled the Extended AMF Name IE at NG setup.
reasonForChange:
The Extended AMF Name IE was added to the NG SETUP RESPONSE message following a request from operators to have a human readable AMF name signaled to the NG-RAN node.

Currently the NG REMOVAL RESPONSE message carries the AMF Name IE but it is not possible to add the Extended AMF Name IE. If the AMF had previously signaled the Extended AMF Name IE in the NG SETUP RESPONSE message, the AMF Name IE was ignored by the gNB. Hence, when removing NG to the same AMF, it may not be possible to correlate the information received in the two procedures. This may cause errors.

Therefore, it is needed to also include the A-IoT Support IE in the RAN CONFIGURATION UPDATE message.

Likewise, when the source gNB selects an SP CSI-RS for activation, it also needs to determine the appropriate TCI State and indicate it to the candidate gNB, this ensures that the SP CSI-RS can be properly activated with the correct TCI State.

As the LTM procedures in F1AP introduced for intra-CU LTM in Rel-18 are reused for inter-CU LTM. In principle, the same indicator should be introduced in the Handover Request procedure in XnAP for inter-CU LTM to have a harmonized design with F1AP.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The specification is not clear.
reasonForChange:
In NR Femto, the new GW Context Release Indication IE is introduced in UE context release request message, however the corresponding procedural text is missing. It is better to add procedural text for the new IE to make the specification clearer.
The Target RAN Node ID IE is introduced in NR Femto. In case of NG handover towards an NR Femto node connected to an NR Femto GW, to allow the NR Femto GW to identify the target NR Femto node, AMF includes the Global RAN Node ID of the target NR Femto node in the HANDOVER REQUEST message, which is specified in TS 38.300. Suggest to add the reference.
In the semantics description of GW Context Release Indication IE, it described that “This IE indicates to the AMF that the gNB has successfully performed an Xn HO for the UE to a target gNB.”. The main point is if receiving the indication, the NR Femto GW shall release the UE context. No need to specify this indication is sent due to which scenario / what the Femto GW consider about. Since the IE description is clearly enough, suggest to remove the semantics description of GW Context Release Indication IE.
summaryOfChange:
In clause 8.3.2.2, add corresponding procedural text for the new GW Context Release Indication IE.
In clause 8.4.2.2, add the reference TS 38.300 to the description for Target RAN Node ID IE.
In 9.3.1.274, remove the semantics description of the GW Context Release Indication IE.
title: Corrections for Femto

consequencesIfNotApproved: Cannot support SBFD RACH configuration optimization.
reasonForChange:
Two RACH configuration options are specified for SBFD RA in TS 38.331. A cell can configure only one RACH configuration option. This can be either: 1) A single RACH configuration that supports both non-SBFD RA operation and SBFD RA operation, or 2) A dual RACH configuration where a RACH configuration is used for non-SBFD RA operation and an additional RACH configuration is designated for SBFD RA operation. 
For option 2, the exchange of SBFD RACH configuration between NG-RAN is needed for RACH optimization. For CU/DU split case, gNB-DU provides SBFD RACH configuration to gNB-CU firstly and then gNB-CU further provide it to neighbour gNB-DU(s) by neighbour gNB-CU(s).
summaryOfChange: Add SBFD across symbol type in NR PRACH Configuration List.
title: Correction on SBFD RACH configuration for F1AP

consequencesIfNotApproved: The RF parameters in NR cell information IEs remain inaccurate.
reasonForChange:
For E-UTRA Cells, we include one “EARFCN” (indicating the central frequency of the transmission band) and one “transmission bandwidth” per UL/DL/TDD within the “Cell Information” IEs. These two IEs are enough to deduce the exact location of the entire transmission band, i.e. the frequency of the lowest carrier and the highest carrier.
For NR Cells we include one “NR ARFCN” (indicating the “Point A” rather than the central frequency), one SCS and one “transmission bandwidth” per UL/DL/TDD within the “Cell Information” IEs.
However, the mechanism to determine the frequency raster has changed a lot for NR cells compared with E-UTRA ones, making these parameters far not enough to deduce the location of the entire transmission band, e.g. lack of the “offset to carrier” to indicate the frequency of the lowest carrier.
For the UL,it has been corrected in Rel-16 SON/MDT WI.However,for DL,it is suggested to correct via a separate CR.
summaryOfChange:
Adding one optional DL Carrier List for each DL, which further contains one NR SCS, one Offset to Carrier and one Carrier Bandwidth, and clafitying that if this IE is present the original “transmission bandwidth” IE should be ignored.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR is a clarification and has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the Cell information.
This CR is backward compatible.
title: Correction on RF parameters in NR cell information(XnAP)

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the CR is not approved, in the case of an gNB-DU becomes supporting IAB-node access after its F1 interface establishment, this gNB-DU is unable to obtain its BAP address unless it re-establishes its F1 interface with the gNB-CU, then all connected UEs’ context are erased and need to be re-setup, this will cause two much signaling overhead and long time service interruption.
reasonForChange:
In current specification, if gNB-DU is IAB-donor-DU, IAB-donor-CU can only assign a BAP address to IAB-donor-DU during the F1 Setup procedure.  
However, from the perspective of implementation, the gNB-DU may be upgraded to be IAB-donor-DU after its F1 interface establishment, or the IAB-donor-DU’s served cell may be updated to allow IAB-MT access at some later stage after the F1 Setup due to the operator’s deployment strategy changes. In such two cases, it is unable to obtain BAP address for the upgraded gNB-DU unless it re-establishes its F1 interface with the gNB-CU, which will introduce a lot of signaling overhead and service interruption for some existing UE traffic served by this gNB-DU because the F1 setup procedure will erase any application level configuration data and all UE context. 
To address the above issue, the existing procedures of gNB-DU Configuration Update and gNB-CU Configuration Update can be modified to allow the BAP address allocation for IAB-donor-DU. Since the IAB-donor-CU can know an gNB-DU is an IAB-donor-DU from the SIB1 of this gNB-DU and by other way (e.g. OAM), and it has been agreed in last meeting that “How to identify the IAB-donor-DU is up to gNB-CU implementation” , the following two cases should be supported. 
Case 1: After gNB-DU supports IAB node access, it sends gNB-DU Configuration Update message to gNB-CU. Based on the iab-Support IE in SIB1 carried in this message, the gNB-CU can know the gNB-DU is an IAB-donor-DU, and assign a BAP address to the the gNB-DU via gNB-DU Configuration Update Acknowledge message.
Case 2: gNB-CU knows the gNB-DU becomes supporting IAB-node access from other means, e.g. via the notification from OAM. Then the gNB-CU assigns a BAP address to the upgraded gNB-DU via gNB-CU Configuration Update message.
summaryOfChange:
Add BAP Address IE in gNB-DU Configuration Update Acknowledge message in section 9.2.1.8, and add the corresponding description in section 8.2.4.2. 
Add BAP Address IE in gNB-CU Configuration Update message in section 9.2.1.10, and add the corresponding description in section 8.2.5.2. 
Add the corresponding ASN.1. 


Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because the changes only impact IAB functionality.
This CR has an impact under functional point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the IAB related definitions and IAB procedure.
The changes are backward compatible.
title: Correction on BAP address configuration for IAB-donor-DU

consequencesIfNotApproved: The UE IP maximum data rate included in the security indication may not be sent to the NG-RAN node when the SMF acquires the UE UP IP maximum data rate after the handover from EPC to 5GC.
reasonForChange:
Currently the Maximum Integrity Protected Data Rate IE included in the Security Indication IE, is only transferred in the PDU session resource setup procedure, path switch request and Handover Resource Allocation procedure. 

In section 5.17.2.2.2 of TS 23.501, it is described that:


It can be observed after the EPC to 5GC handover, the UE shall initiate the PDU session modification procedure to provide the maximum IP data rate to the SMF, in case these PDU sessions are established at the EPC side. 

This procedure is also described in the section 4.3.3 of TS 23.502 for PDU session modification procedure. 

Hence, when the SMF acquires the UP IP maximum data rate from the UE, it should provide the updated UP IP maximum data rate included in the Security Indication IE in the PDU session resource modify procedure.
summaryOfChange:
Include the ability to change the maximum IP data rate within the Security Indication IE in PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY REQUEST message.
 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the UP integrity protection after EPC to 5GC handover.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The measurement periodicity is not agligned with SRS periodicity and the measurement may fail or be totally wrong withtout possibility to detect the mistake.
reasonForChange:
The current values of the Measurement periodicity for UL and UL&DL positioning are as follows:

The measurement periodicity share the same IE with E-CID positioning measurement periodicity, which is aligned with UE RRM measurment report interval in RRC, which is as follows:

ReportInterval ::=                  ENUMERATED {ms120, ms240, ms480, ms640, ms1024, ms2048, ms5120, ms10240, ms20480, ms40960,
                                                    min1,min6, min12, min30 }

This is incorrect because that for UL and UL&DL positioning it is gNB to measure the SRS sent from the UE, while the RRM measurement is for the UE to measure DL reference signals. The SRS periodicity has the following values:


It is obvious that in the measurement periodicity, at least the following values are not aligned with the SRS periodicity: 120ms, 240ms, 480ms, 1024ms, 2048ms, 1min, 6min, 12min, and 30min.


Thus, the measurement periodicity for the UL and UL&DL positioning should be aligned with SRS periodicity, rather than the RRC report interval. The values of SRS periodicity should be added in the measurement periodicity for UL and UL&DL positioning, including 160ms, 320ms, 1280ms 2560ms, 81920ms.

Some of the values in current measurement periodicity should be subtituded by the similar value that can be aligned with the SRS periodicity. For example, the value 1min should be subtituded by a similar value, such as 61440ms. The value of 6min, 12min, and 30min can be subtituted by a similar value such as 368640ms, 737280ms, and 1843200ms.

If SRS periodicity interval is not accurate, there will be some redudency in mesurements, inacurate reporting, shifting of the report measurements update, that could not be deteced by the LMF. As conscequence the report could be totally incurate …
summaryOfChange:
Add the missed values of SRS periodicity including 160ms, 320ms, 1280ms 2560ms, 81920ms in the Measurement Periodicity to align with SRS periodicity.
Add the value of 61440ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 1min in the Measurement Periodicity.
Add the value of 368640ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 6min in the Measurement Periodicity.
Add the value of 737280ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 12min in the Measurement Periodicity.
Add the value of 1843200ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 30min in the Measurement Periodicity.
Add the description that the newly added values are not applicable in E-CID MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST message.
Add the description that some of the values, which are not aligned with SRS periodicity, are not applicable in Measurement Request message.

Rev1: it is proposed to add a new code point to the Measurement Periodicity IE and introduce a new Extended Measurement Periodicity IE in the MEASUREMENT REQUEST message.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release). The change has functional impact and ASN.1 backward compatible impact.
title: Correction on Measurement Periodicity

consequencesIfNotApproved: CU/DU may decode the parameters with wrong QoS mapping table. No suitable PQI values/QoS parameters would be applicable for sidelink communication or the explanation of a value (value 90) exists in both 5QI and PQI table would be incorrect.
reasonForChange:
For R16 NR sidelink, PQI is defined and used as a reference to PC5 QoS characteristics. In addition, the one-to-one mapping of standardized PQI values to PC5 QoS characteristics is specified in TS 23.287. In 9.3.1.126, for the Non Dynamic PQI Descriptor, it shall be the PQI instead of 5QI used to indicate the QoS Characteristics for a standardized or pre-configured PQI for sidelink.
In 9.3.1.127, wrong IE names are used in the explanation of condition “ifGBRflow”. Specifically, GBR QoS Flow Information IE and QoS Flow Level QoS Parameters IE are used for Uu DRB setup. However, for indication of PC5 GBR QoS flow, the PC5 QoS Flow Bit Rates IE shall be present in the PC5 QoS parameters IE.
For better reading of a superior specification, the “PC5 Flow Bit Rates” is suggested to change to “PC5 QoS Flow Bit Rates”. The reference specification for IE “Guaranteed Flow Bit Rate” and “Maximum Flow Bit Rate” are suggested to change to TS 23.287.
summaryOfChange:
Change 1: In 9.3.1.126, in the semantics description of 5QI IE, the “5QI” is changed to “PQI”, and the reference specification is changed to TS 23.287 [40] accordingly.
Change 2: In 9.3.1.127, the explanation of condition “ifGBRflow” is changed to “This IE shall be present if the PC5 QoS Flow Bit Rates IE is present in the PC5 QoS parameters IE.”.
Change 3: In 9.3.1.122, the “PC5 Flow Bit Rates” is changed to “PC5 QoS Flow Bit Rates”. The reference specification for IE “Guaranteed Flow Bit Rate” and “Maximum Flow Bit Rate” are changed to TS 23.287.

Impact Analysis: 
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because no suitable values/QoS parameters would be applicable for sidelink if 5QI QoS mapping table is used by CU/DU to decide PC5 QoS parameters for SL DRB configuration.
This CR has an impact under functional point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects the determination of PC5 QoS parameters when configuring SL DRB.

In TS 38.331, RAN2 agrees to introduce SIB15 containing Provision of disaster roaming information, which enables network to indicate which PLMNs' UEs are allowed to do disaster roaming.

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear what is to be expected by the target NG-RAN node for active and inactive MBS sessions.

1/ Area Session ID shall be sent for both inactive and active sessions for location dependent sessions, otherwise the function is broken.

2/ for active sessions, area information shall be sent when available, however it is useless and heavy to send all MBS service areas of location depdendent MBS sessions even for the active session: only one service area can be sent.

3/ for inactive sessions MBS session QoS parameters, MBS service Area and Data forwarding information are not needed. 
It is cleaner to organize this in two lists to make it clear what source is ecpected to send in which case and what target should expect to receive.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Not aligned with SA2 specifications.
reasonForChange:
At previous SA2#151-e meeting, SA2 agreed in S2-2204909 and S2-2204910 to clarify that the NG-RAN should consider that the UE is only allowed to access non-CAG cells (i.e. can not access CAG cells) if the Allowed PNI-NPN List is not received.  
-	During transition from RRC Inactive to RRC Connected state:
-	When the UE initiates the RRC Resume procedure for RRC Inactive to RRC Connected state transition in a CAG cell, NG-RAN shall reject the RRC Resume request from the UE if none of the CAG Identifiers supported by the CAG cell are part of the UE's Allowed CAG list according to the Mobility Restrictions received from the AMF or if no Allowed CAG list has been received from the AMF.
<Skip the irrelevant>
-	During connected mode mobility procedures, within NG-RAN, i.e. handover procedures as described in clause 4.9.1 of TS 23.502 [3]:
-	Source NG-RAN shall not handover the UE to a target NG-RAN node if the target is a CAG cell and none of the CAG Identifiers supported by the CAG cell are part of the UE's Allowed CAG list in the Mobility Restriction List or if no Allowed CAG list has been received from the AMF;

While in section 9.4 of TS 38.300, the following descriptions are provided. 
If the roaming and access restriction information is not available for a UE at the gNB, the gNB shall consider that there is no restriction for subsequent mobility actions

Hence there exists misalignment between the stage 2 and SA2 descriptions, which should be corrected.   
Also the procedure texts in the NGAP Initial Context Setup Request message, Handover Request message, Downlink NAS Transport message  are not aligned with SA2 descriptions.
summaryOfChange:
Update the procedure texts in NGAP Initial Context Setup Request message, Handover Request message, Downlink NAS Transport message so that if no allowed PNI-NPN List is received by the NG-RAN node, the UE is considered not allowed to access CAG cells.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Timing error margin functionality is unnecessarily complex due to potential abnormal scenarios if timing error margin is absent.
reasonForChange:
Timing Error Group (TEG) was introduced in NRPPa/F1AP at RAN3#115 based on RAN1 agreements, and some corrections agreed at RAN3#116 (CR0063r4) to further align with RAN1/RAN2 decisions.

At RAN3#117e, an LS was received from RAN4 (R3-224216) listing agreements on timing error margins for UE/TRP Tx/Rx/RxTx TEGs. Based on the RAN4 agreements, RAN3 added timing error margin associated to the UE/TRP Tx/Rx/RxTx TEGs. Because the timing error margins were introduced as a late correction to complete the TEG framework, the IEs were made optional in order to be backwards compatible but an FFS captured on how to interpret the absence of margin values.

In fact, the sender (UE/gNB) must always know the timing error margins if it is supporting TEG as a feature, and there is no scenario where it makes sense for the TRP/gNB to omit the margin. The only reason the IEs are optional is that they were introduced as a backwards compatible correction to the incomplete TEG framework, which was unfortunately introduced piecemeal in NRPPa/F1AP due to agreements being reached in RAN1 and RAN4 at different meetings.

For the TEG framework to work without undue complexity, the timing error margins should be mandatory to avoid abnormal conditions.
summaryOfChange:
The timing error margins are made mandatory if the associated TEG ID is included, as follows:
9.3.1.168: TRP Rx Timing Error Margin IE is made mandatory if TRP Rx TEG ID IE is included
9.3.1.252: TRP Tx Timing Error Margin IE is made mandatory
9.3.1.253: For RxTxTEG, the TRP RxTx Timing Error Margin IE is made mandatory, and the TRP Tx Timing Error Margin IE is made mandatory if TRP Tx TEG ID IE is included.
9.3.1.253: For Rx TEG, both the TRP Rx Timing Error Margin IE and the TRP Tx Timing Error Margin IE are made mandatory.

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an impact under protocol point of view. The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only timing error margin functionality. This CR is non-backwards compatible.
title: Correction on presence of timing error margin for TRP TEGs

reasonForChange:
Issue 1:
During the Broadcast Context Setup, in case the gNB-DU only successfully start to provide the Broadcast session in part of the requested service area, it will provide a Partial Success Broadcast Cell list in the response message, then the gNB-CU will get the ongoing delivery states of the MBS Session in the cells of this gNB-DU. During Broadcast Context Modification procedure, the gNB-CU may provide an updated MBS Service Area to the gNB-DU, but in current response message, the gNB-DU is not able to provide this Partial Success Broadcast Cell list to the gNB-CU. Therefore in case the gNB-DU only provides the service in part of the cells, it is not able to provide related information to the gNB-CU, then the mtch-neighbourCell information the gNB-CU provide to its gNB-DUs will be incorrect.

reasonForChange:
For Redcap UE, if the initial DL BWP does not include the CD-SSB but with an NCD-SSB, in order to support the CG based or RA based SDT, RAN2 agreed to configure an NCD SSB in the initial Redcap BWP for Tx timing and/or channel estimation etc (see the agreed R2-2302305/ R2-2302306).

SuspendConfig ::=                   SEQUENCE {
    <Skip the irrelavance>
    ncd-SSB-RedCapInitialBWP-SDT-r17   SetupRelease {NonCellDefiningSSB-r17}                                 OPTIONAL    -- Need M

In the CU-DU split architecture, the NCD-SSB associated with the initial BWP, as a lower layer parameter, should be decided by the gNB-DU. Hence the NCD-SSB information should be provided by the gNB-DU to the gNB-CU in the DU to CU RRC Information. The assigned criticality of following IEs is not aligned in the tabular and ASN.1:
For the MBS Session Setup Response Transfer IE in Broadcast Session Setup Response message, the assigned criticality is “ignore” in tabular while it is “reject” in ASN.1.

For the MBS Session Setup Failure Transfer IE in Broadcast Session Setup Failure message and the MBS Session Modification Failure Transfer IE in Broadcast Session Modifciation Failure message, the assigned criticality is “ignore” in tabular while it is “reject” in ASN.1.
summaryOfChange:
1) Change the assigned criticality of the MBS Session Setup Response Transfer IE from ”ignore” to “reject” in the tabular
2) Change the assigned criticality of the MBSSessionSetupFailureTransfer IE from ”reject” to “ignore” in ASN.1
3) Change the assigned criticality of the MBSSessionModificationFailureTransfer IE from”reject” to “ignore” in ASN.1
For case 1) it is important to keep the criticality assigned to “reject” to cause the procedure being unsuccessfully terminated if the IE is not comprehended, while for 2) and 3), non-comprehension of the respective IEs wouldn’t cause the receiving node to not regard the procedure being unsuccessfully terminated.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the broadcast MBS function.
title: ASN.1 and tabular alignment for Broadcast related messages

consequencesIfNotApproved: The inactive UEs will resume failed.
reasonForChange:
In order to assist the NG-RAN node to identify the correct last serving NG-RAN node from a I-RNTI for an inactive UE, RAN3 has agreed to assign two Local NG-RAN node identifiers for each local NG-RAN node and encode them into the full I-RNTI and short I-RNTI when sending the UE to inactive state. The local NG-RAN node identifiers are also exchanged between neighbour nodes via Xn.
When receiving a RRC resume request from an inactive UE, the NG-RAN node extracts the local NG-RAN node identifier from the I-RNTI, and determine the global node ID of the UE’s last serving NG-RAN node by comparing the local NG-RAN node identifier in the I-RNTI and the local NG-RAN node identifier receiving from neighbour nodes.
The stage 2 about the usage of the local NG-RAN node identifier and the structure of the I-RNTI is captured in the Annex F in TS38.300.
According to TS 38.331, both the full I-RNTI and the short I-RNTI are configured to the UE during RRCRelease message. And it is up to the new serving cell to decide which one should be used in RRCResumeReqeust by the useFullResumeID indicator in SIB1.
SuspendConfig ::=                   SEQUENCE {
    fullI-RNTI                          I-RNTI-Value,
    shortI-RNTI                         ShortI-RNTI-Value,
    ran-PagingCycle                     PagingCycle,
    ran-NotificationAreaInfo            RAN-NotificationAreaInfo                                            OPTIONAL,   -- Need M
    t380                                PeriodicRNAU-TimerValue                                             OPTIONAL,   -- Need R
    nextHopChainingCount                NextHopChainingCount,
    ...,
}

SIB1 ::=        SEQUENCE {
   <remove unrelevent part>
    useFullResumeID                     ENUMERATED {true}                                               OPTIONAL,   -- Need R
}
However, the Local NG-RAN Node Identifier IE exchanged over Xn is designed to a CHOICE type for full I-RNTI and short  I-RNTI, which implies that only one local NG-RAN node identifier could be exchanged.
The NG-RAN node will not be able to identify the correct last serving node when the local NG-RAN node identifier in the I-RNTI is mismatched with the ones receiving from neighbor nodes.
In fact, it should be flexible whether the Local NG-RAN Node ID feature is used in a network for “full I-RNTI”, “short I-RNTI” or both “full and short I-RNTI”.
summaryOfChange:
Correct the Local NG-RAN Node Identifier IE to exchange the local NG-RAN node identifiers for either one or both full I-RNTI and short I-RNTI.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) 
This CR has an impact under protocol & functional point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects  one system function. 
There is no RRC spec impact.
title: Correction on the local NG-RAN Node Identifier on Xn [RRCInactive]

consequencesIfNotApproved: The Source gNB cannot signal the UE Inactive Time to a Target gNB in disaggregated gNB architecture with CP-UP separation.
reasonForChange:
In handover scenarios, a gNB is able to over Xn, forward the “inactive” time spent for the UE to the target gNB. This is part of RRC: HandoverPreparationInformation can include rrm-Config, which can include ue-InactiveTime IE.

However, for disaggregated architecture with CP-UP separation, the gNB-CU-CP is not aware of the “inactive” time as it is measured at gNB-CU-UP and not reported with E1AP. Hence, this has negative result that for mobility, the gNB-CU-CP cannot forward the “inactive” period to the target gNB even though it is supported to be signaled over Xn interface. Thus, UE inactivity at the Source gNB is not accounted for.

To support this functionality in disaggregated gNB architecture with CP-UP separation, at the source gNB, the gNB-CU-CP needs means to request the gNB-CU-UP to report the “inactive” time.
summaryOfChange:
Add Inactivity Information Request IE to BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message.
Add UE Inactivity Information IE in BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE message.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change is limited to inactivity reporting.
title: Inactive Time Signaling over E1 for Mobility

consequencesIfNotApproved: LMF may not be able to know the new cell identity where a RRC_INACTIVE UE is resumed from, consequently, it may not be able to select the proper gNBs/TRPs to perform the UL Positioning measurement.
reasonForChange:
To make support of Inactive Positioning, in case of SDT without UE context relocation has been decided for the MO-SDT transmission (LCS event report), when the last serving gNB receives the POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST and still keep the UE context, it may request for the SRS resources from the receiving gNB (see XnAP CR 1085), and reply LMF the POSITIONING INFORMATION RESPONSE. 
However, the LMF does not know the new serving cell where is currently resumed from / located in. Without the accurate cell identity where the UE is located in, the LMF may not be able to select the proper gNBs/TRPs to perform the UL positioning measurement.
Therefore, the last serving gNB should indicate LMF the new cell identity where the UE is resumed.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The CU can not determine whether to deliver the system information to the UE via HO command in CU/DU split architecture.
reasonForChange:
When a non-RedCap UE accesses a first active DL BWP in the target cell upon handover, the first active BWP is either the initial BWP or the BWP associated with CD-SSB. Therefore, there is no problem for it to receive broadcast information in the target cell.  

In Rel-17, the NCD-SSB feature is introduced for RedCap UEs. A RedCap UE may not receive broadcast information in target cell upon handover if the first active DL BWP associated with an NCD-SSB is not configured with CSS (common search space). In this case, SIBs information can be provided via dedicated signaling,e.g,HO command to the UE, In this way, the UE can receive system information from the target cell in time during the handover. 

However, for a CU/DU split gNB, the CU is not aware of whether the UE can receive broadcast information in the target cell during handover. That is, the CU does not know the UE's first active DL BWP and the NCD-SSB/CSS information associated with this BWP. Then, there is no way for the CU to decide whether there is a need to send SIBs to UE via HO command. 

To support NG-RAN node determining the delivery of system information via HO command, it is proposed that DU should report to CU that the UE can receive broadcast information in the first active BWP of the target cell during handover.

consequencesIfNotApproved: When the IAB-node uses NR-DC where only the SN supports IAB-donor functionality, the IAB-DU may continue serving UE(s) even if it has been deauthorized.
reasonForChange:
In TS38.413, Sections 8.3.1.2 (Initial Context Setup Request) and 8.3.4.2 (UE Context Modification Request) state for the IAB Authorized IE:
 If the IAB Authorized IE is set to "not authorized" for an IAB-MT, the NG-RAN node shall, if supported, initiate actions to ensure that the IAB node will not serve any UE(s).
In Rel-17, IAB supports an NR-DC scenario where the IAB-node’s SN is the F1-terminating IAB-donor while the IAB-node’s MN has no donor functionality. Since the MN maintains the CP connection towards the 5GC, it receives the IAB Authorized IE, but it itself cannot initiate any actions to ensure that the IAB-node will not service any UE(s). It is therefore necessary to allow this MN to inform the SN about the IAB authorization status so that the SN can apply the actions defined above. This issue can be addressed by allowing the MN to insert the IAB Authorized IE into the S-NODE ADDITION REQUEST message and the S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUEST message toward the SN. In this manner, the SN can apply the above actions.
