consequencesIfNotApproved: The use of the XnAP IDs is unclear in some scenarios.
reasonForChange:
The Xn-U Address Indication procedure was originally defined for mobility in NG-RAN and later adapted for NR-DC purposes (bearer setup with the SN as the hosting node). In case of the single connectivity mobility, the XnAP IDs used in the message are set up by the “new” and “old” nodes and so they were defined in the semantics of the message. However, when the NR-DC scenario was defined, it was not extended thus creating ambiguity which node is “new” and which one is “old”. 
Similar issue exists in case of the RRC Transfer procedure, but there it is reversed: the IDs are defined for DC, but their use in case of SDT mobility is unclear. 
Yet another issue concerns the Activity Notification: there, the textual definition refers to nodes ‘1’ and ‘2’, the “direction” does not refer to anything, while the semantics mention M-NG-RAN and S-NG-RAN nodes.
summaryOfChange:
The issue is addressed correctly in the Error Indication message, which can also be used in both, single- and dual-connectivity: in case of DC, the “new” node is the M-NG-RAN node and the “old” node is the S-NG-RAN node. The same semantic descritpion is proposed to be used in case of the Xn-U Address Indication and in the RRC Transfer procedures.
For the Activity Notification procedure, it is proposed to add missing numbers at the “direction” definition and to add the link between the M/S-NG-RAN nodes and the nodes ‘1’ and ‘2’ in the semantics.
title: Clarification of the use of the XnAP IDs

For A2X authorization requirement, two IEs(e.g. NR A2X Services Authorized, LTE A2X Services Authorized) have been introduced in multiple RAN3 specifications(e.g. TS 38.413, TS 38.423, TS 38.473). Currently, 2 sub IEs with the name UAV-UE and UAV- controller UE respectively has been used in the A2X Service Authorized aspects in TS 38.413. 
However, the abbreviation of the “UAV” has not been introduced in any RAN3 specifications(including TS 38.413). It is not appropriate for RAN3 to directly use the name “UAV” without further explanation in the related specification.

Sync up with other related specifications(e.g. TS 38.423 and TS 38.473). Change the name “UAV UE” to “Aerial  UE” and change the name “UAV Controller UE” to “Aerial Controller UE” in both tabular and ASN.1 part.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The stage2 descriptions of managing PC5 Relay RLC channels for L2 U2U Remote UE and L2 U2U Relay UE is missing.
Editorial exist.
reasonForChange:
RAN2 has specified a feature to support 5G ProSe UE-to-UE (U2U) Relay operation to provide connectivity between U2U Remote UEs. In this feature, the U2U Remote UE can communicate with the peer U2U Remote UE(s) which are not reachable within the sidelink coverage.

In TS 38.300, RAN2 agrees that the serving gNB can provide each hop configuration (e.g. PC5 Relay RLC Channel configuration) for SL-DRB to the UE (i.e., L2 U2U Remote UE or L2 U2U Relay UE) in RRC_CONNECTED. As in Rel-17 UE-to-Network (U2N) Relay operation, the establishment of PC5 Relay RLC channels should be triggered by the gNB-CU. The establishment and modification is accepted/rejected by the gNB-DU. The modification of PC5 Relay RLC channels can be triggered by the gNB-CU or the gNB-DU.
Therefore, the corresponding specifications needs to be modified to support the U2U Relay operation.
Other editorial on Multi-Path Relay operation.
summaryOfChange:
Add the stage2 descriptions to manage PC5 Relay RLC channels for L2 U2U Remote UE and L2 U2U Relay UE.
Editorial change on Multi-Path Relay operation.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Not able to transfer from MN to SN the received sk-Counter value received from the UE
reasonForChange:
TS37.340 figure 10.20-1 and 10.20-2, the inter-SN S-CPAC has included in step 12 SN RECONFIGURATAION COMPLETE message where it describes:
“12. The MN informs the SN of the selected candidate PSCell that the UE has completed the reconfiguration procedure successfully via SN Reconfiguration Complete message, including the RRCReconfigurationComplete** message. If the sk-Counter value is received by the RRCReconfigurationComplete* message, the MN also indicates the received sk-Counter value to the SN.”, 
and then according to the received LS from SA3 in R3-237737, “the SN, having stored the KSN keys and the corresponding SN counter values, selects the appropriate KSN based on the received SN counter value.”

Since the RRCReconfigurationComplete* message is only received by the MN, this means that the MN needs to transfer to the SN the received sk-Counter value from the UE.
However 38.423 S-NODE RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE message has not included such sk-Counter value.

consequencesIfNotApproved: NG-RAN nodes do not know how to handle the IAB authorization status which is transferred by the core network.
reasonForChange:
To support IAB operation, the CN that the IAB-node connects provides authorization status of the IAB-node to RAN. In Rel-17, the IAB-node can connect to 5GC via SA based network integration procedure. 
If the IAB-node connects to 5GC, the AMF initiates the NG procedure to provide the IAB authorization status to the IAB-donor which provides the C-plane connection to 5GC for the IAB-MT. It’s specified in TS38.413 that if the authorization status is received for an IAB-MT from the AMF, the NG-RAN should use it accordingly, e.g., to ensure that the IAB-node will not serve any UE if the status is set to “not authorized”.
However, it has not been specified how the RAN node uses the authorization status of IAB-node that is received from the core network.
summaryOfChange:
Clause 8.3.1, 8.3.4, 8.4.2, 8.4.4 add the reference to TS 38.401 with respect to IAB-node authorization.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Without the proposed changes, the core network does not know when to de-register the unauthorized IAB-node.

The wording is not clear in 8.9.17.2.2 and 8.9.17.3 for IAB authorization in SA.
reasonForChange:
At the RAN3#123 meeting, RAN3 specified authorization handling for IAB-nodes, and made the following agreements to address the leftover issues on de-registration handling:
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the RAN node serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After RAN node serving the IAB-MT is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the AMF that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting. 
After the donor CU serving the IAB-DU has received the authorization status = “not authorized” and removed the F1 connection, it sends an indication to the eNB serving the IAB-MT about the release of F1. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting.
After the eNB serving the IAB-MT in EN-DC is informed that the F1 connection of the IAB-DU has been released, it sends an indication to the MME that the unauthorized IAB-MT can be deregistered. Signaling details to be discussed at the next meeting. 
Based on the above, RAN3 should specify the 4 agreements above in stage 2.

In the present TS 38.401 Sections 8.9.17.2.2/8.9.17.3 for IAB authorization in SA, it says that the IAB-donor performs the SA equivalent of the steps described for NSA in 8.9.17.1 upon reception of the IAB-node authorization status, however, it’s more accurate that Section 8.9.17.2.2 and 8.9.17.3 refer to 8.9.17.2.1 instead of 8.9.17.1, since 8.9.17.2.1 can be reused more.
8.9.17.2.1 misuses the term “mobile IAB”.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 5/10/2024. Original source : CATT, Ericsson, Huawei, ZTE
summaryOfChange:
Add following description in clause 8.9.17 for IAB-node authorization:
In case the IAB-node connects to EPS via EN-DC in NSA, the IAB-donor may indicate to the eNB serving the IAB-MT that no UE or descendant node is served by the IAB-node anymore, and removing of the F1 interface and backhaul resources for the unauthorized IAB-node via a SGNB MODIFICATION REQUIRED or SGNB RELEASE REQUIRED message, then the eNB may indicate to the EPC that the IAB-MT can be deregistered.
In case the IAB-node connects with single IAB-donor using NR-DC in SA and the IAB-donor is the SN, the SN may send an indication to the MN that no UE or descendant node is served by the IAB-node anymore, removing the F1 interface and backhaul resources of the unauthorized IAB-node via a S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUIRED or S-NODE RELEASE REQUIRED message, then the MN may indicate to the AMF that the IAB-MT can be deregistered.
In other cases, the RAN-node serving the IAB-MT may send an indication to the 5GC indicating that the IAB-MT can be deregistered after it knows the F1-terminating donor-CU releasing the F1 interface to the unauthorized IAB-node.

In 8.9.17.2.2 and 8.9.17.3, change the sentence “performs the SA equivalent of the steps described for NSA in 8.9.17.1” to “performs the same steps described in 8.9.17.2.1” in several places.

In 8.9.17.2.1, the misuse of the term “mobile IAB” is corrected.

This CR has impact on the functional point of view, will only impact the RAN handling for the IAB-node authorization.

reasonForChange:
According to TS 38.331, the sl-PathSwitchConfig IE is used to support the path switching from direct path to indirect path and from indirect path to indirect path. This IE is also used to only release the direct path during the multi-path. However, in current F1 interface, the Path Switch Configuration IE is provided to the gNB-DU only in case of the path switching from direct path to indirect path.
According to TS 38.331, the gNB sends the sl-IndirectPathMaintain IE in the ReconfigurationWithSync IE to indicate that the L2 U2N Remote UE keeps the PC5 connection with its connected L2 U2N Relay UE. Hence, in order for the gNB-DU to generate the ReconfigurationWithSync IE, the gNB-CU needs to provide the Direct Path Addition IE to the gNB-DU in the inter-DU case.

consequencesIfNotApproved: DU could not identify the Peer UE of a PC5 RLC channel so could not make proper SL logic channel configuration and interpret SL BSR correctly.
reasonForChange:
Peer UE ID is needed when CU request DU to provide configuration for a PC5 Relay RLC channel to be setup for L2 U2U relay operation, considering the following reasons:
When receiving a request from CU to configure PC5 Relay RLC channels for a L2 U2U Remote/Relay UE, DU should know which PC5 Relay RLC channels are belonging to the same peer UE so that to configure the logical channel configuration (e.g. priority, LCG ID) for each PC5 Relay RLC channel, e.g. to decide which PC5 Relay RLC channels/logical channels are configured to the same/different LCG. 
On the other hand, when receiving SL BSR from U2U UE, DU should identify the involved PC5 Relay RLC channels belonging to the LCG ID for the reported buffer size for a DST index and the LCH priority/configuration of each PC5 Relay RLC channel, to perform mode 1 resource allocation.  
  So, DU should know the association of the peer UE and the PC5 Relay RLC channel to make proper SL logical channel configuration and interpret the SL BSR correctly.
summaryOfChange:
Peer UE ID is added in PC5 RLC channel to be Setup Item IEs IE in UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION  REQUEST message.

consequencesIfNotApproved: DL-PRS Aggregation is not aligned with RAN1/2 specifications and can not be proper supported.
reasonForChange:
The IE "PRS Configuration" may include the "Aggregated PRS Resource Set List" per "PRS Resource Set Item", but is missing in the ASN.1 (i.e., there is an ASN.1 definition for the AggregatedPRSResourceSetList, but this is nowhere included). 
According to RAN1 parameter list and LPP TS 37.355, the linkage information ("Aggregated PRS Resource Set List") in the tabular for IE "PRS Configuration" should be per positioning frequency layer (PFL) (and not across Sets within a single PFL) and should therefore be moved up to the "PRS Resource Set List" level. 
To indicate the linkage information, in the "Aggregated PRS Resource Set List", the Point A and the DL-PRS Resource Set ID are currently used. However, there are the following issues:
The {Point A, Resource Set ID} alone does not define a PFL.
A single TRP can have up to 4 PFLs where each PFL can have up to 2 DL-PRS Resource Sets. DL-PRS Aggregation can be across 2 PFLs or 3 PFLs, as well as 2+2 PFLs (see e.g., RAN1 LS in R3-237136 (RAN3#122) and RAN1 parameter list). The latter (2+2 PFLs) can not be supported with the current structure.
summaryOfChange:
The IE "Aggregated PRS Resource Set List" (AggregatedPRSResourceSetList) is added to the "PRS Configuration" (PRSConfiguration). 
The linkage information ("Aggregated PRS Resource Set List") is defined as an index to the entries in the "PRS Resource Set List" in the "PRS Configuration" IE, and allows aggregation information of 2 or 3 PFLs, as well as 2+2 PFLs.
title: Correction to DL-PRS Aggregation

consequencesIfNotApproved: Coding of tunnel release unspecified.
reasonForChange:
At RAN3#124, RAN3 received the LS from CT4 in C4-241525 informing that CT4 has agreed the CR 0076 in C4-241524 specifying the restoration solution to recover from an NG-U failure in the case of split PDU session. RAN3 agreed the CR in R3-243965 at RAN3#124 to implement the CT4 solution. However RAN3 implementation has some issues:
R3-243965 specifies one of the following three options for the action of the Master gNB: The Master gNB may either send back an updated D-FTEID, decide to offload (or “move”) the QoS flows of the lost F TEID to the healthy F-TEID or release the tunnel. 
However the meaning of the latter option is unclear because the current PDU Session Modify Indication procedure currently only describes the “move” of QoS flows. Actually, “release the tunnel” can either mean:
Master gNB wants to release the broken F-TEID and move the associated QoS flows to the healthy F-TEID, (1) or,
The master gNB wants to release the tunnel together with all its associated QoS flows (2).
If the intention is (1) it is already covered by the codepoint “QoS flows to be moved”.
If the intention is (2) the release of the QoS flows is currently not specified in the PDU Session Modification Indication but normally uses the PDU Session Notify procedure.
summaryOfChange:
The missing function of “releasing QoS flows and tunnel” is specified using the PDU Session Notify procedure instead of the PDU Session Modify Indication.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Unclear behaviour of gNB-DU when receiving the Positioning Broadcast Cells IE.
reasonForChange:
The description of the Positioning Assistance Information IE in the POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION CONTROL message is not clear. If the information is received, it is immediately broadcasted and not stored.

The Positioning Assistance Information has to be present when the Broadcast IE is set to ‘start’.

The Broadcast IE is mandatory. There is no gNB-DU behavior defined for the case when the Broadcast IE is absent. therefore the procedure should fail in this case.

If the gNB-DU receives the Positioning Broadcast Cells IE in the POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION CONTROL message, then the information in the procedure (i.e., Positioning Assistance Information and Broadcast IE) is valid only for the indicated list of cells.

In POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION FEEDBACK message, the Semantic description for Positioning Assistance Information Failure List IE refers to the Assistance Information IE as defined in TS 38.455. It should be instead referring to the Assistance Information Failure List IE as defined in TS 38.455.
summaryOfChange:
Clarify in 8.13.1.2 that the received Assistance Information IE replaces any previously received assistance information, rather than “stored”.
Clarify in 8.13.1.3 that the Assistance Information IE has to be included when the Broadcast IE is set to ‘start’.
Clarify in 8.13.1.3 that the Broadcast IE is mandatory.
Clarify that when the Positioning Broadcast Cells IE is received, the procedure is limited to those cells only. Deletion of IE semantics.
Correct semantics description of Positioning Assistance Information Failure List IE in POSITIONING ASSISTANCE INFORMATION FEEDBACK message.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
The CR has isolated impact because the change affects only the Positioning Assistance Information Control procedure.
The CR is backwards compatible from a protocol point of view.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Misalignment between TS 23.247 and TS 38.413.
reasonForChange:
TS 23.247 specifies in clause 7.2.4.2.1 that during shared delivery setup the NG-RAN node may provide the list of tracking areas supported by the gNB which is not supported in NGAP.
If the RAN determines the shared delivery is not established for the MBS Session ID and Area Session ID, the NG-RAN initiates the shared delivery establishment as specified in clause 7.2.1.4 and provides the Area Session ID, tracking area ID(s) concerning the RAN node in addition to MBS Session ID in the request for shared delivery establishment. The MB-SMF provides MBS service area information (Area Session ID(s), MBS service area(s)) associated with the same MBS session to NG-RAN in the shared delivery establishment response. MB-SMF may either provide only the service areas concerning the target RAN node or all service areas associated with the MBS session. If the MB-SMF only provides the service areas concerning the target RAN node, which includes the cell ID(s), the cell ID is included if the tracking area IDs associated with the indicated cell ID is received by the MB-SMF.
summaryOfChange:
The list of tracking areas is added to the MBS Distribution Setup Request Transfer IE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The CPAC MCG configuration, once configured, cannot be cancelled for the split gNB.
reasonForChange:
For CPAC, it was captured that the MN sends to the UE an RRC reconfiguration message including a list of RRC reconfiguration* messages including both MCG and SCG configuration (RRC reconfiguration**) which are to be applied together upon CPAC execution. In addition, in RAN3#115 chairman notes, the following agreements can be found for CPAC:
In CPA and MN/SN initiated inter-SN CPC, MN can: 
Update/modify previous CPAC configurations provided in CPAC addition using MN initiated SN modification procedure 
Cancel all prepared PSCells at target SN and release the target SN using MN initiated SN release procedure 
In CPA and MN/SN initiated inter-SN CPC, target SN can:
Update/modify previous CPAC configurations provided in CPAC addition using SN initiated SN modification procedure 
Add prepared PSCells within the limit given by the MN or source SN using SN initiated SN modification procedure
Cancel some of the prepared PSCells using SN initiated SN modification procedure. 
Cancel all prepared PSCells using SN initiated SN release procedure 
In SN initiated inter-SN CPC, source SN can:
Update/modify previous CPC configurations provided in CPC preparation using SN change required procedure
Cancel all prepared PSCells at target SN and release the target SN using SN change required procedure
New IEs are introduced in SN change required message indicating CPC configuration modification and target SN release. 
In MN/SN initiated inter-SN CPC, MN can inform source SN about the triggered target SN release or some prepared PSCells cancellation at a target SN using:
A new class2 XnAP procedure
A new class2 X2AP procedure 
However, in case that the MN is a split gNB, it is unclear how the MN cancels the prepared MCG configuration(s) at the gNB-DU corresponding to the cancelled conditional SCG configuration(s) for CPAC.
summaryOfChange:
Editorial reorgnization of the procedure text for the CPAC MCG Information IE 
Add a new codepoint CPAC-cancel to the CPAC Trigger in the CPAC MCG Information IE to handle the cancellation scenario
Add correspodning procedure text
Add corresponding ASN.1 changes

consequencesIfNotApproved: It is not possible to exploit the existence of several AoA per TRP when MIMO transmission is active, which could be reported in the E-CID measurement report, each with a measurement quality indicator. This would improve positioning accuracy with UL-AoA measurements for calculating the UE position using E-CID method.
reasonForChange:
Current E-CID framework in NRPPa is designed on the concept of “one cell level measurement”, however one cell can comprise several measuring TRPs, which can report different measurements, e.g., AoA based on legacy SRS for MIMO signals.
To allow for multiple reporting of measurements, it is proposed to allow the gNB to report Angle of Arrival per TRP measurements in the E-CID Measurement procedures by introducing a new dedicated measurement request type. This will improve the accuracy of E-CID positioning method.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce a new “NR Angle of Arrival per TRP” measurement codepoint in the E-CID defined Measurement Quantities Value IE.
Introduce a Angle of Arrival per TRP in the E-CID Measurement Result IE containing a list of AoA measurements per TRP. The IE also includes the geographical coordinates, time stamp and quality.
title: E-CID measurement enhancement [ECID_enh1]

consequencesIfNotApproved: The specification is not clear.
reasonForChange:
In clause 6.1.6, editorial change to align with the terminology “Intermediate U2N Relay UE”.

RAN2 agreed that “When the RRC_CONNECTED intermediate relay UE does re-establishment as a remote UE, the intermediate Relay UE sends a notification downstream, with the cause value to be confirmed in CR implementation.”. And the definition of Intermediate U2N Relay UE shows the intermediate U2N Relay UE connects to the network as a U2N Remote UE.
“Intermediate U2N Relay UE: a U2N Relay UE having both PC5 connection to a parent UE and PC5 connection to a child UE or a U2N Remote UE for serving the U2N Remote UE in case of multi-hop L2 U2N Relay communication. In this release, an intermediate U2N Relay UE first establishes a connection to the network as a U2N Remote UE before beginning to relay traffic for connected U2N Remote UEs.”

It means that the Remote UE RRC Re-establishment (in clause 8.19.2) and RRC resume (in clause 8.19.3) procedures are applicable to Intermediate U2N Relay UE in multi-hop relay. So it is suggested to clarify this in the spec.

The RRC connection resume procedure is in clause 8.19.3, so it is suggested to add 8.19.3 as reference.

Upon the reception of RRCReconfiguration, the Intermediate Relay UE may at most establish two PC5 RLC channels for relaying of Remote UE’s SRB0 over PC5, one PC5 RLC channel towards the First Relay UE, and the other towards the Last relay UE. So the current wording is not accurate enough.Upon the reception of RRCReconfiguration, the First Relay UE may establish a PC5 RLC channel towards the Intermediate Relay UE for relaying of Remote UE’s SRB0 over PC5; while for the PC5 RLC channel towards the Remote UE, a specified PC5 RLC channel is used as specified in the latest 38.300. So the current wording is ambiguous.

For SL multi-hop, the preparation of Uu relay RLC channels and PC5 relay RLC channels may take place before the interaction between the gNB and the AMF. However, the current procedural text does not specify the exact step at which this occurs, which may lead to mistake regarding the timing of the establishing the channels.
summaryOfChange:
In clause 6.1.6, editorial change to align with the terminology “Intermediate U2N Relay UE”.
In clause 8.19.2 and 8.19.3, clarify these procedures are also applicable to Intermediate U2N Relay UE in multi-hop relay.
In clause 8.19.5, add clause 8.19.3 as reference for RRC connection resume procedure.
In clause 8.19.5, clarify the Intermediate/First U2N Relay UEs may need to establish PC5 Relay RLC channels towards both the parent UE and child UE.
In clause 8.19.5, add “i.e., after step 27” for NOTE 2.
title: Corrections for Multi-hop relay

consequencesIfNotApproved: The SP SRS Activation/Deactivation procedure cannot be fully supported.
reasonForChange:
According to RAN2 agreement, both Periodic and Semi-Persistent (SP) resource types are supported for area-specific SRS configuration. The procedure of area-specific SRS activation should cover both SP SRS and periodic SRS cases. And also, according to latest TS 38.305, the area-specific SRS activation procedure supports both anchor relocation case and no anchor relocation case.

If LMF makes activation decision for area-specific SP SRS, for non-achor relocation case, the activated SRS Resource Set ID(s) is needed to be added in XnAP RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT FAILURE message. And for achor relocation case, the activated SRS Resource Set ID(s) is still needed. For deactivation procedure, no matter non anchor relocation case or anchor relocation case, the SP SRS deactivation related information should be involved in RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT RESPONSE/FAILURE message to support SP SRS Deactivation procedure.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Both MN and SN may configure the default DRB, and then the UE does not know how to do the QoS to DRB mapping.
reasonForChange:
Currently at most only one default DRB per PDU session may exist, irrespective whether the DRB’s PDCP entity is located at the MN or the SN. As suggested by RAN2, coordination between MN and SN is required regarding the configuration of a DRB as a default DRB, and the agreements are:
The SN is allowed to setup a default DRB for SN-terminated bearers (i.e., and for PDU sessions associated with an SDAP entity mapped to the SN). 
The MN decides whether the SN is allowed to setup the default DRB.
The MN informs the SN whether it can configure a default DRB via an indication included in the Xn signaling and then it is up to the SN to decide whether and when to configure a default DRB.

consequencesIfNotApproved: If the MN does not inform the SN on the need of resource coordination with its SL resource configuration, resource collision can happen for the SN’s served Uu UEs through SRB3
reasonForChange:
In MR-DC, resources being interfered by other concurrent transmission in neighboring cells is a general issue that is addressed today by the means of the MR-DC Resource Coordination Information IE present in Dual Connectivity procedures. 

When V2X comes into scope, nodes other than the MN cannot know of the bandwidth used for the sidelink resource configuration. This can cause resource collision when e.g. the SN’s served UEs through SRB3 are on the same bandwidth as the MN’s sidelink (SL) allocated resources.

To address this issue and complement the Rel-15 MR-DC resource coordination for Uu, SL resource configuration must be allowed to be communicated from the MN to the SNs, so that MR-DC communication will not be impacted during SL transmission.
summaryOfChange:
This CR proposes to enable the legacy MR-DC Resource Coordination Information IE to be used for allowing coordination of sidelink resource utilisation between MR-DC nodes.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The paging RAN node (except the anchor RAN node) does not know whether the extended DRX is configured by upper layers for the UE, and does know the PTW position, if configured.
If the RAN node always sends RAN paging based on the shortest of the RAN paging cycle, the UE specific paging cycle, if allocated by upper layers and the default paging cycle, RAN paging loss may occur outside the PTW, if configured, in the case that RAN Paging cycle is larger than the shortest of the UE specific paging cycle, if allocated by upper layers and the default paging cycle.
If the RAN node always sends RAN paging based on the RAN paging cycle, the RAN node may page the UE using a longer DRX cycle than the DRX cycle which the UE is monitoring within the PTW, if configured, and UE’s paging occasions are under-used in RRC_INACTIVE, particularly if the PTW is long, in the case that RAN Paging cycle is larger than the shortest of the UE specific paging cycle, if allocated by upper layers and the default paging cycle.
reasonForChange: Based on the TS 36.304, in RRC_INACTIVE state when extended DRX is configured by upper layers, the paging DRX cycle (T) of the UE is determined by the shortest of the RAN paging cycle, the UE specific paging cycle, if allocated by upper layers and the default paging cycle during the PTW, and by the RAN paging cycle outside the PTW. But based on the current XnAP specification, the paging RAN node (except the anchor RAN node) does not know whether the extended DRX is configured by upper layers for the UE, and does know the PTW position, if configured.
summaryOfChange:
Include Paging eDRX Information IE in the RAN PAGING message.

Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on the Paging function in RRC_INACTIVE.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The CU-UP is not able to assign the approriate data TNL addresses for direct data forwarding.
reasonForChange:
In case of the non-disaggregated node case, the target NG-RAN node is aware of whether direct data forwarding was requested so as to assign the correspinding TNL addresses for data forwarding for the EPS to 5GS handover. 

But for the disaggregated node case, the CU-UP is not aware of the above information. Typically, CU-UP needs to differentiate with the following two cases. 
For the handover with direct data forwarding, the CU-UP can assign the TNL addresses from the  direct UP interface space. 
For the handover without direct data forwarding, the CU-UP can assign corresponding data fowarding addresses from the 5GS address space. 

This direct data forwarding availability information is also needed for the intra-5GS handover if the target CU-CP knows such information.
summaryOfChange:
Add a Direct Forwarding Path Availability in the BEARER CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message to indicate the handover with direct data forwarding.  
 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only impacts the handover with direct data forwarding.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The measurement periodicity is not agligned with SRS periodicity and the measurement may fail. or be totally wrong withtout possibility to detect the mistake.
reasonForChange:
The current values of the Measurement periodicity for UL and UL&DL positioning are as follows:

The measurement periodicity share the same IE with E-CID positioning measurement periodicity, which is aligned with UE RRM measurment report interval in RRC, which is as follows:

ReportInterval ::=                  ENUMERATED {ms120, ms240, ms480, ms640, ms1024, ms2048, ms5120, ms10240, ms20480, ms40960,
                                                    min1,min6, min12, min30 }

This is incorrect because that for UL and UL&DL positioning it is gNB to measure the SRS sent from the UE, while the RRM measurement is for the UE to measure DL reference signals. 

The SRS periodicity has the following values:


It is obvious that in the measurement periodicity, at least the following values are not aligned with the SRS periodicity: 120ms, 240ms, 480ms, 1024ms, 2048ms, 1min, 6min, 12min, and 30min.


Thus, the measurement periodicity for the UL and UL&DL positioning should be aligned with SRS periodicity, rather than the RRC report interval.
The values of SRS periodicity should be added in the measurement periodicity for UL and UL&DL positioning, including 160ms, 320ms, 1280ms 2560ms, 81920ms.

Some of the values in current measurement periodicity should be subtituded by the similar value that can be aligned with the SRS periodicity. For example, the value 1min should be subtituded by a similar value, such as 61440ms. The value of 6min, 12min, and 30min can be subtituted by a similar value such as 368640ms, 737280ms, and 1843200ms.

If SRS periodicity interval is not accurate, there will be some redudency in mesurements, inacurate reporting, shifting of the report measurements update, that could not be deteced by the LMF. As conscequence the report could be totally incurate …
summaryOfChange:
Add the missed values of SRS periodicity including 160ms, 320ms, 1280ms 2560ms, 81920ms in the Measurement Periodicity to align with SRS periodicity.
Add the value of 61440ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 1min in the Measurement Periodicity.
Add the value of 368640ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 6min in the Measurement Periodicity.
Add the value of 737280ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 12min in the Measurement Periodicity.
Add the value of 1843200ms, which is aligned with SRS periodicity, to subtitute the 30min in the Measurement Periodicity.

consequencesIfNotApproved: CSI-RS configuration will be sent to other nodes having no actual use of it, or cell information to which CSI-RS does not apply will be sent unnecessarily over network interfaces,  which increases Xn message size and breaks the principle of gradual building up cell list information.
reasonForChange:
The current CSI-RS Transmission Indication IE is assumed to be valid for all the gNB neighbour and served cells information signalled in the Xn Setup and NG-RAN node Configuration Update procedures. However, such assumption breaks the principle of building up neighbour cell information step by step, which was agreed in the past to avoid the receiver not being able to decode ASN.1 due to huge Xn message size.

In order to avoid the same mistake as in the past and comply with the current principle, it is necessary to make the CSI-RS based transmission for mobility valid only for the cells which are concerned with such configuration and that will use it for CSI-RS based mobility.
summaryOfChange:
Include detailed neighbour NR and served cell NR CSI-RS resource configuration information in the Xn Setup and NG-RAN node Configuration Update procedures, as follows:
Explicit CSI-RS configurations contained in the Measurement Timing Configurations (MTC), which is used for CSI-RS based mobility 
Indices of the present CSI-RSes in this MTC
the status of their CSI-RS transmission
For each present CSI-RS, the cells neighbouring it in the neighbourhood coverage area, and their CSI-RS indices.
title: Signalling of Neighbour cell CSI-RS configuration information over Xn [CSIRSXn]

consequencesIfNotApproved: The specification text is not correct.
reasonForChange:
RAN2 specified that the UE QMC capability is included in the UE Radio Capability in 38.331.  
QoE-Parameters-r17 ::=                    SEQUENCE {
qoe-Streaming-MeasReport-r17              ENUMERATED {supported}    OPTIONAL
qoe-MTSI-MeasReport-r17                   ENUMERATED {supported}     OPTIONAL,
    qoe-VR-MeasReport-r17                     ENUMERATED {supported}     OPTIONAL,
    ran-VisibleQoE-Streaming-MeasReport-r17   ENUMERATED {supported}  OPTIONAL,
    ran-VisibleQoE-VR-MeasReport-r17          ENUMERATED {supported}   OPTIONAL,
    ul-MeasurementReportAppLayer-Seg-r17      ENUMERATED {supported}   OPTIONAL,
    ...
}

UE-NR-Capability-v1700 ::=               SEQUENCE {
    inactiveStatePO-Determination-r17        ENUMERATED {supported}          OPTIONAL,
    highSpeedParameters-v1700                HighSpeedParameters-v1700        OPTIONAL,
    powSav-Parameters-v1700                  PowSav-Parameters-v1700       OPTIONAL,
    mac-Parameters-v1700                     MAC-Parameters-v1700             OPTIONAL,
    ims-Parameters-v1700                     IMS-Parameters-v1700             OPTIONAL,
    measAndMobParameters-v1700               MeasAndMobParameters-v1700,    qoe-Parameters-r17                       QoE-Parameters-r17                      OPTIONAL,
redCapParameters-r17                     RedCapParameters-r17                 OPTIONAL,

RAN3 include the UE Radio Capability and UE QMC Capability in the UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION. So the UE QMC Capability is duplicated in the message to AMF. 
We may have more thinking on the usage of UE QMC Capability in AMF. The AMF does not decode the UE Radio Capability and use the explicitly UE QMC Capability to check the qualification for the UE when s-based QMC is initiated. But in the SA5 QMC specification 28.405 v17.1.0 section 4.4.2, they state the RAN is responsible for the capability match.” 4)The eNB checks if the UE capability that matches the criteria for serviceType in the ActivateAreaQMCJob.” 

So based on the above discussion, the UE QMC Capability does not need to be explicitly included in the message UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION to the AMF.

Solution: in case RAN is responsible for capability match for S-based QMC, remove the UE QMC Capability from UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION and remove the contents of 9.3.1.226 UE QMC Capability
summaryOfChange:
RAN is responsible for capability match for S-based QMC, the change is as below:
remove the UE QMC Capability from UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION 
remove the contents of  9.3.1.226 UE QMC Capability and change it to void
remove the corresponding ASN.1 code of above changes

The Measurement Periodicity IE is included in Measurement Request message and E-CID Measurement Initiation Request message. To support the LMF requesting the measurement results from the NG-RAN, the codedpoints were extended to align with the periodicity of SRS transmissions. Currently, this extension was not applicable in E-CID Measurement Initiation Request message for the reporting of E-CID measurements. 
However, E-CID positioning method has now been enhanced to support the reporting of NR UL Angle of Arrival (AoA). Then the measurement periodicity extended codepoints should also be applicable to E-Cell ID positioning.
summaryOfChange:
Add the Measurement Periodicity NR-AoA IE, to contain all codepoints applicable to NR UL Angle of Arrival. The new IE is conditional on Report Characteristics IE set to “Periodic” and Measurement Quantities Item IE set to “NR UL AoA”.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Not possible to indicate to LMF that UE’s SRS transmission (for periodic and semi-persistent) has stopped
reasonForChange:
For several positioning measurements, the gNB is requested to allocate SRS resources to the UE and to request the UE to start sending the SRS, periodically, semi-persistently or aperiodically (one-shot). 
There are cases where the periodic or semi-persistent SRS configuration has stopped to be reported by the UE, e.g., due to deteriorating radio conditions, an RLF or intra-gNB mobility event, or when the SRS is released by the gNB implementation while maintaining the UE connection, etc. In such cases, the LMF may not know immediately that the transmission of the SRS (periodic or semi-persistent) has stopped. An explicit indication from the gNB to the LMF that the SRS has stopped is necessary so that the LMF can (timely) abort the measurements in the neighboring cells and deactivate the positioning. 
Since this corresponds to a change in the UE’s SRS configuration detected by the gNB-CU, we propose to enhance the NRPPA POSITIONING INFORMATION UPDATE message to indicate that the UE is no longer transmitting UL SRS.
summaryOfChange:
Addition of a new SRS Transmission Status IE coded as ENUMERATED(stopped,...) in the POSITIONING INFORMATION UPDATE message to indicate that UE is no longer transmitting positioning information (UL SRS), with adequte procedural text.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release). 
This impact can be considered isolated because it affects only the Positioning Information Transfer procedures.
This CR is BC

For each PDU session resource successfully setup at the target NG-RAN, the target NG-RAN node may allocate resources for additional Xn-U PDU session resource GTP-U tunnels, indicated in the Secondary Data Forwarding Info from target NG-RAN node List IE.

In case the source NG-RAN node is a disaggregated node with CU-CP and CU-UP separation, for a PDU session, the source CU-CP should also be able to provide two data forwarding addresses for different set of QoS flows, especially in case of PDU session split during Handover, or split PDU session QoS flow reallocation during Handover.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Packet loss occurs when e.g. the UE re-connects in a new cell of another gNB in which no contexts of its joined multicast sessions have been established yet, as multicast data forwarding in case of UE context retrieval is not supported.
reasonForChange:
In the current Rel-17 specifications, the data forwarding for multicast session is not supported when e.g. a UE in RRC_CONNECTED re-connects at a new NG-RAN node during an active multicast session as the first UE in the new NG-RAN node that has joined the multicast session.
This CR introduces Rel-17 functionality on which Rel-18 functions can be built.
In details, XnAP currently supports the old NG-RAN node requesting MBS data forwarding by MBS Session Information List IE in the RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT RESPONSE message, if there is multicast data pending to be forwarded. However, the new NG-RAN node cannot currently provide the forwarding addresses to the old NG-RAN node. Then, it will cause data lost for the above-mentioned scenarios.
In S6-232609, SA6 clarifies that based on 3GPP TS 22.179 clause 6.15, there is the following requirement: 
[R-6.15.3.2-016] There shall be no (0 ms) initial lost audio at receiving user.
Therefore, to avoid potential data loss, it is needed to enable the MBS data forwarding in case of UE context retrieval.

Introduce MBS Session Information Response List IE to provide the MBS forwarding addresses to the old NG-RAN node.

consequencesIfNotApproved: RTT between UE and serving gNB (i.e., physical distance between UE and gNB) is less accurately known which may adversely affect location determination during e.g., Emergency Calls.
reasonForChange:
NR Timing Advance (TA), i.e., NR TA Type 2, for NR UL E-CID was introduced in NRPPa in Rel-17 as a TEI17. NR TA Type 1 which more accurately reflects RTT from serving gNB to UE, however, is currently not supported in NR UL E-CID. 

To calculate NR TA Type 1 at the gNB, the gNB needs to know UE Rx-Tx Time Difference as well as gNB Rx-Tx Time Difference. Both measurements are defined in TS 38.215. Without the reporting of UE Rx-Tx, we have a gap with LTE E-CID method, where such measurement was reported over LPPa, and over NRPPa, in case NG-RAN is an ng-eNB, but not from a gNB.

In NR, the gNB Rx-Tx Time Difference (i.e. NR Timing Advance) is by definition always available at the gNB. 
Regarding UE Rx-Tx Time Difference, a procedure for sharing the measurement by the UE with the gNB is defined in TS 38.300 section 16.8 within the context of Propagation Delay Compensation (PDC) for Time Sensitive Communications (TSC). This means that both measurements as well as procedures to make these measurements available at the gNB are already supported in Rel-17. The only missing aspect for supporting reporting NR TA Type 1 and addressing the gap with LTE UL E-CID is the signalling over NRPPa.

Below is the measurement definition in TS 38.331 (No F1AP impacts are needed, since the measurement is avialable at RRC level).

It is up to gNB implementation to ensure the time alignment between the two measurements when receiving the request from the LMF containing the two measurement UE Rx-Tx Time Difference Measurement and  gNB Rx-Tx Time Difference (i.e. NR Timing Advance)quantities codepoints
summaryOfChange:
Add support for NR UE Rx-Tx time difference for NR UL E-CID measurement reporting.

Note:
LMF is expected to request also request gNB Rx-Tx TD (i.e. NR Timing Advance) if it requests UE Rx-Tx TD.
If gNB provides UE Rx-TX TD measurement result, it should ensure (via implementation) time alignment with the gNB Rx-Tx TD measurement (i.e. NR Timing Advance) result.
title: Introduction of NR UE Rx-Tx time difference measurement in NR UL E-CID

consequencesIfNotApproved: Unnecessary signalling and cost foreseen.

Then the gNB-CU-CP sends BROADCAST BEARER MODIFICATION REQUEST message to the gNB-CU-UP, including MRB ID IE and BC Bearer Context F1-U TNL Info at DU IE. 
Currently the F1-U tunnel Not Established IE is introduced per MBS Session, in such case, in some scenarios, the gNB-CU and gNB-DU has to establish F1-U tunnels multiple times for some area sessions. In order to fulfil the agreement and avoid unnecessary cost, it is needed to introduce the F1-U tunnel Not Established IE also in per Area Session granularity.

Introduce F1-U tunnel Not Established IE in the BC Bearer Context F1-U TNL Info IE, in the location independent branch for the MBS session, and also in the location dependent branch in per Area Session granularity.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The UE-based TA measurement feature in Rel-18 LTM may not work as intended.
reasonForChange:
Rel-18 Intra-CU LTM specified two mechanisms of pre-calculating UL TA values for faster RACH-less access to a candidate cell (called “early TA acquisition”): 
NW obtains UL TA values of candidate cells before cell switch (by PDDCH-ordering the UE to initiate RACH) and configures the pre-acquired TA value to the UE in the LTM Cell Switch Command. 
 “UE-based TA measurements”, where CU configures the UE to derive UL TA on its own based on the Rx timing difference between the current serving cell and candidate cell, together with the current TA value. 

The second mechanism has been designed in a way that it cannot be used unless the serving DU explicitly indicates so (set to “FFF”) via LTM Cell Switch Command (even though configured to the UE via RRC by CU). However, DU is currently obvilous of whether CU configured the UE-based TA measurements to the UE and for which cells. As a result, the serving DU (who is not aware) won’t be able to indicate the UE to use it at all. Instead, it will execute the first mechanism for a candidate cell (for which the UE-based TA measurement has already been configured) to provide the TA value in the LTM Cell Switch Command, where the UE has to unnecessarily follow the PDCCH order and initiate RACH to that candidate cell. Due to its cascaded design, the UE-based TA measurement feature may not work as intended, if such configuration from CU is not known to DU who controls early RACH and decides cell switch.
summaryOfChange:
In the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST, 
Reshape the Early Sync Information List IE into two separate IEs, one for candidate cell information (Early Sync Candidate Cell Information List IE) and the other for serving cell information (Early Sync Serving Cell Information IE), 

(2) For each separated IE, added OCTET STRING of 
UE Based TA Measurement Configuration IE, which refers to ltm-UE-MeasuredTA-ID-r18 IE when in Early Sync Candidate Cell Information List IE and refers to ltm-ServingCellUE-MeasuredTA-ID-r18 IE when in Early Sync Serving Cell Information IE
so that CU can provide the UE-based TA measurement configured to the UE for the candiate cells and serving cell toward a DU. 

The corresponding descriptions and semantics are added. 


Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only has an impact on LTM early UL acquisition function between CU and DU.

reasonForChange:
The LTM can coexist with the feature of MIMO with 2TA. In particular, one cell can have two TA values, each of which is associated with one TAG. In current F1AP signaling, the TAG information of TA value of the candidate cell is provided from the candidate gNB-DU to the source gNB-DU via gNB-CU in the DU-CU TA INFORMATION TRANSFER and CU-DU TA INFORMATION TRANSFER messages. 
To avoid triggering PDCCH order to obtain TA of candidate cell(s) in target gNB-DU, source gNB-DU can transfer valid TA information to target gNB-DU when LTM is triggered. Therefore, the valid TA value can be reused in target gNB-DU for the following LTM execution. However, the TAG information of TA value is not provided.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN cannot be supported.
reasonForChange:
In TS 23.316, the AUN3 device is define as follows. 
Authenticable Non-3GPP (AUN3) device: A device that does not support NAS signalling, is connected to 5GC via a RG and can be authenticated by 5GC over the RG.
In section 7.2.8.1, the AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN procedure is specified as follows.

7.2.8.1	AUN3 device Registration via W-5GAN
An authenticable non-3GPP devices (AUN3) may get connected behind 5G-RG as defined in clause 4.10c.
This clause specifies how an AUN3 device can be registered via 5G-RG.
<Irrelevant Text Omitted >
4.	The W-AGF selects an AMF based on the received AN parameter provided by the 5G-RG and based on local policy, as specified in clause 6.3.5 of TS 23.501 [2]. The W-AGF shall determine that a W-CP connection is for an AUN3 device and apply corresponding policies.
	The W-AGF sends an NGAP INITIAL UE message to the selected AMF. For an AUN3 device, the W-AGF indicates to AMF if the N2 connection relates to an AUN3 device and if there is an existing N2 connection for a 5G-RG connected to the same GLI/GCI (where the initial NAS message related with NGAP INITIAL UE message has been received).
	If the W-AGF indicated for an AUN3 device that there is no existing 5G-RG N2 connection for a 5G-RG connected to the same GLI/GCI, then the AMF rejects the registration request and further steps of this procedure are skipped. Otherwise, the procedure continues.
It can be observed that during the AUN3 device Registration procedure, in the Initial UE message, the W-AGF needs to indicate:  
if the N2 connection relates to an AUN3 device, and
if there is an existing N2 connection for a 5G-RG connected to the same GLI/GCI. 
 But it is missing in the NGAP specification.

Opt1: configure the ServingCellNoResetID and the noResetID of each candidate cell to the gNB-DU
Opt2: after gNB-CU receives the DU-CU Cell Switch Notification message, the gNB-CU triggers UE Context Modification procedure to indicate whether RLC reestablishment is needed or not.  

Compared with Opt1, Opt2 may delay the RLC re-establishment handling since it relies on the configuration from gNB-CU after triggering LTM. Moreover, the Opt1 is more aligned with RAN2’s design, and RAN3 determines to use the similar design for the UE based TA measurement. Thus, Opt1 is a preferable solution.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
CN is not able to get the up-to-date user location information in case of UE context resume and suspend.
Wrong handling of slice information at old ng-eNB side upon receiving AMF CP Relocation Indication, e.g., in case these IEs are wrong, the old ng-eNB will not be able to return the non-delivered NAS PDUs to the AMF.
reasonForChange:
#Issue 1 missing ULI in UP CIoT optimization procedures
SA2 has discussed ULI reporting enhancements since Rel-12 and requires the RAN node to report the most up to date User Location Information (refer to S2-133865/R3-131887) to CN. Therefore, the RAN node reports the ULI during the initial access, handover, context release procedures, etc.

In Rel-16, UP CIoT optimization with 5GC was specified, and the UE Context Resume and UE Context Suspend procedures were introduced. In such scenario, the UE changes from RRC_IDLE to RRC_CONNECTED state during UE Context Resume and moves to RRC_IDLE again after UE Context Suspend, but User Location Information was missing in these two procedures in the messages to CN (i.e., UE CONTEXT SUSPEND REQUEST and UE CONTEXT RESUME REQUEST messages).

And there is a common understanding that only UE Context Resume and UE Context Release procedures are allowed to take place on a suspended UE-associated signalling connection. Therefore, it is preferable to send the ULI using those procedures, rather than providing it via separate Location Reporting procedures, which will lead to increased signalling load, and may not possible after UE Context Suspend.  

#Issue 2 wrong additional IEs in CP CIoT optimization procedure
In NB-IoT CP solution, when the UE moves to a cell belongs to another ng-eNB, RLF + RRCResetablishment will happen, upon receiving INITIAL UE MESSAGE message from new ng-eNB, the AMF may inform the old ng-eNB that the UE is to be relocated via AMF CP Relocation Indication procedure, to trigger the old ng-eNB to return the non-delivered NAS PDUs to the AMF, and UE context release will happen between the AMF and the old ng-eNB afterwards. Therefore, the AMF CP Relocation Indication procedure is not a procedure to establish something, the slice related information was wrongly added here based on R3-193410 CR.
summaryOfChange:
For Issue #1, adding User Location Information in the following messages:
UE CONTEXT SUSPEND REQUEST
UE CONTEXT RESUME REQUEST

For Issue #2, mark the following slicing related IEs in AMF CP RELOCATION INDICATION as shall not be included, and to be ignored if received:
S-NSSAI
Allowed NSSAI

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only adding the missing ULI in the UP CIoT optimization related resume and suspend procedures, and removing the IEs which should not be included in the AMF CP relocation Indication procedure. 
This CR has functional and protocol impact.
title: Correction on CIoT optimization with 5GC

When the Signaling based MDT PLMN List is not provided in the MDT configuration, the MDT configuration is propagated to the target node in case of intra-PLMN mobility but not in case of inter-PLMN mobility. A clarification is therefore needed to describe how the NG-RAN node fills in the mandatorily present Signaling based MDT PLMN List IE in the intra-PLMN mobility case.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Candidate gNB-DU is unable to know the TCI State for Semi-Persistent CSI-RS activation.
reasonForChange:
For each periodic CSI-RS resource, the candidate gNB-DU provides each CSI-RS associated with pre-configured QCL-info (via qcl-InfoPeriodicCSI-RS, which indicates a TCI state ID). However, for Semi-Persistent CSI-RS, this is not possible. The reason is that Semi-Persistent CSI-RSs are pre-configured but activated dynamically, based on needs determined from periodic SSB or CSI-RS measurements.

Therefore, when the source gNB-DU selects an Semi-Persistent CSI-RS for activation, it also needs to determine the appropriate TCI State and indicate it to the candidate gNB-DU(s), this ensures that the Semi-Persistent CSI-RS can be properly activated with the correct TCI State.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The migrating IAB-node will not send the buffered RRCReconfiguration to its child IAB-node if the IAB-MT handover failure. 
The information about the neighbour node cell list may not interpreted correctrly by the receiving gNB-DU.  
The neighboring node cell information is not applicable for intra-CU dual connected IAB-node.
The buffer size threshold for congestion determination is not align with BAP specification.
The RB set index is not aligned with ASN.1.
reasonForChange:
RAN3-114bis has the following working assumption: “WA: Upon migration/HO failure case, the buffered RRC message is still transferred to child node”. And RAN2-117e agreed that “RAN2 does not have specific concerns about RAN3’s WA that upon migration/HO failure, the buffered RRC message is still transferred to the child node.” After HO failure, the migrating IAB-MT will perform RLF recovery by initiating RRCReestablishment, 
If the recovery fails, the migrating IAB-node will send BH RLF notification to its child node, and then the child node will perform RLF recovery. In this case, it doesn’t matter whether the buffered RRCReconfiguration message is released to the child node or not.
If the recovery is successful, the migrating IAB-node should release the buffered RRCReconfiguration message to the child node. This is to let the child node perform reconfiguration of IP address and default BAP configuration in the target path if the migrating IAB-node connects to the target partent node after successful recovery, or to avoid the PDCP SN gap with the subsequent RRCReconfiguration if the migrating IAB-node connects to a different target parent node.
Therefore, the condition that the migrating IAB-node has successfully recovered after handover failure should also be captured in the UE context modification procedure.
The sentence “for each parent-node cell serving an IAB-node indicated by the gNB-CU UE F1AP ID IE and the gNB-DU UE F1AP ID IE” in the paragraph of about the Neighbour-Node Cells List is confusing. It reads like the gNB-DU will only store the peer parent node information. However, other neighbour cells which are not the peer parent node should also be take into account for the interference mitigation. 
The Buffer size threshold for determining the congestion in clause 9.2.9.1 is in bytes, it does not match the unit for available buffer size defined in BAP specification TS38.340.
In the neighboring-node cells list IE, the information of peer parent node’s cell should cover both intra-CU DC and inter-CU DC scenario, as described in RAN1 LS (R3-222799), but the semantics description for the peer-parent node indicator only mention the “boundary IAB-node”, so the intra-CU dual connectivity case is not included.
In section 9.2.9.3, the constant maxnoofServingCells is used in Serving Cells List IE but not defied in the range bound table. 
In clause 9.3.1.107, the RB set index is not extendable in the table, not aligh with the ASN.1 part.
RAN1 send LS R1-2205644, to notify the new agreements in RAN1 #109e : If the RB sets of a Rel-17 IAB-DU H/S/NA resource configuration do not cover the entire carrier bandwidth: The remaining RBs not part of an RB set configuration are considered as included in the last RB set. This agreement needs to be captured in the RB set configuration.
summaryOfChange:
In  section 8.3.4.2, add “migrating IAB-MT has successfully performed RLF recovery after handover failure, and if the migrating IAB-node has one or more routing entries for the target path. ” as new condition for the gNB-DU to release the buffered RRCReconfiguration towards the child node. And made some editorial changes to the other conditions.
In clause 8.10.2.2, remove the confusing sentence “for each parent-node cell serving an IAB-node indicated by the gNB-CU UE F1AP ID IE and the gNB-DU UE F1AP ID IE”. And clarify how to interpret the UE F1AP IDs as well as the Peer Parent-Node Indicator which is also optional IE in the message.
Change the bytes to kilobytes in the semantics description for the Buffer Size Threshold in clause 9.2.9.1.
In section 9.2.9.3, change the “boundary IAB-node” as “dual connected IAB-node” in the semantics description of the “Peer Parent-Node Indicator”. 
In section 9.2.9.3, add the Maxnoofservingcells in the range bound table.
In clause 9.3.1.107, change the RB set index to be extendable.
In 9.3.1.230, capture the following agreements in the semantics description of RB set size IE: If the RB sets of a Rel-17 IAB-DU H/S/NA resource configuration do not cover the entire carrier bandwidth: The remaining RBs not part of an RB set configuration are considered as included in the last RB set. consequencesIfNotApproved: The inter-frequency no GAP feature is not supported, and it may lead to unexpected consequences if the interFrequencyConfig-NoGap-r16 IE has to be generated by the CU itself while transparent to the DU.
reasonForChange:
In TS 38.331, in the MeasConfig configured to the UE, the interFrequencyConfig-NoGap-r16 IE is included (which was agreed in R2-2006261). The purpose of this IE is that: 
If the field is set to true, UE is configured to perform SSB based inter-frequency measurement without measurement gaps when the inter-frequency SSB is completely contained in the active DL BWP of the UE, as specified in TS 38.133, clause 9.3
Also as described in R2-2006261, RAN4 makes agreements that: 
If network configures the flag, when SMTC is partially overlapped with network configured MG, UE perform inter-frequency without MG measurement outside gap
If network does not configure the flag, when SMTC is partially overlapped with network configured MG, UE perform inter-frequency measurement within gap.


In the CU-DU architecture, the measurement gap configuration is generated by the DU and sent to the CU. However, in the current DU to CU RRC Information, only two gap related IEs (MeasGapConfig and MeasGapSharingConfig) are included, while the interFrequencyConfig-NoGap is missing.
summaryOfChange:
Add the interFrequencyConfig-NoGap IE in the DU to CU RRC Information.

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).

reasonForChange:
RAN3-121 meeting agreed the following for the mobile IAB:
Agree that the mIAB-DU’s CU to be informed about the mIAB-authorized status by mIAB-MT´s CU when IAB MT and IAB DU connect to different IAB donor Cus.
And RAN3 121bis meeting agreed the TP R3-235916 which introduce the Mobile IAB Authorization Status in the IAB TRANSPORT MIGRATION MODIFICATION REQUEST.
In release 17, the decoupled connection scenario is also possible for a fixed IAB node, i.e., an IAB-MT may connect to a non-F1 terminating donor, while its co-located IAB-DU connects to an F1 terminating donor, and the two donors are different. In such scenario, the non-F1 terminating donor will connect to the IAB-MT’s AMF, and can get the latest IAB authorization status from the AMF via NGAP. The IAB node authorization status should also be known by the F1 terminating donor. For example, if the IAB-node is not authorized, the F1 terminating donor may perform orderly F1 release to this IAB-DU. And if the IAB node is authorized again, the F1 terminating donor can react properly to allow the IAB-node serve UE again. But it is not clear how can the F1 terminating donor know the IAB authorization status.
We tend to think the solution for mobile IAB node can be copied for the IAB node in Rel-17 also, and this will be the easiest way.

consequencesIfNotApproved: There remains mistakes in the specification on multi-path relay.
reasonForChange:
For multi-path split SRB without duplication, DU should identify the MP split SRB and setup one RLC entity if necessary (for case 2.1) and associate the SRB to the Uu Relay RLC channel based on SRB Mapping Info (for case 1 and case 2.1). Specifically,
-1 for indirect path addition on top of direct path, when indirect path addition is configured, the SRB Mapping Info should be included. DU can identify the MP split SRB, and then associate the SRB with the Uu Relay RLC channel based on the SRB Mapping Info besides the direct path RLC entity(which is already existed). 
-2 for direct path addition on top of indirect path, when the direct path addition is configured:
-2.1) if SRB Mapping Info is included, it implies the SRB is a MP split SRB. DU should setup one RLC entity on direct path and associate the SRB to the Uu Relay RLC channel based on SRB Mapping Info.
-2.2) if SRB Mapping Info is not included, it implies the previous indirect bearer is changed to a direct bearer. DU should setup one RLC entity on direct path while release the previous stored SRB Mapping Info and indirect bearer configuration.
Based on the analysis above, in clause 8.3.4.2, the text description for MP split SRB without duplication case is added, i.e. “If Path Addition Information IE is configured, and if the SRB Mapping Info IE is contained in the SRB To Be Setup List IE, the gNB-DU shall, if supported, setup one RLC entity if necessary for the direct path and map the indicated SRB to the Uu Relay RLC channel based on the SRB Mapping Info IE.”.
It is possible that DU initiates UE context modification required message to modify a DRB configured with multi-path relay based duplication. The description of multi-path relay based duplication is missing in clause 8.3.5.2.
Execute Duplication IE could also be applied to SRB configured with MP relay based duplication. That is, if SRB duplication is activated, and the Execute Duplication IE is indicated, the gNB-DU can perform CA based duplication or multi-path relay based duplication for the SRB. The related description is missing. 
In R17 U2N relay, RAN3 agreed Uu RLC channel may be configured during relay UE context setup procedure considering the UE may act as a U2N relay UE later to forward remote UE’s SRB0/1 by using the Uu RLC channel. While for MP scenario 2 (indirect path using N3C), single indirect N3C path and direct path addition on top of indirect path are not supported, there is no benefit/no reasonable to configure the Uu RLC channel for N3C path in advance.
It is not clear why “or the logical channel” is included in the following sentence. The terminology Uu Relay RLC channel is also used in MP scenario 2 in RAN2 300/331 specs. “If the Additional Duplication Indication IE and SRB Mapping Info IE are both contained in the SRB To Be Setup List IE, the gNB-DU shall, if supported, setup the indicated RLC entities for the indicated SRB, and map the indicated SRB to the Uu Relay RLC channel or the logical channel based on the SRB Mapping Info IE.”   Suggest to remove “or the logical channel” from the sentence.
summaryOfChange:
In clause 8.3.4.2, the text description for MP split SRB without duplication case is added, i.e. “If the Path Addition Information IE and the SRB Mapping Info IE are both contained in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, the gNB-DU shall, if supported, setup one RLC entity if necessary for the direct path and map the indicated SRB to the Uu Relay RLC channel based on the SRB Mapping Info IE.”.
In clause 8.3.5.2, add multi-path relay based duplication.
In clause 8.3.4.2, 8.3.5.2, 8.4.2.2, if SRB duplication is activated, and the Execute Duplication IE is indicated, the gNB-DU can perform CA based duplication or multi-path relay based duplication for the SRB.
In clause 8.3.1.2, for Uu RLC channel to be setup list, suggest to remove “or a L2 MP Relay UE using N3C”.  And, in clause 9.2.2.1 and 9.2.2.2, for maxnoofUuRLCChannels, remove “or L2 N3C relaying”.
In clause 8.3.4.2, remove “or the logical channel”.

reasonForChange:

Target SMF need to trigger an NGAP PDU Session Modification procedure after every Xn handover or connection resume and include the MBS Assistance Information in the NGAP PDU Session Modification Request message but this generates significant additional processing and signaling.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The gNB-DU cannot understand the forbidden and/or affected band combinations, and unable to generate the proper lower layer configuration.
reasonForChange:
In order to indicate temporary capabilities restriction, it was specified in TS 38.331 that: 
the gNB will configure musim-CandidateBandList-r18 to the UE for reporting temporary capabilities restriction, as the band-filter list.
in the UAI, the UE signals its temporary capabilities restrictions as forbidden band combinations with band indexed to the band-filter list and/or affected band combinations with band indexed to the band-filter list along with explicit fields for restricted (lower) capabilities e.g. maximum MIMO layers. 
Thus, the forbidden/affected band combinations need to combine the UAI and band-filter list provided by gNB.

In the CU/DU split architecture, the band-filter list is generated by the CU. When the CU receives MUSIM UAI from the UE, it should deliver it to the DU with the band-filter list together so that the DU can understand what the temporary capabilities restriction is to generate the proper configuration (e.g. MIMO layers configuration) based on UE temporary capabilities restriction. Otherwise, the DU cannot derive the forbidden/affected bands.
summaryOfChange: -	Introduce the “musim-CandidateBandList” IE in the CU to DU RRC Information in the UE context setup request message and modification request message.
title: Filter information for temporary capabilities restriction in Multi-SIM

consequencesIfNotApproved: The continuity of QMC during NG-based inter-MN HO is not supported.
reasonForChange:
The continuity of QoE measurement collection in NR-DC scenario was discussed in Rel-18, but only XnAP signalling is enhanced to support it. However, when inter-MN HO happens, the NGAP HO messages could also be used to forward the QMC configuration information from the source MN to the target MN (via AMF). Specifically, Source NG-RAN Node to Target NG-RAN Node Transparent Container IE is used to forward the information to the target MN transparently. So, we believe the Source SN to Target SN QMC Information IE should be added in this NGAP container, to support the NG-based inter-MN handover, for the continuity of QMC in NR-DC.
To support the continuity of QMC in dual connectivity, the QoE and RVQoE reporting path shall also be passed to the target MN, similar as in XnAP. So, the QoE and RVQoE reporting paths IE shall be added into the QMC configuration, so that it could be sent in the source to target transparent container during NG-based HO.

consequencesIfNotApproved: DL-PRS Aggregation is not aligned with RAN1/2 specifications and can not be proper supported.
reasonForChange:
The Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics may include a "PRS Bandwidth Aggregation Request Indication" flag whose meaning is nowhere defined.

DL-PRS aggregation is defined across DL-PRS Resource Sets of different positioning frequency layers (PFLs), and a TRP may configure DL-PRS aggregation across 2, 3 or 2+2 PFLs.
A UE may indicate to the LMF the desired DL-PRS in the LPP IE NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Request. The LPP IE NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Request may include the IE NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Information, which defines the desired DL-PRS parameter (the UE can request these explicit DL-PRS parameter which are within the scope of previously provided (predefined) on-demand DL-PRS configurations (NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Configurations)). These DL-PRS parameter in LPP are the same as in the NRPPa Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics. For DL-PRS aggregation, a UE may indicate in addition which NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Information elements are desired for aggregation. However, the corresponding functionality is missing in the Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics IE. Therefore, it is unclear how an LMF can indicate to the NG-RAN node which DL-PRS configuration information is requested/applicable for aggregation.
The TRP INFORMATION REQUEST message may include a request for available/supported on-demand DL-PRS information ('on-demand prs'). However, the corresponding response element On-demand PRS TRP Information (9.2.65) does not include any information on whether the on-demand PRS Request is allowed also for aggregated DL-PRS.
The TRP INFORMATION REQUEST message may include a "PRS Bandwidth Aggregation Request Indication" flag whose meaning is nowhere defined.
summaryOfChange:
The PRS Bandwidth Aggregation Request Indication (ENUMERATED {true}) in Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics is replaced by a new IE PRS Bandwidth Aggregation Request Information List, which is defined as a list of indices to the Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics to indicate which of the Requested DL-PRS Resource Set Items are requested for aggregation (analogous to LPP TS 37.355).
An additional bit in the On-demand PRS Request Allowed IE in the On-demand PRS TRP Information IE is allocated for aggregated DL-PRS.
The PRS Bandwidth Aggregation Request Indication IE in the TRP INFORMATION REQUEST message is removed, since not needed. If the TRP INFORMATION REQUEST message includes a request for DL-PRS (‘prs config’), the response may or may not include the Aggregated PRS Resource Set List in PRS Configuration. There is no need for an explicit request flag.

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
The CR has a protocol and function impact.
The change is isolated to DL-PRS with bandwidth aggregation.
The CR is non-backwards compatible from protocol point of view.
title: Correction to Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics

consequencesIfNotApproved:
CN is not able to get the up-to-date user location information in case of UE context resume and suspend.
Wrong handling of slice information at old ng-eNB side upon receiving AMF CP Relocation Indication, e.g., in case these IEs are wrong, the old ng-eNB will not be able to return the non-delivered NAS PDUs to the AMF.
reasonForChange:
#Issue 1 missing ULI in UP CIoT optimization procedures
SA2 has discussed ULI reporting enhancements since Rel-12 and requires the RAN node to report the most up to date User Location Information (refer to S2-133865/R3-131887) to CN. Therefore, the RAN node reports the ULI during the initial access, handover, context release procedures, etc.

In Rel-16, UP CIoT optimization with 5GC was specified, and the UE Context Resume and UE Context Suspend procedures were introduced. In such scenario, the UE changes from RRC_IDLE to RRC_CONNECTED state during UE Context Resume and moves to RRC_IDLE again after UE Context Suspend, but User Location Information was missing in these two procedures in the messages to CN (i.e., UE CONTEXT SUSPEND REQUEST and UE CONTEXT RESUME REQUEST messages).

And there is a common understanding that only UE Context Resume and UE Context Release procedures are allowed to take place on a suspended UE-associated signalling connection. Therefore, it is preferable to send the ULI using those procedures, rather than providing it via separate Location Reporting procedures, which will lead to increased signalling load, and may not possible after UE Context Suspend.  

#Issue 2 wrong additional IEs in CP CIoT optimization procedure
In NB-IoT CP solution, when the UE moves to a cell belongs to another ng-eNB, RLF + RRCResetablishment will happen, upon receiving INITIAL UE MESSAGE message from new ng-eNB, the AMF may inform the old ng-eNB that the UE is to be relocated via AMF CP Relocation Indication procedure, to trigger the old ng-eNB to return the non-delivered NAS PDUs to the AMF, and UE context release will happen between the AMF and the old ng-eNB afterwards. Therefore, the AMF CP Relocation Indication procedure is not a procedure to establish something, the slice related information was wrongly added here based on R3-193410 CR.
summaryOfChange:
For Issue #1, adding User Location Information in the following messages:
UE CONTEXT SUSPEND REQUEST
UE CONTEXT RESUME REQUEST

For Issue #2, removing the following slicing related IEs in AMF CP RELOCATION INDICATION:
S-NSSAI
Allowed NSSAI

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only adding the missing ULI in the UP CIoT optimization related resume and suspend procedures, and removing the IEs which should not be included in the AMF CP relocation Indication procedure. 
This CR has functional and protocol impact.
title: Correction on CIoT optimization with 5GC

consequencesIfNotApproved: LTM cell switch may fail due to missing TCI states information.
reasonForChange: In Rel-18 LTM, the TCI states configuration are only included when early synchronization is requested, but they are also required during a cell switch (since the LTM cell switch MAC CE includes a TCI state which the UE should use). If no TCI state list is configured for an LTM candidate, an LTM cell switch MAC CE indicating that TCI state cannot be executed by the UE since the UE would not have any TCI state to refer to and the result would be that the procedure will fail. To ensure TCI state information is always available for cell switch, it should be included beyond early synchronization. Therefore, we propose adding a new IE in the F1AP LTM Configuration Information IE to reference it.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce new TCI States Configurations List IEs to the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST, and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE messages, to transfer the TCI states configurations.

consequencesIfNotApproved: L2 measurements calculated at CU-UP per mapped 5QI will be not supported.
reasonForChange:
In the LS [R2-1902806] from RAN2, RAN2 asks RAN3 to check the feasibility of some L1 and L2 measurements listed in SA5 spec TS 28.552.
Some measurements which should be counted at PDCP layer in CU-UP including Packet Loss Rate, Packet Drop Rate, Packet Delay, and PDCP Data Volume, needs to be calculated per mapped 5QI. RAN3 has agreed to use the 5QI assigned to a DRB to represent the Qos level of DRB (named as 'mapped 5QI' by SA5). All Qos flows mapped on the same bearer will receive the same Qos treatment.
Currently, the CU-UP does not know the mapped 5QI of each DRB. Therefore, in order to support those measurements, the gNB-CU should inform the CU-UP of the mapped 5QI of each DRB.
In RAN3 #103bis meeting, it was agreed that :
“DRB QoS IE mapping over E1 is feasible and shall be introduced (can be done in Rel-15 as a correction)”.

consequencesIfNotApproved: F1-C transfer path cannot be configured correctly.
reasonForChange:
In EN-DC case, to support CP-UP separation, the F1-C transfer path can be configured to the IAB node. In TS38.331, such configuration is included in CellGroupConfig IE, which is generated by the DU of parent node. In this sense, the current specification assumes that the F1-C transfer path is determined by the DU of the parent node. However, our original intention is to let IAB donor CU make the decision. Thus, the current spec. is not aligned with our original intention. Moreover, the parent node is not a suitable entity to determine F1-C transfer path since it does not have the full-picture of LTE leg and NR leg. 

With above considerations, some revisions to the current specification are needed for F1-C transfer path configuration.
summaryOfChange:
