consequencesIfNotApproved:
For the inter-gNB-CU handover, the target gNB-CU needs to extract the sidelink related UE information and includes the sidelink UE information in the CG-ConfigInfo. 
For the intra-gNB-CU inter-gNB-DU handover, the gNB-CU needs to send both HandoverPreparationInformation and CG-ConfigInfo to the gNB-DU, which causes duplicate sidelink related UE information sent to the gNB-DU.
The LTE UEAssistanceInformation cannot be sent to the gNB-DU.
The CU is required to generate sl-TimeOffsetEUTRA-List-r16 and parent IE “SL-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA-Info-r16”.
reasonForChange:
The HandoverPreparationInformation can include the sidelink related UE information in the scenarios below. 
For the inter-gNB-CU handover, the gNB-CU receives a HandoverPreparationInformation from the source node so it seems the gNB-CU does not need to use an additional CG-ConfigInfo for the sidelink related UE information.
For the intra-gNB-CU inter-gNB-DU handover, if the sidelink UE related information is received from the source gNB-DU, the gNB-CU can also generate a HandoverPreparationInformation to include it for the target gNB-DU.    
The reference of UEAssistanceInformationEUTRA is not defined in TS38.331 and should be referred to TS36.331 instead of TS38.331.
The following is defined in 38.331. Currently, the gNB-DU only provides the SL-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA in the DU to CU information. The gNB-DU should provide sl-TimeOffsetEUTRA-List-r16 as well.

SL-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA-Info-r16 ::=            SEQUENCE {
    sl-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA-r16                    OCTET STRING                                              OPTIONAL,  -- Need M
    sl-TimeOffsetEUTRA-List-r16                    SEQUENCE (SIZE (8)) OF SL-TimeOffsetEUTRA-r16             OPTIONAL    -- Need M
}
summaryOfChange:
Add TS36.331 to the References section
Add descriptions that if the HandoverPreparationInformation IE containing the sidelink related UE information is included in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message, the gNB-DU shall regard it as an indication of V2X sidelink information.
Correct the semantics description for UEAssitanceInformationEUTRA
In the DU to CU infomration, the DU provides SL-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA-Info-r16 instead of SL-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA-r16.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the sidelink operation in UE Context Setup procedure, the EUTRA UE Assistance Information, and the SL-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA.
This CR has impact on ASN.1.
title: Correction on V2X related information

consequencesIfNotApproved: DAPS handover cannot work properly for CU-DU split case.
reasonForChange:
In TS38.401, a NOTE is given for inter-gNB-DU mobility as below:
This note indicates that the source gNB-DU will perform as normal case (non-handover) for data packet transmission, i.e., 
gNB-CU continuously sends DL packets of DAPS bearers to the source gNB-DU
Source gNB-DU continuously schedules DL resource for packet transmission of DAPS and non-DAPS bearers, where packets include the ones already buffered at the source gNB-DU for both DAPS and non-DAPS bearers and the ones from gNB-CU for DAPS bearers
Source gNB-DU continuously schedules UL resource for packet transmission of DAPS and non-DAPS bearers
These behaviors are not aligned with the intention of DAPS handover, and may cause that: non-DAPS bearers may interrupt the data transmission of DAPS bearers

To solve the above problem, it is better to allow the source gNB-DU know the data transmission of which bearers should be stopped during the DAPS handover procedure.

Add Transmission Stop Indicator IE in UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message

Impact Analysis:

This CR is ASN.1 backward compatible.

consequencesIfNotApproved: If a UE connects to an IAB-DU is configured with a DRB support packet duplication for intra-gNB-DU CA, the IAB-node will not be able to add appropriate BAP Routing ID and select BH RLC channel for some UL packets of the GTP-U tunnels of such DRB. And then the transmission of some UL duplicated packets is not really supported in the BH links.
reasonForChange:
For intra-gNB-DU CA-based PDCP duplication, at most 4 F1-U GTP-U tunnels can be configured for one UE DRB. However, according to the current UE context management procedures which include the UE Context Setup procedure, the UE Context Modification procedure, only the “UL UP TNL Information to be setup List” IE is configured with the “BH Information” IE in the messages sent by the gNB-CU. For the “Additional PDCP Duplication TNL List”, the  “BH Information” IE is missing. 
Besides, in the current UE Context Modification Required procedure, the “BH Information” IE is missing for both the “UL UP TNL Information to be setup List” IE and the “Additional PDCP Duplication TNL List” IEs in the confirm message sent from the gNB-CU to the gNB-DU.
summaryOfChange:
In Section 8.3.1.2, add “or the Additional PDCP Duplication TNL List IE” between “UL UP TNL Information to be setup List IE” and “for a DRB”.

In Section 8.3.4.2, add “or the Additional PDCP Duplication TNL List IE” between “UL UP TNL Information to be setup List IE” and “for a DRB”.

In Section 8.3.5.2, add “If the BH Information IE is included in the UL UP TNL Information to be setup List IE or the Additional PDCP Duplication TNL List IE for a DRB, the gNB-DU shall, if supported, use the indicated BAP Routing ID and BH RLC channel for transmission of the corresponding GTP-U packets to the IAB-donor, as specified in TS 38.340 [30].” 

In Section 9.2.2.1, add the “BH Information” IE to the “Additional PDCP Duplication TNL Items” of the “UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST” message.

In Section 9.2.2.7, add the “BH Information” IE to the “Additional PDCP Duplication TNL Items” of the “UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST” message.

In Section 9.2.2.11, add the “BH Information” IE to the “UL UP TNL Information to Be Setup Item IEs” and the “Additional PDCP Duplication TNL Items” of the “UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION CONFIRM” messages.

In section 9.4.5, add the “BHInfo” in the “AdditionalPDCPDuplicationTNL-ItemExtIEs”

Impact analysis
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impacts with the previous version of the specification (same release) because the changes only impact IAB functionality.
This CR has an impact from a functional point of view. 
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the configuration of DRBs which are configured with CA based duplication in IAB network.
The changes are backward compatible.
title: Correction on UL BH information configuration for DRBs  support CA based duplication

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The UL Data Notification can not be used by the CU-UP to notify the arrival for those QoS flows over the default DRB at DRB setup phase. 
The procedure specified in TS 38.300 Annex A.6 can not be fully supported by E1AP.
reasonForChange:
The UL DATA NOTIFICATION procedure is described as follows. 

This procedure is initiated by the gNB-CU-UP to notify the gNB-CU-CP that an UL packet including a QFI value in the SDAP header not configured by the Flow Mapping Information IE is received for the first time at the default DRB. The procedure uses UE-associated signalling.

But here only the Flow Mapping Information IE, which is included in the DRB To Modify List IE in the BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, is mentioned. This means, the UL DATA NOTIFICATION can only be applied to the DRB modify case, but not DRB setup case for the default DRB. 

In addtion, the QoS Flows Information To Be Setup IE is mandatorily included for DRB setup in the Bearer Context Setup/Modification procedure. However, as described in TS 38.300 Annex A.6, there are cases where the NG-RAN may decide not to configure the mapping rule for the default DRB immediately when establishing PDU sessions, but decide the mapping rule only when it receives the UL data flows from the UE over the default DRB. 
That is, over E1, there may be the case where CU-CP does not configure mapping rule for the default DRB in the bearer context related procedure.
summaryOfChange:
Update the text description for the UL Data Notification procedure to include the QoS Flows Information To Be Setup IE. 
Introduce a new IE to ignore the mapping rule of the QoS Flows Information To Be Setup IE for the default DRB


 
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it impacts on the UL DATA NOTIFICATION procedure, and the QoS Flows list for the default DRB. 
The impact can be considered isolated.
title: Correction for UL Data Notification over E1

consequencesIfNotApproved: The ng-eNB cannot know the Masked IMEISV for UEs using CP only CIoT 5GS solution
reasonForChange:
The IMEISV value with a mask is used to identify a terminal model without identifying an individual Mobile Equipment. Currently, the ng-eNB can get this information from AMF via the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST or HANDOVER REQUEST messages.
However, for UEs using Control Plane CIoT 5GS optimisation, the ng-eNB cannot get the “Masked IMEISV” from AMF since AS security is not activated.
One possible way to fix this issue is to add the Masked IMEISV IE into the UE INFORMATION TRANSFER, so that ng-eNB can retrieve this IE from AMF after msg3.
summaryOfChange:
Addition of the Masked IMEISV IE in the UE INFORMATION TRANSFER,  DL NAS TRANSPORT and the CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION messages from AMF to ng-eNB.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the changes only affect the  CP CIoT 5GS optimisation procedures.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Inconsistency between tabulars and asn.1 protocol definitions.
reasonForChange:
(1) In previous meetings, the Source MRB ID IE was added in the UE Multicast MRB to Be Setup Item IEs IE in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message, which is intended to be used in case of moblity. It is noticed that the upper layer IE UE Multicast MRB to Be Setup Item IEs IE is also included in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message. Therefore, the tabular of the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message is inconsistent with the asn.1, i.e. Source MRB ID IE missing in the tabular.
But the Source MRB ID IE should not be used in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, therefore, to avoid the inconsistency between tabular and asn.1, it is needed to add the Source MRB ID IE in the message and add clarification in the Semantics description that the IE is not used.
(2) In 9.2.14.1 MULTCAST GROUP PAGING message, the Paging Cell Item IEs IE includes the NR CGI IE only, but in asn.1 part, the PagingCell-Item was extended to include LastUsedCellIndication and PEISubgroupingSupportIndication, therefore the tabluar and asn.1 are also not aligned. As for (1), a correction is needed.
(3) Wrong IE name and missing IE Reference in section 9.3.2.8 for the Multicast F1-U Context Reference F1 IE.

(ad 1) Define a new UE Multicast MRB to Be Setup at Modify List IE which does not include the Source MRB ID IE . Note, that this approach is infact creating a non-backwards compatibilitly issues towards the previous version of F1AP, given the presence and the criticality assigned to the UE Multicast MRB to Be Setup List IE (optional/reject). 
(ad 2) Define a new MC Paging Cell List IE to avoid future cross-functional protol issues between the Paging and the Mutlicast Group Paging procedures. This new IE would only include the NR CGI IE. Note, that this approach does not create non-backwards compatibilitly issues towards the previous version of F1AP, given the presence and the criticality assigned to previously included Paging Cell List IE and the new MC Paging Cell List IE  (optional/ignore).
(ad 3) Update the IE name and add IE Reference in section 9.3.2.8.

This CR has an isolated impact towards the previous version of the specification.
The CR causes a non-backward compatible issue towards the previous version of the specification.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The conditional MCG configuration cannot be configured during CPAC operations.
reasonForChange:
For CPAC, it is captured that the MN sends to the UE an RRC reconfiguration message including a list of RRC reconfiguration* messages including both MCG and SCG configuration (RRC reconfiguration**) which are to be applied together upon CPAC execution. For (immediate) DC operation, the MN may reconfigure/update the MCG configuration based on the SCG configuration/information and in a disaggregated MN it is captured that the CG-Config IE might be included in the CU to DU RRC Information for lower layer parameter coordination. 
It is not specified how the disaggregated MN generates the conditional RRC reconfiguration* message including MCG configuration for CPAC given that the MCG configuration is also conditional and the candidate SN provides the CG-CandidateList instead of a single CG-Config to the MN when multiple PSCells are prepared.
It is also not specified, upon CPAC execution, how the MN gNB-DU knows that a candidate PSCell has been selected by the UE and a corresponding MCG L1/L2 configuration shall be applied.
It is not specified how MN restriction information (e.g., powerCoordination-FR1, powerCoordination-FR2, or p-maxNR-FR1-MCG) is provided to the MN-DU.
summaryOfChange:
Add a conditional indicator, CPAC MCG Information IE, in the UE context modification request procedure for MN purpose in CPAC
Add a description in procedure text and gNB-CU provides the CG-Config and/or CG-ConfigInfo corresponding to the candidate PSCell to the gNB-DU and obtains MCG configuration upon CPAC initiation
Add a description in procedure text and gNB-CU provides the PSCell ID corresponding to the selected candidate PSCell to the gNB-DU and the gNB-DU applies the MCG configuration upon CPAC execution
Add the conditional indicator in the UE Context Modification Request message

Impact Analysis:

The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the MCG configuration and the related procedure text for the CPAC operation.

consequencesIfNotApproved: When the target device operates as a L2 U2N Remote UE, the LMF may trigger positioning operations that are not possible, resulting in a failed operation.
reasonForChange:
In R2-2313814 CR#0444 to TS 37.355 LPP spec, RAN2 have added indication to LMF that the target UE for positioning is a Layer 2 UE-to-Network Remote UE (i.e., L2 U2N Remote UE).
The indication of L2 U2N Remote UE was also added in the Error cause values in LPP.
The motivation of adding such indications to LMF is to avoid sending inappopriate assistance data or request inappropriate measurements from a UE that is connected to the network via a relay UE.
Since the LMF may also send assistance data and request for positioning  measurements via NRPPa, a similar indication that UE is L2 U2N Remote UE is also needed in NRPPa; and a cause value is needed in case the LMF requests for measurement or trigger an operation that is not possible to handle for the remote UE.
Also, it has been commented in RAN3#125 that some positioning methods do not require LPP, like UL-TDOA, where LPP “may” be used according to TS 38.305 section 8.13.3.4 step 2.
Also, if for some reason the UE changes configuration and becomes a remote UE, at any given time, then an indication in the POSITIONING INFORMATION UPDATE message is needed.
summaryOfChange:
A request indicator remote UE-Indication Request IE is added in the POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST message and the corresponding response indicator remote UE-Indication IE in the POSITIONING INFORMATION RESPONSE message to notify the LMF that the UE being configured is a L2 U2N Remote UE.
An indication that UE became remote UE is added in the POSITIONING INFORMATION UPDATE message.

This CR may have an impact from functional point of view because it adds possibility of indicating remote UE type to LMF based on request from LMF.

consequencesIfNotApproved: There remain mistakes in the specification on multi-hop relay.
reasonForChange:
The Peer UE ID is added to the PC5 RLC Channel Setup Item and the PC5 RLC Channel Failed to be Setup Item in ASN.1 but not in the tabular.
In current specification, it is possible that the gNB-DU receives both the Peer UE ID IE and Remote UE Local ID IE for the PC5 RLC channel between the U2N Remote UE and the First U2N Relay UE. However, it was clarified in RAN3#129 that the Remote UE Local ID IE is only provided to the gNB-DU for the PC5 RLC channel between the U2N Remote UE and the First U2N Relay UE in multi-hop relay. This needs to be clarified in the specification.
Since PC5 RLC channel ID towards the parent UE and the child UE could be the same, Peer UE ID is needed to identify a PC5 RLC channel together with the PC5 RLC channel ID. It means that to configure a PC5 RLC channel for a L2 U2N Relay UE in multi-hop relay, the Peer UE ID shall be included. This needs to be clarified in the specification.

Clarified that the PC5 RLC channel between two L2 U2N Relay UEs is for multi-hop relay in clause 9.3.1.265.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Measurements for DRB and QoS Flow retainability are not fully supported in case of 3-split scenario
reasonForChange:
RAN3 received an LS from SA5 in R3-192503, asking RAN3 to support measurements for DRB and QoS Flow retainability in case of 3-split scenario. The gNB-CU-CP needs to report if the DRB or the QoS flow was in session (active) while released: “For DRBs with bursty flow, a DRB is said to be active if any data (UL or DL) has been transferred during the last 100 ms”. The accumulated session time for each DRB or QoS Flow needs also to be reported in case of release.
However, these informations can only be retrieved by the gNB-CU-UP, while the measurement itself is gNB-CU-CP related. Therefore, the gNB-CU-UP needs to inform the gNB-CU-CP if the released DRB or QoS Flow was in session, together with the accumulated session time.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Nodes following implementations that are not able to decode extremely large messages due to the high number of served and neighbour cell information included in such messages, will not be able to setup an Xn interface with peer nodes.
reasonForChange: In an Xn Setup procedure a gNB is able to signal up to 16384 served cells information and for each of such served cell it is able to signal up to 1024 neighbour cells information. This leads to very large Xn messages that may not be decodable due to ASN.1 decoding capability issues. It is therefore necessary to allow for reduced size messages and for failrue notifications pointing at excessive message size as the main root of failure.
summaryOfChange:
The Xn Setup Request and Xn Setup Response are amended so to remove the mandate for a gNB to signal a ful list of served cells. These messages are enhanced with an indication of the desired received message size for the sending node and with an indication of whether the list of served cells ais full or partial. Cell assistance information is also provided.

Impact analysis:
The CR has an impact on the specifications limited to transmission of list of served cell information.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The non-integer DRX cycle configuration is not supported for disaggregated gNB.
reasonForChange:
RAN3-123 meeting discussed the non-integer DRX cycle issue for XR in F1AP design and agreed that “For CU -> DU direction, no need to add a new IE”. And it is marked as “to be continued” about whether need behaviour text for gNB-DU is needed for non-integer DRX configuration. However, after some further checking, such agreement should be reverted due to the following reasons
In previous discussion for CU-DU split, it was agreed that CU decide DRX cycle length and the timer for short DRX cycle, while DU generate remaining parameters for DRX configuration. CU informs DU to setup DRX configuration by providing DRX parameters. The corresponding agreements from previous RAN3 meetings are pasted as following:
RAN3-97bis:
DRX Cycle length is controlled by CU
WA: All other DRX parameters are controlled by DU except timers which are FFS
RAN3-98:
CU->DU
RRC containers: SCG config info (name FFS pending RAN2), UE capabilities
List of target cells (PScell, SCG cell(s)) / NCGI of each cell which is going to serve the UE
Bearer list
DRX cycle length
In the semantics description, the sub IEs (i.e., Long DRX Cycle Length, Short DRX Cycle Length, Short DRX Cycle Timer) included in the DRX cycle IE are corresponded to the field preferredDRX-LongCycle, preferredDRX-ShortCycle and preferredDRX-ShortCycle Timer defined in RRC, separately. The correspondance means the format and value of these sub IEs are same as these fields defined in RRC specification, but not meaning that the CU send these UE preferred fields received from UAI to the gNB-DU and let the DU to decide which value to be used for the DRX cycle length and the timer for short DRX configuration. 
Therefore, to align with the principle that CU control the DRX Cycle length, R3 should introduce a new IE for non-integer DRX cycle in UE Context Management related procedures. In addition, to avoid cause further mis-understanding (e.g. CU provides UE preferred value on the DRX cycle while DU make the final decision), it is suggested to update the semantics description of the existing DRX Cycle IE and link it to the RRC field name contained in the DRX-Config IE.

2.Update the semantics description for the Long DRX Cycle Length IE, Short DRX Cycle Length IE, Short DRX Cycle Timer IE to link them to the fields contained in the DRX-Config IE as defined in 38.331.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Upon relocation of SDAP/PDCP termination point, it would not be possible to avoid re-allocation of DRB IDs.
reasonForChange:
A basic mechanism was introduced to co-ordinate the DRB ID usage between the Master NG-RAN node and the Secondary NG-RAN node.
One other aspect of co-ordination is the fact that upon changing the termination point of SDAP/PDCP w/o changing Cell Group configuration, it would require re-establishing Cell Group resources, if another DRB ID was chosen by the target node than the one assigned by the source side.
It is therefore proposed to clarify that providing source side mapping information to the target node would implicitly mean that the source node “offers” the DRB ID to the target node. When providing target forwarding information, the target node also provides information whether the offered DRB ID was used by the target node.
summaryOfChange:
A new IE was introduced in the Data Forwarding Info from target NG-RAN node IE to indicate whether the target node has taken the DRB-ID into use.
In the Data Forwarding and Offloading Info from source NG-RAN node IE tabular specification, a semantics description was added to refer to stage specification in 37.340.
In addition procedure text was updated where necessary.

SA3 in TS 33.501 section 6.10.4 makes clear also that IP UP would not be applied in the option 4 scenario.

To avoid exhaustively considering all cases, add statement that the SN behaves according to TS 33.501, section 6.10.4, for cases of IP Indication = “preferred”.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
Not possible for DU to configure RedCap UE on NCD-SSB when one servingCellMO can be pointing to different frequencies in the cell.

Not possible for CU to compare (CD or NCD) SSB frequency in UE’s active BWP with neighbor cell SSB frequency and know if measurement GAPs are needed.
reasonForChange:
In Rel-17, RAN2 have introduced Non-Cell-Defining SSB (NCD-SSB) dedicated for RedCap UE. One Bandwidth Part (BWP) can have up to one SSB (CD-SSB or NCD-SSB). BWP with NCD-SSB is in different frequency from CD-SSB. Hence, servingCellMOs pointing to NCD-SSB or CD-SSB are different.
However, in F1AP there is only one servingCellMO IE assigned by CU and signalled in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message to inform DU of UE’s servingCellMO to use for legacy CD-SSB. This means, when CU delivers servingCellMO to DU in the F1 request message, CU doesn’t know if DU will choose active BWP with NCD-SSB or CD-SSB for UE. It is proposed to update F1AP by adding an optional list of candidate servingCellMOs, i.e., servingCellMO List IE to be used for NCD-SSBs, with both servingCellMO and SSB frequency info so that after DU chooses the active BWP for the UE, the DU can select related measObjectId as servingCellMO for NCD-SSB using the new list IE instead of impacting legacy servingCellMO IE that is used for CD-SSB.

Furthermore, feedback from DU to CU over F1AP is needed so that CU knows which MeasObjectIDs will be used by DU and CU can free up the resources for those unused measObjectIds for a given UE. CU will also be able to determine the need of Measurement Gaps based on DU selected BWPs.
.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 08/03/2023. Original source : Ericsson, CATT, China Telecom, Qualcomm Inc., ZTE, Huawei, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell
summaryOfChange:
Addition of an optional list of candidate servingCellMOs, servingCellMO List IE for NCD-SSBs, in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST messages with SSB frequency.
Addition of ServingCellMO-encoded-in-CGC List IE by UE in the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE messages
Note: the understanding is that legacy servingCellMO IE points to CD-SSB

This impact can be considered isolated because it affects only the F1 context management procedures with the addition of a new IE ServingCellMOs List from CU to DU and the feedback from DU to CU of the used measObjectsIds.
This CR is BC
title: Correction to support NCD-SSB RedCap requirements in F1AP

consequencesIfNotApproved: No support of the preconfigured gap configuration in CU/DU split architecture.
reasonForChange:
In RAN2 LS reply R3-234560, it was clarified that:
only one pre-configured measurement gap is allowed per gap type (i.e, UE type or per FR type), by using “gapToAddModList IE” in MeasGapConfig. 
pre-configured MGs are applicable to both RedCap and non-RedCap UEs

Considering the Rel-17 restriction of one pre-MG, to support the preconfigured gap for all the configured BWPs, the following actions are needed:
The gNB-DU should inform gNB-CU of the list of all configured BWPs information 
Based on the BWP information received from gNB-DU, the gNB-CU requests gNB-DU to generate the pre-configured measurement GAP for all the configured BWPs in CGC. To avoid generating any RRC Reconfiguration message at this step, the gNB-CU should ignore the received CGC from the gNB-DU. 
The gNB-DU schedules the preconfigured Measurement GAP and signals the information to gNB-CU together with the contents of the new generated CGC. Based on this, the gNB-CU sends the preconfigured MG and CGC to UE via RRC signaling
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 20/11/2023. Original source : Ericsson, Qualcomm Inc., Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, CATT, Huawei, ZTE
summaryOfChange:
It is proposed to add the following IEs:
Include a Configured BWP List IE with the BWP ID and BWP Location And Bandwidth IEs in the UE CONTEXT REQUEST RESPONSE and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE messages to indicate that gNB-DU configures multiple BWPs for UE. Include BWP ID in ServingCellMO-encoded-in-CGC Item IEs 
Include a Preconfigured Measurement GAP Request IE in the CU to DU RRC Information IE to ask gNB-DU to generate the preconfigured measurement GAP for the indicated list of BWPs. Also clarify that the gNB-DU should consider, when receiving this IE, that the gNB-DU should include the new CGC including both the preconfigured measurement GAP and previous CGC configuration in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE message.
Clarify that the legacy MeasGapConfig IE can be used for  Preconfigured measurement GAP.
Add limitation in the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE messages that for  UE configured with BWP specific ServingCellMO, the gNB-CU shall ignore the CGC and not perform RRC Reconfiguration of the UE 


Impact analysis:

The impact can be considered isolated because it only impacts the F1 context management procedures to support the preconfigured gap configuration.

The following PDU set information specified in RAN user plane protocol is not aligned with the information specified in RTP Header Extension
1. the length of EDB is 1 bit and there’s no EDB indicator in RTP.
2. the length of PSSN is 10 bits in RTP.
3. the value 0 in PSI means the sender cannot define the importance in RTP, and value 1 means the highest importance.
4. the PSSize is in bytes in RTP.
5. the general description of the PDU set information container is not aligned with SA4.

2. Remove the EDBI

4. Update the length of PSSN to 10 bits

6. Update the descriptions in EDB, PSI, PSSN, and PSSize

consequencesIfNotApproved: IE encoding for SRS BW aggregation, Redcap Positioning are not clear which may cause confusion.
reasonForChange:
1. SRS for Positioning with Tx Frequency Hopping for RedCap UEs, RAN1 agreed that the number of hops: ENUMERATED {2,3,4,5,6} (new IE).
However, in the F1AP, the value range of Number of Hops is defined as INTEGER(1..6), which should be corrected. NBC way was acceptable.

2. For Positioning SRS BW Aggregation, RAN1/RAN2 agreed that the number of “aggregated combinations” is up to 32, and for each combination, only one SRS resource set from each of the 2 or 3 carriers are aggregated, e.g. CC#1 SRS resource set 1 + CC#2 SRS resource set 2 + CC#3 SRS resource set 3. In F1AP, the Aggregated Positioning SRS Resource Set List IE includes at most 48 SRS resource sets to be aggregated in one combination, which equal to 3CCs * 16 SRS Resource sets per CC. It’s not well aligned with the design of TS 38.331, which may cause erroneous during SRS configuration. 
To make alignment with NR-Uu, and make the IE encoding more clear, it’s proposed to move the Aggregated Positioning SRS Resource Set List IE to the top level of the SRS Configuration IE. And make corresponding change to Positioning Activation/Deactivation procedure.
summaryOfChange:
The changes include:
Correct the value range of number of Tx Hopping
Redefine the IE “Aggregated Positioning SRS Resource Set List” to support up to 32 combinations, and move the IE to the top level of the SRS Configuration IE. Corresponding changes are also provided to POSITIONING ACTIVATION REQUEST and POSITIONING DEACTIVATION.

Impact Analysis:

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it affects the Positioning SRS BW Aggregation related function and Redcap Positioning related function..
The CR has impact from functional and protocol point of view.
The CR is non-backwards compatible from protocol point of view..

In RAN3 #108e meeting, the TP R3-204193 was agreed to support Alternative QoS Profile over Xn during HO and Notification control procedure. However, no changes were introduced to the S-NG-RAN node addition procedure and S-NG-RAN node modification procedure.

For MN initiated SN addition/modification procedure, according to current specification, if a GBR QoS flow with alternative QoS profile is mapped to a SN terminated bearer, the S-NG-RAN can only rely on the basic QoS profile to determine to accept or reject the QoS flow. 

If a GBR QoS flow with alternative QoS profile is mapped to a MN terminated bearer, the S-NG-RAN can only rely on the DRB QoS to accept or reject the DRB. In other words, the AQP feature is not supported in S-NG-RAN addition or modification procedure. 

In addition, with respect to the Notification Control Indication procedure, in the procedure texts, S-NG-RAN node is only allowed to indicate current QoS parameter set index for SN terminated bearer, i.e., it is not supported for MN terminated bearer. But the MN also needs to know this for MN terminated bearers in order to inform CN.
summaryOfChange:
Enable the S-NG-RAN node to feedback the current QoS profile index during the S-NG-RAN node addition procedure and M-NG-RAN node initiated SN-NG-RAN node modification procedures.
Update the procedure text of Notification Control Indication procedure to enable S-NG-RAN node to provide QoS parameter set index for MN terminated bearer.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
This CR only introduces the support of alternative QoS profile during the S-NG-RAN node addition procedure and S-NG-RAN node modification procedure.
title: Correction of alternative QoS profile

consequencesIfNotApproved: Reporting of UE Tx TEG associations by the gNB to the LMF does not work as intended. Misalignment with RRC/LPP.
reasonForChange:
The UE can report the UE Tx TEG association to the LMF via the gNB. The gNB configures (via RRC) the UE to report the UE Tx TEG association either “on demand” or “periodic” based on request from LMF (via NRPPa). However:
The UE TEG Information Request IE in the POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST contains only a single codepoint (“true”) which cannot differentiate between “On Demand” and “Periodic”.
In case of “Periodic”, the LMF cannot indicate the desired periodicity.
The encoding of the UE Tx TEG Association over NRPPa does not match RRC/LPP.

From TS 38.331 V17.1.0 (RRC):
UE-TxTEG-Association-r17 ::=     SEQUENCE {
    ue-TxTEG-ID-r17              INTEGER (0..maxNrOfTxTEG-ID-1-r17),
    nr-TimeStamp-r17             NR-TimeStamp-r17,
    associatedSRS-PosResourceIdList-r17 SEQUENCE (SIZE(1..maxNrofSRS-PosResources-r16)) OF SRS-PosResourceId-r16,
    servCellId-r17               ServCellIndex       OPTIONAL
}

From TS 37.355 V17.1.0 (LPP):
NR-SRS-TxTEG-Element-r17 ::= SEQUENCE {
	nr-TimeStamp-r17		NR-TimeStamp-r16	OPTIONAL,	-- Need OP
	nr-UE-Tx-TEG-ID-r17		INTEGER (0..maxNumOfTxTEGs-1-r17),
	carrierFreq-r17			SEQUENCE {
			absoluteFrequencyPointA-r17		ARFCN-ValueNR-r15,
			offsetToPointA-r17				INTEGER (0..2199)
							}					OPTIONAL,
	srs-PosResourceList-r17	SEQUENCE (SIZE (1..maxNumOfSRS-PosResources-r17)) OF INTEGER (0..maxNumOfSRS-PosResources-1-r17),
	...
}
summaryOfChange:
8.2.6.2, 8.2.7.2: Procedural text for periodic reporting of UE Tx TEG Association is added.
9.1.1.10: In the POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST message, three codepoints are used for the UE TEG Information Request IE: “onDemand”, “periodic”, and “stop”. In case of “periodic”, periodicity values are added which are aligned with RRC.
9.2.78: The information in the UE Tx TEG Association List IE is aligned with RRC/LPP. Note that the gNB is expected to translate servCellID received from the UE to carrierFreq sent to LMF.
9.2.42: The description of the Time Stamp IE is modified, since it can be included with UE Tx TEG Association (i.e. usage of Time Stamp IE is not limited to measurements).
Miscellaneous editorials.

Impact analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release):
This CR has an impact under protocol point of view. The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the reporting of UE Tx TEG Associations. This CR is non-backwards compatible.
title: Correction for UE Tx TEG Association

consequencesIfNotApproved: F1AP would not support establishment of F1-U ptp retransmission tunnels in case the gNB-DU requests to change the MRB type configuration of a UE or for retransmission based on source side PDCP SN transmission state

F1AP currently does not support 
- establishment of F1-U ptp retransmission tunnels in case the gNB-DU requests to change the MRB type configuration of a UE
-  releasing MRBs for a UE configuration.
- establishment of F1-U “ptp forwarding” tunnels based on the source side provided MRB Progress information state
Further, the F1-U Context Descriptor IE needs to be re-structured
summaryOfChange:
Protocol elements are included in the gNB-DU triggered UE Context Modification Required procedure to inform the gNB-CU about the gNB-DUs decision to modify the MRB type configuration for a UE and to inform the gNB-DU that the gNB-CU decided to configure the UE with PDCP Status Report for the affected MRBs.

In addition the purpose of the Multicast Distribution Release procedure was generalised to also include the release of F1-U ptp-retransmission resources.

Support of establishment of “ptp forwarding” tunnels enabling retransmission based on source side provided MRB Progress information state is included

Reducing the content of the MBS Multicast F1-U Context Descriptor IE to a 3-octet reference which may include in addition an MBS Area Session ID (to indicate which location dependent content needs to be provided) and an indication whether a ptp F1-U context needs to be established for ptm transmission or ptp transmission or ptp retransmission.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The Additional PDCP Duplication UP TNL Information cannot be correctly indicated in the Tabular.
reasonForChange:
The Additional PDCP Duplication UP TNL Information IE was introduced to indicate the additional TNL addresses for the PDCP duplication up to four legs, in the PDU session resource related IEs (see the agreed R3-204503). 

In the tabular this IE is referring to UP Transport Parameters which contains the cell group ID and its associated UP Transport Layer Information.  
 
However, in the ASN.1, it is encoded as UP Transport Layer Information only as follows. 
	additional-PDCP-Duplication-UP-TNL-Information	UPTransportLayerInformation,

There is no need to refer to the UP Transport Parameters IE, because it is understood that there is no need to indicate the cell group ID or to provide more than one TNL address for the Additional PDCP Duplication UP TNL Information IE, given the fact that the PDCP duplication is supported with dual connectivity (MCG/SCG).  

To resolve this issue, it can be considered to update the Tabular to refer to the UP Transport Layer Information.
summaryOfChange:
In the Tabular, update the Additional PDCP Duplication UP TNL Information IE by referring the UP Transport Layer Information instead of the UP Transport Parameters. 

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release).
The impact can be considered isolated because the change only affects the Additional PDCP Duplication UP TNL Information for PDCP duplication.

consequencesIfNotApproved: IE encoding for SRS BW aggregation, Redcap Positioning are not clear which may cause confusion.
reasonForChange:
1. SRS for Positioning with Tx Frequency Hopping for RedCap UEs, RAN1 agreed that the number of hops: ENUMERATED {2,3,4,5,6} (new IE).
However, in the NRPPa, the value range of Number of Hops is defined as INTEGER(1..6), which should be corrected.

2. For Positioning SRS BW Aggregation, RAN1/RAN2 agreed that the number of “aggregated combinations” is up to 32, and for each combination, only one SRS resource set from each of the 2 or 3 carriers are aggregated, e.g. CC#1 SRS resource set 1 + CC#2 SRS resource set 2 + CC#3 SRS resource set 3. In NRPPa, the Aggregated Positioning SRS Resource Set List IE includes at most 48 SRS resource sets to be aggregated in one combination, which equal to 3CCs * 16 SRS Resource sets per CC. It’s not well aligned with the design of TS 38.331, which may cause erroneous during SRS configuration. 
To make alignment with NR-Uu, and make the IE encoding more clear, it’s proposed to move the Aggregated Positioning SRS Resource Set List IE to the top level of the SRS Configuration IE. And make corresponding change to Positioning Activation/Deactivation procedure.
summaryOfChange:
The changes include:
Correct value range for number of Tx Hopping.
Redefine the IE “Aggregated Positioning SRS Resource Set List” to support up to 32 combinations, and move the IE to the top level of the SRS Configuration IE. Corresponding changes are also provided to POSITIONING ACTIVATION REQUEST and POSITIONING DEACTIVATION.

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it affects the Positioning SRS BW Aggregation related function and Redcap Positioning related function.
The CR has impact from functional and protocol point of view.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The specification remains mistakes.
reasonForChange:
The “BH-AMF” has not been used, suggest to remove the definition.
In the Figure 6.1.7-1, the backhaul PDU Session(s) may also be used for transporting of Xn-C/Xn-U/OAM traffic, but this is missing in the line description. 
Resource coordination is not supported. Add a note to clarify the in-band operation of WAB-node can be supported by implementation.
It was agreed that the Additional ULI can be included in both UE-associated signalling and non-UE associated signalling. However, in clause 12.5, only the case that there is UE served by the WAB-gNB is mentioned, the non-UE associated case is not been covered. In SA2 spec as shown below, it referred to TS 38.401 for non-UE associated case. So, it is suggested to change the title to emphasize the Additional ULI and to capture the non-UE associated case as well.
The WAB-gNB has same functionality as the gNB defined in TS 38.300, which can support network sharing. When the WAB-gNB is shared, it can broadcast multiple PLMNs/SNPNs (e.g. PLMN A and B). For a specific UE from PLMN A, it is unclear which PLMN/SNPN is used in AULI. E.g. in case the WAB-gNB sends the AULI related to PLMN B, the UE’s CN (PLMN A) cannot use the AULI since it does not have the information of PLMN B.
A WAB node includes a WAB-gNB and a WAB-MT. The NG connection can be established between the WAB-gNB and the AMF(s). When the UE’s AMF is changed due to the WAB-gNB’s mobility, after all the UEs in RRC_CONNECTED state are handed over, the NG connection(s) between the old logical WAB-gNB and the old AMF(s) should be removed, rather than the NG connection(s) between the WAB-node and the old AMF(s).
In clause 12.8, the first sentence may cause misunderstanding that the WAB-MT is co-located with the BH-gNB. Suggest to make it clear. And some editorial changes to keep align with stage 3.
The specification does not capture the fact that a BH-gNB may be configured with respect to whether it should accept Xn setup requests from WAB-gNBs. In some networks, the operator may want to prevent a BH-gNB and other static gNBs to establish Xn connections with WAB-gNBs, because such a connection will likely be short-lived due to WAB-node movement. On the other hand, for nomadic WAB-nodes, an operator may want to allow Xn setup between WAB-gNBs and static gNBs, given that it facilitates UE HO between the WAB-gNB and static gNBs.
Several wording and interpunction errors.

In clause 6.1.7, add a note to clarify the in-band operation of WAB-node can be supported by implementation.
In clause 12.5, change the title to “Additional User Location Information for WAB”, and capture that the WAB-gNB can indicate the Additional ULI to the core network by NG Setup and RAN Configuration Update procedures.
In clause 12.5, clarify the PLMN/SNPN in AULI is the UE’s serving PLMN/SNPN.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Not possible to disable LP-WUS per UE. On the other hand, if LP-WUS is disabled over NAS but gNB still enable LP-WUS subgroup paging to UE, in case the UE is paged, other UEs which share the same subgroup with that UE will be falsely alarmed due to the associated LP-WUS aimed towards that UE, which is not desirable.
reasonForChange:
RAN2 agreed to support enabling/disabling LP-WUS for a UE with NAS signalling. RAN2 assumes that NAS signalling needs to be extended to enable/disable LP-WUS per UE in IDLE and INACTIVE and CN needs to inform gNB that LP-WUS is enabled/disabled per UE in IDLE and INACTIVE. RAN2 assumes that without such NAS signalling, UE is allowed to use LP-WUS in IDLE and INACTIVE.

Based on RAN2 agreements, it is suggested to introduce an indication to disable LP-WUS in the NG Paging message and in the Core Network Assistance Information for RRC INACTIVE IE.

IAB Transport Migration function/IAB Resource Coordination function for mobile IAB is not supported. 
Improper criticality is assigned to Mobile IAB Authorization Status IE in RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT RESPONSE message.

reasonForChange:
The definitions for mobile IAB-node, Mobile IAB-MT, and RRC-terminating IAB-donor of a mobile IAB-node are missing. 
It was agreed that the Rel-17 term “non-F1-terminating donor” is not applicable to mobile IAB and the term “RRC-terminating donor” should be used instead. However, it’s not reflected in TS 38.423.
During RAN3#122 meeting, it was agreed to add mIAB authorization status indicator in Xn Context Retrieve Response message. However, the motivation is that the the mIAB authorization status indicator is used as to indicate that the UE is a mobile IAB node. Since there is no need to indicate the mobile IAB authorization status in the Xn Context Retrieve Response considering that the new IAB donor allocates IP address, TNL address, default BAP configuration after the path switch procedure, and the new IAB donor can obtain the mobile IAB authorization status via path switch procedure. So the criticality of the Mobile IAB Authorization Status IE in RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT RESPONSE should be reject, which is similar as the IAB Node Indication IE. 
The procedure text for handling of mobile IAB authorization status in Handover Preparation and Retrieve UE Context procedure is not accurate. 
When the non-F1-terminating IAB-donor reject the XnAP TMM procedure, the REJECT message need to contain an appropriate cause value. However, none of the existing cause value can be used to indicate that the Reject is due to “No Backhaul Resource”, or “IAB not authorized”.

Support IAB Transport Migration function/IAB Resource Coordination function between F1-terminating IAB-donor and RRC-terminating IAB-donor of a mobile IAB-node.
Correct the criticality of Mobile IAB Authorization Status IE in RETRIEVE UE CONTEXT RESPONSE to be reject.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The NG-RAN is not able to locate the correct AMF from which the UE-associated logical NG-connection is redirected. 
The NG-RAN is not able to locate the correct AMF during AMF reselection.
reasonForChange:
As agreed in NGAP CR0463 in R3-205747, the Extended AMF Name IE, encoded as VisibleString or the UTF8String, was introduced due to the misalignment with the one used in OAM and the type of legacy PrintableString may have problem in displaying some special characters. And in the procedure texts, it is described that the AMF name shall be ignored, when receiving the Extended AMF Name IE. 

If the Extended AMF Name IE is included in the NG SETUP RESPONSE message, the NG-RAN node may use this IE as a human readable name of the AMF and shall ignore the AMF Name IE. 

First, the Old AMF IE encoded PrintableString may be included in the Initial Context Setup Request, Connection Establishment Indication, Downlink NAS Transport messages. When the legacy AMF name is ignored, the NG-RAN cannot identify from which AMF the UE-associated logical NG-connection was redirected.  Hence the extended old AMF IE needs to be introduced.   


Second, for the backup AMF name IE included in the NG interface management messages, it is used to assist the NG-RAN to perform the AMF reselection, and encoded as PrintableString. However, when the NG-RAN node tries to locate the AMF based on the backup AMF name, it cannot identify the correct AMF, due to the fact the legacy AMF name as PrintableString is already ignored by the NG-RAN node when it receives the extended AMF name as indicated above.   

Below provides an example: 
The AMF#2 provides its AMF name (PrintableString) and the Extended AMF Name (VisibleString or the UTF8String) to the NG-RAN node, and the NG-RAN ignores the AMF name; 
The AMF#1 provides the backup AMF name (PrintableString) corresponding to the AMF#2 to the NG-RAN node for AMF reselection;
In case of AMF#1 failure, the NG-RAN cannot identify the AMF#2 based on the backup AMF name. 

Hence a new extended backup AMF name should be introduced, with the same format as extended AMF name.
summaryOfChange:
Introduce an extended old AMF in the following messages. 
INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST
CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT INDICATION
DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT 
Introduce a new extended backup AMF name, with the same format as extended AMF name for AMF reselection by the NG-RAN node.  


Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it only impacts those procedures containing the old AMF IE for AMF redirection, and impacts the backup AMF name in the NG interface management messages for AMF reselection.
title: Correction of Old AMF and Backup AMF Name

consequencesIfNotApproved: Upon relocation of SDAP/PDCP termination point, it would not be possible to avoid re-allocation of DRB IDs.
reasonForChange:
A basic mechanism was introduced to co-ordinate the DRB ID usage between the Master NG-RAN node and the Secondary NG-RAN node.
One other aspect of co-ordination is the fact that upon changing the termination point of SDAP/PDCP w/o changing Cell Group configuration, it would require re-establishing Cell Group resources, if another DRB ID was chosen by the target node than the one assigned by the source side.
It is therefore proposed to clarify that providing source side mapping information to the target node would implicitly mean that the source node “offers” the DRB ID to the target node. When providing target forwarding information, the target node also provides information whether the offered DRB ID was used by the target node.
summaryOfChange:
This CR is only for MR-DC with 5GC

A new IE was introduced to indicate whether the target node has taken the DRB-ID into use.
In the Data Forwarding and Offloading Info from source NG-RAN node IE tabular specification, a semantics description was added to refer to stage specification in 37.340.
In addition, procedure texts were updated where necessary.

Impact Analysis:

This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it enhances the DRB ID coordination function between SN and MN for MR-DC with 5GC.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only DRB ID coordination function between SN and MN for MR-DC with 5GC.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The term in specification is inconsistence. 
The receiver will not interprete the RB set configuration correctly.
reasonForChange:
In  section 8.5.4.2,  “The non-F1-terminating/F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU may respond with the IAB RESOURCE COORDINATION RESPONSE message to the F1-terminating/non-F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU”. The “may respond” is not suitable since the procedure is a class 1 procedure and the response message is necessary. 
Inconsistence of terminology : the term “F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU” and “non-F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU” are use in some places, but in the procedure description and the figures of the procedures, we use “F1-termianting IAB-donor” and “non-F1 termianting IAB-donor” instead. And the “IAB-donor” is more appropriate than the “IAB-donor-CU” in this XnAP specification.
In section 9.1.4.3, the IE “cause” refers to a wrong clause.
In section 9.2.2.83, the IE name “Ingress BH RLC CH” should be “Ingress BH RLC CH ID”
In section 9.2.2.95, the value range for the IE “RB Set Index” is start from 1, not align with the semantic description and the F1AP specification.
RAN1 send LS R1-2205644, to notify the new agreements in RAN1 #109e : If the RB sets of a Rel-17 IAB-DU H/S/NA resource configuration do not cover the entire carrier bandwidth: The remaining RBs not part of an RB set configuration are considered as included in the last RB set. This agreements needs to be captured in the RB set configuration.
In clause 9.2.2.97, the following constant: maxnoofRBsetsPerCell1, maxnoofPhysicalResourceBlocks, maxnoofPhysicalResourceBlocks1 are not used in the IE tabular, so the three constants are not necessary in the range bound table.
summaryOfChange:
In  section 8.5.4.2, use “shall” instead of “may” in the sentence “The non-F1-terminating/F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU may respond with the IAB RESOURCE COORDINATION RESPONSE message to the F1-terminating/non-F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU”.
Replace the “IAB-donor-CU” by “IAB-donor” in the term “F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU” and “non-F1-terminating IAB-donor-CU” across the whole specification. 
In section 9.1.4.3, change the IE “cause” reference to 9.2.3.2.
In section 9.2.2.83, change the IE name “Ingress BH RLC CH” to “Ingress BH RLC CH ID”.
In section 9.2.2.95, the value range for the IE “RB Set Index” in the IE type and reference part is changed as INTEGER (0.. maxnoofRBsetsPerCell1,…), to align with the semantic description and the F1AP specification. And update the ASN.1 part in 9.3.5 accordingly. 
Capture the following agreements in the semantics description of RB set size IE: If the RB sets of a Rel-17 IAB-DU H/S/NA resource configuration do not cover the entire carrier bandwidth: The remaining RBs not part of an RB set configuration are considered as included in the last RB set. This agreements needs to be captured in the RB set configuration.
In clause 9.2.2.97, remove following constants from the range bound table: maxnoofRBsetsPerCell1, maxnoofPhysicalResourceBlocks, maxnoofPhysicalResourceBlocks1.

summaryOfChange:
On-demand PRS:
Introduce a new function PRS Information Transfer with a class1 non-UE associated NRPPa procedure to support on-demand PRS. 
The new NRPPa procedure enables LMF to request gNB to (re)configure PRS transmission, and gNB to indicate the updated PRS configuration to LMF. 
Details regarding information (e.g. parameters, PRS utilization, measurements in general, etc.) to be exchanged by the procedure are based on RAN1/RAN2 agreements.
The gNB can indicate via the TRP Information Exchange procedure whether a particular on-demand PRS transmission parameter is allowed to be requested by the LMF.
The Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics IE in the PRS CONFIGURATION REQUEST message can include the following parameters (per TRP): DL PRS Periodicity, DL PRS resource bandwidth, and DL PRS QCL information. 
Parameters of the DL-PRS configuration determined by the gNB for a given TRP “should” match those requested by the LMF in the Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics IE.
The PRS CONFIGURATION RESPONSE message includes the full DL-PRS Configuration (per TRP) decided by the gNB.
The gNB sends the PRS CONFIGURATION FAILURE message if it cannot configure DL-PRS transmission for any of the requested TRPs.
Introduce a Number of DL PRS frequency layers (max 4) 
Support new structure of the Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristic IE (with dedicate sub IE), new IEs (e.g. Comb Size IE), and removal of some IE (PRS Resource) 
Introduce a Start Time IE (encoded as the existing Relative Time 1900 IE) and Duration IE (INTEGER type in seconds with max value 90060 in alignment with LPP) within the Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics IE at the TRP level and at the PRS Resource Set level.
Introduce a PRS Configuration Request Type IE in the PRS CONFIGURATION REQUEST, encoded as ENUMERATED type with two values (configure, off, …). For the “off” request type, introduce a PRS Transmission Off Information IE in the PRS CONFIGURATION REQUEST which includes a choice of TRP, PRS resource sets, or PRS resources to be turned off.

Positioning Accuracy improvements
Define a new Assistance Information for UL-AoA IE with the Expected AoA/ZoA values and their mandatory Uncertainties Range using a CHOICE structure. 
Introduce the UL-AoA assistance information in NRPPA MEASUREMENT REQUEST message, within the TRP Measurement Request List IE
Introduce the UL-AoA assistance information in NRPPA MEASUREMENT UPDATE message, within a new TRP Measurement Update List IE with procedural description. 
Introduce a Zenith Angle of Arrival to the TRP Measurement Result IE for linear array AoA. The LCS to GCS Translation IE is optional. No need to introduce the “ZoA” codepoint in the TRP Measurement Type IE.
Addition of the UL-SRS-RSRPP in the TRP Measurement Result IE with the first path power. The i-th path (i>1) power is included in IE 9.2.x12 Extended Additional Path List. 
Addition of an extended additional path list IE in UL-RTOA and gNB-Rx-Tx measurements
Introduce Multiple UL AoA IE in the TRP Measurement result IE and in the additional path list and extended additional path list IEs
Support ARP ID based solution for providing ARP association with UL measurements
Support of signalling the UE Tx TEG association using the Positioning Information Exchange procedure and the TRP Tx TEG association using the TRP Information exchange procedure to LMF.
Support signalling the TRP Rx and TRP group RxTx IDs with UL measurements to LMF
Support of signalling the SRS Resource type for the UL measurement with TEG to LMF.
Implementation of RAN1 agreements from R1-2202541
Merge all applicable "measurement request" items from LMF in the MEASUREMENT REQUEST message in a new Measurement Characteristics Request Indicator IE coded as BIT STRING(16)
For DL-AoD, support to communicate the beam information to the LMF by enhancing the TRP Information Exchange procedure. The signalling allows a choice of how the information is provided, i.e. either the full list following the LPP format, or by referencing existing data for a TRP ID if the information coincides, or an indication that no change has occurred since last signalled configuration. 

Positioning Latency improvements
Addition of Response Time in NRPPa. The encoding of the IE follows LPP 
Addition of text procedure clarifying that the Response Time IE applies only for on Demand request
A new Measurement Preconfiguration Information Transfer function is introduced to enable the LMF to request the NG-RAN node to configure and activate measurement gap, and/or to pre-configure PRS processing window. 
The UE-associated class 1 procedure Measurement Preconfiguration supports the LMF to send the PRS information to the gNB and request for MG/PPW pre-configuration; the maximum number of TRPs in the MEASUREMENT PRECONFIGURATION REQUIRED message is 256 
The UE-associated class 2 procedure Measurement Activation supports the MG activation request by the LMF.
Include the similar information to that in RRC LocationMeasurementIdication message in the MEASUREMENT ACTIVATION message. The message indicates the MeasPRS Periodicity and Meas PRS Offset IEs.
For activation request procedure initiated by non-LMF, an unified signaling procedure over NRPPa can be adopted for the delivery of pre-configured MG and PRS processing Window configuration information.

Positioning with RRC_INACTIVE 
Introduce a new cause value in NRPPa when the UE has moved to another serving gNB node during RRC_INACTIVE mobility.
Include a UE Reporting Information IE in the POSITIONING INFORMATION REQUEST message to help gNB to configure CG-SDT resource. For Rel-17, the content of the UE Reporting Information IE follows LPP format

Rapporteur corrections
Section 9.2.38 (LCS to GCS Translation IE) is factorized
ASN.1 Corrections, such as from R3-216124.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Work item not completed.
reasonForChange:
The conclusion of TR 39.799 and the work item agreed on specifying an NR Femto architecture with an optional NR Femto Gateway. This leads to the following necessary changes in TS 38.413:
1/ at initial connection, the NR Femto indicates the received selected GUAMI, GUAMI Type or requested NSSAI to the NR Femto GW in order to route the message to the correct AMF. Then the NR Femto needs to know which AMF UE NGAP ID is assigned by AMF. This is needed for e.g. subsequent Xn handover.
2/ At incoming Xn handover to NR Femto, the NR Femto indicates in the Path Switch Request to the NR Femto GW the GUAMI of the AMF to route the message.
3/ At overload start/stop the NR Femto GW indicates to the NR Femtos which AMFs are affected by the overload (respectively overload stop). 
4/ when an Xn handover is performed successfully from an NR Femto connected to an NR Femto GW, the NR Femto GW needs to know if it needs to release its context.
5/ when an NG handover is performed towards a target NR Femto behind an NR Femto Gateway, the NR Femto Gateway needs to identify the target NR Femto node to route the Handover Request message.
summaryOfChange:
Introduction of NR Femto architecture with optional NR Femto GW. 

1/ The GUAMI, GUAMI type and Requested NSSAI are added to the NGAP Initial UE Message. The AMF UE NGAP ID2 is added to the Initial Context Setup Request, the Handover Request and the Path Switch Request Acknowledge messages. 

2/ add the Source GUAMI into the Path Switch Request message.

3/ Add a list of GUAMI(s) to the Overload Start/Overload Stop messages.

4/ Add a GW Release Indication in the NGAP UE Context Release Request message. 

5/ Add a Target RAN Node ID IE in the Handover Request message.

In most cases where the semantics description contains a “shall” statement, the “shall” is entirely unnecessary (e.g. introduced by mistake or poor drafting) and thus removed/reworded.

consequencesIfNotApproved:
The inter-donor re-routing is not able to open again once disabled.
The parameters for resource multiplexing and interference coordination is absent in the ASN.1 part.
The FDM is not able to be supported for IAB-node.
reasonForChange:
The F1-C Transfer Path NRDC IE is included in UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message, but the procedure text is missing.
The inter-donor-DU re-routing can be switch off by the re-routing disable indicator included in the BAP MAPPING CONFIGURATION message, but the indicator only contains value "true”. Thus, in current specification, it is unclear how can the Network to enable the re-routing if it was disabled by such indication
In section 9.3.1.108, the DU_RX/MT_RX, DU_TX/MT_TX, DU_TX/MT_RX and DU_RX/MT_TX in Multiplexing Info IE are not extendable in both tabular and ASN.1 part since Rel-16, the new value “supported and FDM required” should not be added directly to these four IEs. 
The “RB Set List” is not necessary with the latest RAN1 agreement “The start RB index of the first RB set for the Rel-17 IAB-DU HSNA resource configuration is the lowest index of RB of the IAB-DU cell”.
In section 9.3.1.107, the parameter “maxnoofRBsetsPerCell-1” has no dedinition in range bound tabular.
In the semantic description of IAB Conditional RRC Message Delivery Indication IE, the gNB-DU should be restricted to an IAB-DU.
The current description of the backhaul link in gNB-DU Status Indication procedure (i.e. “the backhaul link to the child node”) is not clear which link is congested, if the child node is dual connected or has multiple grandchild nodes, because a child node can has backhaul link with two parent nodes, as well as some grandchild nodes.
The wordings of “IP address(es)” and “IP address” both appear in the text of IAB TNL Address Exception IE included in IAB TNL ADDRESS REQUEST message, which causes ambiguity. 
In section 9.2.9.3, the order of TDD and FDD in the CHOICE IAB-DU Cell Resource Configuration-Mode-Info in the Neighbour-Node Cells List Item IE is not aligh with ASN.1 part. And the “FDD” label is missing in the tabular. Same problem is observed for the IAB-MT Cell NA Resource Configuration-Mode-Info in the Serving Cells List Item IE.
In 8.3.4.2, the following part is missing: how to handle conditional RRC message delivery in the case of migration/HO failure or arrival of a second RRC Reconfiguration.
The order of the IEs included in IAB-MT-Cell-NA-Resource-Configuration-FDD-Info IE not align with that in the table of clause 9.2.9.3.
The order of the IEs in IAB-DU-Cell-Resource-Configuration-FDD-Info-ExtIEs IE not align with that in the table of 9.2.9.3.
 In the current BAP Mapping Configuration message, there is only BAP Header Rewriting List IE. The IE is designed to configure BAP header rewriting and cannot be used to modify or remove a rewriting entry.
The terminology “Non-F1 terminating topology” has no relation with the IAB topic
In 8.10.1.2: Buffer Size Threshold is used to determine the DL congestion rather than trigger the DL local rerouting.
The gNB-CU/DU UE F1AP ID of child node in the Child IAB-nodes NA Resource List Item IE should be mandatory.
Some wording update is necessary, e.g. “collocated” is wrongly used in the specification
summaryOfChange:

In BAP MAPPING CONFIGURATION message, change the RE-Routing Disable Indicator IE to the Re-Routing Enable Indicator IE, and clarify how to enable the re-routing operation.
In section 9.3.1.108, add four new extended IEs to support FDM, and deleted the FDM support in the current multiplexing IEs.
 In section 9.3.1.230, remove “RB Set List” and add “Number of RB sets” in RB Set Configuration IE, and change the corresponding ASN.1.
In section 9.3.1.107, add the item of maxnoofRBsetsPerCell-1 in the Range Bound Explanation tables.
In section 9.2.2.7, for the semantic description of IAB Conditional RRC Message Delivery Indication IE, add sentence to indicate that the gNB-DU is an IAB-DU.
In section 8.2.7.1, describe the congested backhaul link in gNB-DU Status Indication procedure more accurately.
In section 8.10.3.2, use the wording of “IP address(es)” in the procedure text of IAB TNL Address Exception IE included in IAB TNL ADDRESS REQUEST message. 
In section 9.2.9.3, switch the order of TDD and FDD in the CHOICE IAB-DU Cell Resource Configuration-Mode-Info in the Neighbour-Node Cells List Item IE, as well as the CHOICE IAB-MT Cell NA Resource Configuration-Mode-Info in the Serving Cells List Item IE. Add the missing “FDD” label.

Correct the order of the IEs in IAB-MT-Cell-NA-Resource-Configuration-FDD-Info IE in ASN.1 as it is shown in the table of 9.2.9.3.
Correct the order of the IEs in IAB-DU-Cell-Resource-Configuration-FDD-Info-ExtIEs IE in ASN.1 as it is shown in the table of 9.2.9.3.

Use “Non-F1-Terminating IAB-donor Topology” to replace “Non-F1-Terminating Topology” in 9.2.9.1, 9.3.1.98, 9.3.1.114.
In 8.10.1.2: clarify the Buffer Size Threshold IE is used to determine the DL congestion.

consequencesIfNotApproved: RAN sharing with multiple Cell ID broadcast would not be supported.
reasonForChange:
RAN sharing with multiple Cell ID broadcast is not yet fully supported on F1AP. Dependent on whether PLMN specific F1-C interface instances with shared or separate signalling transport are used, additions have to be introduced.
For PLMN specific F1-C interface instances with separate signalling transport, 
the setup of an F1-C UE associated signalling connection might end up in the wrong gNB-CU, therefore protocol support is needed to cope with this situation.
For PLMN specific F1-C interface instances with shared signalling transport, the F1-C interface instance would need to be kept apart by proper F1AP protocol means.
summaryOfChange:
For separate signalling transport
1) The gNB-DU initiated UE Context release procedure is allowed to be initiated before the UE Context Setup procedure was issued.
2) The Served Cell Information needs to contain the information how the broadcast PLMN maps to the PLMN Index provided in some RRC msg3.

For common signalling transport
3) re-binding of UE associated signalling connections by means of allocating new UE F1AP IDs during the lifetime of a UE associated signalling connection.
4) adding a NOTE to hint to the fact that an implementation maps values of the Transaction ID and the UE F1AP IDs to the specific F1-C interface instance in order to identify the interface instance
5) an F1 Removal procedure is introduced

Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it introduces full support of the RAN sharing function with multiple Cell ID broadcast.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the RAN sharing function.
title: RAN sharing with multiple Cell ID broadcast

Rel-18, in CR1069r8, introduced in the ASN.1 PDU definition of the HANDOVER REQUEST message, the HandoverRequest PDU definition, the new Source SN to Target SN QMC Information IE with the ProtocolIE-ID id-QMCConfigInfo. 

While it is possible to include IEs referring to the same TYPE definition, including a new IE with a ProtocolIE-ID set to the same value as for IE already included in the ProtocolIE-Container makes this new IE undistinguishable to the already existing one.

As CR1069r8 introduced the new Source SN to Target SN QMC Information IE also within the ASN.1 PDU defintion of the the S-NODE ADDITION REQUEST, the S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE, the S-NODE MODIFICATION REQUIRED and the S-NODE CHANGE REQUIRED messages, the reference to ProtocolIE-ID id-QMCConfigInfo would need to be replaced by the new ProtocolIE-ID id-SourceSN-to-TargetSN-QMCInformation.

consequencesIfNotApproved: L1/L2 triggered mobility based procedures cannot be supported on F1.
reasonForChange: In order to fulfil the objectives of the WID in RP-221799 (NR_Mob_enh2) a number of changes are required. This CR implements the changes in the affected procedures between gNB-DU, and gNB-CU.
secretaryRemarks: Source modified on 11/24/2023. Original source : Ericsson, Huawei, Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, ZTE, NEC, LG Electronics Inc., Lenovo, CATT, Samsung, Qualcomm Incorporated
summaryOfChange:
Add an abbreviation “LTM” to represent “L1/L2 triggered mobility”.
Introduce new LTM Information Setup IE, Early Sync Information Request, and LTM Configuration ID Mapping List IEs to the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message.
Introdue new IEs named Early Sync Information and LTM Configuration to the UE CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message.
Introduce new LTM Information Modify IE, Early Sync Information List, Early Sync Information Request, LTM Configuration ID Mapping List, and LTM Cells to be Released List to the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message.

Add the LTM Cells to be Released List in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUIRED messages.
Add description to the UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST and UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND messages for the release of configured LTM cells.
Introduce two new Class 2 procedures for Cell Switch Notification i.e., DU-CU Cell Switch Notification, and CU-DU Cell Switch Notification.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Incomplete or incorrect specification.
reasonForChange:
1/ Multicast: The MBS Session TNL Information 5GC IE and the MBS Session TNL Information NG-RAN IE are not correctly defined in the tabular, and the asn1 is also not aligned.

2/ Multicast: CT4 has agreed for a scenario of MB-UPF recovery that the MB-SMF will update the mulitcast addresses towards the NG-RAN node via the MB-SMF container of a Multicast Session Update message.

3/ Multicast: sections 9.3.1.111, 9.3.1.212, 9.3.1.213, 9.3.1.214 are missing descriptive sentences.

4/ Multicast: the unsuccessful operation of section 8.18.5.3 says “not applicable” but the MBS Session Update actually has a failure message which should be described.

5/ Multicast: the section 8.4.2.2 mentions the the MBS Session Information IE to be included in the HANDOVER REQUEST message but such IE does not exist (need to be removed). The section 8.18.1.2 also mentions the Shared NG-U TNL Information IE which does not exist and should be replaced by the Shared NG-U Unicast TNL Information IE

6/ Multicast: SA2 has agreed tdoc S2-2201324 enabling AMF to prioritize among the paging request of different MBS sessions by giving the most demanding ARP/5QI to the AMF. 
However an NG-RAN node receives group paging messages for different MBS sessions from multiple AMF and it is also needed that it can prioritize among these different request.

7/ Broadcast: SA2 has agreed tdoc S2-2201321 which specifies that during Broadcast Sesion Start and Broadcast Session Update the MB-SMF may include the MBS FSA ID(s) for the MBS session and send them to the NG-RAN nodes via the AMF. The NG-RAN nodes may then use those MBS FSA ID(s) to determine cells/frequencies within the MBS serice area to broadcast MBS session data.

8/ Broadcast: SA2 has agreed tdoc S2-2202143, for gNB triggered broadcast session release required, SA2 decided to add the DL TEIDs to be release in the Broadcast Release Response container. There could be one per area session.

9/ Broadcast/Multicast: the term “location independent” MBS session is not aligned with SA2 and should be replaced by “local” MBS session.

consequencesIfNotApproved: The NG-RAN cannot know the V2X UE authorization status from a trusted node. Also the sidelink AMBR and other PC5 QoS parameters for UE’s sidelink communication cannot be supported.
reasonForChange: In order to support NR V2X, changes are needed on the NGAP protocol. This is the baseline CR covering all the agreed changes.
summaryOfChange:
The new extensible NR V2X Services Authorized IE and LTE V2X Services Authorized IE are introduced in the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST, HANDOVER REQUEST and PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLEDGE messages. It provides “authorized” and “not authorized” values for NR V2X services and LTE V2X services, which include Vehicle UE, Pedestrian UE or both. 
In addition, the new NR UE Sidelink Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE and LTE UE Sidelink Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE are introduced in the INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST, HANDOVER REQUEST and PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLEDGE messages.
The PC5 QoS Parameters are introduced in INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST, UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST, HANDOVER REQUEST and PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLEDGE messages.
Support of Alternative QoS in PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP REQUEST, PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY REQUEST, HANDOVER REQUEST and PATH SWITCH REQUEST messages.
title: Support of NR V2X over NG

In most cases where the semantics description contains a “shall” statement, the “shall” is entirely unnecessary (e.g. introduced by mistake or poor drafting) and thus removed/reworded.

consequencesIfNotApproved: Incomplete, contradicting and erroneous specification text will remain.
reasonForChange:
1/ Usage, semantics and allocation of MRB IDs is not sufficiently specified
2/ A reference to the term MBS session resource is missing and the term is not consistently used.
2.2a/ For broadcast MBS sessions there is no need to distinguish between “MBS context” and “MBS session resources”.
7.1/ The procedure text of the Multicast Session Update procedure in the “General” section needs to be simplified and the term “MBS information” should be replaced by the defined term “NG-RAN MBS session resource”. Also the case where the Multicast Session Update Request Transfer IE is including the MBS Session TNL Information 5GC IE is missing in the procedure text. Also, the MBS Session TNL Information 5GC IE is applicable for broadcast and multicast MBS sessions.
7.2/ The MBS Session ID, according to TS 23.247, identifies an MBS session, not an MBS service, as stated in the respective IE subclause §9.3.1.206 for the MBS Session ID IE. 
7.3/ The term “flow” as a short form for “MBS QoS flow” is used. 
7.4/ In addition, TS 23.247, the term “MBS QoS profile” is used to denote the set of MBS QoS flow level QoS paramters information for all MBS QoS flows associated with an MBS Session. However, this term is not used consistently.
7.5/ Minor updates on errors and incosistencies in the specification text are necessary.
summaryOfChange:
1/ For MRB ID IE a reference to TS 38.401 is included where the usage and allocation of MRB IDs is specified
2/ a reference to the term MBS session resource is included and its usage aligned within specification text
2.2a/ For broadcast MBS session NGAP protocol definition, the term “MBS session resources” is used instead of “MBS context”.
7.1/ The term “NG-RAN MBS session resource context” is introduced in the definition section and referenced within the Multicast Session Update procedure and the procedure text of that EP completed to also cover the case where the Shared NG-U Multicast TNL Information is modified (at the 5GC) and remove the restriction that the MBS Session TNL Information 5GC IE is applicable for broadcast MBS sessions only.
7.2/ Correct in §9.3.1.206 that the MBS Session ID identifies an MBS session rather than an MBS service. 
7.3/ The term “MBS QoS flow” is introduced where only its short form “flow” is used.
7.4/ The term “MBS QoS profile” is used consistently.
7.5/ Minor updates on errors and incosistencies in the specification text are performed.
Impact Analysis:
Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): 
This CR has isolated impact with the previous version of the specification (same release) because it corrects incomplete, contradicting and erroneous definitions of the NR MBS function only.
The impact can be considered isolated because the change affects only the NR MBS function.
The extension of the MRB ID IE range has protocol and ASN.1 impact.
